# WWI CEF War Diaries — Master Searchable Index
The single searchable index for the whole archive, merged daily by the digest task (`wwi-war-diary-daily-digest`) from the eight per-eighth indexes (`INDEX-A.md` … `INDEX-H.md`). Rebuilt from scratch each day, so corrections in the eighth indexes replace stale entries here.
- **Coverage:** 467 CEF unit war diaries with a diary line in the LAC finding aid (RG 9 III-D-3), transcribed from Library and Archives Canada digitized pages. (The ~1,587 figure in early planning counts diary volumes/folders; the guide's with-diary unit total is 467.)
- **Status (28 Oct 2026):** 23313 dated entries from 37 unit(s) so far; 23313 entries merged from 8 eighth index file(s). Date range 1914-09-15 to 1919-06-30.
- **Entries are sorted by date, then unit.** Each entry keeps: date, unit, location, people named, companies/platoons, casualties, movements, what happened — plus a pointer to the full transcript under `diaries/<unit-slug>/` (see Sources below).
- **Uncertain readings** in the transcripts are marked [uncertain]; nothing is guessed.

- **November 1917** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1917-11.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0179`–`page-0191`, `manifest.json`). Readability note: the November hand is the same cramped hand as August–October, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C & D Companies move south to Lebuquiere (3rd Army North) on 6 November; from then the diary covers both the 1st Army area (A & B Coys at Barlin) and the 3rd Army area (C & D Coys at Lebuquiere). The O.C. changes during the month: the diary is signed at month end by W. Stewart [uncertain], Lt. Col., not J. B. Macdonald.

- **December 1917** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1917-12.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0192`–`page-0208`, `manifest.json`). December has 19 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 17 physical pages. Contents page lists "Diary Text 7 Pages" but the diary text in fact runs 11 pages (pp. 6–16, 1–31 Dec); Appendices 1–3 are pp. 17–19 (congratulatory messages, 28 Nov – 24 Dec 1917). Readability note: the December hand is the same cramped hand as August–November, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C & D Coys return from the 3rd Army area to Barlin on 6–8 Dec and begin the "Cape to Cairo" lateral light-railway line. The diary is signed at month end by J. B. L. Macdonald, Lt.-Col. Reconciliation note: the 16 Dec casualty is recorded as "Pte Cooney [uncertain] No 279834" (p. 11) but the 30 Dec entry reports "Sgt Cooney J. D. (No. 22983), awarded M.M., killed by shell fire 16th inst." — rank and number differ between the two entries and are NOT reconciled; see the transcript's reconciliation notes.

- **January 1918** — Source: LAC Collection Search Item ID 2004961 (RG 9 III-D-3, vol. 5012, folder 733; reels T-10861–T-10862). Full transcript: `diaries/3rd-battalion-canadian-railway-troops/transcript-1918-01.md`. Page images: same folder (`page-0209`–`page-0221`, `manifest.json`). January has 15 numbered pages; pp. 4–5 are absent from the LAC manifest, so 13 physical pages. Contents page lists "Diary Text 9 Pages" — diary text is pp. 6–14 (9 pages) and p. 15 is Appendix 1 (typed letter dated 18 Jan 1918 proposing standardisation of light-railway rules), so the contents page is exact. Readability note: the January hand is the same cramped hand as August–December, and many words are only partly legible — entries below record what could be read reliably. C Coy begins work on the Cape to Cairo lateral line; 300 Chinese labourers start on it 3 Jan; Lt-Col Macdonald is awarded the D.S.O. and Sergt Glisson the D.C.M. (10 Jan); Macdonald proceeds on leave 22 Jan and the month is signed by J. [uncertain] Stewart, Major. Reconciliation note: 1 Jan confirms Spr J. W. Cooney, No 279834, killed 16 Dec 1917, but the 30 Dec entry's "Sgt Cooney J. D., No 22983" still conflicts — not reconciled; see the transcript's reconciliation notes.

- **1915-02-03 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Camp No. 6, Le Havre** — Arrived by route march at 11 P.M. and encamped. | Casualties: none. | Movement: route march to Camp No. 6 and encamped.
- **1915-02-03 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Le Havre** — Disembarked at Quai Pondicherry. | Casualties: none. | Movement: disembarked at Le Havre.
- **1915-02-04 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Le Havre** — Under canvas at Camp No. 6 from 9 A.M. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Unit prepared to disembark from H.M. Transport, reported to the Base Commandant at the Palais de Justice, and billeted 4 N.C.O.s and 22 men at Caserne Trupel, Rue de Lyons. | Casualties: none. | Movement: disembarked at Rouen.
- **1915-02-08 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Reported to A.D.M.S. No. II Base, indented for ordnance and stationery, arranged for the section's N.C.O.s to learn duties from the Rouen sanitary section, and sent an orderly for standing orders and daily orders. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-09 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Detailed corporals and lance corporals for duty with the Sanitary Police in the city and indented for completion of clothing. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Medically examined the entire personnel of the Sanitary Section at 8 a.m. and drew ordnance and supplies as completely as were available. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — The section's motor lorry collided with motor car 780-Y 4 at about 3 miles an hour, springing a mud guard (righted by hand, undamaged) and cracking a brass axle cap in two, the repair probably costing 4 francs. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Rouen** — Visited by Lieut Dickson, A.S.C., in charge of an ambulance convoy, who had orders to proceed and verbal orders for Woodhouse to accompany him; the orders were verbally confirmed at A.D.T. and orders issued for movement at 8.30 a.m. | People: Lieut Dickson. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-11 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Neufchâtel** — Unit left Rouen at 8.30 a.m. with the ambulances and arrived at Neufchâtel at 3 p.m. for the night, the Quartermaster Sergeant, groom and horse being left behind, the horse and groom attached to the Cavalry Division for transport to the destination. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Rouen → Neufchâtel.
- **1915-02-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Abbeville** — Left Neufchâtel at 6.40 a.m. and arrived at Abbeville at noon. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Neufchâtel → Abbeville.
- **1915-02-13 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Arques** — Left Abbeville at 8.30 a.m., arrived at St. Omer at 3 p.m., reported to A.D.M.S., and was assigned billets at Arques, billeted at 5 p.m. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Abbeville → Arques (via St. Omer).
- **1915-02-15 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Outtersteene** — Marched out of Arques at 7.30 a.m., reported to D.M.S. Hazebrouck, the men being conveyed by ambulance to Merris and marching to billets at Outtersteene, distributed chloride of lime to units of 1st Brigade for water purification, and reported to A.D.M.S. Canadians at 8 p.m. in heavy snow (the events of 14 February are reported inside this entry). | Casualties: none. | Movement: Arques → Outtersteene (via Hazebrouck and Merris).
- **1915-02-16 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — On orders received at noon, moved the corps to new billets at Strazeele Station, occupying them by 4 p.m., and supplied 1st Brigade Office with 20 extra tins of chloride of lime and a supply to the Brigadier, 3rd Brigade. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Outtersteene → Strazeele.
- **1915-02-17 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Despatched a party by lorry to Outtersteene for house-to-house visitation to locate enteric fever among civilians, present or within six months past, and to make a sanitary survey and report, with one squad on guard during the night and a fourth squad cleaning the section's own billets. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-18 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Despatched men to complete the enteric enquiry and sanitary survey of Outtersteene and Merris. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-19 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Completed the enquiry and survey of Strazeele and personally visited houses reported by the squads in Strazeele, Merris and Outtersteene to enquire into cases of illness, none of which proved to be a reportable communicable disease, and arranged hot baths for the whole section the next morning. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-20 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Pradeele and Borre were surveyed as above. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Caestre was surveyed as above. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-22 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Caestre survey completed and Flêtre undertaken, with house-to-house enquiry into infectious diseases completed that day in Merris and Outtersteene, suspicious houses being placed out of bounds for Canadians. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-23 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Flêtre and Meteren were surveyed. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-23 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Le Havre** — Entrained with equipment from Quai Pondicherry at 4.30 P.M. | Casualties: none. | Movement: entrained at Le Havre.
- **1915-02-24 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — No separate summary is given for this date; the line appears to continue the Flêtre / Meteren survey. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-24 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Boulogne-sur-Mer** — Arrived at Boulogne-sur-Mer at 12.30 P.M., detrained; equipment stored and the company quartered at the Convalescent Camp, Boulogne. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Le Havre → Boulogne-sur-Mer.
- **1915-02-25 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Meteren survey completed and four squads placed to police Outtersteene, Merris and Strazeele in the afternoon. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-26 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Troops of 1st Brigade were re-billeted under the section's personal supervision, suspicious houses not being used, and a case of civilian enteric near Caestre was ordered cleared to Bailleul. | Casualties: civilian enteric case near Caestre cleared to Bailleul; none among the section.
- **1915-02-27 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Strazeele** — Accompanied A.D.M.S. to visit a new area and spent the day with D.A.D.M.S. and O.C. Sanitary Section, 7th Division, preparing to take over their area, and received orders to move tomorrow. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-02-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Left Merris at 9 a.m. and marched until 8 p.m. before receiving billets. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Merris → Sailly-sur-la-Lys.
- **1915-03-01 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Proceeded to MERRIS, destroyed horse, ordered removal and burial, paid for same, also for keep. Remark: Judging from the condition of the feet of sick horses received, it appears that there must either be a shortage of shoes, or else feet are not receiving sufficient attention. | Casualties: 1 horse destroyed. | Movement: Proceeded to Merris.
- **1915-03-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Granted temporary accommodation in the offices occupied by the O.C. Sanitary Section of the 7th Division and made rounds with him. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Proceeded to CAESTRE, found horse dead, paid for removal, burial and keep. | Casualties: 1 horse died. | Movement: Proceeded to Caestre.
- **1915-03-02 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had the men's billets scrubbed from top to bottom, mapped out areas for inspection purposes, and instructed the section as to the nature of the work desired. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — No forage for horses or rations for men, owing to Supply Column moving to SAILLY and making no arrangements for supplies for Unit. Purchased forage out of Imprest Account. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Investigated three billets which had been occupied by an enteric case and saw to the cleansing of them. | Casualties: civilian enteric case (billets cleansed); none among the section.
- **1915-03-04 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Meteren** — Removed to CROIX DU BAC. Billeted at farm between CROIX DU BAC and BAC ST. MAUR. Still without rations. Purchased forage for horses. Remark: This would be of considerable advantage in dealing with cases of skin disease, which is very prevalent here. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Removed to Croix du Bac.
- **1915-03-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Inspected the General's château and a factory occupied by Ordnance. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 5 sick horses from 6th. Division Mobile Veterinary Section, belonging to Canadian Division, also 2 from 2nd and 3rd Infantry Brigades. | People: 6th. Division Mobile Veterinary Section; 2nd and 3rd Infantry Brigades. | Casualties: 7 horses received.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Installed a new portable sanitary closet at the château made [uncertain] of biscuit tins, with a reversible tightly fly-proof covered seat, and had the Ordnance depot made [uncertain] and reported its defects to its O.C. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-05 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Montreal, Canada** — Mobilised under G.O. Headquarters, 4th Div., Canada, at McGill University Buildings. | Movement: mobilisation at Montreal.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 5 sick horses. 1 died. | Casualties: 5 horses received, 1 horse died.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had the factory near Ordnance cleaned by the section and made fit for billets. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-06 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Montreal, Canada** — Internal economy arranged and organised; stretcher and squad drill; instruction.
- **1915-03-07 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 1 sick horse, 1 died, 1 [uncertain] cured. | Casualties: 1 horse received, 1 horse died, 1 horse issued cured.
- **1915-03-07 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Located four infected houses and attended to them, with [uncertain] information from the local French physician. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-08 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Proceeded to METEREN and BORRE, paid for keep of 4 horses and brought same to CROIX DU BAC. Remark: I consider a light Float essential for evacuating severe cases of lameness &c. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Proceeded to Meteren and Borre.
- **1915-03-08 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Investigated a house where a child had died presumably of scarlet fever and had the soldiers billeted there placed under quarantine. | Casualties: child died presumably of scarlet fever.
- **1915-03-09 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 6 sick horses. Proceeded to ARMENTIERES in afternoon & purchased drugs. | Casualties: 6 horses received. | Movement: Proceeded to Armentieres.
- **1915-03-09 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had a house refused to [uncertain] cleaned and reported the matter to A.D.M.S. re the platoon previously occupying the billet. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-10 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 19 sick horses. Remark: Difficulty is experienced in obtaining sufficient bran for sick horses. | Casualties: 19 horses received.
- **1915-03-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Made a complete survey of the division as to the practice of chlorinating wells for troops and the use of milk. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-11 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 1 sick horse. | Casualties: 1 horse received.
- **1915-03-11 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Complete water and milk enquiry started the previous day. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-12 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — 12 sick horses evacuated to Base Veterinary Hospital. Went to PRADELLES, METEREN, STRAZEELE and BAILLEUL. Remark: A large number of the cases received were in my opinion of a septic form, due in all probability, to bad water. | People: No. 5 Mobile Veterinary Section. | Casualties: 2 horses died, 12 horses evacuated, 8 horses issued cured. | Movement: Went to Pradelles Meteren Strazeele and Bailleul.
- **1915-03-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had squads doing fatigue work or overseeing work done by others in cleaning up unsanitary billets. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-13 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 3 sick horses & issued 3 cured to replace [uncertain]. | Casualties: 3 horses received, 3 horses issued cured.
- **1915-03-13 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had squads make sanitary surveys of their allotted areas. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-13 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Honeault Camp [uncertain]** — Ground staked 13–15 March for establishing a tented hospital of 300 beds; the remainder of the month was spent establishing and equipping the hospital. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-14 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 7 sick horses. Went to BORRE, paid for keep of horse abandoned at farm & brought same in. | Casualties: 7 horses received. | Movement: Went to Borre.
- **1915-03-14 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Sailly-sur-la-Lys** — Had squads organise a new area to be occupied for billets and enquire into the incidence of disease among civilians, continued and completed to 15 March. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-03-15 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Croix du Bac** — Received 3 sick horses. Issued 3 cured to replace. | Casualties: 3 horses received, 3 horses issued cured.

- **1915-06-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Honeault Camp, France** — Patients remaining in hospital 16; patients admitted during the month: sick 238, wounded 397, total 635; the character of the cases has been of a light nature, usually requiring some minor operative work and nursing and evacuable in a short time; several interesting medical cases came under observation — pericarditis 1, Vincent's angina 1, atropine poisoning 1, typhoid 1 [uncertain] 3 paratyphoid [uncertain] — and the atropine poisoning case, following an inoculation or re-vaccination [uncertain], developed symptoms typical of atropine poisoning which subsided under treatment, returned the following day resembling meningitis, could not be confirmed by puncture, and did not react to treatment, with prominent meningeal symptoms and a strong hysterical element; the case was transferred (as written, "to No 1 Stationary Hosp.") under suspicion, and the diagnosis since received is uncertain, with no confirmation of meningitis; average days in hospital during the month 3.27. | Casualties: 635 admitted in the month (238 sick, 397 wounded); no deaths recorded.
- **1915-06-30 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre** — Admitted 11 horses and 19 mules from Remounts; during the month of June 991 horses and mules were dealt with — 100 discharged cured to Remount Depot, 194 to Convalescent Farm, Gournay-en-Bras, 12 died and destroyed, 12 sold to butcher for slaughter, 2 cast and sold by auction, 671 remaining under treatment; much work put into [paving — uncertain] flooring of stables, badly broken up by the heavy horses [formerly — uncertain] in the hospital, a new quality of [brick — uncertain] obtained tougher than the [brick — uncertain] used formerly; dangerous areas railed in; three small [exercise — uncertain] rings built in the "dells" of the [picket — uncertain] field, particularly useful in catarrh cases; grazing grounds acquired and being fenced in; subdivisional forage sheds put up; present average strength of sick horses and mules about 700; strength in personnel 196 NCOs and men, at least 25 more men required; Expeditionary Force Canteen established in a marquee for NCOs and men; watering difficult, some 150 horses on lines near the exercise ring on the north side of [Moles — uncertain], necessitating [two — uncertain] water carts going constantly to fill a tank in the exercise ring; Leckie recommended a water tank with a force pump be put up so enough pressure could carry water down to a row of troughs on the north side of the exercise ring. | Casualties: monthly totals — 12 died and destroyed; 12 sold to butcher for slaughter; 2 cast and sold by auction.

- **1915-10-01 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Hut accommodation increased by the addition of 2 huts, so the hospital can now accommodate 550 patients; still some difficulty in getting food supplies outside of rations; dysentery cases on the increase and of a more resistant nature; weather exceptionally fine, when very warm flies increase; sanitary conditions much improved. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-10-01 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre** — Capt. W. T. W. T. Stedman, Medical Officer. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Capt. Stedman on leave to England.

- **1915-10-09 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Reinforcements of seven men arrived by the hospital ship Delta on 9 October; Col Agnew, Camp Commandant, inspected the hospital; eleven hospital ships in the harbour on 10 October; troops leaving for Salonica; commenced use of water from a tank brought through pipes from the condenser on 13 October; 90% of patients in hospital from troops on Lemnos, i.e. having contracted dysentery since coming here in the majority of cases; evenings become quite cool, days very fine; amoebic dysentery becoming less, bacillary on the increase; all cases lack the very acute symptoms of early cases but are more severe owing to delay in reaching hospital. | People: Col Agnew. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-10-31 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Month summary (written up 31 October, covering the rest of the month): Col McKee sailed for England on the hospital ship Aquitania on 18 October and Major E. J. Williams assumed temporary command; progress of patients in hospital very slow owing to the severity of the disease, with rheumatism(?) and jaundice common sequelae to dysentery; one case of beri-beri in hospital; a tent section was opened for venereal and infectious cases — syphilis, gonorrhoea, scarlet fever, diphtheria, chicken pox, mumps and measles, 50 cases in all — with diphtheria from the Australian Rest Camp, 17 cases developing in one week; 638 cases in hospital on 18 October and an average daily state for the month of 550; the death rate in the last two weeks of September was 6 times any previous two weeks, due to cases arriving in hospital in a late stage of disease; S.S. Aquitania left for England on 21 October; high winds for 4 days blowing down some tents; General Munro, who succeeded Sir Ian Hamilton, inspected troops and hospitals on 27 October; the Welsh Division returning from the Peninsula and Australians preparing to return; many severe cases of bacillary dysentery in hospital; six post mortems held during the month; health of personnel good except among the new drafts of men, everyone seeming to develop enteritis and diarrhoea a few days after arriving on the island, the attacks as a rule not lasting longer than one week; general improvement in all supplies except equipment; besides the reinforcements of 7 men there was a further addition of 27 men and one officer, Capt. Creighton; five men of the unit were invalided home to England; all nursing sisters are comfortably accommodated in canvas huts, officers and men still in tents; buildings for ordnance stores, offices etc. not yet erected; the X ray department moved into the Operating Room building; very much cramped for room for patients, 550 being accommodated in 12 huts planned to hold 25 patients each; 18 deaths in October as compared with 4 in September, 90% being due to dysentery. | People: Col McKee; Major E. J. Williams; General Munro; Sir Ian Hamilton; Capt. Creighton. | Casualties: 18 deaths in October (90% dysentery), as compared with 4 in September; 638 cases in hospital on 18 October; average daily state 550.
- **1915-10-31 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre** — 13 horses admitted to hospital; monthly totals: 512 under treatment 1 October, 259 admitted, 771 total cases, 267 cured to Remounts, none destroyed unfit for food, 3 died unfit for food, 13 destroyed fit for food, 488 remaining under treatment 31 October. | Casualties: monthly totals — 3 died unfit for food, 13 destroyed fit for food.
- **1915-10-31 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — O.C.'s memorandum on the hospital's condition: the 25 October storm accentuated the conditions; transferring patients to the operating theatre under canvas adds considerably to shock; situation "totally unsuitable for the purpose for which it was originally intended". Surgical report (Lt-Col J. M. Elder): 1,650 patients admitted to surgical wards, 36 deaths, 450 operations, 21 deaths among operated patients; septic knee joints, anaesthesia, X-ray and laboratory work praised. Laboratory report (Capt. L. J. Rhea): clinical and bacteriological work; September examinations (urine 659, blood 179, faeces 20, sputum 25, gastric 12); typhoid group; special cases. Ambulances gifted by Mrs. Huntley Drummond, Mrs. W. R. Miller, the citizens of Montreal through Lady Allan and the citizens of Quebec through Mrs. Turner: 350 runs, 2,035 patients carried August–October, at no cost to the Government. | People: Lt-Col J. M. Elder, Capt. L. J. Rhea, Mrs. Huntley Drummond, Mrs. W. R. Miller, Lady Allan, Mrs. Turner. | Casualties: surgical wards — 36 deaths of 1,650 admitted; 21 deaths among 450 operated.

- **1915-11-22 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hazebrouck** — The regiment paraded at 7 a.m., vacated billets and arrived at Hill 63 at noon, with squadrons and H.Q. staff occupying huts at Hill 63 and transport occupying billets at Petit Pont Farm with the Machine Gun Section, in cold and misty weather. | People: — | Companies: Machine Gun Section | Casualties: none | Movement: Hazebrouck to Hill 63.
- **1915-11-22 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 8 sick horses. | Casualties: 8 horses received.
- **1915-11-22 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Nieppe** — Handed over the Convalescent Company definitely to Lieut. Hirsch, retaining 10 as a fatigue for the new location, and the first load started for St Jans Cappel at 8.30 a.m. in charge of Sgt Maj Ross but broke down half a mile away, was towed in by the D.M. Workshop and replaced, reaching St Jans at noon instead of 10 a.m., with the unit occupying the billets not yet moved, and the Convalescent Company moved to farm billets on Neuve Eglise Road above Bulford Camp. | People: Lieut. Hirsch, Sgt Maj Ross. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Nieppe to St Jans Cappel (first load).
- **1915-11-22 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Selection of cast animals for decision by the D.D.V.S.; D.D.V.S. (Southern) visited the hospital 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.; Garrison Quartermaster inspected stores 3 to 5 p.m.; 12 horses and 3 mules admitted. | People: D.D.V.S. (Southern), Garrison Quartermaster. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-22 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Lt. Colonel H. B. Yates evacuated to England 8.30 a.m.; O.C.'s tribute to Yates as second in command since mobilisation. O.C. with Lt-Col McCrae, Maj Meakins (A/Registrar) and Capt. Lew (Quartermaster) again inspected the Meerut Hospital with Senior Sanitary Officer Maj Tyndall: conditions "totally unsuited for a British Unit"; officers' accommodation for only 11 of 35 officers. | People: Lt-Col H. B. Yates, Lt-Col J. McCrae, Maj Meakins, Capt. Lew, Maj Tyndall. | Casualties: Lt-Col H. B. Yates evacuated sick to England.
- **1915-11-23 | 18th Battalion | In field** — "A" and "B" Companies battalion reserve; "C" and "D" Companies in the trenches.
- **1915-11-23 | 24th Battalion | France** — Marched out from Locre and relieved the 25th Bn. in the same trenches as on 15 November. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Locre to trenches near Kemmel | Locations: Kemmel
- **1915-11-23 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — A and B Squadrons occupied Trenches 131 and 130 respectively, B Squadron with one squadron of the 4th C.M.R. relieved the regimental reserve of the 5th Battalion, and two troops of C Squadron held the reserve dugouts on Hill 63 while the remainder garrisoned Stable Fort, all reliefs completed by 5:30 p.m. with no casualties. | People: — | Companies: A, B, C Squadrons | Casualties: none | Movement: into Trenches 130 and 131, Hill 63 and Stable Fort.
- **1915-11-23 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Proceeded to METEREN for purpose of collecting 3 sick horses left at farms by Canadian Mounted Rifles. The horses were unfit to move and arranged to hire floats for this purpose. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Proceeded to Meteren.
- **1915-11-23 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Spent the morning straightening up grounds and getting things in order, the last (6th) load arriving in the afternoon, and at 12.30 p.m. Gen. Alderson, accompanied by Col. [uncertain] D.M.S., inspected the Sanitary Section at their billets — 22 men and 10 fatigues paraded — speaking encouragingly and praising their conduct. | People: Gen. Alderson. | Casualties: none. | Movement: move to St Jans Cappel completed.
- **1915-11-23 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — D.V.S. I.G.C. visited and inspected the hospital; horses are being kicked in the shelters because they stand in couples with no [bails — uncertain] between; Engineers say the sheds are not strong enough for bails; the General suggests [larch — uncertain] poles and uprights to prevent kicking; Col. Neill objected to Capt Stedman (attached temporarily, surplus to establishment) being sent to 2nd Army, Imperial; General Moore states Stedman may be sent to England if Col. Neill so desires; 29 horses admitted. | People: D.V.S. I.G.C., Col. Neill, Capt Stedman, General Moore. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-23 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Completely packed up and ready for evacuation at a moment's notice.
- **1915-11-24 | 18th Battalion | In field** — "B" and "C" [uncertain] Companies relieved by "A" and "D" in the trenches (company letters unclear; the reading does not square with the 23 November entry).
- **1915-11-24 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Battalion marched out to the trenches, taking over from the 25th Battalion; quiet along the frontage. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Locre to the trenches
- **1915-11-24 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — C Squadron furnished a working party of one officer and 25 men for the support trenches, Pte Roper J. [uncertain] was accidentally wounded in the foot in a subsidiary trench at Ash House, and our artillery heavily bombarded the enemy trenches while the enemy stayed quiet except for snipers. | People: Pte Roper J. [uncertain] No 110030 | Companies: C Squadron | Casualties: 1 wounded — Pte Roper J. [uncertain] (accidental foot wound, Ash House).
- **1915-11-24 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 4 sick horses. | Casualties: 4 horses received.
- **1915-11-24 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Men held in camp until 1 p.m. to finish settling, inspection parties started their usual inspections, visited Aldershot and Bulford Camps in the morning where disinfectors are progressing slowly, the Bulford well started on Monday was commenced without curbing and fell in this morning, liberated the measles quarantine at Cour Dreve with no cases having developed, and in the afternoon visited the Dranoutre area and Woods Camp, where the mud is probably the worst in the Division. | Casualties: none; measles quarantine at Cour Dreve lifted, no cases developed.
- **1915-11-24 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — High wind which has lasted 5 days subsiding and weather quite warm; evacuated 194 patients to the Aquitania (27th); the new draft of nurses, 13 in number, landed on the island today and were taken on strength of the unit; two cases of acute mania in hospital; a consignment of Red Cross goods arrived today. | Casualties: 194 patients evacuated to the Aquitania; 2 cases of acute mania in hospital.
- **1915-11-24 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 8 horses and 6 mules admitted; 28 horses and 10 mules discharged cured. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-24 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Captain J. W. Hutchison returned from leave.
- **1915-11-25 | 18th Battalion | In field** — "A" and "D" Companies in the trenches; "B" and "C" in reserve at Vierstraat. | Locations: Vierstraat.
- **1915-11-25/26 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Fairly quiet on the front; Cpl A. Cameron #65147 received a slight shrapnel wound in the leg. | People: Cpl A. Cameron #65147 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded
- **1915-11-25 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — The usual working party was supplied in the morning, the 4th C.M.R. relieved two troops of C Squadron in Stable Fort, and at 5 p.m. C Squadron relieved B Squadron in the trenches by 7:35 p.m. without casualties, in clear and cold weather with very muddy ground. | People: — | Companies: B, C Squadrons | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-25 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 3 sick horses and 2 surplus from 8th. Labour Battn. Returned 3 cured. Evacuated 9 to No. 10 Veterinary Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. | People: No. 10 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 3 horses received, 9 horses evacuated, 3 horses issued cured.
- **1915-11-25 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — In the morning visited the Neuve Eglise areas, the Bulford well being commenced anew after Monday's caved in, the disinfectors at a standstill, liberated the measles quarantine with no cases in 14 days, and the Convalescent Camp getting in good running order; in the afternoon visited Dranoutre Camp. | Casualties: none; measles quarantine lifted, no cases in 14 days.
- **1915-11-25 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 1 horse destroyed. | Casualties: 1 horse destroyed.
- **1915-11-25 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-11-26 | 18th Battalion | In field** — Battalion relieved by the 19th Battalion; 18th Battalion to brigade reserve at Ridgewood. | Companies: 19th Battalion. | Movement: Vierstraat → Ridgewood.
- **1915-11-26/27 | 24th Battalion | In the Field / Locre, Belgium** — Relieved by the 25th Battalion and returned to billets in Locre; exchange effected safely; Cpl J. Coulson #65000 received a wound in the leg. | People: Cpl J. Coulson #65000 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded | Movement: trenches to billets in Locre | Locations: Locre
- **1915-11-26 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — Men in the trenches repaired parapets and drained trenches while our artillery stayed very active and the enemy did not retaliate, and Pte R. Freke of C Squadron was wounded in the foot while with the squadron ration party on Messines Road about 6 p.m. | People: Pte R. Freke No 110462 | Companies: C Squadron | Casualties: 1 wounded — Pte R. Freke (foot wound, Messines Road).
- **1915-11-26 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 3 sick horses. | Casualties: 3 horses received.
- **1915-11-26 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Raining and snowing all day, got money from the Paymaster to pay the men, a complaint that one battalion had gone away without clearing their [uncertain] lines was investigated and cleaned up, and in the afternoon visited the 7th Battalion in [uncertain] rest on the road between Berthen and Dranoutre, very comfortably housed and playing football, then visited the A.D.M.S. 2nd Division at Westoutre and Dranoutre, and met Col. Frith and Col. Lindsay, the A.D.M.S. and D.A.D.M.S., at Bulford Camp to go over the water situation and disinfectors — the new well progressing, the disinfectors promised for a week from today. | People: Col. Frith, Col. Lindsay. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-26 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-26 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-11-27 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Battalion at Ridgewood.
- **1915-11-27 | 24th Battalion | France** — Relieved by the 25th Bn. and marched back to Locre. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: trenches to Locre | Locations: Locre
- **1915-11-27 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — Enemy snipers and machine guns were active overnight and artillery on both sides was active during the day, a German aeroplane was reported brought down, La Basse Farm was shelled to the ground after snipers were suspected there, and at 5 p.m. B Squadron relieved A Squadron in the trenches by 6:30 p.m. with no casualties. | People: — | Companies: A, B Squadrons | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-27 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Issued 2 horses cured. | Casualties: 2 horses issued cured.
- **1915-11-27 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Went to Bailleul to see the A.D.M.S. about orders and to the D.D.M.S. [uncertain] on duty, all going smoothly, and in the afternoon with the A.D.M.S. and D.A.D.M.S. visited headquarters of the 5th Battalion and gave them an address on transmission of infectious diseases; getting colder tonight. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-27 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — Cold wind and some snow and rain; very heavy on the Peninsula, causing hundreds of cases of frozen feet, some cases very bad, admitted 29 November; Capt. Foster sick in hospital. | People: Capt. Foster. | Casualties: hundreds of frozen-feet cases from the Peninsula (admitted 29 November).
- **1915-11-27 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 9 horses and 1 mule admitted; 25 horses and 7 mules cured to Remounts. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-27 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-11-28 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Battalion at Ridgewood (ditto).
- **1915-11-28/30 | 24th Battalion | Locre, Belgium** — In billets; usual routine; Medical Officer made changes in the Stretcher Bearer Section and trained fresh men to replace those returned to duty, holding some in reserve for emergencies. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Locre
- **1915-11-28 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — The enemy was quiet during the night except for snipers, and the regiment's first death was reported: No 110150 Lance-Corporal [uncertain] of B Squadron killed in action. | People: Lance-Corporal [uncertain] No 110150 | Companies: B Squadron | Casualties: 1 killed — Lance-Corporal [uncertain] No 110150, B Squadron (killed in action; regiment's first death).
- **1915-11-28 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. Evacuated 8 to No. 10 Veterinary Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. | People: No. 10 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 2 horses received, 8 horses evacuated.
- **1915-11-28 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Sunday — kept all men at home, church parade, weather very cold, the coldest yet, ground frozen 3 inches and not thawing in daylight, and Col. Frith is getting one large and one small "fireless-Cooker" built after the section's plan for each battalion to try, with arrangements to supply Col. Lindsay two men for iron, glazing and carpentry jobs and to protect water pipes from frost. | People: Col. Frith, Col. Lindsay. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-28 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-28 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Twelve degrees of frost; water supply pipes frozen, cutting off water from the various departments.
- **1915-11-29 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Battalion at Ridgewood (ditto).
- **1915-11-29 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — The ditch in front of the parapet in Trench 130 was completed during the night, Lance-Corporal [uncertain] was buried in the afternoon with a simple service by Corporal Hodge of the 4th C.M.R. (grave T.18.d.3.8), and A Squadron relieved C Squadron in the trenches at 5 p.m. by 6:30 p.m. with no casualties. | People: Lance-Corporal [uncertain]; Corporal Hodge (4th C.M.R.) | Companies: A, C Squadrons | Casualties: burial of Lance-Corporal [uncertain] (killed 28 November).
- **1915-11-29 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 4 sick horses. Issued 2 surplus horses to 118th. Bde. R.F.A. | Casualties: 4 horses received.
- **1915-11-29 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Raining in the morning and freezing on the ground as it fell, sent one man to No. 1 Field Ambulance with a temperature of 102.4°F, found the water pipe behind [uncertain] at Bulford Camp frozen, and the well progressing slowly with pipes being placed in the disinfectors. | Casualties: one man sent to No. 1 Field Ambulance with temperature 102.4°F, hoped to be only a "cold".
- **1915-11-29 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 23 horses and 1 mule admitted; 1 horse sold to the butcher with a fractured leg. | Casualties: 1 horse sold to butcher.
- **1915-11-29 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Heavy downpour of rain with strong cold south-easterly gale; tents almost uninhabitable, roads almost impassable with mud; visit by Surgeon-General Woodhouse, D.M.S., L. of C., 11 a.m. | People: Surg-Gen Woodhouse.
- **1915-11-30 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Battalion at Ridgewood (ditto).
- **1915-11-30 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — The enemy showed nervousness during the night, [uncertain] reinforcements arrived from the Canadian Cavalry Base, and artillery was active on both sides with two buildings opposite our lines set on fire by our artillery, in cold and clear weather. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 reinforcements from Canadian Veterinary Hospital, HAVRE. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Sent in reports and certificates on absence of cameras and roll-call on 28 November, sent an iron worker to protect water pipes at the Brasserie in [uncertain] from freezing, received a report from [uncertain] Major's inspection of C.M.R. care of [uncertain] below Bulford, reported not clean and ordered cleaned, and visited [uncertain] Officers Rest and [uncertain] Rest Station, then the A.D.M.S. in Bailleul; all going well in the unit. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — 623 patients in hospital, 157 cases frost bite; health of personnel good with the exception of 3 officers and 5 men; food and water satisfactory. | Casualties: 623 patients in hospital, 157 frostbite cases.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 13 received from Remounts; 12 horses and 5 mules discharged cured. Monthly totals (Appendix I): 488 under treatment 1 November; 320 admitted (808 total); 300 cured to Remounts; 54 cast and sold; 1 died unfit for food; 7 destroyed fit for food; 446 remaining under treatment 30 November. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-11-30 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Heavy rains of yesterday continued throughout the night and early morning. Departmental reports appended to the volume: Dental (Capt. C. H. A. Stevenson) — 350 patients, 220 fillings, 150 extractions, 75 prophylaxis, 20 prosthetic, 19 July–31 October; X-Ray (Capts. Pirie and Wilkins) — 1,540 radiographs 8 August–5 November, two "Interruptless Transformer" machines, 23 good tubes; Sanitary (Capt. R. St. J. Macdonald) — camp site, water supply, excreta and sullage disposal, flies, disinfection; Medical (Lt-Col J. McCrae) — rheumatic fever, pneumonia, exanthems, enteric diseases, painful shins, chilblains/trench feet, neurasthenia, circulatory disturbances, malaria, dysentery, haemothorax. | People: Capt. C. H. A. Stevenson, Capt. L. H. Thornton, Capts. Pirie and Wilkins, Capt. R. St. J. Macdonald, Lt-Col J. McCrae.
- **1915-12-01 | 18th Battalion | In field** — Battalion relieved the 19th Battalion at Vierstraat at 4.30 p.m.; "B" and "D" Companies in the trenches and "C" and "A" Companies in battalion reserve; 6 other ranks struck off strength. | Companies: 19th Battalion. | Locations: Vierstraat.
- **1915-12-01/02 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Showery and warm; relieved the 25th Battalion in the trenches without casualty; intermittent rifle and machine-gun fire; Pte M. Murray #67945 (25th Bn) shrapnel wounds in left chest, thigh, leg and foot, and Pte D. Drew #65282 (24th Bn) shrapnel wound in the right thigh. | People: Pte M. Murray #67945 (25th Bn); Pte D. Drew #65282 | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 wounded (one 25th Bn)
- **1915-12-01 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — After a quiet night and a heavy noon bombardment of the German lines, the regiment was relieved and dispersed to Grande Munque Farm (Headquarters Staff and A Squadron), [uncertain] (B Squadron) and Hill 63 (C Squadron), with the Regimental Grenade Company at English Farm; shells near Regimental H.Q. killed one man of the 4th C.M.R. and injured four, with no damage to men of the 5th C.M.R. | People: — | Companies: A, B, C Squadrons; Regimental Grenade Company | Casualties: none (5th C.M.R.); 1 killed and 4 injured, 4th C.M.R. | Movement: relieved from Hill 63 trenches; H.Q. and A Squadron to Grande Munque Farm, B Squadron to [uncertain], C Squadron remained at Hill 63.
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 3 sick horses. | Casualties: 3 horses received.
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Sent a fatigue to finish the water-pipe at the Brasserie, visited a shell-damaged house at Vlamertinghe formerly occupied by No. 1 Fld Amb. and now occupied by No. 43 Fd Amb., saw 7 cases of trench-feet, and visited the Bulford baths where the disinfectors were nearly complete. | People: Dr. [uncertain]ons, Capt. McConnell. | Casualties: 7 trench-feet cases seen, 2 of them severe.
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West, Lemnos** — Large influx of patients; 800 treated today due to frost bite cases (trench feet) following heavy rain and low temperature on the Peninsula on 27–29 November; different degrees of trench feet, from simple numbness to gangrene of toes and feet causing loss of the same. | Casualties: 800 treated today (trench feet / frostbite).
- **1915-12-01 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 6 men and 2 N.C.O.s transferred to No 1 Mobile Veterinary Section on Command. | Casualties: none. | Movement: 6 men and 2 N.C.O.s transferred to No 1 Mobile Veterinary Section.
- **1915-12-01 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Capt. Colin Russel left for England to report as Neurologist at the Canadian Special Hospital, Granville Hotel, Ramsgate; Rontgen Society of London memorandum: Capt. A. Howard Pirie elected seventh honorary member (with Rontgen, Sir W. Crookes, Sir Oliver Lodge, Sir Ernest Rutherford, Professor Holznecht, Professor Stephen Leduc). | People: Capt. Colin Russel, Capt. A. Howard Pirie.

- **1915-12-02 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hill 63** — A conference of officers in the morning reviewed the twelve days in the trenches, and squadrons supplied working parties in the morning and afternoon, in misty weather. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.

[uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Kemmel

- **1915-12-03 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.

- **1915-12-18 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — The C.O., Adjutant and a party of officers and N.C.O.s from each squadron visited the Kemmel defences, Toronto area, finding the trenches well sited and in splendid condition, in very misty weather. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: visit to Kemmel defences, Toronto area.
- **1915-12-18 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Issued 1 horse cured. | Casualties: 1 horse issued cured.
- **1915-12-18 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Completed arrangements for mess, visited [uncertain] Fld Ambulance and Dranoutre with the A.D.M.S., addressed the N.C.O.s of the 1st Bn. on the outposts, and had the car returned repaired. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-18 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Still without transport, had grounds drained and tents put in order and prepared a recreation room for the men in a farm room, open 6–8.30 p.m. for warmth, games and lounging. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-18 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 1 horse destroyed for incurable disease. | Casualties: 1 horse destroyed.
- **1915-12-18 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Advance party of 6 N.C.O.s and 18 Privates proceeded to Boulogne to put up kitchens and alter lavatories at the Jesuit College, 8.30 a.m. | Movement: advance party to Boulogne.
- **1915-12-19 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — A gas attack was attempted this morning on an Imperial division (49th) on the battalion's left flank about Ypres; the battalion "stood-to" from 4 a.m. until 9.30 a.m.; the gas was not thick on the battalion's front but sufficient to make the eyes irritable; nothing [uncertain] on the battalion's front; 4 other ranks returned from hospital, 3 other ranks admitted to hospital. | Companies: 49th Division. | Locations: Ypres.
- **1915-12-19 | 24th Battalion | France** — Ordered to "Stand To" at 7 a.m. on account of a gas attack. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none recorded | Locations: Locre (Divisional Reserve)
- **1915-12-19 | 24th Battalion | Locre, Belgium** — In billets; usual routine; Medical Officer visited other units as S.M.O.; unit now in Divisional Reserve and not available for fatigue parties; hour of sick parade changed to 9 a.m. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Locre
- **1915-12-19 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — A gas attack on part of the line north of here in the early hours of the morning was faintly noticed by the regiment, and at 10 a.m. the regiment attended divine service in the field at X 1 d 5.2, parading 385 strong including 14 officers, with Canon Almond of Trinity Church, Montreal and Brig. General Mercer present. | People: Canon Almond; Brig. General Mercer | Companies: — | Casualties: none (traces of gas faintly noticed; no particulars).
- **1915-12-19 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. | Casualties: 2 horses received.
- **1915-12-19 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Visited Neuve Eglise baths, where disinfectors worked when coal was available but baths were being given with no disinfection done, got a promise of 15 men from the O.C. Convalescent Company for the water-system work, and visited Dranoutre. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-19 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-19 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Lt. Colonel H. B. Yates, invalided to England 22 November 1915, struck off the strength of this unit from that date. | People: Lt-Col H. B. Yates.
- **1915-12-20 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Everything quiet; 1 other rank returned from hospital.
- **1915-12-20 | 24th Battalion | France** — Church parade at 7.30 a.m. to attend Christmas service conducted by Hon. Capt. P. P. Shatford. | People: Hon. Capt. P. P. Shatford | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Locre
- **1915-12-20/24 | 24th Battalion | Locre, Belgium** — In billets; usual routine; Christmas festivities on the 23rd, each company taking its turn at a special dinner in the Y.M.C.A. school hall; on the 24th Maj Gen R. E. W. Turner visited the battalion and gave his Christmas greetings to all ranks; at 4 p.m. the battalion moved to the trenches; drizzling rain; quiet on the front; no casualties. | People: Maj Gen R. E. W. Turner | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Locre to the trenches | Locations: Locre
- **1915-12-20 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — Small parties from each squadron visited the Kemmel defences while the regiment carried on instruction with physical drill, squad drill and care of arms in the morning and a route march in the afternoon, in fine weather. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: visits to Kemmel defences.
- **1915-12-20 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 6 sick horses. | Casualties: 6 horses received.
- **1915-12-20 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Saw work started on the Bulford Camp water system, visited Dranoutre, and praised the water works at Locre as splendid, convenient and business-like. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-20 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — Increase in patients to 450, due to no hospital ships leaving for Alexandria or England lately; health of the unit personnel remarkably good, none in hospital. | Casualties: 450 patients in hospital.
- **1915-12-20 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 40 horses and 10 mules admitted from No 14 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-20 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Additional party of 4 officers, 1 N.C.O. and 9 Privates detailed to precede the unit to Boulogne to take over the Jesuit College.
- **1915-12-21 | 18th Battalion | Ridgewood** — Major R. Emmerton [uncertain] returned from hospital, also 2 other ranks; 2 other ranks admitted to hospital. | People: Maj. R. Emmerton.
- **1915-12-21 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — Regimental H.Q. moved at 9 a.m. and took up fresh billets at X 20 b 1.9 and X 20 a 9.10 south of Meteren, with rain most of the day. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Regimental H.Q. to fresh billets south of Meteren.
- **1915-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 6 sick horses. Evacuated 16 to No. 13 Vety. Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. 1 Died. | Casualties: 6 horses received, 1 horse died, 16 horses evacuated.
- **1915-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Continued the canteen report, urging hot food and drink and lounges in front-unit areas to keep men out of the estaminets, blamed for a large percentage of the infectious diseases experienced. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — In rain and quiet guns, visited the front-line trenches of the 1st Bde. with the A.D.M.S., finding them badly drained with water in most dug-outs but clean and the men cheerful, visited [uncertain] patients who were not serious, and submitted a report praising the Expeditionary [uncertain] canteens. | Casualties: none serious.
- **1915-12-21 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — All horses in the hospital subjected to the Mallein Test; 11 horses admitted; 33 horses discharged cured. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-21 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Base Commandant Col Graham Thomson, C.B., inspected the men at noon and said "there was no finer Medical Unit in this District"; six privates, fourth-year medical students, proceeded to England 9 p.m. to be discharged to return to Canada; five N.C.O.s — Sgt-Maj Kennedy G.L.D., Staff-Sgt Wilkes A.B., Sgt Wilson R.D., Sgt Neilson H.K., Sgt Baby G.R. — to be Captains, C.A.M.C., posted to the C.A.M.C. Training School. | People: Col Graham Thomson, Sgt-Maj Kennedy G.L.D., Staff-Sgt Wilkes A.B., Sgt Wilson R.D., Sgt Neilson H.K., Sgt Baby G.R.
- **1915-12-22 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — Relieved the 19th Battalion at Vierstraat and the trenches at 4.30 p.m.; 11 other ranks struck off strength, having been transferred to England; "A" and "C" Companies in the trenches, "B" and "D" in battalion reserve. | Companies: 19th Battalion. | Movement: Ridgewood → Vierstraat.
- **1915-12-22 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — The regiment spent most of the day at the regimental baths, and a report was received from Lieutenant E. Chown, O.C. Regimental Bombers, that on the night of 19/20 December Pte J. R. Beckett of the 5th C.M.R. grenadiers went 40 yards in front of a 4th C.M.R. listening post, found the body of a German killed by a German patrol's bombing, and carried it in. | People: Lt E. Chown; Pte J. R. Beckett No 110033; Lieutenant Mar[uncertain] H.H. C.M.R. | Companies: Regimental Bombers | Casualties: 1 German killed (by German patrol bombing, 4th C.M.R. listening post, night of 19/20 December).
- **1915-12-22 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 4 sick horses. | Casualties: 4 horses received.
- **1915-12-22 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Replied to the A.D.M.S. that 10 men had not yet had leave since coming to France, and found the Bulford water system still unfinished with digging delayed by wet ground. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-22 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 3 horses admitted into hospital. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-22 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — O.C. proceeded on duty to England, 8.30 a.m., placing Lt-Col J. M. Elder A/O.C. during his temporary absence. | People: Lt-Col J. M. Elder.
- **1915-12-23 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — Battalion in the trenches at Vierstraat; 2 other ranks admitted to hospital, 2 other ranks returned from hospital.
- **1915-12-23 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Fletre, France** — The Company moved to new headquarters at Fletre, opened the signal office and established communication with Canadian Corps and the 7th and 8th Infantry Brigades. | People: — | Companies: 7th and 8th Infantry Brigades. | Casualties: none | Movement: Meteren–Fletre.
- **1915-12-23 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | near Meteren** — The regiment carried out advanced drill in the morning by squadrons and a route march in the afternoon, in clear weather with rain at intervals. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-23 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 2 sick horses. | Casualties: 2 horses received.
- **1915-12-23 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Nothing special to note, reports good from all quarters, a very wet afternoon and spring-like warm weather with only occasional guns heard. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-23 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-23 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-12-24 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — Battalion as yesterday; machine-gun section detached for the Brigade Machine Gun Company; Lieut. C. E. - **1915-12-24 | 24th Battalion | France** — Maj. Gen. A.E.W. Turner visited the battalion orderly room and wished all ranks Christmas greetings. | People: Maj. Gen. A.E.W. Turner | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: Locre
- **1915-12-24 | 24th Battalion | France** — Moved from Locre at 8 p.m. and relieved the 25th Bn. in the Right Sector of the 5th Can. Inf. Bde. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Locre to Right Sector | Locations: Locre, Right Sector
- **1915-12-24–1915-12-31 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Fletre** — Organization, training and equipping proceeded, with 1 officer and 50 N.C.O.s and men attached during the period. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1915-12-24 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Meteren** — The regiment carried on by squadrons in changeable weather, and in the evening the Brigadier [uncertain] and officers of the staff gave a dinner to the officers of the regiment, the only absentees being Major [uncertain] and Lieutenant Cotton through sickness. | People: Major [uncertain]; Lieutenant Cotton | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-24 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 3 sick horses. | Casualties: 3 horses received.
- **1915-12-24 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — A suspected cerebro-spinal meningitis case was reported from 6th Cdn R., the spinal fluid clear with practically no polymorphonuclear cells and the culture negative, roads at food distribution points were flooded, mails delayed 3 days, and a man tried for insolence to an N.C.O. was made to apologize publicly before the unit. | Casualties: one suspected meningitis case, culture negative.
- **1915-12-24 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 29 horses discharged cured to Remounts. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-24 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Nothing worthy of comment occurred.
- **1915-12-25 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — Battalion as yesterday; everything very quiet tonight and all day; very little firing but no casualties on either side.
- **1915-12-25/26 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Fairly quiet along the front; in the afternoon the enemy made attempts to fraternize with our men; this was stopped and fire opened on them. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1915-12-25 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Meteren** — By the Brigadier's kindness the men were relieved of all but absolutely necessary duties, communion services were arranged in Bailleul, every man sat down to a Christmas meal, the regimental staff dined in the officers' mess by courtesy of Colonel J. R. Baker, and in the morning the regiment paraded for an address by the Brigadier, Colonel C. A. Smart. | People: Colonel C. A. Smart; Colonel J. R. Baker | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-25 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Passed a very quiet Christmas with hardly any gun firing, the men of the unit got up a dinner, and all avoidable fatigues were dispensed with. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-25 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — Progress of patients in hospital more satisfactory of late, due in a measure to fine weather and better food; Major Munro and Capt. Foster are to return to England, paratyphoid in each case. | People: Major Munro; Capt. Foster. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-25 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Christmas Day; Sunday routine; special dinner for the men. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-25 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Special dinners at the different messes; general routine duties dispensed with as far as possible.
- **1915-12-26 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — "B" and "D" Companies relieved "A" and "C" Companies in the trenches; wishes for Christmas and the New Year received from H.M. the King, H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught and Major-General Sir Sam Hughes; Pte Newlands and Pte [uncertain] killed in action; 3 other ranks admitted to hospital. | People: King George V; H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught; Maj.-Gen. Sir Sam Hughes; Pte Newlands; Pte [uncertain].
- **1915-12-26 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Meteren** — Squadrons carried on independently, church services were held by squadrons, and three reinforcements arrived from the Base, in more settled and colder weather. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-26 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Evacuated 22 to No. 13 Veterinary Hospital, NEUFCHATEL. | People: No. 13 Veterinary Hospital. | Casualties: 22 horses evacuated.
- **1915-12-26 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Nothing of note in fine weather, and advised against [uncertain] entering [uncertain] quarantined for foot-and-mouth disease, where 14 cows were sick, 2 died, 12 pigs died and 2 human beings were affected. | Casualties: foot-and-mouth disease at a farm — 14 cows sick, 2 died, 12 pigs died, 2 humans affected.
- **1915-12-26 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-26 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Dannes-Camiers, France** — Maj E. W. Archibald proceeded for temporary duty to No. 1 Canadian Casualty Clearing Station, 9 a.m. | People: Maj E. W. Archibald.
- **1915-12-27 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — Battalion as yesterday; Pte Shoring [uncertain] killed in action; 3 other ranks sent to hospital. | People: Pte Shoring.
- **1915-12-27 | 24th Battalion | In the Field, Belgium** — Fairly quiet until 3 p.m., when the enemy shelled a working party returning through the woods behind the first aid post; shrapnel burst in the mining section huts: Pte J. Bourgeois #67244 (25th Bn) wounded in the throat and died, and L/Cpl Northington #68333 (25th Bn) wounded in the right arm, left forearm and left lower leg. | People: Pte J. Bourgeois #67244 (25th Bn); L/Cpl Northington #68333 (25th Bn) | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 died, 1 wounded (both 25th Bn)
- **1915-12-27 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Meteren** — Squadrons carried on independently in bright and chilly weather; the entry ends mid-sentence with "Three [uncertain]". | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-27 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Nieppe** — Received 4 sick horses. | Casualties: 4 horses received.
- **1915-12-27 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Col Ross took up with Gen. Currie having a disinfector at Dranoutre as at Neuve Eglise, and Col Firth the completion of the Bulford water system. | People: Col Ross, Gen. Currie, Col Firth. | Casualties: none.
- **1915-12-27 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Daily routine as usual. | Casualties: none.

- **1915-12-28 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — D.D.V.S. inspected the hospital. | People: D.D.V.S. | Casualties: none.

Farms, Belgium** — In billets as Brigade Reserve; usual routine; General Remarks: Report on Water Carts — after 3½ months the issued water carts proved unserviceable (thin galvanized tanks, rivets starting, filters and pumps failing; 25 minutes to fill a tank with both pumps, 45 minutes through one filter). | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Locations: R.E. farms

A. S. Williams, and Colonel C. A. Smart's valedictory address was copied into the diary. | People: Lt-General Alderson; Brigadier General T. A. S. Williams; Colonel C. A. - **1915-12-31 | No. 1 Canadian Stationary Hospital | Mudros West** — 276 patients in hospital, all progressing well; weather conditions particularly fine; very few admissions to hospital for the past 10 days; health of officers, nursing sisters and rank and file remarkably good; food supply now much better in quantity and quality. | Casualties: 276 patients in hospital.
- **1915-12-31 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — Usual routine. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-02-16 | 24th Battalion | Right Sector, Kemmel, Belgium** — At 2.45 a.m. a patrol of three scouts (Cpl E. A. Mott, Scouts Dwyer and Williams) left H.4 trench, went through our wire into No Man's Land, surrounded and captured a single German scout about 20 yards ahead of two others, and brought him to battalion headquarters; the 25th Canadian Battalion relieved the 24th in the Right Sector and the 24th moved to Brigade Reserve at R.E. Farm. | People: Cpl E. A. Mott; Scout Dwyer; Scout Williams | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Right Sector trenches to R.E. Farm | Locations: H.4 trench; R.E. Farm

- **1916-02-16 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 136–141** — Eleven small shells landed near Stink Farm with no damage, relief of "D" Company in trenches 136–138 by "A" Company from Fletchers Field commenced at 6.30 p.m. and completed at 9.15 p.m., and small enemy working parties were dispersed by machine-gun and sniper fire, while patrols covered the front and leave for the battalion commenced. | People: — | Companies: A; D | Casualties: none | Movement: "A" Company relieved "D" Company in trenches 136–138.

- **1916-02-16 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | St Jans Cappel** — Visited the 4th C.M.R. at Red Lodge about the inspector's complaint, the O.C. and M.O. undertaking to straighten it out, inspected the water supply at Hyde Park Corner and latrines along the road to Red Lodge, fairly good, and inspected the units about Dranoutre, all in very fair condition. | Casualties: none.

Tidmarsh returned from No. 1 Convalescent Camp, Boulogne; convoy of 116 patients received (11.45 p.m.), total 386 in hospital. | People: Hon. Capt G. C. Hepburn, Hon. Capt R. W. Ridgeway, Capt F. W. - **1916-02-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 136–141** — A small red flag flew all day at U.1.B.8.6, three H.E. shells fell in rear of Trench 141 and one in rear of Trench 139, enemy machine guns opened on the party working at Well Walk at 7.00 p.m., letters were reported signalled by flash lamp from the enemy lines and answered from behind our own lines with search parties finding nothing, and Brig.-General Leckie was wounded in both legs near Gabion Farm while Lt.-Col. Baker left for England on leave. | People: Brig.-General Leckie; Lt.-Col. Baker | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 wounded — Brig.-General Leckie (both legs).

- **1916-03-24 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Belgian Chateau to Trenches** — There was heavy snowfall during the night and cold weather with a north-easterly wind, two red flares were seen south of Ypres at about 7.45 p.m. and two green flares at 9.45 p.m., the enemy used a powerful searchlight all night north of Ypres and a Zeppelin was reported travelling near Ypres, and the battalion moved off from Belgian Chateau at 7 p.m. via Kruisstraat, Ypres, Menin Gate, Hell Fire Corner, Gordon House and Yeomanry Post to relieve the 4th C.M.R. Farm to Right Sector trenches
- **1916-03-26/27 | 24th Battalion | Right Sector, Kemmel, Belgium** — Night of 26/27 March: three scout patrols of three scouts each reconnoitred routes to the enemy wire for Bangalore torpedoes; one torpedo was successfully laid in the enemy wire in front of trench K1 and fired at 4.15 a.m.; the party for H4 trench was seen by the enemy and forced back with the torpedo; two attempts to place a torpedo opposite J3 Right trench failed, and a third attempt left the party in No Man's Land when the bombardment began — Scout F. Juteau (No. 41158) was killed making his way back, and Scout W. J. Dimmer (No. 6598) [also written "Dwyer" in the diary] was found by a scout patrol (Pte S. J. Bethune, No. 65077, and Pte E. C. Collins, No. 65192) sheltering in an old trench about 150 yards from the enemy wire and led safely back. | People: Scout F. Juteau No. 41158; Scout W. J. Dimmer No. 6598 [also written "Dwyer"]; Pte S. J. Bethune No. 65077; Pte E. C. Collins No. 65192 | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed | Locations: K1; H4; J3 Right trench

- **1916-03-26 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches** — The wind was mild south-east and the weather overcast with showers, our bombers bombed the Birdcage continually during the night and a patrol of three men reported the enemy very nervous, enemy artillery opened up at 1.30 p.m. and continued until 5.30 p.m. doing considerable damage to dugouts at Lovers Walk and Warrington Ave., our batteries put 72 eighteen-pound shells into the Birdcage, partly demolishing it, and Pte. H. J. Mills was killed by a fragment of H.E. shell hitting him in the head. | People: Pte. H. J. Mills | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed — Pte. H. J. Mills (fragment of H.E. shell, head).

- **1916-03-27 | 18th Battalion | Vierstraat** — At 4.15 a.m. several mines were fired under the Mound at St. Eloi by the division on the battalion's left; the battalion's artillery co-operated in a heavy bombardment on the enemy trenches and supports, under cover of which the Northumberland Fusiliers and Royal Fusiliers attacked on the left; 2 other ranks killed in action, 6 wounded, 2 returned from hospital. | Companies: Northumberland Fusiliers; Royal Fusiliers. | Locations: The Mound, St. Eloi.
- **1916-03-27 | 24th Battalion | Right Sector, Kemmel, Belgium** — Organized bombardment began at 4.15 a.m. in co-operation with a neighbouring operation; after the explosion of a mine on the left the enemy sent up flares, and four minutes later our artillery opened up, the enemy retaliating with heavies, trench mortars, grenades and field artillery forming a barrage behind the support trenches and heavily shelling the communication trenches until 6 a.m.; telephone communication between battalion headquarters and the trenches was broken at 5 a.m. and restored at 7.15 a.m.; casualties six wounded and one killed; the rest of the day unusually quiet. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 6 wounded

- **1916-03-27 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches** — The wind was mild south-west and the weather overcast and cloudy and cold, a bombing patrol went out to investigate a reported mining sap at J.13.c.2.8, was stopped by exceptionally strong wire, placed a charge under a sandbag and wire blocks about 15 yards from the enemy trench, exploded it and threw about 50 bombs, returning safely and finding the enemy were not mining but had run out a sap about 15 yards, while artillery was active all day, five enemy aeroplanes flew over, and an enemy working party at the Birdcage was dispersed by machine guns. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none.

- **1916-04 | No. 1 Company, Canadian Forestry Corps | Petit Couronne / Oissel, France** — At the beginning of April the company extended and built a siding and commenced shipments from Petit Couronne as well; by this time 700 to 800 civilians were working, with a Company of R.E. Labour (some 250 men) attached, motor transport of 8 Loydenes [uncertain] and Claytons, 2 steam tractors with trailers and 10 petrol lorries, and 2 saw mills (Petit Couronne and the Belgian Siding at Oissel) turning out 20,000 to 25,000 F.B.M. per day; shipments averaged 14 cars at Petit Couronne and 30 to 36 at Oissel (450 to 500 tons per day). No. 2 Forest Party (22 men and a corporal) had begun operations in the Forest of Senarpont, and No. 3 Forest Party (a corporal and some 20 other ranks) in the Forest of Brettone (from the retrospective narrative history). | People: none named. | Casualties: none.

Greenshields reconnoitred Crater No. 3, finding a parapet 8–10 feet high extending about 300 yards, probably joining Crater No. 2; in this sector all garrisons were relieved every 24 hours owing to the heavy bombardment; casualties 1 other rank killed, 4 wounded, Capt. - **1916-05-14 to 1916-06-01 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Right Sector / Sanctuary Wood / Maple Copse / Zillebeke, Belgium** — Batteries into Right Sector and Sanctuary Wood. Major [uncertain] gun crew with 4 Stokes ready; Zillebeke Village gun crew and extra men in reserve; other Battery back in Rest Camp relieving about 22 May. Guns: Stokes, 2 × 4" R.M.L and 3 × 3.7s. Orders kept Stokes 1,000 yds back of front line except when firing, making prompt retaliation and registering almost impossible. At end of month 3 officers went to Stokes Gun Course. - **1916-05-16 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was clear with a north-west wind, the enemy was quiet overnight and a German aeroplane was driven down east of the trenches at 8.30 a.m., but in the afternoon the enemy kept up very active rifle-grenade and trench-mortar fire and put high-explosive shells over, causing many casualties including Pte. Baskin killed by a rifle grenade at his bombers post in Trench 63 and Major Woodside and Captain Sneath suffering shell shock, and enemy snipers were very active while 15 H.E. shells fell near Battalion H.Q. without damage. | People: Pte. G. Baskin; Major H. J. Woodside; Captain J. D'A. Sneath; Pte. C. A. Rogerson; Signalling Corporal H. W. Atkinson; Pte. B. Murray; Pte. Rankin [uncertain]; Pte. R. P. Campbell | Companies: A; B; D | Casualties: 1 killed — Pte. G. Baskin ("A" Coy; rifle grenade, Trench 63); 7 wounded/injured — Major H. J. Woodside (shell shock, at duty); Captain J. D'A. Sneath ("B"; severe shell shock); Pte. C. A. Rogerson (bruised head and face, trench mortar, Trench 64); Signalling Corporal H. W. Atkinson (shell shock and injured knee, Trench 64); Pte. B. Murray ("D"; gunshot, right shoulder and fingers, Appendix); Pte. Rankin [uncertain] (shell shock, at duty); Pte. R. P. Campbell ("A"; gunshot, head, Trench 63).
- **1916-05-16 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke / Maple Copse, Belgium** — Enemy sniping galling in Maple Copse; enemy artillery quiet; night machine guns harass our men; our M.G.s register on the line but were not successful in silencing them. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
