- **1916-05-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was clear with a north-west wind, Pte. Baskin, killed yesterday, was buried at 9.30 p.m. last evening in Maple Copse Cemetery with the Rev. Hon. Captain C. Reagan officiating, the enemy continuously swept the section of defence all day with rifle and machine-gun fire with occasional artillery and trench-mortar activity, and casualties were Pte. J. Kay killed by gunshot in the head and Pte. R. McDonough wounded by gunshot in the right arm with a compound fracture, Pte. Kay being buried in Maple Copse Cemetery with the Rev. Father Captain M. R. Tompkins officiating. | People: Pte. G. Baskin; Rev. Hon. Captain C. Reagan; Pte. J. Kay; Pte. R. McDonough; Rev. Father Captain M. R. Tompkins | Companies: D | Casualties: 1 killed — Pte. J. Kay ("D" Coy; gunshot, head); 1 wounded — Pte. R. McDonough ("D" Coy; gunshot, right arm, compound fracture).

- **1916-05-18 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was clear and bright with a north-west wind, the morning was much quieter and our snipers had the enemy snipers well in hand, the enemy was a little more active in the afternoon with a few rifle grenades, enemy transport was heard at 9 p.m. and our artillery opened up, one casualty was Pte. A. Meakins injured in the right eye, slightly, by glass from a periscope broken by a sniper, and notice was received of promotions to Captain for Lieuts. H. Pines, E. Gill, C. H. Lawson and J. D'A. - **1916-05-19 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was fine and warm with a north-west wind, the enemy was quiet during the night but at 9.30 a.m. sent H.E. shells into the front line, killing Major A. C. Fletcher and Lieutenant H. M. Macdonald, both of "B" Company, by a shell making a direct hit as they stood together outside Coy. H.Q. dugout, and the day brought many more casualties from rifle grenades, trench mortars and shell fire, including Ptes. Landsdell and Worsley dying of wounds at the dressing station at 4.30 a.m., with about 30 feet of parapet in Trench 66 blown in and the floor of Trench 64 damaged. | People: Major A. C. Fletcher; Lieutenant H. M. Macdonald; Pte. C. Landsdell; Pte. G. M. Inman; Pte. R. M. Parr; Pte. E. Worsley; Pte. L. R. White; Pte. McGillivray; Pte. J. R. Keane; Pte. C. J. Stewart; Pte. J. Landsdell ("A"; gunshot, left breast; died at dressing station 4.30 a.m.); Pte. E. Worsley ("A"; gunshot through body while acting as stretcher bearer for Landsdell; died at dressing station 4.30 a.m.); 15 wounded — Pte. G. M. Hall (Bombing Section; slight shrapnel, left shoulder); Pte. R. A. Brown (shrapnel, left hip and arm); Pte. R. Grant ("A"; head wound and shell shock); Pte. R. A. Smith ("A"; wounded left side); Pte. J. J. Johnson (gunshot, head, not serious).

- **1916-05-20 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was fine and clear with a north-west wind, the enemy sent 12 5.9 H.E. shells between 9.30 and 10.30 a.m. on the front line, aeroplanes were very active in the early morning, three patrols were out during the night and a company relief was effected by 10.30 p.m. last evening, then at 9 to 9.30 a.m. the enemy sent 80 H.E. shells over Battalion H.Q. and again at 1 p.m., and at 6.15 p.m. a bombardment searched the vicinity of Battalion H.Q., smashing in two dugouts and damaging Gourouck Road, while our trench mortars retaliated and eventually silenced the enemy batteries, and casualties were Ptes. Bennett and Paslow wounded by rifle grenades and Sgt. Upton wounded by gunshot in the head. | People: Pte. R. F. Bennett; Pte. G. E. Paslow [uncertain]; Sgt. R. Upton | Companies: A; C | Casualties: 3 wounded — Pte. R. F. Bennett (slight wound, hand and face, rifle grenade); Pte. G. E. Paslow [uncertain] ("A"; slight wound, arm and face, rifle grenade); Sgt. R. Upton ("C"; gunshot, head, not serious).

- **1916-05-21 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches 63–66** — The weather was dull and raining with a south south-west wind, the enemy was quiet overnight and put groups of four H.E. shells over the front line and support, aeroplanes were active observing, the O.C. "D" Coy reported sounds of mining from Trench 66 and O.C. Tunnelling Coy No. 177 was summoned but nothing could be detected, the situation was quiet until dusk when the enemy shelled Zouave Wood, Gourouck Road and Battalion H.Q., and news was received that Transport Sergt. J. B. Duncan was killed by shell at 9 p.m. last evening whilst bringing up rations, with Pte. Cox wounded and Pte. McQuaker slightly wounded at the same time and place and three light draught horses shot owing to injuries from the same shell, plus Ptes. Price, Witherspoon and Stevens wounded during the day. | People: Transport Sergt. J. B. Duncan; Pte. A. Cox; Pte. W. C. McQuaker; Pte. A. H. Price; Pte. D. Witherspoon; Pte. J. W. G. Stevens | Companies: A; B; C | Casualties: 1 killed — Transport Sergt. J. B. Duncan (shell, whilst bringing up rations); 5 wounded — Pte. A. Cox (Staff; wounded); Pte. W. C. McQuaker ("B"; slightly wounded, kept at duty); Pte. A. H. Price ("A"; shell splinter); Pte. D. Witherspoon ("C"; wounded in knee by bomb, wiring party); Pte. J. W. G. R. F. Gagnon wounded by shrapnel in the left leg, Pte. J. Jackson suffering shell shock and Pte. R. Christian killed by machine-gun fire in Maple Copse while on a ration party. | People: Pte. R. F. - **1916-05-23 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Trenches to Camp "A"** — The weather was fine and bright with a north north-west wind, the enemy was quiet during the night but opened up with H.E. shells about 8.00 a.m. making the vicinity of Battalion H.Q. very "warm", Pte. Christian was buried at Maple Copse Cemetery with the Hon. Captain Father Thornton officiating, Sergt. B. Duncan, killed on the night of 21st inst., was buried at Vlamertinghe Military Cemetery (Row 4 No. 14) with the Rev. Captain Robertson officiating, the enemy shelled the trenches and Battalion Headquarters all day with little damage, and the battalion was relieved by the 9th Battalion and returned to Camp "A" with only one casualty, Pte. W. D. Anderson wounded by a shell splinter in the right ankle, while the diary gives the eight-day tour total as 5 killed, 2 died of wounds and 39 wounded, 46 all ranks. | People: Pte. R. Christian; Hon. Captain Father Thornton; Sergt. B. Duncan; Rev. Captain Robertson; Pte. W. D. Anderson | Companies: A | Casualties: 1 wounded on 23 May — Pte. W. D. McKinnon officiating and Holy Communion in the Y.M.C.A. hut afterwards, during the service an enemy aeroplane overhead was driven off by anti-aircraft guns and one of our own machines, and in the afternoon the battalion football team beat the P.P.C.L.I. 3–1 and the baseball team beat the 4th C.M.R. Battalion 22–18, while the enemy shelled Poperinghe with large H.E. during the night. | People: Hon. Colonel Rev. J. Almond; Hon. Capt. McKinnon | Companies: — | Casualties: none.

- **1916-05-30 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke, Belgium** — Three casualties from shell fire in front line; new emplacement and one dugout wrecked in Trench 59; Hedge Street M.G. emplacement wrecked; work rebuilding the wrecked emplacements; Zillebeke shelled; two further casualties in front line today; enemy heavy trench mortar very active all day; front line badly wrecked, looks as if an attack were to be launched; our M.G.s very active on German saps; frontage extended today to the south as far as trench 66. | Casualties: 5 casualties from shell fire. | Movement: —

Monthly summary: wire laid connecting all guns in the Right position with H.Q. at Maple Copse and the O.P.; St. Peter St. gun connected by telephone; Bydand Ave. gun connected with the O.P. on Sackville St. Enemy artillery very active in the last week, all guns heavily shelled but no direct hits. - **1916-06-01 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Maple Copse** — The battalion paraded last night, entrained at 9.40 and detrained 40 minutes later at Asylum, proceeded independently across the fields through Ypres to Maple Copse with only two shells coming in while passing through Ypres, completed the relief at 1.35 a.m. with no casualties, directly after which Pte. Dobson of "A" Coy was hit by a rifle bullet in the left forearm whilst lying in a dugout at Maple Copse, Brigadier-General V. A. Williams visited Battalion H.Q. at 2.15 p.m. with A.D.C. Captain H. Fraser, and the enemy shelled the north-east corner of Maple Copse and south-west of Sanctuary Wood, with "A" Coy and Battalion H.Q. in Maple Copse, "C" Coy in S.P.s 13, 14, 16 and 17 and "D" Coy at Zillebeke Dugouts. | People: Pte. Burnstead L.B. | Companies: none | Casualties: 1 officer wounded | Movement: none
- **1916-06-02 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi Front** — Officers and N.C.O.s spent considerable time reconnoitring their front; under cover of artillery fire the following points were registered: No 2 Crater, Piccadilly Fm., and the sap head at O.3.b.7.1. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank / Convent School** — Work at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank continued, good progress being made; the 26th Battalion supplying a work party of 8 men each night; a sentry box started and partly completed at Convent School; all guns, spare parts and ammunition gone over and thoroughly cleaned. | People: — | Companies: 26th Battalion. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-02 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Maple Copse** — The morning broke bright and clear and at about 8.30 a.m., after the enemy sprang a mine in front of the line held by the 4th C.M.R. Battalion, a very heavy bombardment of the front line and Maple Copse began, the 4th C.M.R. sending the message "Our wires are cut, please have Corps Artillery turned on; General Mercer is here and wants it; General Williams has been hit", runners sent to the front line were killed or wounded and all telephone communication was broken by about 1.30 p.m., the battalion held the east side of Maple Copse and the communication trench on its south side, Captain Pitts was mortally wounded reinforcing S.P.14, Captain Roscoe brought "B" Company up through the open into Maple Copse and established a line on its east end, Major Draper took 20 men to reinforce S.P.16 and C.S.M. Gill held it until his force was practically wiped out, and during intense bombardment until 9.40 p.m. the Commanding Officer, Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker, was hit and died shortly after, while several enemy attacks on the east and south-east sides of Maple Copse were repelled. | People: Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker; General Mercer; General Williams; Capt. J. A. Symonds; Captain C. J. Pitts; Captain B. W. Roscoe; Major D. E. Draper; C.S.M. Gill; Lieut. J. D. Fraser | Companies: A; B; C; D | Casualties: Heavy — Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker (killed, died shortly after 9.40 p.m.); Captain C. J. Pitts (mortally wounded, reinforcing S.P.14); General Williams reported hit in 4th C.M.R. message; full battalion totals given on 4 June.
- **1916-06-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | B Camp / E Camp, Belgium** — 10 a.m. while parading for inspection by G.O.C., message arrives to prepare to move at 1 hour's notice; warned to move at once, ordered to Camp E and await orders; left Camp B 3.30 p.m.; D.A.D.O.S. leave 8 guns in their hands, take only 8 guns to advance; operation order No. 19 received: move 4 guns to occupy 4 positions in Lille Road; A Section moved 6 p.m. and in position 2 hours later; C Section ready to move at short notice; 9 p.m. B.H.Q. and M.G.C. H.Q. move to Chateau Belge. | Companies: A Section; C Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: B Camp to E Camp to Chateau Belge.
- **1916-06-02 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Fine bright and warm. O.C. attended 7th I.B. H.Q.; men at Advanced Billets ordered to stand by. Heavy enemy bombardment of front-line trenches 8.30 a.m. to noon. Arrangements made for two sections of sappers to carry on work and for working parties with Pioneer Battalion; C.R.E. approved. Two columns of 12 and 18 wagons of engineer material arrived and were off-loaded. Orders from C.R.E. arrived 11.30 p.m.; Mr Dunsmore with his section and Pioneers began work on Zillebeke Switch and Dormy House Road; Mr Robertson with half of No 2 Section and Pioneers improved G.H.Q.2 [uncertain]; Mr Young and his section stood by in R.S.8 and worked on China Wall. O.C. suggested charges be placed in canal bridges to Mr Dawson of 8th F.C.C.E., and remained all night at B.H.Q. | People: Capt. Robertson; Mr Dunsmore; Mr Robertson; Mr Young; Mr Dawson. | Companies: No 2 Section.
- **1916-06-02 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe S.** — Evacuated to No. 13 Vety Hospital Neufchatel 18 horses, Eleven of these are skin disease cases — Corpl. - **1916-06-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank / Convent School** — The saps at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank advanced a distance of 3 feet and timbered; the work party promised by the 26th Battalion unable to come owing to a stand to, so the work was carried on by the company's own men; a trench dug from the Convent School emplacement connecting it with the main trench; at M.G. Headquarters a surface dugout started and the roof braced up with timber. | People: — | Companies: 26th Battalion. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-03 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Maple Copse** — During the morning of 3rd June a desultory bombardment was kept up until about noon and diminished in the afternoon, the 14th Battalion advanced across the open at about 7 a.m. in a gallant manner but was apparently unavailing, at about 6.00 p.m. the bombardment again became severe as the 9th Brigade was brought up, during this time there were only two of our officers left in the line, at 8.30 p.m. another demonstration with flares, trench mortars and bombs lasted one hour, and at 1.30 p.m. as written the remainder of the battalion under Captain Hewson and Lieutenant Barnes, having evacuated their wounded and all possible rifles and equipment, came out of the line on being relieved by units of the 9th Brigade. | People: Captain Charles Walsby Hewson; Lieutenant George Roland Barnes | Companies: — | Casualties: Heavy fighting continued; totals given on 4 June | Movement: Relieved by units of the 9th Brigade; out of the line.

Lalor, for A.A.G., Canadian Section, 3rd Echelon, G.H.Q., enclosing the synoptical diary 15 Mar–18 Jun 1916; unable to render a complete diary owing to ignorance of Circular 7 Feb 1916 (A-27-157-2A); circular letter handed to Mr. Ryerson, O.C. C-9-1 & 2. | People: Capt. H. J. Horan; Capt. R. C. Lalor; Lieut. J. E. Ryerson.
- **1916-06-03 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Chateau Belge / Ypres, Belgium** — 1 a.m. B.H.Q. moves to Ypres Ramparts; 2 a.m. C Section reports Ypres and despatched to be held in reserve at the Bund, I 21 b; 9 a.m. D Section reports Ypres with 4 guns from ordnance, one gun into emplacement in Ramparts, remainder kept under cover in Ypres; 8 men of A Section sent to 7th Bde. M.G.C. at Halfway House to replace casualties; communication trenches heavily shelled all day; enemy aeroplanes busy; 7.15 p.m. enemy bombardment begins in Sanctuary Wood and a feint made on our lines in Lovers Walk; 7.30 p.m. D Section 4 guns moved from Ypres to Lille Road; 8.30 p.m. 4 guns from Bund advanced to form new line of defence from I 22 d.4.6 north to I 16 a 7.8; 10 p.m. 2 guns of B Section under Lieut. Cordingly reported Bund and ordered by 8th B. M.G.C. to go to Zillebeke; C Section withdrawn from new line to relieve 8th B. M.G.C. | People: Lieut. Cordingly. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section; 7th Bde. M.G.C.; 8th B. M.G.C. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Chateau Belge to Ypres; Ypres to Lille Road; Bund to Zillebeke.
- **1916-06-03 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Bright and warm. By reason of enemy bombardment, C.R.E. order to take over Left Brigade Sector work not feasible; other orders received. Mr Dunsmore returned about noon from Zillebeke Switch. O.C. attended Brigadier 7th I.B. and O.C. Pioneer Battalion; new arrangements for the night as desired by Infantry; orders from C.R.E. for special work. O.C., with Lt. Robertson and West and 1, 3 and 4 Sections, engaged on trench 48 [uncertain] Manry Post, caught in heavy barrage for 25 minutes and remained in trench. Sappers detailed to assist Pioneer officer carrying out wounded Pioneers. Infantry attack partially successful in regaining lost ground but unable to retain captured positions. Lieut Walley escorted 11 wagons of engineer material to Hell Fire Corner Dump. | People: Mr Dunsmore; Lt. Robertson; West; Lieut Walley. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-06-04 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field (Sanctuary Wood)** — After the bombardment of 2 June, 21 N.C.O.s and men reported missing: Sgt. Aminder E. (now officially reported killed), Cpl. Ockenden E. (since reported in hospital), Bdr. Carter (now officially reported prisoner of war), Bdr. Scott W. (now officially reported wounded and prisoner of war), Bdr. Wright R.E., L/Cpl. Herron J., Gn. D'Aoust J.C., Williams W. (now officially reported prisoner of war), Sigsworth T.C., Thompson F. (now officially reported prisoner of war), Carnahan V., Powell C.H., Lauder W. (now reported at Canadian Base Depot), Brown G. (unofficially reported prisoner of war), Ridsdale R.H., Lepper B.R. (officially wounded at CCAC), Bastien A.G. (officially wounded at CCAC), Mansfield P.F. Very little news from the batteries; all guns behind the front line trenches reported out of action. The gun crews of X.3.C. and Z.3.C. stood to their guns during the heavy bombardment of 27 May–2 June, firing till the last moment when the enemy attacked on 2 June; only 4 gunners got out of the crews of all 7 guns in action. Gunner Heaps T. alone remained unwounded of the crew of B.4. Gun and served it himself until ammunition was exhausted, then joined the infantry with a rifle and helped carry out wounded even after being wounded himself. | People: Sgt. Aminder E.; Cpl. Ockenden E.; Bdr. Carter; Bdr. Scott W.; Bdr. Wright R.E.; L/Cpl. Herron J.; Gn. D'Aoust J.C.; Williams W.; Sigsworth T.C.; Thompson F.; Carnahan V.; Powell C.H.; Lauder W.; Brown G.; Ridsdale R.H.; Lepper B.R.; Bastien A.G.; Mansfield P.F.; Gnr. Heaps T. | Companies: X3C Battery; Z3C Battery | Casualties: 1 sergeant killed (Aminder); 21 missing (4 prisoners of war, 1 wounded and prisoner, 3 wounded at CCAC, 1 in hospital, 1 at Base Depot); Gnr. Heaps T. wounded | Movement: none
- **1916-06-04 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi Front** — Germans more active than usual with their trench mortars; retaliation by one Stokes mortar firing into crater 4 and artillery on their T.M. positions near Piccadilly Fm soon silenced them; Lt Johnstone [uncertain], 5½ Battery, and two N.C.O.s returned from the Stokes gun course at Terdeghem. | People: Lt Johnstone [uncertain] | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-04 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | A.P.1 / Hill Top / Lock Post / Spoil Bank** — Good progress at A.P.1, Hill Top, Lock Post and Spoil Bank, but owing to the unrest in this part of the line no work parties could be obtained from the battalions, and every available man in the company was used. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-04 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Rest Camp** — The weather was squally, the remains of the battalion were back at rest camp, a muster parade showed "A" Coy 80 other ranks, "B" Coy 80, "C" Coy 50, "D" Coy 42, Staff 63 and Lewis Gun Section 26, of whom 54 were not in the line, giving a total of 325 rank and file returning out of nearly 650, only twelve officers remained, four of them non-combatants and two returned from leave, leaving six officers out of 18 who went into the line, casualties altogether were 57 other ranks killed, 271 wounded and 50 missing and four officers killed, seven wounded and one missing, and Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker, O.C. since the regiment was recruited in January 1915, was buried with full military honours today in the new Military Cemetery at Poperinghe (Lot 2. G1), the Rev. Major A. W. Woods officiating. | People: Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker; Rev. Major A. W. Woods; Major D. E. Draper; Captain W. Rhodes; Captain C. Hewson; Captain J. Baker, Captain C. J. Pitts, Lieutenant P. D. Ottey and Lieutenant T. L. Darling, the wounded were Major D. E. Draper, Captain W. Rhodes, Captain B. W. Roscoe, Lieut. W. H. Rankin, Lieut. H. G. Rogers, Lieut. A. H. Lee and Lieut. J. Adam, and the missing was Lieut. J. Docker, and Major D. E. Draper, now Officer Commanding, made recommendations for honours including the D.S.O. for Captain Barry Wentworth Roscoe and Lieutenant George Roland Barnes, the Military Cross for Captain William Rhodes and Captain Charles Walsby Hewson, the D.C.M. for Pte. J. E. Brayley, C.S.M. G. Gill, C.S.M. F. Hughes, Sergt. T. W. Martin, Sergt. R. B. Rogers and Cpl. H. B. Walton, and the Military Medal for ten other ranks, with further Military Medal recommendations and direct commissions from the ranks. | People: Lt.-Colonel J. H. Baker; Captain C. J. Pitts; Lieutenant P. D. Ottey; Lieutenant T. L. Darling; Major D. E. Draper; Captain W. Rhodes; Captain B. W. Roscoe; Lieut. W. H. Rankin; Lieut. H. G. Rogers; Lieut. A. H. Lee; Lieut. J. Adam; Lieut. J. Docker; Lieutenant George Roland Barnes; Captain Charles Walsby Hewson | Companies: — | Casualties: Officers: 4 killed, 7 wounded, 1 missing (as listed 5 June) | Movement: To farmhouse billets on the outskirts of Steenvoorde.
- **1916-06-05 to 1916-06-15 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Zillebeke Bund / S.P. 16 / Maple Copse / Dormy House, Belgium** — Evening orders to proceed with 4 Stokes guns to Zillebeke Bund (4 gun crews, 2 officers); awaited orders two days; two guns and ammunition taken up to S.P. 16 near Maple Copse in anticipation of an attack. Nothing of moment. 11 June Mr. Ryerson ordered up with two crews as relief; on the way up received instructions covering attack of 10th–11th June. More ammunition brought up but rain for over 24 hours before the attack, no shelter for ammunition, fields impracticable for firing. 13 June relief went up to Dormy House, S.P. 16 having become untenable. 15 June orders to retire to Divisional Rest with the Brigade. | People: Lieut. J. E. Ryerson. | Locations: Zillebeke Bund; S.P. 16; Maple Copse; Dormy House.
- **1916-06-05 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Heavy artillery duel most of day; Zillebeke heavily bombarded; evening fairly quiet; 1 man suffering from shellshock evacuated. | Casualties: 1 O.R. evacuated (shellshock). | Movement: —
- **1916-06-05 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Cold and showery. Verbal report phoned to C.R.E. on work accomplished; message received from Gen Byng congratulating Canadians on defence against enemy attack. Orders from C.R.E. to reclaim 65 S [uncertain], to be unoccupied by either side. Lieuts Young and Dunsmore with their sections and some men of No 3 Section found the trench occupied by the enemy and the communication trench badly smashed, and that there had been an enemy infantry attack against 65 R; work carried on repairing 65 R, levelled in places and very lightly held, and sappers stood by in 65 R with infantry expecting an attack. O.C. reported to C.R.E. and to Gen. Ketchum of 6th I.B. Lieut Harrison moved up to Advanced Billets to live. Enemy shelled neighbourhood of horse lines. | People: Gen Byng; Lieuts Young and Dunsmore; Lieut Harrison; Gen. Ketchum. | Companies: No 3 Section. | Casualties: Lieut Young slightly wounded in head by pieces from H.E. shell; one Sapper also slightly wounded; both returned to duty.
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — O.C. completes morning inspection Billeting Papers amounting to 8 Francs and 5 Centimes was forwarded to B.R.O. Second Army. Received today from 7th Belgium Artillery 40 horses and 3 mules, also admitted 5 sick horses from 1st Can Division — A.D.V.S visits section and inspects horses — Reserved from R.T.O. Poperinghe Ten Cars for shipment of horses tomorrow — Ambulance calls at Can. Cycl. Battalion and returns with Case No. 2044. | Casualties: 45 horses received, 3 mules received.
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Dickeybusch Huts** — Dickeybusch Huts were being shelled, the majority of shells falling around the incinerator, which from an aeroplane might look like a howitzer, but the camp was empty, the troops having moved up, and convalescents were set to clean up, while Scottish and Dominion Lines were also empty and the Camp Commandant had returned to [uncertain]. | Casualties: none (camp empty).
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | Havre, France** — 202 horses, 34 mules admitted.
- **1916-06-05 | No. 1 Railhead Supply Detachment, CASC | Reninghelst Siding, France** — Men employed on Railhead Supply Duties. Weather — Showery. Cool heavy wind. | People: none named. | Casualties: none. | Movement: none.
- **1916-06-05 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Captains C. A. Graves and H. K. Neilson struck off the strength (to report to the D.D.M.S., Canadian Army Corps); Captain F. G. Logie posted to the Central Medical Inspection Room for temporary duty; Captain L. H. McKim returned from leave; convoy of 53 patients at 10.15 p.m. | People: Capt C. A. Graves, Capt H. K. Neilson, Capt F. G. Logie, Capt L. H. McKim.
- **1916-06-06 | 18th Battalion | Front line** — Position as yesterday; heavy evening bombardment of Bern and Pollock and the reserve trenches from 6.15 p.m. [uncertain]; a small enemy party penetrated the right junction of Bern and Pollock after the destruction of the machine-gun emplacement at Bern [uncertain] Junction, entering by an old communication trench, but was driven out by the remainder of the Bern garrison under Cpl Routley; the Loop garrison stood to on sentry Pte Montgomery's warning and opened rapid fire as the enemy retired; a wounded German was secured in front of Pollock; 10 other ranks killed in action, 30 wounded; 24 other ranks arrived as reinforcements. | People: Cpl Routley; Pte Montgomery. | Locations: Bern; Pollock; The Loop.
- **1916-06-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Reninghelst** — Increased activity and severe shelling put practically every circuit except the six-foot buried route out several times, and 1,218 telegrams and despatches were handled, the largest day's business since the beginning of operations. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-06-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | —** — The O.C. visited Col. Anderson about the Shorncliffe report that Webb was appointed O.C. 4th Train; no official word had reached the Train. | People: Col. Anderson; Webb. | Companies: Headquarters Company; 4th Train. | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-06 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field** — No. 300035 Gr. Clairmont reported missing (now officially reported wounded at CCAC). Y.3.C. Clairmont | Companies: X3C Battery; Y3C Battery | Casualties: 1 man missing (later officially wounded at CCAC) | Movement: none
- **1916-06-06 | 5th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | St Eloi** — The 4-in mortars in the right half did good work firing on the German T.M. which were active in the evening; Lt Wayfield [uncertain] from 3rd Bde T.M. Batteries reconnoitres part of line and takes over from us. | People: Lt Wayfield [uncertain] | Companies: 3rd Bde T.M. Batteries | Casualties: none
- **1916-06-06 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — All men returned to camp rest billets at 3 a.m. and rested all day. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-06-06 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Heavy artillery fire on Hooge Front; enemy advances in afternoon on our front line and on to our 2nd line where they were held up; M.G.s proved valuable; front line shell-proof emplacements impossible to obtain, but shell-proof dugouts can be made; 1 O.R. wounded. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Dull, cold and showery. Heavy shelling at Advanced Billets: one N.C.O. and two sappers went out in the street, one killed, one died within three hours and the other badly wounded, all by the same shell. Orders from C.R.E.; Lieuts Harrison and Dunsmore and sections prepared to go out to continue work of last night. O.C. attended 6th I.B. and Col. Lamb D.S.O.; instructed to stand by as enemy attack expected at 65 R; enemy attack at Hooge repulsed. At 10.15 p.m. counter attack abandoned and working parties, 2, 3 and 4 Sections, proceeded to work. O.C. remained at B.H.Q. all night with runners. Lieut Walley escorted wagons with engineer supplies to Zillebeke Dump. | People: Lieuts Harrison and Dunsmore; Col. Lamb; Lieut Walley. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section. | Casualties: Spr Grove F.J. killed by H.E. shell #502825; Spr Campbell J wounded #502770, died of wounds; 2nd Cpl. Ennis wounded #500033.
- **1916-06-06 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Poperinghe** — (continued) Officers Strength Return Forwarded to Officer i/c Officers Pay 7 Millbank London — Copy of Horses evacuated also copy of Belgium horses Evacuated was rendered to A.D.V.S. — O.C. receives June Pass Twenty Four skin disease Cases was included in the shipment today — Ambulance calls at 7th Batt. 2nd Inf Bde. Transport lines and returns with Case No. [blank in original] Four Horses admitted to M.V.S. today. | Casualties: 4 horses received.

- **1916-06-07 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Artillery duel intense; our artillery getting very heavy; Zillebeke shelled for 2 hours 5 to 7 p.m., whole village razed; machine gun emplacement in church wrecked; shelters in ruins rendered untenable; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1916-06-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Steenvoorde** — The weather was bright and warm, the companies carried on checking up new drafts and nominal rolls in the morning and paid particular attention to bayonet fighting in the afternoon, and reinforcements were 24 other ranks to "A" Coy from the 12th Reserve Battalion, 25 to "A" Coy from the 40th Reserve Battalion, one to "A" Coy from the 39th Reserve Battalion and 21 to "B" Coy from the 37th Reserve Battalion, 71 in all. | People: — | Companies: A; B | Casualties: none.

O.C. inspected front line and various working parties. Lieut Young put in fire bays on Lower Regent St and wired same; Lieut Dunsmore constructed communication trench and shell trenches Yeomanry Post to Maple Lodge with cyclists and his section; Lieut Robertson and his section wiring north of Menin Road towards Outpost Farm; Lieut West and section building fire step and repairing China Wall. - **1916-06-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Violent artillery duels all day with periods of intense bombardment of German front line and flanks; orders for assault issued; ordered to obtain fire effect on German old lines; one gun advanced to S.P. 17 for enfilade fire on Loop and Birdcage, one gun at Dormy House for indirect fire on Birdcage trenches, one gun from Tuilerie for indirect fire on German support line in front of trenches 59, 60, 61, one gun at Zillebeke Switch for fire on Tor Top and German old line, all to open fire at 1.20 a.m. 13 June; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1916-06-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — 12.45 a.m. after a quiet spell violent bombardment of German front line begins; 1.30 a.m. attack launched on Mount Sorrel, Hill 61, Hill 62, and a bomb attack by a battalion of 9th Canadian Brigade on Hill 56, Rigo St. and the old front line along Warrington Ave and Byland Ave; several prisoners made; on Hill 62 machine guns survived the bombardment and held up the attack, had to be bombed from the flanks; recommendation that deep dugouts be made for all M.G. emplacements advanced in front of front line; no casualties. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Cold and cloudy with rain. Heavy bombardment by our artillery 12.45–1.30 a.m. on enemy front line; infantry and smoke attack on flanks at 1.30 a.m. successful in clearing Hill 62, Observatory Ridge and Mt. Sorrel; enemy prisoners taken. O.C. and O/C Pioneers interviewed O.C. Right Battalion re work for tonight; also interviewed Brigade Major 9th I.B.; arranged for 9th F.C.C.E. to wire Hill St front line and Pioneers to take rear line. Working parties under Lieuts Young and Dunsmore carried up material to wire Hill St, but shelling started and the infantry covering party would not remain out as German attack expected; little work accomplished. Lieut Walley came up to line at Advanced Billets. | People: Lieuts Young and Dunsmore; Lieut Walley.

- **1916-06-14 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bund, Belgium** — Whole front remarkably quiet; occasional salvoes from Germans along communication trenches and routes; consolidation going on; men much exhausted, in since 14 May with only two days rest; 1 O.R. wounded. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1916-06-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Cloudy and cold with rain. Heavy bombardment of enemy front line by our artillery 2–2.30 a.m. Orders from C.R.E. to wire Hill St, and late orders to wire 65 S. O.C. attended 9th I.B. to arrange covering party. Lieuts Young, Dunsmore and Robertson with sections carrying up material and wiring in front of Hill St under heavy intermittent shelling all night; O.C. also went up to the work and found 65 S occupied by the enemy; infantry patrol endeavouring to investigate was bombed; unable to wire 65 S. Wiring on Hill St completed. Infantry covering party had 6 casualties and would not remain out. Lieuts West and Walley, Sgt Bate and other 9th F.C.C.E. N.C.Os, with guides from 7th F.C.C.E., went out to inspect new trenches on Mt. Sorrel before taking over; H.E. shell badly wounded three guides and wounded Lieut Walley in arm and leg. Sgt Bate commended for going out under shell fire and getting in wounded men, one of whom had been again wounded. | People: Lieuts Young, Dunsmore and Robertson; Lieuts West and Walley; Sgt Bate. | Casualties: Lieut Walley wounded in arm and leg; three guides from 7th F.C.C.E. badly wounded; infantry covering party 6 casualties.

- **1916-06-15 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Cold and cloudy with rain. Orders from C.R.E. to take over supervision of work in trenches 47–52. O.C. attended Maj. Hertzburg and Capt Lynn, obtained maps and discussed situation; also attended Brigade Major 5th I.B. and discussed work proposed; reported to C.R.E. Lieuts Young and Dunsmore with 1 and 2 Sections returned to Camp "G" for a rest. Lieut Robertson [uncertain] with [uncertain] inspected new front line to be taken over and reported on poor condition of trenches. Lieut West with No 4 and part of No 3 Section erected 710 yards 4-strand wire fence, 1 row French wire [uncertain], Dormy House to China Wall. - **1916-06-16 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13 d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium, Sh 28 N.W.** — Fine and clear. Lieut Robertson, No 3 Section, repaired tunnel trench Sorrel Hill; caught by heavy enemy bombardment, stood to with infantry of 22nd Bn [uncertain] in front line to repel expected enemy attack, continued work between bombardments and returned to Advanced Billets with section without casualties on being relieved by O.C. trench; also inspected new trenches for 9th Field Co. Lieut West with No 4 Section as carrying party to wire Mt Sorrel front line trench; wiring interrupted by bombardment. O.C. had conference with O.C. 3rd Pioneer Bn and, scouting ground with Lieut Sawyer and siting Battersea House communication trench, was caught in heavy bombardment. Pioneer officer wounded before commencing work with Pioneers; work not started. O.C. collected three large working parties of different infantry battalions who were without officers and reported with same to 5th I.B. H.Q. when bombardment started. - **1916-07-01 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.2.7, Ref Map Belgium Sht 28 N.W.** — O.C. and Mr Dunsmore with a party of sappers attended the funeral of #502624 Sapper Fox R.E. at Brandhoek Cemetery, buried at line "G", 3rd grave from south end (G 12 b.6.9); word received from Mr Young that he had commenced his course of instruction to 8th I.B. on 26 June (wiring parties, working parties, trench digging, machine gun emplacements, etc.); party of 1 N.C.O. and 10 sappers at Hutting Dump, Lieut West with No. 4 Section on New Oxford St, Lieut Robertson on drains Areas 18 C; sports in the afternoon at the camp of the Eaton Machine Gun Battery under the Y.M.C.A.; O.C. arranged with Capt. McNamara, Chaplain of 49th I.B., to hold divine service tomorrow at 11 a.m.; O.C. proceeded to Advanced Billets to relieve Mr Harrison; War Diary for June forwarded to A.A. & Q.M.G. 3rd Echelon. | People: Sapper Fox R.E. (#502624); Mr Young; Mr Dunsmore; Lieut West; Lieut Robertson; Mr Harrison; Capt. - **1916-07-08 to 1916-07-09 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill St. / Culvert / Trench #61 / Forrester Lane, Belgium** — Night 8/9 July: 44 rounds fired from Hill St.; firing ceased 12.00 A.M. promptly. Bombing officer of 58th Battn., in trench at junction of old front line + Darlington [uncertain], observed fire and reported it well directed and placed, searching bombing post and vicinity and enfilading trench #61 (old); bombing post unoccupied on arrival of bombing party of 58th Battn.; ground in vicinity badly cut up. 11.45 P.M. Stokes mortar in Culvert opened fire on old bombing post No. 8 (Hooge) and trench on either side, mortar being traversed gradually. 12.00 A.M. fire directed on trench at head of Forrester Lane. 12.00 [as written] ceased fire. 40 rounds in all fired. Bombing officer of 52nd Battn. reported old bombing post #8 badly broken up and scarcely recognizable, unoccupied on his arrival. Results of setting up guns at night by compass from bearings obtained from maps more satisfactory than anticipated. No casualties sustained. Splinter-proof cover most valuable. | People: bombing officers of 58th and 52nd Battalions. | Companies: 58th Battalion; 52nd Battalion. | Locations: Hill St.; Culvert; Trench #61; Forrester Lane; Hooge. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-08 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill St. / Culvert / Halfway House, Belgium** — 5.30 P.M. Lieut. Ryerson received verbal instructions from B.Gen. Hill, Brigadier 9th Can. Inf. Bde. (confirmed by 9th Can. Inf. Bde. Operation Order 25) regarding operations night 8/9 July. Stokes mortars in Hill St. and Culvert to be used, although neither emplacement complete. Temporary splinter-proof cover hurriedly erected over Hill St. emplacement, hole left just large enough for discharge of shell. 7.00 P.M. Lieut. Reade given charge of Hill St. gun. 44 rounds [uncertain] prepared at Halfway House and carried by reserve men to gun position, all available red or long-range cartridges being used. 9.00 P.M. Lt. Ryerson left Halfway House for Culvert to give detailed instructions to Lt. MacDonald, in charge of operations there. Carrying party arranged to carry ammunition from Halfway House to Culvert as supply was low — 45 rounds carried. 11.45 P.M. Stokes mortar in Hill St. (I 24 B 2 1/2 1 1/2) opened fire on enemy bombing post in old front line trench #61 and from J 19 A 0 2 1/2 to J 19 A 7 2. Range 360 to 380 yards. | People: Lieut. J. E. Ryerson; B.Gen. Hill; Lieut. Reade; Lt. MacDonald. | Locations: Hill St.; Culvert; Halfway House. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-07-22 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Steenvoorde area (K34 D), France** — 6.00 A.M. registering on trenches in preparation for tactical scheme. 9.30 A.M./12.00 [uncertain] tactical scheme: 4 mortars dug in, in bush of wood K34 D. - **1916-07-23 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Steenvoorde area, France** — 9.00 A.M./12.00 [uncertain] men attached given [uncertain] practise in firing live ammunition. Lieut. MacDonald and 3 Corporals returned from Trench Mortar School, Terdeghem. Model emplacement tested out to see what traverse could be obtained: emplacement 6'×6' with floor 8' below surface, aperture 2'×3' in roof for discharge of shell; allowed traverse sufficient to bombard 100 yds of trench supposing emplacement 200 yds behind front line. On examination of craters, total traverse of mortar at 300 yards is LESS than at 200 yds., whereas various Trench Mortar Schools including 2nd Army school at Terdeghem teach traverse at 300 yards is 50% greater than at 200 yards. | People: Lieut. MacDonald. | Locations: Terdeghem. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-07-28 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Crab Crawl, Belgium** — 1.30 A.M. mortars in Mount Sorrel fired 25 rounds on enemy front line in retaliation to whizz-bangs. Enemy immediately ceased fire. 5.00 P.M. mortar in Crab Crawl fired 3 rounds registration. 10.00 P.M. ditto 6 rounds retaliation to rifle grenades. 11.00 P.M. mortars in Mount Sorrel fired 20 rounds in retaliation to about 10 T.M. bombs. Casualties nil. Our patrols went out + we were obliged to cease fire. Gun No. 6 from R.S. 8 taken to Mount Sorrel, where it will be of more use — a third emplacement available there, slightly damaged by a shell about a week ago, easily put in usable shape. [Remarks: patrol report — enemy M.G. put out of action, catching crews during a relief + causing several casualties.] | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Crab Crawl; R.S. 8. | Casualties: none (battery).

- **1916-07-31 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Crab Crawl / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — Day quiet. Work on dug-out continued. General: 43rd Battn. report mortar in Crab Crawl of value to them in silencing enemy rifle grenade fire; also that direct hit was obtained on enemy bombing post and on more than one occasion men in our bombing post heard commotion in enemy trench following our fire — a distinct change of attitude of this battalion toward our trench mortars. 58th Battn. report mortars in Mount Sorrel very useful in silencing enemy T.M. fire, especially as retaliation can be obtained immediately wherever and whenever wanted, which is more difficult with artillery. Stokes mortars especially useful in this sector as lines are so close artillery fire cannot be brought to bear on enemy front line. Signed John E. Ryerson, Capt., O.C. 9th Canadian Trench Mortar Battery. | People: Capt. J. E. Ryerson. | Companies: 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion. | Locations: Crab Crawl; Mount Sorrel. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-07-31 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Zillebeke Bund, Belgium** — Very quiet; indirect fire on enemy tram-lines, roads and dumps carried on; 10 O.R. reported for duty with the company. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

Rhoades, Adjutant, was promoted Major to date from 2nd June 1916 while the honours and awards list was published, with the D.S.O. for Lt.-Colonel J. C. Draper, Military Crosses for Captain (Major) W. Rhoades, Captain C. W. Hewson and Lieutenant G. R. Barnes, D.C.M.s for C.S.M. G. Gill, C.S.M. F. Hughes, Corporal H. B. Walton and Corporal J. E. Pringley, and Military Medals for Sgt. T. E. Sorrel enemy fired 7 flares in quick succession from a point [uncertain] and a machine gun [uncertain] in front of his trench about opposite our trench 51 [uncertain]. Casualties nil. | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Crab Crawl; trench 51. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-08-03 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Crab Crawl / St. Peter St. / Hill 60, Belgium** — 1.30 A.M. one of our patrols encountered an enemy patrol opposite trenches 50/51 and a number of bombs were thrown. - **1916-08-08 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Machine Gun Camp, Erie, Belgium** — Parades as usual: physical drill, care and cleaning, gun drill, stoppages; our transport caught in a cloud of gas from the north and as a result 2 horses had to be destroyed; gas attack put on by enemy north of Menin Road, followed by heavy shelling by both sides; helmets used by transport drivers proved satisfactory; gas densest about Hell Fire Corner and Ypres; none in 9th Bde. frontage. | Casualties: 2 horses destroyed (gas). | Movement: —
- **1916-08-08 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.3.7** — Clear and cool. Lieut. Robinson with No. 1 Section finished West St. ready for revettment, deepened, widened and backfilled Leinster St., and built traverses and revetted on the Front Line; Lieut. Dunsmore with No. 2 Section worked on the revettment of Savoy St., reclaiming trench 68, deepening the dugout at the Tuilerie, reclaiming Grange Rd., repairing Roslyn St., building a parapet on Gourock Rd. and revetting Bond St.; the C.S.M. continued cleaning out Culvert C and Cork St., worked on the Island Traverse and repaired revettment on Regent St. East. Operation Order No. 11, received at 5.45 p.m., instructed the Company to take over work in trenches 29 to 33 from 1st F.C.C.E. and trenches 34 to 38 from 2nd F.C.C.E. after work on the night of 9th/10th August, and to take over 1st F.C.C.E. Advanced Billets in the Bluff Tunnels. A siren gas alarm sounded at 11.15 p.m.; helmets were put on at 11.45 p.m. and kept on until 12.25 a.m.; two men vomited and six horses had running eyes and were slightly dazed in the morning, and a sapper on gas guard at the Advanced Billets was slightly overcome. Officers and N.C.O.s of the 9th escorted those of the 7th F.C.C.E. over the work to be taken over by the 7th. Lieut. Young reported to Camp "G" from Steenvoorde at 11.30 p.m. under instructions from the C.R.E. | People: Lieut. Robinson, Lieut. Dunsmore, Lieut. Young, Lieut. Harrison. | Companies: No. 1 Section, No. 2 Section, 1st F.C.C.E., 2nd F.C.C.E., 7th F.C.C.E., P.P.C.L.I., 52nd Battn., R.C.R. | Movement: Takeover of trenches 29–38 and Bluff Tunnels Advanced Billets ordered for after the night of 9th/10th August.

Dunsmore with No. 2 Section on reclaiming Grange Rd., repairing Roslyn St., strutting Savoy St., cutting a doorway in the Tuillerie dugout, banking the parapet on the Gourock Rd. bombing post and repairing trench 68; the C.S.M. on the centre dugout in "A" culvert, clearing out "C" culvert, constructing a flying traverse near the culverts and carrying material from Gordon House Dump. Trench wardens stood to with the R.C.R. from 12.00 to 1.30 a.m.; no working parties. The O.C. attended 1st and 2nd Field Companies; Lieuts. Harrison, Young and Robertson with N.C.O.s attended 1st F.C.C.E. [uncertain] at the Bluff going over the works in the 1st area, and Lieuts. Dunsmore and West with N.C.O.s attended 2nd F.C.C.E. at the Railway dugouts going over the works in the 2nd area. | People: Lieut. Robinson, Lieut. Dunsmore, Lieut. Harrison, Lieut. Young, Lieut. Robertson, Lieut. West. | Companies: No. 1 Section, No. 2 Section, 1st F.C.C.E., 2nd F.C.C.E., R.C.R.

- **1916-08-11 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bluff, Belgium** — Relief completed at 1.30 a.m., the battalion now holding the Bluff and craters and Trenches 29–32, with 'A' Coy in Trenches 29, 30, 30a, King St. and Wynd (138 rifles), 'B' Coy in Trenches 32 and 32a (118 rifles), 'C' Coy in Pollock, Bank, International and 31a (153 rifles), 'D' Coy in Thames St, Gordon Post, Tunnel and New Crater (155 rifles) and battalion H.Q. in the tunnels and dugouts (33 rifles), for a total of 597 rifles, 4 Lewis guns, 4 Colt guns, 59 gunners, 45 company bombers, 43 battalion bombers, 19 scouts, 26 signallers and 21 stretcher bearers, while the front was very quiet all day except between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m., when the enemy searched the front and support lines with shrapnel, small H.E. shells and trench mortars and our 18-pounders and 4.5 howitzers retaliated with good results. | People: — | Companies: 'A' Coy; 'B' Coy; 'C' Coy; 'D' Coy; 1st C.M.R. Battalion; 28th Canadian Infantry Battalion; 4th C.M.R. Battalion. | Casualties: **Killed: L/Cpl W. R. Coles (No. 111102, 'A' Coy, G.S.W. in head, Trench 32a, 10.20 a.m.), Pte. H. K. Paterson (No. 141998, 'C' Coy, trench mortar, New Crater, 4.50 p.m.). Died of wounds: Sgt. W. R. Smith (No. 110522, 'C' Coy, G.S.W. in stomach, front of Crater, 9 a.m.). Wounded: L/Cpl O. R. Stenson (No. 110532, 'B' Coy, G.S.W. through both cheeks, Bombing Post, 1.15 a.m.), Pte. H. W. Steele (No. 142366, 'C' Coy, trench mortar in head, New Crater, 4.50 p.m.), Pte. J. Wilson (No. 114609, 'B' Coy, shrapnel wound right eye, Trench 30a), Sgt. W. J. A. King (No. 110898, Bomber 'A' Coy, shrapnel in head and arm, slight, Bluff, 8.30 p.m.), Pte. J. A. Dunnington (No. 115232, Bomber 'A' Coy, shrapnel in left thigh, slight, Bluff, 5.30 p.m.).**

- **1916-08-11 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Promenade, Belgium** — Intermittent shelling by enemy with much heavier retaliation by our batteries; enemy shelled Dormy House, Cotting, Square Wood; 10 O.R. arrived from Base as reinforcements; 60th Battn, 9th C. Bde. relieved 10th Can. Battn, last battalion of 1st Canadian Division to be relieved; 8th Can. Bde. on our right and 7th Can. Bde. on our left. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1916-08-12 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bluff, Belgium** — Bright overhead with a slight south-west wind and ground mist clearing about 9.30 a.m.; L/Cpl. Coles, Pte. Paterson and Sgt. Smith, killed the previous day, were buried in the cemetery at Bedford House the previous night with Captain Rev. Hepburn officiating, the enemy bombarded trenches to the left about Mount Sorrel from 9 a.m. until noon with a few shells falling in rear of Trench 31a and no damage, the engineers, protected by a screen of our bombers and scouts, exploded a small surface mine in front of and to the north of the Old Crater and recovered German mining tools and [uncertain] apparatus from the damaged gallery, and a raid by the 28th Battalion on our right the night before last proved successful, accounting for several Germans and bringing back one prisoner. | People: Capt. Rev. Hepburn. | Companies: 28th Battalion. | Casualties: **Killed (accidentally): Pte. J. A. Keenan (No. 141368, 'C' Coy, accidentally killed by No. 142209 Pte. Henderson J.). Wounded: Pte. O. Gervais (No. 416287, 'B' Coy, self-inflicted wound, third finger right hand).**
- **1916-08-12 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill 60 / Mount Sorrel, Belgium** — 8.30 A.M. enemy opened heavy bombardment on Hill 60 sector + to right of it. 10.00 A.M. enemy infantry attacked. During bombardment and attack, mortars #1 + #2 in this sector fired 129 rounds and #2 37 rounds on enemy front line, creating barrage in "No Man's Land". Corpl. of 60th Can. Battn. states he saw bombs exploding among enemy troops as they advanced across No Man's Land. Dug-outs + emplacements stood the bombardment well. Casualties nil. Mortars in Mount Sorrel joined in retaliatory bombardment, firing #1 35 rounds, #2 25 rounds, #3 25 rounds. Bombing post opposite trench 48 registered on by #3 mortar, 8 rounds being fired. | Companies: 60th Battalion. | Locations: Hill 60; Mount Sorrel; trench 48. | Casualties: none (battery).
- **1916-08-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Promenade, Belgium** — Very heavy artillery and trench mortar bombardment by enemy started 8.15; at 8.30 intense bombardment concentrated on trenches around Railway Cutting; about 9.45 information received Germans are in trench 38; bombing heard but nothing seen owing to intense dust; 10.40 42nd Battn report dense barrage of 5.9 on routes from Valley Cottages; reports trench 46 taken but not confirmed; communication with front line suspended, communication attempted through 52nd Battn at Verbrandenmolen; 6 runners despatched to front line but failed to make connection; 11.35 communication with front battalion established; 60th Battn report trenches much battered, feared casualties heavy; things not serious, situation well in hand; two Lewis guns out of commission but replaced by Colt guns. | Casualties: none (60th Battn casualties feared heavy, unconfirmed). | Movement: —
- **1916-08-12 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.3.7** — Fine and very warm. Heavy enemy bombardment of the front line began at 8.30 a.m.; working parties of No. 4 Section on the left sector were cancelled for the day and No. 4 Section stood by. The enemy penetrated trench 38 and was ejected; the trench had been held by a portion of the 60th Battn., [uncertain] Battn. on the left of the railroad cutting, and partly by the 1st Canadian Mounted Rifles. The O.C. attended 9th I.B. Headquarters and remained at 8th I.B. Headquarters during the day, and inspected the Right Sector trenches held by the 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles. Miners working in the Right Sector exploded a camouflet in the Bluff and damaged the enemy's gallery in the old crater next to the canal. Lieut. Young with No. 1 Section worked on Thames St., the craters and tunnelling; Lieut. Robertson with No. 3 Section on International trench, Davidson Lane, Pollock (31), the Diagonal trench and the Drive; Lieut. West with No. 4 Section on repairing trench 34 and Pat Alley, trench 35 and dugouts in 36, revetting trench 37 and putting in dugouts in 35. Two sappers from No. 4 Section returned from the Front Line carrying in wounded. | People: Lieut. West, Lieut. Young, Lieut. Robertson. | Companies: No. 1 Section, No. 3 Section, No. 4 Section, 60th Battn., 1st Canadian Mounted Rifles, 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles. | Casualties: Nil.

- **1916-08-13 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bluff, Belgium** — Bright and warm with a south-west wind; the O.C. recommended L/Cpl. Macnamara of 'C' Coy for the Victoria Cross for going out from the Crater in broad daylight in the face of enemy machine-gun and rifle fire to bring in Sgt. Smith, mortally wounded in the stomach by a sniper, after two previous rescue attempts had been frustrated by enemy fire, and the early part of the day was quiet but about 4.30 p.m. the enemy shelled the craters and vicinity for an hour, inflicting several casualties and damaging New Crater and Thames St. | People: L/Cpl. Macnamara; Sgt. Smith; Lieut. Stewart Basil Simpson. | Companies: 'C' Coy. | Casualties: **Killed: A/Sgt. W. R. Pearson (No. 110443, 'B' Coy, H.E. shell explosion, New Crater, 7.50 p.m.). Drury (No. 121559, 'B' Coy, slight shrapnel wound, attached to Brigade Machine Gun Company), Pte. W. A. Kelly (No. 123318, 'B' Coy, slight wound, attached to Brigade Machine Gun Company), Pte. D. L. Dunsden (No. 142359, 'B' Coy, shrapnel wound head, shoulders and arm, New Crater, 7.50 p.m.), Pte. C. A. Mason (No. 142236, 'B' Coy, shrapnel wound right shoulder, New Crater, 4.50 p.m.), Lieut. Stewart Basil Simpson (shrapnel wound knee and arm, New Crater), Pte. J. d Parkes (No. 114616, 'A' Coy, shrapnel wound left side of head, New Crater, 4.50 p.m.), Pte. H. W. Steele (No. 142366, 'C' Coy, shrapnel wound left arm, New Crater, 4.50 p.m.), Sgt. G. McIver (No. 110411, 'C' Coy, injuries to back by being buried by shell explosion), Pte. J. Burke (No. 141588, 'C' Coy, shrapnel wounds chest, arms and back).**
- **1916-08-13 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Mount Sorrel / Hill 60, Belgium** — 2.30 A.M./1.00 A.M. [as written] 10 rounds fired on bombing post [uncertain], destroying it; 9 rounds ditto opposite trench 50, destroying it. 1.00 A.M. [as written] enemy bombarded vicinity of #1 and #2 mortars in Mount Sorrel with 4.2" H.E., obtaining a direct hit on #1, exploding 142 rounds ammunition, completely destroying mortar and emplacement as well as 4 rifles and some other equipment. #2 emplacement half filled with earth + debris, burying the mortar and partially burying the crew; mortar quickly dug out and again ready for action in a short time. Casualties nil. Day quiet. 11.00 P.M. mortars in Hill 60 fired 39 rounds in retaliation to rifle grenades. | Locations: Mount Sorrel; Hill 60; trench 50. | Casualties: none.
- **1916-08-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Promenade, Belgium** — Quiet throughout the day; machine gun fire not so active; intermittent shelling by enemy on transport during night; Lieut. - **1916-08-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.3.7** — Fair and cooler, slight westerly wind. Lieut. Young and No. 1 Section worked on 2-man dugouts at the New Crater at A, tunnelling at the New Crater at B, and raising and thickening the parapet on Canal St.; Lieut. Robertson and No. 3 Section on deepening and revetting International St., laying bath mats on Davidson Lane, deepening and widening the Diagonal trench and Pollock St.; Lieut. Thornley and No. 4 Section on a dugout and revetting on Pat Alley, cleaning out and revetting trench 36, repairing crumps and revetting trench 35, digging trench 37 and repairing overhead traverses and revetting. The Advanced Billets at the Railway dugouts were shelled all morning and telephone communication was cut off. Day parties worked on the revettment of trench 30, drainage of Wynde St., dugouts at S.P. 7, Thames St., King St., Pear Tree Lane, bridges 20 to 29, the Drive, International trench, Hastings trench and Davidson Lane. | People: Lieut. Young, Lieut. Robertson, Lieut. Thornley. | Companies: No. 1 Section, No. 3 Section, No. 4 Section.

- **1916-08-14 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Hill 60 District; Mt. Sorrell; Metropolitan Left (Fir Lane; Pinch Gut; Davidson St; Hedges St)** — Fir Lane gun repaired and in action again; ten rounds fired in retaliation to hostile trench-mortar shelling. Pinch Gut gun: new bed put in. Davidson St. gun: repair work continues. Hedges St. guns (2) registered on the German front line. At 2.30 p.m. opened up with all guns in the district and sent over 75 rounds, good results; all crews now using D.A. (Direct Action) fuses, found more satisfactory than the time fuses, which are not dependable. Hedges St. guns: left gun again buried with a Minenwerfer shell and out of action; crews repairing. Twenty-nine rounds fired in retaliation; the enemy was shelling very heavily. | People: G. Hanson Davison (Lieut.) | Companies: none | Casualties: none | Movement: none

- **1916-08-14 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Hill 60 / Railway Dugouts, Belgium** — 3.00 P.M./6.00 P.M. enemy bombarded Hill 60 sector with trench mortars and Minenwerfer (heavy), doing considerable damage. About 5.00 P.M. a direct hit was obtained on Emplacement #2, completely destroying emplacement, mortar, 170 rounds ammunition, and rendering adjoining dug-outs unserviceable. Casualties: **3 killed, 6 wounded and shocked** — 4 men were in dug-outs and door was sealed by earth from explosion; men wounded by flying pieces and by partial collapse of dug-out and affected by gas. Owing to casualties and destruction of ammunition it is unknown what firing was done during the day; 2 of the casualties being from crew of mortar #1, gassed. 7.00 P.M. wired to billet for 2 N.C.O.s + 6 men to replace casualties, arriving at Railway Dug-outs about 10.00 P.M. New mortar set up in Old 60 [uncertain] T.M. emplacement in Allen St., 25 yds in rear of [uncertain] one destroyed. | Locations: Hill 60; Allen St.; Railway Dugouts. | Casualties: **3 killed, 6 wounded and gassed** (battery's heaviest loss of the diary; two of the killed are named in the following entries — Pte. Jeacke and Corpl. A. F. Nelson; the third is not named in the diary).

- **1916-08-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.3.7** — Cool with showers and westerly wind. Lieut. Young with No. 1 Section worked on the Glide, Canal and Thames Sts., the New Crater and trench 29, and the tunnel extension at the New Crater and cleaning out the tunnel between trench 29 and the Old Crater; Lieut. Robertson with No. 3 Section on the Diagonal St., Davidson Lane, Pollock St. and Hedge Row, inspecting bridges and running levels on International Trench; Lieut. Thornley with No. 4 Section on the revettment of trenches 35, 34 and 37 and cleaning out and revetting Grand Fleet St.; Lieut. West with No. 4 Section on the Reserve Left, Crescent, 36 S., trenches 34, 35 and 37, Grand Fleet St., Reserve Right and Thorne St., drove a gallery on Reserve Right and sunk a 4 ft. shaft for a machine gun dugout on Leighton St. Lieut.-Col. McBrien of the 3rd Divisional Staff inspected the horse lines. Heavy bombardment opened about 9 a.m. on the front line to the right of the Company sector. The C.R.E. accompanied by the O.C. visited the trenches in the area of the Railway dugouts and inspected progress of work. | People: Lieut. Young, Lieut. Robertson, Lieut. Thornley, Lieut. West, Lieut.-Col. McBrien. | Companies: No. 1 Section, No. 3 Section, No. 4 Section. | Casualties: No. 502537 Spr March S., wounded severely in head by shell.

- **1916-08-19 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Mt. Sorrell; Hill 60 District; Drive (St. Peter St; Marshall Walk; Benham Road)** — At 2 p.m. opened up with all guns in the district and fired 86 rounds, all very effective; shelled the enemy's front and support lines and did considerable damage to his emplacements. St. Peter St. gun needs repairing, having been put out of action after firing its 75 rounds by a 5.9". Twenty-nine rounds fired in retaliation. Marshall Walk emplacement and magazine wrecked by a direct hit. Benham Road emplacement must have been hit several times, as the original position could not be located. Opened up a "Strafe" and fired 83 rounds in all; one gun fired 50 rounds inside an hour, and a Captain of the 2nd C.M.R.s, who was observing, reported a direct hit on a German Minenwerfer machine. | People: Captain of the 2nd C.M.R.s (unnamed); G. - **1916-08-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | H.13.d.3.7** — Cool with heavy showers. Lieut. Robertson with No. 3 Section on Hastings St., Davidson Lane, International, 32 S., Drive, 32 R, patrolling bridges and making repairs, taking levels on Fir Lane, and Pollock, Bean, Diagonal, Central and Hedge Row; Lieut. West with No. 4 Section on Crescent, 35 S., 36 S., Grand Fleet, Rat Alley, R trench right, Thorne St., tunnel dugout, R trench, Deansgate and trench 33; Lieut. Harrison promoted to Captain of the 9th F.C.C.E. to fill the establishment, dating from 18th February 1916 according to D.R.O. No. 868, 20 Aug./16; the promotions were gazetted on 19th August as posted to Artillery in error. Operation orders were received for the relief of the 3rd Canadian Division by the 4th British Division, in particular the relief of the 9th F.C.C.E. by the Renfrew Field Coy. R.E. on the night of 24th/25th August. Men in camp were painting and cleaning up wagons and technical equipment. | People: Capt. N.R. Robertson, Lieut. E.W. Harrison, Lieut. Young, Lieut. West with No. 4 Section on Deansgate, Crescent, 35 S., Rat Alley, Thorne St., Grand Fleet and Petticoat Lane. - **1916-08-26 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | L.25.c.2.4** — Cool with strong westerly wind. Reveille 4 a.m.; camp and horse lines cleaned and refuse burnt. The Company moved off in column of route at 7 a.m., passed through Ouderdom, Reninghelst and Abeele to new billets at H.30.d.7.2 and L.25.c.2.4, arriving at 10.45 a.m.; the drivers and No. 1 Section were billetted at the former place and the remainder of the Company with the officers at the latter, just north of the English aerodrome. No accommodation being available for the officers, a tarpaulin shelter was erected in the field. Very heavy rainfall at 10 a.m. The C.R.E. overtook the column on the march. Lieut. Dunsmore with cyclists remained at Camp G as a rear guard party and turned it over to the Renfrew Field Coy. R.E. on their arrival about 10 a.m. at Camp G, then followed the Company to the new billets. Lieut. Thornley with 5 N.C.O.s and sappers remained at the Advanced Billets, Railway Dugouts, and continued work with the Renfrew Company and 4th Division English working parties; R.E. officers took over bridges 20–29 inclusive, were shown the magazines of explosives, and were handed a map showing the demolition arrangements in detail. Lieut. Robertson proceeded to Abeele and arranged for baths for the Company at Boeschepe. The C.R.E. with the Adjutant called at the billets with the syllabus of training for the Company as laid down by 3rd Division Headquarters. | People: Lieut. Dunsmore, Lieut. Thornley, Lieut. Robertson. | Companies: No. 1 Section, Renfrew Field Coy. R.E., 4th Division. | Movement: Camp G to new billets at H.30.d.7.2 and L.25.c.2.4 (near Abeele), via Ouderdom and Reninghelst.

- **1916-08-27 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | L.25.c.2.4** — Showery. Training carried on as per syllabus: reveille 6 a.m., physical drill 6.15–6.45 a.m., breakfast 7 a.m., infantry training 8.00–8.30 a.m., field works and organisation of working parties and siting of trenches by day 8.45 a.m.–12 noon, dinner 12 noon, field works and Company marching in small parties in turn for baths at the Corps baths at Boeschepe 1–3 p.m., and officers' instruction 1.30–4.30 p.m. Scheme No. 1, construction of strong points: the O.C., Capt. Harrison and the Sergeant-Major went out scouting through the woods and arranged the scheme, consisting of siting machine gun emplacements and trenches for rapid consolidation (a) on the near side of the woods, (b) in the middle of the woods, and (c) on the far side and clear of the woods. All subalterns, including supernumeraries, with all available N.C.O.s left at dusk, marched to the woods and carried out the scheme as arranged, returning at 1.30 a.m. The O.C. attended the Corps Park at Abeele and arranged for engineering material for 8th I.B. required for training purposes. | People: Capt. Harrison. | Companies: 8th I.B.

McDowall went with the Supply Section to the railhead at Caestre; Gibson's convoy went on to Coulonvillers and McDowall's returned to Steenvoorde; ordnance and postal details moved to their new locations. | People: Lieut. F. A. Gibson; Lieut. McDowall. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Steenvoorde–Coulonvillers.

Richards; Lieut. Greer. | Companies: — | Casualties: none human; 2 horses left behind | Movement: Steenvoorde–destination not named in the diary, via Hazebrouck and Doullens.

McCorkell and Roy paid a visit to the [uncertain] line in front of Albert; health of the company of the best. | People: Lt. McCorkell; Roy. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Halloy–Layicogne.
- **1916-09-07 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bayinghove, France** — Fine and warm; the battalion paraded at "B" Coy billet (K.70.c.6.6) shed 27 [uncertain] at 4.30 p.m., proceeded to the cross roads K.35.d.1.5 and met buses which conveyed us to the outskirts of Cassel [uncertain] (P.20.0.6.9), then route-marched to Bayinghove (0.16.C.4.9) and entrained there, leaving at 21.51, with a parade state of 37 officers and 890 other ranks, 58 horses and 14 wagons. | People: — | Companies: Headquarters Coy.; 'A' Coy; 'B' Coy; 'C' Coy; 'D' Coy. | Casualties: none | Movement: North Steenvoorde–Bayinghove (entrained 21.51 for Candas).
- **1916-09-07 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Steenvoorde → Bavinchoove → Arques → Auxi-le-Château → Maison Rolland, France** — 2.00 A.M. reveille. 3.00 A.M. breakfast. 4.00 A.M. parade. In preparation for move to new area (9th Brigade Operation Order No. 31). 4.30 A.M. left billet pushing 7 push wagons with mortars, stores, cooking dixies, etc.; 3 mortars and several boxes of stores had to be left behind owing to absolute inadequacy of push wagons as transport — Stokes boxes will not fit in, when loaded very difficult to balance, no drag ropes provided; one G.S. wagon would be far more useful. "Why should men of Light trench mortar batteries do the work that is done in other units by horses and mules?" Tedious march: loads kept slipping, kits fell off, wheels struck stone cobbles and wrenched handles out of men's hands, whole load upset on road. Hills about Cassel especially hard pulling; men soon fatigued even with only about one half the load they would have had if everything had been brought. 9.30 A.M. arrived at Bavinchoove; wagons + loads loaded on motor lorries, men boarded other lorries, 25 men per lorry. 9.15 [uncertain] lorries started, went to railway station at Arques. Arrived at Arques; push wagons loaded on flat cars, men entrained in box cars. 12.49 [uncertain] train moved off. Travelled all day until 1.30 A.M. 8 Sept, when arrived at Aux-I-Le-Chateau. Men detrained, push wagons unloaded. Marched via Maizecourt, Domleger and Cramont to billets in Maison Rolland; march very hard owing to extreme darkness and high hills; on arrival men pushing "push wagons" very fatigued. | Locations: Steenvoorde; Cassel; Bavinchoove; Arques; Aux-I-Le-Chateau; Maizecourt; Domleger; Cramont; Maison Rolland. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Steenvoorde area → Arques by lorry and train → Auxi-le-Château → Maison Rolland (march).
- **1916-09-07 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Steenvoorde, France** — Marched from billets at 5 a.m. to Bavincho[le] [uncertain] where conveyed by lorries to Arques and entrained. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Steenvoorde to Arques.
- **1916-09-07 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | L.25.C.2.4** — O.C. interviewed the farmers owning the two billets occupied by the Company, obtained particulars of alleged damage to property, particulars sent to Claims Officer, 3rd Canadian Division, and certificate of having occupied billets sent to Mayor of the Municipality of Watou. Company engaged in cleaning camp, packing wagons and bathing in a tarpaulin bath. Lieut. Thornley with one man proceeded to Cassel Station and accompanied 1st C.M.R. on the first train of the 8th C.I.B. group to the Somme area as billeting officer. Transport and cyclists with Capt. Harrison and Lieuts. Dunsmore and Robertson moved off from billets at 8.30 p.m. and marched via Steenvoorde to Cassel Station and entrained. O.C. with Lieuts. Young, West and Robinson and sappers moved off at 11 p.m. and were conveyed by bus from [uncertain] via Steenvoorde to Cassel Station, where they entrained; usual certificate of billets delivered to the Mayor of the Commune of Watou. | People: Lieut. Thornley; Capt. Harrison; Lieut. Dunsmore; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Young; Lieut. West; Lieut. Robinson. | Locations: Watou; Steenvoorde; Cassel Station; Somme area. | Movement: Watou to Cassel Station, by march and by bus, and entrained.

- **1916-09-08 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Domqueur (Somme area)** — Train moved off from Cassel Station with the Company at 3.51 a.m., also a French Mortar Battery of the Lahore Division on the same train, Major Robertson O.C. train, proceeded via Boulogne to Candas Station, Somme area, arriving 1.55 p.m.; horses watered and fed en route on the train. Company detrained and moved off through Vienvillers, halted on the road east of Bernaville where the Company had tea and horses were fed, then marched through [uncertain], Fransu to Domqueur, arriving 9.20 p.m. Nos. 1 and 2 Sections with the Mounted Section billeted on the east side of the road leading north from the centre of the village; the balance of the Company with transport billeted on the west side of the same road, officers in billets B 8 as arranged by the billeting party met as the Company marched in. None of the men fell out en route. | People: Major Robertson. | Sections: Nos. 1 and 2; Mounted Section. | Locations: Cassel Station; Boulogne; Candas Station; Vienvillers; Bernaville; Fransu; Domqueur. | Movement: Cassel Station via Boulogne to Candas, then marched via Vienvillers, Bernaville and Fransu to Domqueur.

B. Gordon of Montreal on beer for the men during the afternoon, and Major J. C. - **1916-09-10 | 9th Canadian Light Trench Mortar Battery | Maison Rolland → Domart → St. Leger, France** — 10.15 A.M. paraded preparatory to move. Left billet 10.45 A.M., passed starting point Maison Rolland Church at 11.00 A.M. Column delayed on account of very steep hill at Le Plouy, so unit had lunch at Domquer and continued march at 2.30 P.M. via Fransu, Franqueville and Domart, making regular halts of 10 min per hour. At Domart a wrong turning was taken by 9th C.M.G.C., who cut through + passed us on a very steep hill, push carts being too heavy for the men to keep up to marching men or limbers. When top of hill reached, error discovered; necessary to turn about and go down hill again into Domart. When just outside village of Domart, 9th C.M.G.C. made a halt to feed horses. This unit pushed on to St. Leger, arriving at billets in building of the Societe Cooperative La Prevoyance at 6.30 P.M. Men accommodated in open horse sheds, with straw to sleep on. | Companies: 9th C.M.G.C. | Locations: Maison Rolland; Le Plouy; Domquer; Fransu; Franqueville; Domart; St. Leger. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Maison Rolland → St. Leger (march).

- **1916-09-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Fieffes (Somme area)** — Pursuant to 3rd Canadian Divisional Operation Order No. 42 and 8th C.I.B. Operation Order No. 37, the Company, being in the 8th Brigade group for billeting purposes, moved off from Domqueur at 6 a.m. and passed the starting point of the Brigade march at 9.36 a.m., being the junction of the Lanches-Germeuil [uncertain] and the Domart-Berneuil roads. The Company, following the 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion and preceding the 8th Canadian Field Ambulance, marched with the Brigade via Montrelet to Fieffes, about 10 miles, and billeted overnight in a field in Fieffes, some sappers occupying billets on either side of the field. None of the Company fell out during the march. The full march to the Lavicogne area was not carried out upon verbal orders of the 8th C.I.B. Staff Captain. 3rd Canadian Divisional Operation Orders No. 43 received: Company to proceed from Vicogne area to Senlis preceding the 8th C.I.B. group. | Locations: Domqueur; Lanches-Germeuil [uncertain]; Domart-Berneuil; Montrelet; Fieffes; Lavicogne; Vicogne; Senlis. | Casualties: No. 494241 Spr. Harris H. W. and No. 113171 Spr. Delahey G., sent to Field Ambulance in the early morning, both sick. | Movement: Domqueur via Montrelet to Fieffes, about 10 miles.

- **1916-09-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Senlis, Somme area** — Reveille 2.30 a.m. Company moved off from Fieffes at 4.30 a.m. preceding 8th C.I.B. by route Montrelet, Bonneville, Valheureux, Vert Galand Farm, Farm Du Rosel and Le Val de Maison. Orders received from 3rd Divisional Headquarters en route that busses would meet the Company at Le Val de Maison. The dismounted portion proceeded from there at 9.30 a.m. on motor busses under the O.C. with the four Section Officers and Lieut. Thornely en route to Senlis. A billeting party of 1 N.C.O. was sent forward on cycle to Contay and then on to Senlis to choose billets. Horse transport and cyclists followed via Herissart, Contay and Warloy, arriving at Senlis at 9.40 p.m., Capt. Harrison and Lieut. Robinson with the transport. Seven-mile march for sappers and fifteen miles for transport; no sappers fell out and no accidents to transport. Company billeted in Senlis in a field N.E. of the village, map location E.6.9.3, Sheet 11, Sens, France. | People: Lieut. Thornely; Capt. Harrison; Lieut. Robinson. | Locations: Fieffes; Montrelet; Bonneville; Valheureux; Vert Galand Farm; Farm Du Rosel; Le Val de Maison; Contay; Herissart; Warloy; Senlis, E.6.9.3, Sheet 11, Sens, France. | Movement: Fieffes to Senlis, dismounted portion by motor bus from Le Val de Maison, transport by road via Herissart, Contay and Warloy.

- **1916-09-14 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field (Trench 7.4; Peckham House; J.3; J.3R; H.2; H.3)** — Left Section: work on new positions completed; No. 1 gun fired 12 rounds in retaliation, effectively silencing Boche trench mortars. - **1916-09-15 | 18th Battalion | Front Line** — At 6.20 a.m. the battalion attacked the German front and second lines to a depth of 1,200 yards and held the position gained; both objectives gained.

- **1916-09-15 | 24th Battalion | Munster Alley, France** — Attack by the 4th and 6th Canadian Infantry Brigades commenced 6.20am; at 8.30am the battalion, less B Coy, moved to Munster Alley (Bn HQ with 19th Bn HQ); B Coy carried ammunition for the 4th Brigade all day; at 5.30pm the 22nd and 25th Bns, with the 26th in support, attacked and took Courcelette; the 24th, now under the 5th Brigade, supplied carrying parties for the 5th Brigade all night. | People: — | Companies: B | Casualties: none stated | Movement: Chalk Pits to Munster Alley | Locations: Munster Alley; Courcelette
- **1916-09-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Usna Hill, France** — All available linesmen posted at points along the line to ensure that communication was maintained at all cost, shelling very heavy, and communication maintained throughout. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-09-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | Rubempre** — Issued 19,583 men's and 4,881 horses' rations; fine and sharp. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-09-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Brickfields** — Nos. 2, 3 and 4 Companies were visited at Brickfields, the first German aeroplane since leaving the Ypres area was seen, and about 50 German prisoners were seen coming in. | People: — | Companies: No. 2 Company; No. 3 Company; No. 4 Company. | Casualties: none
- **1916-09-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field** — Left Section: men's dugouts being improved; No. 1 gun fired 24 rounds on enemy wire with good effects. Right Section: Nos.
