- **1916-09-15–1916-09-17 | 3rd Canadian Entrenching Battalion | [blacked out] Road** — The battalion furnished a working party of 600 other ranks for work on [blacked out] Road each day, with casualties of 1 killed and 1 wounded (other ranks) on the 15th, 5 other ranks wounded on the 16th, and 5 other ranks [uncertain] on the 17th. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 killed, 1 wounded (15th); 5 wounded (16th); 5 other ranks [uncertain] (17th)
- **1916-09-15 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — During the attacks made by 4th and 6th Cdn Inf Bdes the company was held in readiness to move forward at a minute's notice; day passed uneventfully until 5.15 p.m., when it was moved forward to the immediate vicinity of Bde Hdqs, arriving 6.20 p.m.; at 7.30 p.m. B Section under Lieut. Bowles moved forward and succeeded in placing two guns in position in the sunken road just in front of Gun Pit Trench at 9.30 p.m.; Lieut. W. A. Duthie was killed and Lieut. H. B. Sinclair and three O.R. wounded by a shell landing near Bde. [uncertain] Hdqs. | People: Lieut. Bowles; Lieut. W. A. Duthie; Lieut. H. B. Sinclair. | Companies: 4th Cdn Inf Bde; 6th Cdn Inf Bde. | Casualties: Lieut. W. A. Duthie killed; Lieut. H. B. Sinclair and 3 O.R. wounded. | Movement: Bailiff Wood–Courcelette front.
- **1916-09-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line Cemetery, France** — At zero (6.20 a.m.) an intense barrage opened and "B" and "D" Companies attacked in two waves, capturing and consolidating about 500 yards of German trench by 11 a.m., with 20 prisoners passed back, approximately 250 of the enemy accounted for and three enemy machine guns captured (two used against the enemy), while the 4th C.M.R. Battalion attacked at 6.30 p.m. from the new trench towards Mouquet Farm with entire success and prisoners captured, though the battalion suffered heavily during the afternoon and night bombardment, "B" and "D" Coys especially losing about one third of their effectives. | People: Lieut. William Willison; Lieuts. Lean and Miller; Capt. T. D. Sneath; Lieut. Armour; Capt. Newell Smith; Capt. Hahn. | Companies: 'B' Coy; 'D' Coy; 'C' Coy; 'A' Coy; 4th C.M.R. Battalion; 28th Canadian Infantry Battalion. | Casualties: **As tabulated in the diary: Officers — 3 killed, 4 wounded, 1 shell shock, total 11; Other ranks — 48 killed, 143 wounded, 4 died of wounds, 19 shell shock, 24 missing, total 268. (Named killed: Lieut. William Willison, Bombing Officer, and Lieuts. Lean and Miller, buried in the rear of the Left Sector.)**

- **1916-09-16 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Usna Hill, France** — Difficulty in maintaining a portion of the line to the 7th Bde, with a party of seven men on a length of 300 yds of overland cable, and enemy shelling very heavy. | People: — | Companies: 7th Bde. | Casualties: none

- **1916-09-16 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Brickfields** — Convoys showed the strain of the long haul, up to 28 miles, and the O.C. had a good look at one of the "land ships" damaged in the previous day's advance. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-09-16 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field (Piccadilly; G.7)** — Left Section: No. 1 gun retaliated to hostile shelling with 10 rounds on Hun supports; No. 3 gun fired 10 rounds on wire, doing a lot of damage; also 3 rounds as a demonstration for General Lipsett, who was very pleased with the effects. Right Section: Y.1 gun fired 9 rounds on enemy wire opposite Piccadilly, effects good; Y.3 gun fired 10 rounds on wire and enemy parapet opposite G.7, cut his wire, damaged the parapet very badly and blew up an O.P. | People: General Lipsett | Companies: Left Section; Right Section | Casualties: none | Movement: none
- **1916-09-16 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — At 12.30 a.m. 'D' Section under Lieut. Campbell was sent up to the line with a party of engineers to build and occupy two strong points; Campbell with two guns located along the south side of the Sunken Road 100 yards north-east of the cross roads at R 29 B 6.2, while Sgt. Hobson with the remaining two guns was placed in advanced positions in front of the front line and arrived just in time to assist in repelling the first of a series of five counter-attacks, in all of which these two guns were heavily engaged and assisted materially in repelling; at 9.30 a.m. Lieut. Welch, with two crews of 'A' Section under Sgt. Chamberland, moved off to report to 22nd Bn. Hdqs. in Courcelette; at midnight runners arrived from Lieuts. Bowles and Campbell — Bowles reported a strong enemy counter-attack at 7 p.m. beaten off by his guns assisted by surplus crew acting as riflemen, the enemy coming to a hand-to-hand encounter [uncertain] with the gun crews, and Campbell reported all well; both gun crews suffered casualties from very active enemy snipers and Lieut. Bowles' sergeant was shot and instantly killed early in the day; rations sent up to the gun crews in the line. | People: Lieut. Campbell; Sgt. Hobson; Lieut. Welch; Sgt. Chamberland; Lieut. Bowles. | Companies: 22nd Bn. | Casualties: Lieut. Bowles' sergeant shot and killed; gun crews suffered casualties from enemy snipers.
- **1916-09-16 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line Cemetery, France** — Dull with occasional rain; the situation was normal except for heavy artillery bombardment by both sides, the day was spent improving the new position and evacuating the wounded and burying the dead, and in the evening the 4th Canadian Infantry Brigade attacked the enemy line north and south of the new line, with some objectives not reached and the 42nd and 60th Battalions (Canadian) losing heavily, while the 5th C.M.R. Battalion was relieved by the 9th Lancashire Fusiliers, the relief commencing at 10.30 p.m. and completing at 6 a.m. on 17th September. | People: — | Companies: 4th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 42nd Battalion; 60th Battalion; 9th Lancashire Fusiliers. | Casualties: none | Movement: Front line–Brickfields, Albert (relieved by 9th Lancashire Fusiliers).

MacDonald went over ground La Boisselle Chalk Pits, Pozières, etc. Received preliminary orders to stand to. 3.00 P.M. marched with brigade to Chalk Pits, in conjunction with orders; "stood to" for orders + took shelter for the night. | People: Capt. - **1916-09-16 to 1916-09-17 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Pozieres, France** — 7 Can. Bde. attack the Zollern Graben at 5 p.m.; under cover of this 9th Bde. had orders to take post with right wing on newly captured Zollern Graben and left on our original front line, and at 6.30 p.m. they were to attack in a westerly direction and take the Zollern Redoubt; 7th Can. Bde. relieved by 9th; both had heavy casualties without gaining their objective. | Casualties: heavy casualties (7th and 9th Bdes., numbers not given). | Movement: —
- **1916-09-16 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Pozieres, France** — During evening 2nd Canadian Division took Courcelette; hostile shelling continued heavy since yesterday's attack; German batteries [uncertain] to front line and within range of our guns; our guns ordered to engage a German 77 cm battery; guns trained on German front line at 6 p.m. with orders to open fire if S.O.S. goes up; 1 O.R. killed, 1 O.R. wounded. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed; 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —

- **1916-09-17 | 24th Battalion | Sugar Refinery / Courcelette, France** — At 5pm the battalion, less B Coy (held in reserve by the 25th Bn), attacked the German front line east of Courcelette along a ~700-yard frontage, right on the Bapaume Road, left joining the 22nd Bn near the Quarries: C Coy reached, held and consolidated its objective; A Coy reached its objective but was bombed out, holding a Lewis gun post in a communication trench; D Coy was stopped in the German wire, many killed before crossing the parapet; the diarist blames an artillery barrage placed ~500 yards behind the German line for warning the enemy. Brigade report (BML 216): 24th Battalion casualties 9 officers, 330 other ranks (estimated); 16 prisoners taken. | People: Capt. Ritchie (O.C., C Coy); Major Alexander | Companies: A, B, C, D | Casualties: 9 officers, 330 other ranks (brigade report estimate); A Coy, C Coy and D Coy losses in the attack | Movement: Sugar Refinery to German front line east of Courcelette | Locations: Sugar Refinery; Courcelette; Bapaume Road; Quarries

- **1916-09-17 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field (N 24 a. 8.6, Sheet 28 S.W.)** — At 12.20 a.m., a coordinated wire-cutting bombardment: Right Section bombarded enemy wire and front line, firing 57 rounds. Left Section: No. 4 gun put out of action by a Rum Jar after firing 14 rounds; Nos. 1, 2 and 3 guns fired 77 rounds, effectively cutting enemy wire for the infantry. Centre Section: No. 6 gun registered on N 24 a. 8.6. Right and Centre Sections: all guns retaliated with 48 rounds, and the Operation Order fired 74 rounds, damaging trenches considerably and cutting wire for the infantry. Right Sector, operation cutting wire: Y.1 gun 32 rounds, Y.2 gun 10, Y.3 gun 10 — 52 rounds. Y.2 gun later fired 10 rounds in retaliation for Rum damage which buried Y.3 gun. Diary total for the day: 327 rounds (the diary's own figures sum to 332). | People: none | Companies: Left Section; Right Section; Centre Section | Casualties: none | Movement: none
- **1916-09-17 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — During the night Lieut. Roy was sent in command of 'C' Section to take up positions in Candy Trench between the Bapaume Road and the brigade boundary, guided to its position by Lieut. Grantham, guns placed to command the Bapaume Road and the area in front of Candy Trench; later Roy moved the guns 100 yards further to the right as the area around the Sugar Factory was heavily shelled; at 5 p.m. word received that 1st Cdn. M. G. Coy would relieve the company that night, and at 6 p.m. officers of 6th Cdn. M. G. Coy arrived to arrange the relief; at 7 p.m. Lieut. [uncertain] was sent with two men as guides to take word of the relief to Lieut. Campbell and to locate Sgt. Hobson, the party delayed by heavy shelling and only finding Campbell's position at midnight; two men arrived at Hdqs. with a message from Sgt. Hobson giving his location; Hobson's two gun crews, almost continuously engaged since reaching their position, broke up over five attacks and were in a precarious position as the enemy tried to creep up and bomb them out, one party being put out of action by a shell; his casualties were five. | People: Lieut. Roy; Lieut. Grantham; Lieut. Campbell; Sgt. Hobson; Lieut. [uncertain]. | Companies: 1st Cdn. M. G. Coy; 6th Cdn. M. G. Coy. | Casualties: 5 casualties among Sgt. Hobson's gun crews.

About noon word came through Bde. H.Q. that he had been killed by a sniper, about 10.00 A.M. Party of 1 NCO + 5 men were detailed [uncertain] which had been brought as far as K. dump by party of 58th Bn. 6.30 P.M. Capt. - **1916-09-25 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field** — Right Section, 6 a.m.: the enemy concentrated all his trench mortars on Y.3 gun and put it out of action after it had fired 3 rounds. Right Section, 5.30 p.m.: in retaliation, No. 1 gun 25 rounds, No. 2 gun 10, No. 3 gun 20 (55 rounds); all rounds effective, enemy quiet [uncertain]. Left Section: No. 1 gun fired 17 rounds on the enemy front line; No. 2 gun fired 12 rounds on the enemy front line and destroyed a machine-gun emplacement and dug-out; No. 3 gun fired 16 rounds on the enemy support line; No. 4 gun fired 16 rounds on enemy supports. The enemy retaliated with trench mortars and rifle grenades but was silenced by our trench mortars. Ammunition carried to gun positions. Right Section: Y.2 gun registered on the enemy support line; crews repairing damaged emplacements, rather loose owing to heavy enemy trench-mortar shelling. | People: none | Companies: Right Section; Left Section | Casualties: none | Movement: none

- **1916-09-25 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bouzincourt, France** — Fine and cool; the enemy again shelled the town, causing casualties among men of the 2nd C.M.R. Winslow and 12 men wounded whilst with these parties, and orders were received stating that the Canadian Corps was co-operating with II Corps in the capture of the ridge running N.W. of Courcelette to the Schwaben Redoubt, with the 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade (ours) at Bouzincourt in corps reserve and ready to move at two hours' notice from zero hour (12.35 p.m. 26/9/16). | People: Lt. A. B. Winslow. | Companies: 2nd C.M.R. Battalion; 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 2nd Canadian Division; 1st Canadian Division. | Casualties: **Wounded: Lt. A. B. - **1916-09-27 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Field (Peckham House; G.2)** — Right Section, 2 a.m.: "strafed" the enemy severely at the request of the O.C. Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers; all guns firing, total 60 rounds; smashed communication and support trenches around Peckham House. At 10 a.m. opened up again and fired 40 rounds, destroying a Hun machine-gun emplacement opposite G.2 Trench and a trench-mortar emplacement; fire very effective. Centre Section: no firing; two new positions being made. Left Section: No. 4 gun emplacement hit by a "Whiz-Bang", temporarily out of action; Nos. 1, 2 and 3 guns fired 29 rounds in retaliation, silencing the enemy. | People: O.C. - **1916-09-27 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bouzincourt / Tara Hill, France** — Colonel A. C. Draper's dinner to the officers of the battalion was a great success, held in the Church Army hut with a menu equal to that of a first-class hotel, and good news was still coming in with objectives gained being held, prisoners passing through the billeting area at Bouzincourt all night (about 450), and the battalion paraded at 2.30 p.m. and proceeded by route march via the Brickfields to Tara Hill, reached at 4.30 p.m., rested there for 3½ hours and then proceeded to relieve the 20th Battalion (Canadian) in reserve, picking up the guides at "K" Dump at 10 p.m. | People: Col. - **1916-09-28 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — At 11.20 a.m. word received from senior officer of 'A' and 'D' Sections that the guns were in a very bad place, having come in for heavy shelling owing to the amount of firing done from that location; during the night a direct hit was made on one gun of 'A' Section, gun and tripod destroyed and two men killed and two wounded; at 4 p.m., permission having been obtained through Bde., remaining guns of 'A' and 'D' Sections were withdrawn from strafing positions and placed in company reserve at Hdqs. in Bailiff Wood; at 5 p.m. two guns of 'D' Section under Lieut. Campbell [uncertain] were [uncertain] up to [uncertain] O.C. 26th Bn. and placed at their disposal; at 10 p.m. word received that 'C' Section's area was being heavily shelled, with no further news during the night; during the night 15 of the company transport [uncertain] were sent up by order of the Staff Captain to be used as pack animals. | People: Lieut. - **1916-09-29 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Courcelette, France** — At 6.30 a.m. word received from O.C. Roy, O.C. 'C' Section — during the night his two guns in reserve in the Sunken Road in R 29 a were buried by shells and put out of action, the crews buried with them, [uncertain] four killed, and his sergeant also killed during the night; total casualties to 12 noon: 7 O.R. killed and 5 O.R. wounded and shell shocked; at 3.30 p.m. orders received for two guns from Sugar Trench to report to 25th Bde. - **1916-09-30 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Chalk Pits / Front Line, France** — Clear and cool; the battalion was still in the Chalk Pits but was to go into the front line tonight and carry out an attack on Regina Trench the following day, and at 4 a.m. "C", "B" and "A" Companies in that order commenced to dribble up to the front line to relieve the 1st C.M.R. Wells + McCord practised gun drill + laying. 4.00 [uncertain] Lieut. Macdonald reported at B.H.Q., where under Capt. Sills [uncertain] a party representing all units of Bde. went forward to look over line held by 4th + 5th Can. Inf. Bdes., on the right + left respectively, from approx. R 22 c 7 b, 23 a 9 5, 24 c 5 8, M 19 b 0.10, M 20 b 0.3. Arrived H.Q. of 4th + 5th Bdes. 7 A.M. Macdonald went to Courcelette Quarry, where were 4th C.T.M. Bty. They reported no guns in action, as tactical situation + nature of ground + fighting did not permit it. This unit was standing by in case of counter attack by enemy, leaving guns + ammunition with them. Viewed ground from support trench running E from Quarry, in company with Mr. Carey, Lieut. T.M. Bty.; Mr. Gale, Lieut. C.E., 5th T.M. Bty., reported similarly to 4th T.M. Bty. He has half battery + 4 guns at disposal of Bn. commanders at Bn. H.Q.'s. 4th + 5th Bde. Robertson with N.C.Os and Sappers from Nos 1 & 3 Sections worked on the tram line at R29 B2.5.15; the O.C. attended the C.R.E. 2nd Canadian Division during the attack at 3:15 p.m. in which the 2nd Division and part of the 3rd Canadian Division captured Regina Trench west of Courcelette and were later driven back to the original line; the company moved into quarters vacated by the 6th F.C.C.E. at W23 central. | People: Lieut. - **1916-10-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bouzincourt, France** — Information received that Lieut. Campbell had been shell shocked the evening of the 1st, and that one of his guns in the Sunken Road at R 24 C 8.8 (East Mirailmont Road) had been put out of action during the night with two of the crew killed and a third missing; gun and spare parts salvaged during the day and the two men buried; on 5th Cdn. Inf. Brigade being relieved in the night by 6th Cdn Inf Brigade, orders received that the company was under the orders of 6th Cdn Inf Brigade until ordered to withdraw; orders received at 11.35 a.m. and all gun crews notified; at 5 p.m. the company, having all been withdrawn as far as Bailiff Wood and the limbers packed, moved off for Brickfields, Albert, reaching there at 7.30 p.m.; orders then received to move into billets at Bouzincourt for the night, made after the men had had a meal; transport did not move; health very good. | People: Lieut. Campbell. | Companies: 5th Cdn. Inf. Brigade; 6th Cdn Inf Brigade. | Casualties: Lieut. Campbell shell shocked; 2 of his gun crew killed, 1 missing. | Movement: Courcelette–Albert (Brickfields)–Bouzincourt.

- **1916-10-03 to 1916-10-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Jumping off Trench R23a.9.1–R23.b.6.3 [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report, night of 3–4 Oct: No 4 Section (1 officer, 7 sappers) with 75 men of the 28th Battalion re-traced part of the trench laid out by an infantry officer and laid tape to connect with work done by the 29th Battalion on the night of 2–3 Oct; sappers helped the infantry party dig the trench as far as Kenora Trench; the trench was not dug from Kenora Trench in an easterly direction as the infantry party quit after going as far as Kenora Trench. | People: — | Companies: No 4 Section; 28th Battalion; 29th Battalion. | Casualties: 1 Sapper (appendix report; the diary text for 3 Oct states all parties returned without casualties).
- **1916-10-03 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | W23 Central (Sh 57D S.E.)** — Lieuts Young and Robinson with No 1 Section left to dig the front line trench for the 4th and 6th Brigades from which to make the attack; Lieut. Young located the position and taped out trenches approximately from M14.C.9.3 westerly to R18.C.6.1 (Le Sars Edition 2), in such close proximity to the enemy line that enemy working parties could be seen at work; #529 Sergt. Emrey, D.J. with Sappers from No 1 Section located and laid similar trenches from approximately M14d 4.0.2.5 easterly to M.15.C.3.0.2.5; Lieut. Robinson met difficulties as infantry guides became lost; all parties returned late in the morning without casualties; Lieut. Dunsmore with No 2 Section and parties from the 49th, 60th, P.P.C.L.I. Battalions and R.C.R. carried on work on dug-outs for 7th and 9th Brigade H.Q.; Lieut. Robertson with No 3 Section worked on the tram-line R.35.a 4.4 to R35a 1.5.7; Lieut. Thornely with a party from No 4 Section continued work on the tram line; Lieut. West with No 4 Section and a party from the 28th Battalion worked on the Jumping off Trench R23a.9.1–R23.b.6.3; Lieut. Young was sent for by 2nd Division H.Q. and left at 5:08 p.m. for 4th Brigade H.Q.; the O.C. attended C.R.E. 3rd Canadian Division and 3rd Div. H.Q.; Lieut. Robertson and a party of No 3 Section discovered the body of #4956 Pte Patfield W.M., R.C.R., and removed his identity disc and personal effects, sent to the Adjutant R.C.R. today. | People: Lieut. Young; Lieut. Robinson; #529 Sergt. Emrey, D.J.; Lieut. Dunsmore; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Thornely; Lieut. West; #4956 Pte Patfield W.M., R.C.R.; O.C. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 4th Brigade; 6th Brigade; 7th Brigade; 9th Brigade; 49th Battalion; 60th Battalion; P.P.C.L.I.; R.C.R.; 28th Battalion. | Casualties: #502421 Spr Finnemore H slightly wounded; diary text states all parties returned without casualties.

Robertson was notified by Brigade that there would be no work done on the right sector, so he accompanied Lieut. West and helped on his work; Lieut. West accompanied by Lieut. Robertson and No 4 Section and a party from the 60th Battalion worked on Jumping off Trenches; the O.C. attended C.R.E. in the morning for a conference over last night's work, and a special report was called for; Lieut. Young was sent to the line with 9th Brigade H.Q. near Pozieres as Liaison Officer; the O.C. attended C.R.E. with Lieuts Robertson and West for a conference re work for tonight, the jumping off trench to be dug from M.14.c 6.3 westerly to East Miraumont Road at R.24.a.6.9 1/2 thence to approximately R29.c Central; the conduct of #541821 Spr Feltham R is noted — while in charge of a party he brought truck load after truck load of material urgently required for the Brigade H.Q. dug-outs through artillery barrages on the Pozieres ridge, got the material to its destination, unloaded it, and got his party, horses and trucks back in safety; the General, 9th I.B., was very much pleased with the work accomplished by Lieuts West and Robertson. | People: Lieut. Dunsmore; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Lieut. Young; #541821 Spr Feltham R; O.C. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 4 Section; 60th Battalion; 9th Brigade. | Casualties: #45142 Sgt. Lewis G. wounded by shell fire; #502936 Spr Hampson, J. and #502860 Spr Muckleston R.W. wounded by shell fire.

- **1916-10-07 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (W23 Central) (Sh 57D S.E.)** — The O.C. attended C.R.E. in the morning for a conference and orders received as to work for tonight; Lieut. Young at 9th Brigade H.Q. conferred with 9th Brigade as to work; the O.C. attended C.R.E. with Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Robinson with three men taped out a trench to connect up with the 3rd Brigade jumping off trench on the right from M13d 6.7.3.0 to M13d 6.0.1.5 (Trench Map Le Sars, 57D S.E.-2, 57D S.W.-1), also a communication trench from the new trench back to the old jumping off trench joining at M13d.6.0.1.5; 1 N.C.O. and two Sappers were sent out to report to Lieut. Fellowes, 8th Field Coy C.E., at the junction of Vancouver Trench and West Miraumont Road, to guide him over part of the area of 9th I.B. and assist him in taking out jumping off trenches in front of the 7th Brigade frontage, just to the left of the 9th Brigade frontage; Lieut. Robertson with 1 N.C.O. and 2 Sappers laid out the Jumping off trench, tape run from M13.d.1.7.3 to M13.d.6.1.5 (Le Sars, 57D S.E. & 57D S.W.); 1 N.C.O. and two Sappers met Lieut. Smith of the 8 F.C.C.E. in place of Lieut. Fellowes, who did not appear, and guided him across the 9th Brigade frontage from R.24a 6.9 1/2 through R23b 9.8 1/2 in a westerly direction; Lieut. Dunsmore with No 2 Section and also Sappers from the other sections and parties from the 60th, 5th and Trench Mortar Battery continued work on the dug-out at R36c Central (Sh 57D S.E.). | People: Lieut. - **1916-10-08 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France, W23 Central (Sh 57D S.E. France)** — The O.C., with Capt Harrison, Lieut. West and a party from No 4 Section, attended the funeral of Sapper Clark, who was buried by Chaplain Capt. Stewart, attached to 9th Field Ambulance, formerly of C.M.R., at Tara Hill Cemetery, south side of the Albert–Pozieres road, map location W24d 1.4 (Trench map [uncertain] 57D S.E. 4. France); the O.C. attended C.R.E. in the evening when it was ascertained certain units had penetrated into elements of the enemy trench when the Canadian Corps attacked at 4:50 this morning, but were later compelled to retire; 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order #13, dated 7 Oct 1916, received 1:35 a.m., whereby this company was to furnish guides to the 4th Canadian Pioneer Battalion, who were to work in Courcelette trench north, and two sections of this company were also ordered to stand by; a copy of telegram 3rd Canadian Division G-772, dated 7-10-16, with detailed instructions explaining Operation Order No 13, was received at 1:30 a.m.; the O.C. attended C.R.E. in the afternoon, when orders were received that execution of Operation Order No 13 was to be held in view of the situation, certain units of the infantry having been held up by wire in the attack upon Regina trench, and later the 1st Division on the right was driven out, owing to [uncertain] enemy trenches being heavily counter attacked, and the line practically back in the old jumping off position; the O.C. again attended C.R.E. in the evening when instructions were received for an officer and party to make a reconnaissance of the right-half frontage of the 9th Brigade front line area, with a view to pushing forward the jumping off trench to within 150 to 200 yards of Regina trench (enemy line); Lieut. West with Sgt. Bate and Spr Sinker left at midnight for this work; Lieut. Dunsmore with Sappers from the different sections and a party from the 60th Battalion worked on H.Q. dug-outs. | People: Capt Harrison; Lieut. West; Chaplain Capt. Stewart; Sapper Clark; Lieut. Dunsmore; Sgt. Bate; Spr Sinker; O.C. | Companies: No 4 Section; 9th Field Ambulance; C.M.R.; 4th Canadian Pioneer Battalion; 9th Brigade; 60th Battalion. | Casualties: none.

- **1916-10-09 to 1916-10-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | New jumping off trench, Vancouver Trench at approx. R.18.C.2.0 to R.23.b.7.8 [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report, night of 9–10 Oct: a new jumping off trench was taped out and dug for 175 yds (except 40 ft east of the West Miraumont Road), extended from Vancouver Trench at approx. R.18.C.2.0 to R.23.b.7.8, 2 1/2 ft–3 ft wide by 3 ft deep; a communication trench was extended from the new Vancouver trench to the intersection of the new extension at R.23.b.9.9, 80 yds long; work was discontinued at 4 a.m. so the garrison working party could get the wounded to the dressing stations; Capt. - **1916-10-10 to 1916-10-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Vancouver Trench / West Miraumont Road [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work reports, night of 10–11 Oct: Lieut. H.P. Robertson's party taped out triangular traverses in the new cut-off at 35 ft intervals, 2 1/2 ft wide and 3 ft deep, and taped and dug the remainder of the cut-off to within 10 yards of West Miraumont Road; the working party 'C' allotted for the work (75 men) was in reality 'B' party and contained only 50 men, causing confusion, and 25 more men were picked up by applying to the O.C. Trench [uncertain]; the new cut-off was taped eastwards and dug with triangular traverses to a point of intersection with [uncertain] trench 150 ft east of the original point; the communication trench was deepened to 4 ft and widened to 3 ft. | People: Lieut. - **1916-10-16 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres, France** — Early part of the day passed quietly; during the afternoon the two guns at the east and west sides of the Slag Pile were relieved by the [uncertain] gun of the left Battalion (26th) and withdrawn to company Hdqs. in Bully; at about 10.30 p.m. a "Rum jar" landed in the entrance of the dugout where the crew of the Morrow Trench guns lived, with no casualties but several rifles and equipment destroyed and gun No. 718 put out of action by a piece of the "Rum jar"; during the day 6 men returned from the [uncertain] at Ault [uncertain]. | People: — | Companies: 26th Bn. | Casualties: none

- **1916-10-16 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Outrebois** — 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade Operation Order No 50 received at 10:30 last night — the company to march to Outrebois, not to pass Candas before 10:30 a.m.; reveille at 4:30, the Coy moved off at 7 a.m., proceeded by way of du Rosel Farm, Candas, Fienvillers and Autheux, arriving at Outrebois at 2:45 p.m.; the company stopped for 10 minutes north of Autheux for lunch; the company was billeted in Outrebois as follows: No 3 Section in a separate billet, 1st Section occupying one billet, the remainder of the company, except the Officers, billeted under tarpaulins; while en route the company was held at Fienvillers to permit two battalions (60th and 52nd) of the 9th C.I.B. marching from Montrelet to pass, and the company then joined in rear of the column. | People: — | Companies: No 1 Section; No 3 Section; 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 60th Battalion; 52nd Battalion. | Movement: La Vicogne to Outrebois via du Rosel Farm, Candas, Fienvillers and Autheux, arriving 2:45 p.m.

- **1916-10-19 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Beaumont Hamel** — 51st Division relieved 39th Division and took over our trench mortars; on the left flank of the Division front were 31st Division trench mortars, on the right 63rd Division. 39th Division trench mortars relieved our X.3.C. Battery. Z.3.C. Battery was brought into action on the left of Y.3.C. Battery and X.3.C. Battery was brought into reserve. - **1916-10-19 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Outrebois** — A message was received from H.Q. 9th I.B. at 2 p.m. to send a billeting officer to H.Q.; the O.C. attended Brigade H.Q. at le Meillard when previous orders re billeting were cancelled and men left at proposed billets at Beauvoir were to be withdrawn; orders were received to be clear of Outrebois at 6 p.m. today, and having given up billeting, the company was in the open on the march to Heuzecourt; the company moved in the afternoon to a field adjoining the transport lines on the south side of the road midway between Outrebois and Occoches; tarpaulins were pitched and the Coy bivouaced for the night; a cyclist was sent to Beauvoir to withdraw three men left there as an advance billeting party; Operation Order No 51 of 9th C.I.B. received 9:40 p.m., whereby the company was to march independently to Bonnières, to cross the Outrebois bridge at 3 p.m. in rear of the 8th C.I.B. and to march via Outrebois, Mezerolles–Remaisnil. | People: O.C. | Companies: 9th I.B.; 9th C.I.B.; 8th C.I.B. | Movement: Outrebois to a field midway between Outrebois and Occoches, bivouacked for the night.

- **1916-10-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bonnières** — Orders were received at 7:30 a.m. for the billeting officer to meet the Brigade billeting officer at Bonnières by 10 a.m.; Lieut Robinson with a party of two cyclists proceeded to this meeting point; the company fell in under the O.C. and marched in column of route to Bonnières, crossing the Outrebois bridge of the Authie River at 3 p.m. and proceeding by way of Mezerolles–Remaisnil without incident or casualties; the company passed by the end of the 8th C.I.B. Field Ambulance column just after crossing the Outrebois bridge; billeting at Bonnières was limited: Nos 1 and 2 Sections billeted at one farm building and No 3 Section in a separate building, the Mounted Section divided between these two buildings, No 4 Section and dismounted H.Q. billeted in a separate building north of the church, transport and horses in the field behind the billet of Nos 1 & 2 Sections; Operation Order No 52 received, whereby the company was to march to Houvin-Houvigneul via Frévent, the company to clear the starting point at the road junction just east of Sibiville–pit, Bouret–Frévent–Houvin-Houvigneul–Magnicourt Roads (Lens 11 Edition 2). | People: Lieut Robinson; O.C. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 8th C.I.B. | Movement: Outrebois to Bonnières via Mezerolles–Remaisnil, crossing the Outrebois bridge over the Authie River at 3 p.m.

- **1916-10-21 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Houvin-Houvigneul** — Upon orders from 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade H.Q., Lieut. H.D. Robertson left at 6:10 a.m. with the Brigade billeting party in an ambulance of the 9th Field Ambulance unit, proceeded to Houvin-Houvigneul and selected billets for the company; the company fell in at 8:30 a.m. and moved off later under the O.C., following the 9th Brigade trench mortar battery and followed in turn by the 58th Canadian Infantry Battalion; the company marched past the starting point on time (10:17 a.m.) and proceeded via Frévent to Houvin-Houvigneul, where the company was met by the billeting officer (Lieut Robertson); the company was billeted as follows: No 1 Section in billets No E.9. & 7 [uncertain], No 2 Section in billets No 15 and 16, Nos 3 & 4 Sections in billet No 6, Drivers in billet No 13, transport and horses in an open field north-west of the village (between billets 34 and 35); information was received from C.R.E. that the O.C. was to proceed to look over the line of the new area (Oct 22); the O.C. attended 9th C.I.B. H.Q.; 9th C.I.B. Operation Order No 53 received at 5 p.m., whereby the Coy was to march with the 9th C.I.B. to Chelers on 22 Oct 1916; 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineer's Operation Orders No 17, dated 20 Oct 1916, received at 3 p.m., whereby the 9th Field Coy C.E. was to march from Bethencourt to Anzin to relieve the 2/3rd London Field Coy R.E., one officer and 3 N.C.Os to proceed to take over the work on the new front on the morning of 22 Oct, the party to be met on the cross roads west of Etrun, further orders to be received. | People: Lieut. H.D. Robertson; O.C. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 9th Brigade trench mortar battery; 58th Canadian Infantry Battalion; 9th C.I.B.; 2/3rd London Field Coy R.E.; 9th Field Ambulance. | Movement: Bonnières to Houvin-Houvigneul via Frévent.

- **1916-10-23 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil** — The company fell in and marched off from Chelers at 7:45 a.m. under the O.C., marched by way of Tinques to Maroeuil, arriving at 1:30 p.m.; the O.C. proceeded to Hermaville and interviewed C.R.E. London Divisional Engineers, when a message to him from C.R.E. 3rd Canadian Division stated that this Coy was to relieve and take over the work of the 2/4 London Field Coy R.E. and not the 2/3 London Field Coy, as stated in Operation Order #17 Canadian Divisional Engineers; Lieut Young was instructed to proceed to the 2/4 Coy advanced billets in the forward area, which he did with a party, and went over the trenches and works with an officer of the 2/4 Coy; the O.C. went over the works and matter of relief with the O.C. 2/4 Coy at Maroeuil, when it was arranged that this Coy take over works from 8 a.m. 24 Oct 1916; the O.C. attended the Divisional Baths and arranged for the Coy to obtain baths; Nos 3 & 4 Sections attended the Divisional bath; Lieuts Robertson and West with a party of N.C.Os of No 3 Section and all of No 4 Section with guides of the 2/4 Coy proceeded to and occupied the advanced billets of the 2/4 Coy in the forward area — the same being shelters and bivouacs at A.14. b.6.8 [uncertain]; the balance of the company was temporarily billeted in the upper floor of a vacant mill building, and horses were picketed in the open; the O.C. proceeded to the advanced billets; No 3 Section was unable to move to the advanced billets on account of a shortage of rations and inability to get rations into the forward area in daylight. | People: Lieut Young; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Shorncliffe and are taken on the strength of the company from today. Orders received from the C.R.E. (5-E-42) for the company to turn out one section with an officer to stop a quarrel in the lines of the 8th F.C.C.E.; the O.C. and Lieut. Murdie attended at the horse lines and the disturbance was quieted without difficulty. Lieut. Robertson with Nos 3 & 4 Sections and infantry parties from the 60th and 52nd Battalions carried on cleaning out trenches and working on dug-outs. Parties from Nos 1 & 2 Sections worked on the Divisional Hut, Gas School and Y.M.C.A. Hut, and in the yard making up revetting screens, lathes [uncertain] and signs for Divisional H.Q. Lieut. Robinson proceeded to advanced billets to live [uncertain]. No 2 Section proceeded to advanced billets to relieve No 4 Section, which returned to rear billets. | People: Lieut. - **1916-11-12 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Fine and cloudy. Upon orders from the C.R.E., No 4 Section proceeded to Ecoivres at 12 noon and had new gas helmets issued and fitted; one-half of the Drivers Section and one-half of H.Q. Section left rear billets at 2 p.m. for the same purpose. Capt. MacNamara, Chaplain of the 49th Battn, 7th C.I.B., held church service in the company recreation room at 4:15 p.m. The C.R.E. attended at Coy rear billets with the Adjutant. The O.C. attended at the C.R.E. with a standard plan of stables for infantry battalions, and attended a conference of O's C Field Companies with the C.R.E. at 4 p.m. Sappers at rear billets made bath mats, revetting screens and bath mat supports for the forward area and worked on G.O.C. furniture, and the usual party worked on the new coal dump. Two men reported from each of the 52nd, 58th, 60th and 43rd Battalions for duty with this Coy (Auth 9th C.I.B. 39/106/d 11-11-16). Lieut. Dunsmore with No 2 Section and parties from the 43rd and 58th Infantry Battalions revetted, laid bath mats, cleared out crumps and built dug-outs. Lieut. Walley with No 1 Section and trench warden parties cleaned out trenches, revetted and repaired. Lieut. Murdie with sappers from No 2 Section and parties from the 10th Field Ambulance and 58th Battalion cleaned track, excavated for a switch, revetted and laid trench mats. The O.C. proceeded to advanced billets to relieve Capt. Harrison, who returned to rear billets. | People: Capt. MacNamara; Lieut. Dunsmore; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie; Capt. - **1916-11-28 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Morning clear and bright later turning hazy so work could be done in the open, usual trench mortar activity included three direct hits on Sutherland Avenue, machine gun and rifle fire was more active than usual, enemy working parties near Craters 19 and 20 were dispersed, snipers claimed a hit at A16.C7.5, a German plane crossed the front at 11.25 am and was driven back, four patrols covered the front, and about 10 pm a small mine explosion was observed away on the left on the 1st Canadian Division front. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-11-28 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Fine, clear and cold. Sappers at rear billets made bath mats, bath mat supports and revetting screens; parties worked on the 9th C.I.B. hut and a bridge for artillery. Lieut. West with No 4 Section and infantry parties cleaned and revetted trenches and worked on a new dug-out. Lieut. Walley with No 3 Section and parties from the 60th and 52nd Battalions drained and revetted trenches, ran levels and worked on the Battn. H.Q. dug-out and Y.M.C.A. Canteen, and built a cook house for the M.G. Coy. Lieut. Murdie with four sappers from No 4 Section and parties from the 9th C.A.M.C., 52nd and 60th Battalions ballasted track, dug for a pipe line and repaired water works. Upon orders from the O.C. 60th Canadian Battalion the company stood to in attack quarters at 5:30 a.m.; the attack quarters for the 9th F.C.C.E. was Fork Redoubt; reveille [uncertain] was at 3:30 a.m. and the sections marched off at 4:50 a.m., occupying their respective places quietly and quickly. The drying hut at Bray was completed. | People: Lieut. West; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 9th C.I.B.; 60th Battalion; 52nd Battalion; M.G. Coy; 9th C.A.M.C. | Locations: Bray; Fork Redoubt. | Movement: Company stood to in attack quarters at Fork Redoubt at 5:30 a.m.

- **1916-11-30 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Dull and cold. Parties from rear billets worked on the Artillery Bridge and 9th C.I.B. hut; the remainder of the sappers worked in the yard making bath mats, bath mat supports and revetting screens for the forward area. Lieuts. West, Walley and Murdie with Nos 3 & 4 Sections and infantry parties carried on the same work in the forward area as shown in yesterday's reports. General Plummer, Canadian Corps Commander, presented medals at 11 a.m. to those of the 3rd Canadian Division who won the same at the Somme; the presentation parade was held at Bray for the 9th C.I.B. and units attached, with the 3rd Canadian Div. General and the 9th C.I.B. General and their staffs present, and officers from the various units having recipients in the parade. The 9th F.C.C.E. had four of the six who won Military Medals at the Somme on parade: #502694 L/Cpl Brown R.R., #502802 A/L/Cpl. Coyle J.T., #541821 Spr Feltham, R., and #541767 Spr Sinker H.; of the other two, Sergt Emery D.J. was on leave and #541919 Corp Fletcher J. is wounded and in hospital. The 43rd C.I. Battalion marched past the medal recipients. The reinforcing bridge at L. 3. b. 7.9 Sh 57c 72, E [uncertain] was completed today and reported to the C.R.E.; the work was necessary as 17 tons per axle transport was to be [sentence ends mid-sentence in the original]. No 2 Section proceeded to advanced billets to relieve No 4 Section, which returned to rear billets. The O.C. and Capt. E. W. Harrison being absent on leave, the diary for the month is signed by Lieut. E. J. Young, the senior officer present. | People: General Plummer; Lieut. West; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie; L/Cpl Brown R.R. #502694; A/L/Cpl. Coyle J.T. #502802; Spr Feltham, R. #541821; Spr Sinker H. #541767; Sergt Emery D.J.; Corp Fletcher J. #541919; Lieut. E. J. Young; Capt. E. W. Harrison. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 9th C.I.B.; 43rd C.I. Battalion. | Locations: Bray; L. 3. b. 7.9 Sh 57c 72. | Casualties: #541919 Corp Fletcher J. wounded and in hospital. | Movement: No 2 Section to advanced billets, relieving No 4 Section.

- **1916-12-03 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cold and misty. Lieut. Walley with No. 3 Section carried on engineering work on the Right Sub-section, improving the front line, trench warden work, and improving and building dugouts. Lieut. West with No. 2 Section worked on the Left Sub-section, revetting and clearing out the front line, maintaining communication trenches in good condition and repairing and building dugouts. Lieut. - **1916-12-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Clear and cool. Sappers at Rear Billets making revetting screens, concertinas, bath mat slats and supports; finished repairing the approach to the bridge on the Ambulance Road over the Scarpe. Lieut. Walley with No. 3 Section worked on the Right Sub-section, cleaning out and revetting the front line, keeping communication trenches in good condition and working on dugouts. Lieut. West with No. 2 Section worked on the Left Sub-section, revetting the front line, doing trench warden work and working on dugouts. Lieut. Jones with sappers worked on the Ambulance Siding, lowering and wrapping the water main and maintaining the Vissec [uncertain] tram line. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. when numerous matters were discussed; instructions received from the C.R.E. to detail an officer from this company to deliver three lectures every third week at the 3rd Divisional Engineering School, Lieut. Robinson detailed. Orders received removing Gas Alert. Lieut. Dunsmore returned to Rear Billets preparatory to leaving for the 1st Army School under instructions from the C.R.E.; Lieut. Young proceeded to Advanced Billets to relieve him. Instructions received from the C.R.E. for a special report and sketch re condition of trenches and accommodation of dugouts, required for tomorrow. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Dunsmore; Lieut. Young. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 3rd Divisional Engineering School; 1st Army School.

- **1916-12-08 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Dull with drizzling rain, machine guns were active on the whole front and snipers claimed 4 hits from Craters 19 and 21, cheering was heard in the enemy lines at about 6 pm and guessed to be news of the capture of Boucharet, the whole front was patrolled with nothing unusual, Pte. Tamblin died today at 30 [uncertain] Clearing Station with burial at Aubigny at 2 pm tomorrow, and a patrol from Sap 32a met a strong enemy patrol working from Crater 33 towards our lines which retired towards Crater 29 under Lewis gun fire. | People: Pte. - **1916-12-09 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — M.G. emplacement near completion; earth put on roof and rear; trench job prepared; dugout excavated to average depth of 7 feet; indirect fire as usual with three guns, very little enemy retaliation; "B" Section paraded for bombing today. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-09 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Dull and overcast with a quiet night, at 2 am our 18-pounders opened a lively strafe left of the left company followed by a short bombing attack, patrols were hampered by moonlight, snipers claimed 2 hits and later 3 hits at A.16.C.7.33, Pte. W. R. Ross (B Coy) received a slight shell wound in the neck at 500 Crater, one of our trench mortars caused a fire and white smoke in the enemy lines north of Lille Road, and three bays of Bonnet Trench were blown in by hostile trench mortars with no casualties. | People: Pte. W. R. Ross. | Companies: B Coy. | Casualties: **Pte W. R. Ross (B Coy) — shell wound in neck (slight)**
- **1916-12-09 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Savy Berlette, France** — Left Toutencourt at 7 am and proceeded to Savy Berlette, reached at 7 pm; men went into billets. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Toutencourt–Savy Berlette
- **1916-12-09 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Enemy trench mortars active on right; open emplacement at No. 4 Gun in right subsection destroyed during afternoon; our guns firing as usual at night; about 4 a.m. a party of 60th Can. Bn. attempted to raid enemy trenches at A10 c 9821; first line of wire blown successfully but second line prevented party from entering trench; they bombed the trench and inflicted casualties; artillery, trench mortars and machine guns put on barrage in rear of objective; 1 O.R. wounded. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1916-12-09 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cold and overcast. Sappers at Rear Billets making engineering material at the mill as usual. Lieut. Walley with No. 1 Section and parties worked on improvement of the front line on the Right Sub-section, dugouts, communication trenches. Lieut. West with No. 2 Section and parties worked on improvement of the front line on the Left Sub-section, cleaning out communication trenches, excavating for the Guillermot trench mortar emplacement. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on the Vistula tram line, on the Claudot Ambulance Spur and lowering and covering the water main. The C.R.E. called at Rear Billets, looked over the yard and shops, and attended with the O.C. and chose a site for practical work of the Instructional School in Wiring; the O.C. and Lieut. Young arranging the syllabus of instruction, and Lieut. Young conferred with the C.R.E. re same. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. McBurney. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Dull and overcast turning to drizzle rain in the afternoon and clearing in the evening, patrols covered the entire front with no hostile patrols encountered, trench mortar and artillery activity increased with Sutherland Avenue and Bonnet Trench crumped for 30 or 40 yards, snipers claimed a hit left of Crater 19, an enemy working party opposite Crater 500 was dispersed at 9.30 pm, and the enemy used 4.5-inch and 5.9-inch guns on this front for the first time since the battalion took over the sector. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-10 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Savy Berlette, France** — Resting and awaiting the guns. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-10 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Front comparatively quiet; slight trench mortar activity on right; about 6 p.m. a party from 58th Can. Bn. raided enemy trenches at A4 d 3300 to A4 d 3525; casualties inflicted but no prisoners taken; we co-operated with artillery and trench mortars in barrage work; owing to suspected relief by enemy we fired heavily on communication trenches and roads behind enemy lines. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-12-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cold and cloudy. Sappers at Rear Billets making engineering material at the mill as usual; parties working at the Divisional Baths at Maroeuil and Frevin-Capelle on improvement works. Lieut. Walley with No. 1 Section and parties worked on revetting and cleaning out the front line, communication trenches. Lieut. West with No. 2 Section and parties worked on improvement of the front line, maintaining communication trenches. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on the trench tram, lowering the water main, hauling material along the tram line. One officer and 20 N.C.O.'s and men from each of the three Brigades of the 3rd Canadian Division, 63 in all, reported to Rear Billets for a Course of Instruction in Wiring pursuant to Divisional Orders, the party being rationed with this company and billeted in Maroeuil under arrangements made by the Town Major; Lieut. Young took the party in hand and commenced the course, comprising lectures and practical work in building different types of wire entanglements, barbed wire concertinas, blocking trenches and destruction of wire by demolitions. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Young. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; 3rd Canadian Division (three Brigades). | Locations: Maroeuil; Frevin-Capelle.

- **1916-12-11 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line / Etrun** — Weather overcast with occasional drizzle, Pte. T. E. Kimball (C Coy) was wounded slightly in the right eye, the night passed quietly, the battalion was relieved by the 1st C.M.R. and moved back to billets at Etrun with the front-line relief completed at 12.25 pm, Sgt. G. McNamara (C Coy) was killed instantly by shrapnel at F.17 while handing over trench stores to Sgt. MacKenzie of the 1st C.M.R. and Ptes. Tanner, Cole and Riley (all C Coy) were wounded by the same shell, and four German aeroplanes crossed the lines with two brought down near Etrun, one pilot setting his machine on fire and throwing a bomb at a mounted policeman, breaking the horse's leg. | People: Pte. T. E. Kimball; Sgt. G. McNamara; Pte. W. J. Tanner; Pte. W. P. Cole; Pte. C. A. Riley; Sgt. MacKenzie. | Companies: C Coy. | Casualties: **Sgt G. McNamara (C Coy) — killed instantly by shrapnel at F.17; Pte T. E. Kimball (C Coy) — wounded right eye (slight); Pte W. J. Tanner (C Coy) — shrapnel wound (not serious); Pte W. P. Cole (C Coy) — shrapnel wound (not serious); Pte C. A. Riley (C Coy) — shrapnel wound (not serious)** | Movement: Front Line–Etrun.

- **1916-12-11 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Enemy put trench mortars and shrapnel on support line in right subsection; left subsection normal; our guns fired as usual at night; C Section relieved D Section in overhead fire positions. | Companies: C Section; D Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1916-12-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cold with intermittent rain. Sappers at Rear Billets making engineering material at the mill as usual; parties working at the Divisional Baths at Maroeuil and Frevin-Capelle on improvements to same. Lieut. Robertson with No. 1 Section and working parties worked on the Right Sub-section, revetting, cleaning out trenches, repairing dugouts. Lieut. West with No. 2 Section and parties worked on the Left Sub-section, improving the front line, Guillermot trench mortar emplacement, clearing out communication trenches. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on the trench tram line, repaired a leak in the water main, improved Bessan trench. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. when authority was obtained from Q Branch for attachment to this company of a party from the 3rd Canadian Entrenching Battalion for work in the yard; the party of 15 from the said Battalion remained with the company from this date. A report on work done on trench tramways in the Thelus Section was furnished to the C.R.E., also a report on burying water pipes in the Forward Area. The sappers at Advanced Billets "stood to" with fighting equipment at Fork Redoubt at 6 a.m., and were inspected by the O.C. 60th Battalion, who seemed to be satisfied. Lieut. Young with the Sanitary Officer inspected the well in Maroeuil and made a report on repairs required. Lieut. Walley attended the Divisional Gas Officer as to his design in gas curtains, and attended and made a report on the proposed water system at 9th I.B. Rear Headquarters. | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Young; Lieut. Walley; O.C. 60th Battalion. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; 3rd Canadian Entrenching Battalion; 60th Battalion; 9th I.B. | Locations: Maroeuil; Frevin-Capelle; Guillermot; Bessan; Fork Redoubt; Thelus. | Movement: Party of 15 from 3rd Canadian Entrenching Battalion attached to the company.

- **1916-12-15 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cloudy and cold. Robertson with No. 1 Section and parties worked on improvement of the front line, communication trenches on the Right Sub-section. Lieut. West with No. 4 Section and parties worked on revetment of the front line, upkeep of communication trenches, T.M. emplacement. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on lowering the water main on Elbe, improving the trench tram line. Lieut. Robertson with No. 1 Section and parties worked on the Right Sub-section, cleaning out and revetting the front line, repairing dugouts. Lieut. West with No. 4 Section and parties worked on the Left Sub-section, improving the front line, Zivy Redoubt T.M. emplacements. Lieut. - **1916-12-18 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — Indirect fire as usual, 4,000 rounds S.A.A. expended on usual targets, no retaliation; work progressing favourably on new indirect-fire position in left sector; 15 trench frames built and placed in position at Siding M.G. emplacement and revetting carried on; reserve sections carried out elementary training during the day. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-18 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Dull but fairly clear, patrols were out in a very dark night to prevent the enemy observing preparatory work in the saps and craters for the forthcoming operations, our artillery was very active cutting wire, the enemy retaliated mostly with trench mortars and whizz-bangs, Sgt. C. Rafuse (attached A Coy) suffered a shell wound fracturing his jaw and right leg seriously at 2.30 pm in the Crater 500 area and Spooner, Pte. C. West with No. 4 Section and parties worked on the Left Sub-section, fitting gas screens to dugouts, revetting Zivy Redoubt, the front line. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on protecting the waterworks system against frost, ballasting the tram line. - **1916-12-19 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Dull with fair visibility, the night passed very quietly with machine guns playing on the cut wire, at 11 am heavy artillery opened a slow bombardment on selected points in the enemy lines, Pte. T. White (machine gun) was wounded in the shoulder, snipers claimed three victims and broke an enemy periscope, Lt. Mathews returned from leave, Pte. A. R. Neil (D Coy, battalion bomber) was killed by high explosive in a dug-out, Cpl. H. R. Dayton and Pte. W. Woodrow (both battalion bombers) were wounded in the shoulder, and Sgt. Rafuse died of wounds at No. 42 Casualty Clearing Station and was buried at Aubigny. | People: Pte. T. White; Lt. Mathews; Pte. A. R. Neil; Cpl. H. R. Dayton; Pte. W. Woodrow; Sgt. C. Rafuse. | Companies: A Coy; B Coy; D Coy. | Casualties: **Pte A. R. Neil (D Coy, Bn Bomber) — killed by H.E. in dug-out; Cpl H. R. Dayton (A Coy, Bn Bomber) — S.W. in shoulder; Pte W. Woodrow (B Coy, Bn Bomber) — S.W. in shoulder (serious); Pte T. White (M/Gun) — G.S.W. shoulder (not serious); Sgt C. Rafuse — died of wounds, No. 42 C.C.S.**

- **1916-12-20 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres sector, France** — Inter-company relief carried out today, completed at 12 noon; indirect fire on usual targets, 4,000 rounds S.A.A. expended, no enemy retaliation; at Siding M.G. emplacement work progressed favourably, floor completed, revetting done on sides of trench; at the dugout the stairs are now down 24 and 22 steps respectively; at 1.40 p.m. an enemy aeroplane flying low over Bully was engaged by one anti-aircraft gun at Hdqrs., the plane disappearing towards the German lines; a German plane was engaged by one of the guns in the left sector at 2.30 p.m., one belt being fired. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-20 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Trenches** — Frost overnight with fine clear weather, enemy aeroplanes were very active, at 1.30 pm our artillery opened a heavy bombardment from Lille Road to just north of the Snout until 2 pm, at 3.12 pm 1st C.M.R. parties advanced from Crater 12 and at Zero 3.15 pm followed a heavy barrage into the enemy front line, occupying it without being delayed by wire and bringing in about 50 unwounded prisoners and several wounded with very little resistance, and heavy enemy retaliation continued until after 6 pm with 1st C.M.R. casualties of 6 killed and 18 other ranks wounded while the 5th C.M.R.'s casualties holding on were all wounded. | People: Lieut K. L. Duggan; Lieut W. F. Bynum; Pte. C. Bennett; Pte. J. P. McPhail; Pte. W. G. Davidson; Pte. R. E. Martin; Pte. T. Barnes; Pte. C. L. Jones. | Companies: — | Casualties: **(5th C.M.R., all wounded) Lieut K. L. Duggan; Lieut W. F. Bynum; Pte C. Bennett; Pte J. P. McPhail; Pte W. G. Davidson; Pte R. E. Martin; Pte T. Barnes; Pte C. L. Jones; (1st C.M.R.) 6 killed, 18 O.R. wounded**
- **1916-12-20 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Mt St Eloy, France** — Broken cam in the breech mechanism of "D" Gun put that gun out of action for the day; a cam was taken from one of the other guns and "D" Gun put back into action. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1916-12-20 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Our artillery active with light retaliation; in afternoon (3.15 p.m.) 1st Cdn. Bn. attacked enemy lines at A22 b 3345 to A16 c 9600; under cover of barrage by artillery, trench mortars and machine guns they succeeded in entering front line and supports and held them for 1½ hours, when upon a given signal they withdrew; 2 officers and 56 O.R. German prisoners; 1st Cdn. Bn. lost 6 O.R. killed and 18 O.R. wounded, all evacuated; three of our guns took part in barrage work; our casualties: 2 [uncertain] killed and 2 O.R. wounded; firing as usual at night. | Casualties: 2 [uncertain] killed; 2 O.R. wounded (9th M.G. Coy); 1st Cdn. Bn.: 6 O.R. killed, 18 O.R. wounded; 58 German prisoners. | Movement: —
- **1916-12-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Clearing and cool. Sappers at Rear Billets working in the yard as usual. Lieut. Robertson with No. 1 Section and parties worked on the Right Sub-section, revetting the front line, placing signs on dugouts, working on gas curtains, excavating the H.Q. dugout, working on a drift at the Engineer Shelters. Lieut. West with No. 4 Section and parties worked on the Left Sub-section, keeping communication trenches in good condition, excavating the Guillermot T.M. emplacement, revetting the front line. Lieut. Jones with sappers and parties worked on ballasting and draining the tram line, repairs to the waterworks system, Brigade Dugout. A successful operation by the 8th Infantry Brigade on the right of the 9th Infantry Brigade took place at 3:15 p.m., with a smoke demonstration on the 9th I.B. and 7th I.B. fronts. One O.R. arrived from the Canadian Base Depot as reinforcement. Experiments were made in various types of barbed wire gates for blocking trenches. | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 4 Section; 8th Infantry Brigade; 9th I.B.; 7th I.B. | Movement: 1 O.R. reinforcement arrived from the Canadian Base Depot.

A party worked on the drying room at the Maroeuil Divisional Baths. Lieut. Robertson with No. 1 Section and parties worked on the Right Sub-section, excavating for a drying room at Douai and Rocade, fitting gas curtains to dugout entrances, revetting and cleaning out trenches. Jones with sappers and parties worked on ballasting the tram line near Glasgow Dump, protecting the water main against frost. Walley with No. 4 Section and parties worked on the Left Sub-section, hanging gas screens, revetting and cleaning out the front line. Lieut. - **1916-12-27 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Clear and cool, cold in the evening. Sappers at Rear Billets worked in the yard as usual, making revetting screens, "A" frames, trench mat slats and supports and barbed wire concertinas. Lieut. Robertson with No. 3 Section and infantry parties worked on the Right Sub-section, pumping out water from the front line, excavating for a drying room, putting up gas curtains and putting up a camouflage screen at Ariane Dump. Lieut. Walley with No. 4 Section and infantry parties worked on the Left Sub-section, revetting 12 yards of the front line, excavating for the Guillermot T.M. emplacement, revetting and cleaning out Zivy Redoubt. Lieut. Robinson with sappers and infantry parties worked on lowering 100 yards of the water main and cleaning out caves-in on the trench tram line. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and conferred re confidential matters comprising dugout accommodation in the Forward Area, including part of the 7th C.I.B. Area, also water supply and Engineer Forward Dumps; the O.C. also conferred with the 7th Field Company at their Advanced Billets and with the Brigadier, 7th I.B., at Advanced Headquarters. | People: Lieut. - **1916-12-30 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line** — Weather wet with wind south-west, situation quiet, continuous rain rendered the trenches almost uninhabitable with dug-outs caving in and trenches filling with mud and water, the new men showed up well, enemy parties were seen leaving the front in full equipment for their supports, snipers claimed 11 hits, and the enemy front was patrolled at night with no enemy patrols found. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1916-12-30 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Clearing and cool, very heavy rain early in the morning; trenches badly flooded. Sappers at Rear Billets working in the yard and mill as usual. Captain Young reported to the 8th F.C.C.E. for duty. Lieut. Robertson with No. 3 Section and infantry parties worked on the Right Sub-section, clearing trench and pumping water from the front line, fixing gas curtains and repairing pumps at Glasgow Dump. Lieut. Walley with No. 2 Section and infantry parties worked on the Left Sub-section, repairing dugouts, building a new cook house on Vistula and excavating a dugout at the Engineer Shelters. Lieut. Robinson with sappers and infantry parties worked on clearing the tram line on Bessan, Vistula and Elbe branches. A party was engaged in repairing the banks of the Scarpe River, where flood water was breaking through into low land. The O.C. and a party of sappers were engaged in confidential reports on dugouts, waterworks and tram lines for the Brigadier-General, 9th I.B. | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. - **1916-12-31 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cloudy and cool. Sappers at Rear Billets working in the yard and mill as usual. Lieut. Walley with No. 2 Section worked on the Left Sub-section, pumping out water from the front line and repairing dugouts. No. 3 Section with infantry working parties worked on the Right Sub-section, revetting and cleaning out the front line and fixing gas screens. Lieut. Robinson with sappers and infantry parties worked on clearing the trench tram line and improving the waterworks system. The O.C. and party, engaged yesterday on a confidential report on dugouts, water supply, tram lines, ammunition dumps and engineer dumps, were compiling plans in connection with same; the O.C. late last evening attended Advanced Brigade Headquarters, 9th C.I.B., and handed in the completed report. Lieut. Robertson and a party of 3 N.C.O.'s and 2 sappers proceeded to Frevin-Capelle to take a gas course; one N.C.O. proceeded to Pernes to take a course at the Canadian Corps School. The Chaplain of the 58th I.B. held church services in the company's Recreation Room. A party was engaged in opening head gates and cleaning out the race and penstocks at the mill to improve the Electric Light system. Recent company promotions and appointments to complete establishment were confirmed in Daily Base Orders, Part II No. 48, 26.12.16. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. - **1917-01-01 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Dull and cloudy. - **1917-01-02 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Fine and clear [uncertain]. Special reports drawn up on the progress of work and on the condition of the trenches. Lieut. Walley with No 2 Section and parties from the 43rd and 58th Battalions pumping water out of trenches and clearing out slides, preparing timbers for the drying room and working on Engineers Shelters. - **1917-01-17 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Ecoivres** — La Folie Section fired 40 rounds on enemy wire entanglements and front line, a small lane cut in wire and much damage to enemy front line; Thelus Section fired 25 rounds on enemy T.M. emplacements, no direct hits but considerable damage to enemy communication trenches; Ecurie Section, Z3C fired 15 rounds retaliation. | People: H.R., J.W. | Companies: Z3C | Casualties: none | Movement: none
- **1917-01-17 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Angres–Bully area, France** — All guns and crews again in position at 7 am to assist in the 4th Bde. operation; fire opened 7.45 am and maintained until 8.45 am, 90,500 rds expended on the same targets as the previous day; no casualties in the company or attached sections; attached sections of the 1st M.M.G. Bde. returned to their unit during the night. | People: — | Companies: 4th Bde.; 1st M.M.G. Bde. | Casualties: none

- **1917-01-17 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Maroeuil, France** — Cold and cloudy with snow. A telephone message received from the C.R.E. at 5 p.m. the previous evening, for this company to be prepared to evacuate Maroeuil today, was cancelled later. Sappers at Rear Billets continued the usual work making "A" frames, revetting screens and wire concertinas. Lieut. Jones with 6 sappers and parties from the 9th C.I.B. Reserve Battalion and the 9th Field Ambulance erecting bunks in huts at Maroeuil, Ecoivres and Haute-Avesnes. Lieut. Walley with No 1 Section and parties from the 52nd and 58th Battalions clearing and revetting trenches, building and revetting fire steps and putting in gas screens. Lieut. Robinson with No 1 Section and parties from the 52nd and 60th Battalions revetting trenches, repairing and relaying bath mats, placing gas screens and working on the Aid Post and H.T.M. emplacement. One sergeant with 6 sappers and parties from the 52nd Battalion and a Brigade party cleaning and repairing the tramline, clearing rations and unloading engineering material. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No. 18 received, whereby the villages of Anzin, Maroeuil, Louez, St. Aubin, Etrun and Bray are to be clear of troops of the 3rd Canadian Division by noon on 18 January 1917; the 9th Field Company is to move to Ecoivres. | People: Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Robinson. | Companies: No 1 Section; 9th C.I.B.; 9th Field Ambulance; 52nd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 60th Battalion. | Locations: Maroeuil; Ecoivres; Haute-Avesnes; Anzin; Louez; St. Aubin; Etrun; Bray. | Movement: Company ordered to move to Ecoivres on 18 January under Operation Order No. 18.

- **1917-01-18 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ecoivres, France** — Cold with rain. The 9th F.C.E., excepting No 1 and No 4 Sections at Advanced Billets, moved off from Maroeuil at 11.30 a.m. in accordance with Operation Order No. 18 and marched to Ecoivres via Bray, arriving at Ecoivres at 1 p.m. without incident. Headquarters and Transport lines located at F.13.a.2.3; Sappers and Mounted Headquarters at F.13.a.7.1 (Sheet 51C, 1/10000). A party of 1 N.C.O. and 9 other ranks was left as guard on material left at Maroeuil. Lieut. C.S. Walley with No 1 Section and parties from the 58th and 43rd Battalions cleaning and revetting trenches, working on the drying room, revetting the fire step and placing gas screens. Lieut. Robinson with No 1 Section and parties from the 52nd, 43rd and 58th Battalions revetting and cleaning trenches, working on the T.M. emplacement and placing gas screens. One sergeant and 3 sappers with parties from the 58th Battalion and a Brigade party (9th C.I.B.) clearing and repairing the light railway, clearing rations, unloading engineering material and collecting trucks from the railhead. Lieut. West proceeded to Advanced Billets to live. | People: Lieut. C.S. Walley; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. West; #500583 A/L/Cpl Stanton A.V. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 4 Section; 58th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 52nd Battalion; 9th C.I.B. | Locations: Maroeuil; Bray; Ecoivres; F.13.a.2.3; F.13.a.7.1. | Casualties: #500583 A/L/Cpl Stanton A.V. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | Movement: Company marched Maroeuil to Ecoivres via Bray, 11.30 a.m. to 1 p.m.; Lieut. - **1917-02-09 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | In the Line** — Situation normal; it became known that No. 110320 Sgt. Lewis A., attached 8th Can. Inf. Bde. Trench Mortar Battery, was killed by the premature explosion of a Stokes bomb on 7th inst., and three of our men — 832137 Pte. Horton A.G., 832263 Pte. Lotes S.N. and 909685 Pte. Marconi R., all B Coy — were wounded by a rifle grenade on the 7th inst. at the junction of Bonnel and Green, while a warned enemy raid never materialised and Major Rhoades, Acting O.C., arranged a 100- to 150-round artillery shoot on the enemy front and support lines near the Snout that caused considerable damage. | People: Major Rhoades; Sgt. - **1917-02-10 | 185th Battalion | Witley** — The 85th Battalion, the only other existing unit of the Nova Scotia Highland Brigade, left at a very early hour this morning for France; a close relationship had ever existed between the two battalions, the 85th having assisted in the 185th's organization, furnished many officers and N.C.O.s, and been in camp with them for about five months; their band, which had gained a good reputation, went with them. This evening a Scotch concert was held in the Men's Mess Room, with songs in the Gaelic tongue enjoyed and understood by no small portion of the audience; the 185th departed from Canada with more Gaelic-speaking men than any other unit of the Canadian Expeditionary Forces. | Companies: 85th Battalion.

- **1917-02-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Elbe Trench, France** — Trench mortars of both sides active; our artillery also active in afternoon; one man per crew, with guns and equipment, of 4th C.M.G. - **1917-02-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ecoivres, France** — Fine and clear. The company engaged in cleaning and packing wagons and overhauling kits and equipment. The O.C. went into detail of the works in the Thelus Section with the O.C. 4th F.C. C.E. and handed over additional maps at rear billets; also rear billets and fittings as of midnight 12th and 13th February 1917. The Defence Scheme, 9th C.I.B., Thelus Section, was also handed over to the O.C. 4th Field Coy C.E. The O.C. attended the C.R.E., 3rd Division. Formal instructions received from the C.R.E. that #503 Sgt C.A.H. Carson had been granted a commission and was temporarily posted to this company, to take effect from 11 February 1917. | People: Sgt C.A.H. Carson. | Companies: 4th F.C. C.E.; 9th C.I.B.; 3rd Division. | Locations: Thelus Section. | Casualties: #502776 A/L/Cpl Pemberton, A.W. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | Movement: Handover of the Thelus Section works, maps, rear billets and fittings, and the 9th C.I.B. - **1917-03-01 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | La Folie Section, France** — The 4th Canadian Division launched the largest raid yet undertaken by the Canadian Corps on the Western Front, using gas — the first occasion on which Canadian troops had experience of it; the company employed 10 machine guns with the artillery, laying down an effective barrage on the enemy's main communication trenches and expending some 50,000 rounds, with no casualties; gas was discharged at 3 am, machine-gun and artillery fire followed for 40 minutes, and the infantry assaulted about 2 hours 40 minutes after zero hour, conditions normal by about 7.30 am; usual indirect fire that night, 7,500 rds on Petit Vimy and Thelus, and the anti-aircraft gun fired 250 rounds at five German aeroplanes. | People: — | Companies: 4th Canadian Division. | Casualties: none

Drivers Section wagon drill and riding exercise. 3rd Canadian Divisional Operation Order No 21 Copy #4 received today, reciting Canadian Corps Orders that the 2nd Canadian Division would be relieved by the 3rd Canadian Division on the front from De la Fauche (exclusive) (A.4.a.5.6) to La Salle (inclusive) [uncertain], together with the rear Area "A" Division; further, the 9th C.I.B. would relieve the 5th C.I.B. on the front above mentioned, relief to be complete by 12 March 1917; and further directing that one Field Company, 3rd Canadian Division, would relieve the Field Company of the 2nd Canadian Division working on the front to be taken over, details to be arranged between the C.R.Es of the two divisions, the Field Company to be under orders of the 3rd Canadian Division for work and under the tactical orders of the 2nd Canadian Division. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; Drivers Section; 2nd Canadian Division; 3rd Canadian Division; 9th C.I.B.; 5th C.I.B. | Locations: De la Fauche; La Salle [uncertain]. | Movement: Relief of the 2nd Canadian Division by the 3rd Canadian Division to be complete by 12 March 1917.

- **1917-03-08 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Auchel, France** — Cold with snow flurries. Company cleaning wagons etc. in the forenoon; no work in the afternoon. Officers and N.C.O.s of all the sections rode over to the training trenches near Bruay and went over and studied the system of enemy trenches as laid out. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. at Bruay and received Operation Order No 22 Copy No. 3, wherein the 9th Field Company C.E. is indicated as the Field Company to relieve the 5th Field Company C.E. Two officers and six N.C.O.s of the 9th F.C.C.E. to proceed to the advanced billets of the 5th F.C.C.E. on the 10th inst. and make themselves familiar with the work in hand. 9th F.C.C.E. to establish advanced billets for 3 sections near Fort George X.29.b. Sheet 36 B. on the 11th inst. This company to assume responsibility for the work from 6 p.m. the 12th inst. | Companies: 5th Field Company C.E.; 5th F.C.C.E. | Locations: Bruay; Fort George X.29.b. Sheet 36 B. | Movement: Two officers and six N.C.O.s to 5th F.C.C.E. advanced billets on 10 March; advanced billets for 3 sections near Fort George on 11 March; responsibility for the work from 6 p.m. 12 March.

- **1917-03-08 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — 114 patients admitted and 111 discharged; the Rt. Hon. Sir Robert Borden, P.C., G.C.M.G., K.C., M.P., Prime Minister of Canada, accompanied by the Hon. Robert Rogers, Minister of Public Works, and the Hon. J. D. Hazen, Minister of Marine and Fisheries and Naval Service, visited the hospital and expressed themselves in terms of highest praise of its organisation and work; in the past eight days four cases had a tentative diagnosis of infectious disease — two cases of measles (German?) and one of scarlet fever, transferred to No. 14 Stationary Hospital, and a fourth, cerebro-spinal meningitis, sent to the same hospital after the prescribed regulations were carried out. | People: Sir Robert Borden, Hon. - **1917-03-09 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Cold and dull. Company fell in at 7 a.m. and marched to Villers-au-Bois via Camblain-Chatelain, Divion, Houdain, Ranchicourt and Estree-Cauchie, arriving at Villers-au-Bois at 3.15 p.m. No men fell out during the march. At Houdain the company overtook the 1st Inf Bde, which was marching in a southerly direction and which was being inspected by Sir R.L. Borden at Ranchicourt. Company went into billets at Villers-au-Bois in an old stone building; transport in the open. | People: Sir R.L. - **1917-03-13 | 18th Battalion | Front Line** — At 4.15 a.m. the enemy attempted a raid on our outpost on the right flank of the frontage due north of the Vises group of craters, red and green flares from the German front line appearing to be the signal for the heavy bombardment which followed; our outpost of one bomber and 2 Lewis gunners [uncertain] were withdrawing when the raiders approached in two parties, about 30 men in all; two bombers, Pte R. Wackett and W. H. Webster, covering the withdrawal of outpost No 16, opened fire on the Huns and R. Wackett claims three; one Hun crept up to one of the bombers and said in English "Come with me", but Pte Webster broke away and continued to throw bombs with good effect; one Hun was afterwards found by Lieut Tuck, who secured identification; our casualties were 3 killed and 14 wounded by enemy shell fire. | People: Pte R. Wackett; Pte W. H. Webster; Lieut Tuck. | Locations: Vises group of craters.

Coy. on Paynesley Trench and No. 11 position moved to A.3.d.2.5½, the new Section H.Q. there complete; the 50-man brigade working party returned and 32 other ranks, eight from each battalion in the brigade, were attached as carriers; the division now holds the Thelus Section, this brigade the left half from Stafford Street to De la Fourche. | People: Maj.
