- **1917-03-22 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Cloudy and cold with snow flurries. Lieut. G.A.H. Carson is transferred to the 7th Field Company and struck off the strength of this unit as from today (Auth C.R.E. letter 5.E.29 dated 21-3-17). Lieut. Robinson proceeded on leave to England today. Sappers at rear billets loading material for the forward area and erecting [uncertain] stores and making tables etc. for 3rd Canadian Division Hqrs. Lieut. Robertson with No 3 Section and parties from the 8th Canadian Field Ambulance working on the dressing station and aid post (Report #30). Lieut. West with No 4 Section and parties from the 58th Battalion and 8th Field Ambulance cleaning, deepening and revetting trenches and working on the dressing station (Report #31). Lieut. Walley with No 2 Section revetting M.T.M. emplacements (#32). Lieut. Murdie with two sappers and parties from the 58th Battalion cleaning trenches (#33). The O.C. attended the Brigade Major, 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade, at Neuville-St-Vaast with the O.C. 8th Field Company C.E., and made arrangements for working parties to carry on work on T.M. emplacements, Goodman Subway. The O.C. also attended Hqrs. 9th Infantry Brigade. 17 N.C.O.s and men of No 2 Section moved forward to live in the dugout, Birmingham Dump, while working on T.M. emplacements. A party of 8 N.C.O.s and men from Nos 3 & 4 Sections also moved in to live in the old gun pit in rear of Fort George. The 7th Field Company C.E. moved up to advanced billets at Fort George and work was handed over to the 7th Field Company C.E. from 6 p.m. 22-3-17. Maps etc. of the Left Subsection handed over to Lieut. Peatt, 7th Field Company C.E. Work in the Right Subsection handed over to the 8th Field Company C.E. from 6 p.m. 22-3-17, with the exception of Aid Post "D", the Right Battalion Aid Post, work on which was handed over at 12 midnight 22–23 Mar. The O.C. with officers at advanced billets and the balance of the company moved to rear billets, Villers-au-Bois. Under C.R.E. Operation Order No 24 the 9th Field Company C.E. is to supervise work on trenches in the area west of the Bethune-Arras Road and to continue work on trench mortar emplacements under construction and fitting up subways with track, and a signal system to be commenced. | People: Lieut. - **1917-04-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Dull and cold with rain, S.W. wind. The O.C. attended advanced 9th C.I. Bde. Hqrs. and arranged for parties for work in the tunnels. The O.C. and most of the company officers and a number of the N.C.O.s and men attended a demonstration by the 172nd Tunnelling Company R.E. of a pipe-boring machine used for laying a continuous charge of explosives for the purpose of blowing a communication trench; a 6-inch pipe was laid through the ground at a depth of 10 ft below the surface, filled with ammonal and detonated, and a straight trench from seven to fifteen feet deep resulted. Operation Order No 78 of the 9th C.I. Bde. received with reference to the relief of the said brigade in the line by the 7th and 8th Canadian Infantry Brigades on W/X night. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No 26 received, relating to the operation to take place on Z day, giving details of preparatory moves to be carried out on W, X, Y and Z days, with complete assembly of the 7th and 8th C.I. Bdes. on Y/Z night. The C.R.E. instructed Capt. Ross to interview Lieut. Stitt, officer in charge of the Corps water supply system, with reference to work on the installation of a water supply in the forward area to be undertaken by this company; Capt. Ross attended as arranged but Lieut. Stitt did not appear. Lieut. Muroie [uncertain] with sappers and parties from the 42nd and 58th Battalions worked on Coffe Stall and cleaning trenches (Report #4). Lieut. Robertson with 9 sappers and parties from the 60th Battalion completed the dump on Dowcett Drive, bunking tunnel dugouts and repairing track in Goodman Tunnel. Lieut. West with 8 sappers and parties from the 60th Battalion worked in Orange Tunnel, fixing entrances, completing latrines, making frames for gas curtains; cleared 30 ft of tunnel. Sappers at rear billets made bath mats; 103 signs completed; making stencils. 3rd Canadian Division [uncertain] received advising that the 116th Battalion will march on Friday, 6 April 1917, the C.R.E. to arrange with the O.C. 116th Battalion details of consolidation work [uncertain]. | People: Capt. Ross; Lieut. Stitt; Lieut. Muroie [uncertain]; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West. | Companies: 172nd Tunnelling Company R.E.; 9th C.I. - **1917-04-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Fine and clear in the forenoon, cloudy in the afternoon. The O.C. attended 9th C.I. Bde. Advanced Hqrs. and arranged re continuing of working parties; the O.C. also attended a conference with the C.R.E. re preparation for consolidation etc. C.R.E. 18/162-2 received from the C.R.E. amending G.251 Canadian Corps and 3rd Canadian Division G.613, altering the time referred to therein to 3 a.m. instead of 2 a.m. Copy of Operation Order No 82 dated 5-4-17 received, setting out the operation of the Canadian Corps in detail for the capture of Vimy Ridge in so far as it affects the 3rd Canadian Division, and also showing the alignment of troops engaged. The O.C. with Lieut. Walley and a number of N.C.O.s and sappers attended the funeral of #502864 A/L/Cpl. G. Sherriff, who was killed in action yesterday; he was buried in Villers-au-Bois Cemetery, Plot 6 Row H Grave 49, map location W17.c.5.7 (Sheet 36 [uncertain] France); the brother of the deceased, who is in the 43rd Canadian Infantry Battalion, attended. Preliminary bombardment by our guns continuing. 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade B.M.S. 1266 dated 6-4-17 received re bombardment by gas projectors in 4-inch Stokes Mortars, which operation was to take place on 7 April 1917 if the wind is favourable; same to be carried out by D & E Companies R.E. Secret information received from the C.R.E. that "Z" day is postponed 24 hours. Lieut. Muroie [uncertain] with 11 sappers and parties from the 58th Battalion cleaned out trenches, viz Chassery, Pont St. and Ecoivres (Report #6). Lieut. Robertson with sappers and an infantry party worked in Goodman Tunnel; Lieut. West with sappers and an infantry party worked in Orange Tunnel. Sappers at rear billets worked in the company yard making bathmats, signs, etc. | People: Lieut. Walley; A/L/Cpl. G. Sherriff #502864; Lieut. Muroie [uncertain]; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West. | Companies: 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 43rd Canadian Infantry Battalion; D & E Companies R.E.; 58th Battalion. | Locations: Villers-au-Bois Cemetery (Plot 6 Row H Grave 49); Chassery; Pont St.; Ecoivres; Goodman Tunnel; Orange Tunnel. | Casualties: #502864 A/L/Cpl. G. Sherriff buried, Villers-au-Bois Cemetery, Plot 6 Row H Grave 49. | Movement: "Z" day postponed 24 hours.

- **1917-04-09 | 18th Battalion | Black Objective** — At zero hour, 5.30 a.m., the battalion left the "jumping-off" trenches and attacked the German front line, capturing the first line and support line with very little opposition and reaching the Battalion Objective (Black), a line of trench from A.11.a.79.36. to A.11.a.45.75., by 6.05 a.m.; Major C. C. Gwyn was killed by a machine-gun bullet about 100 yards from the objective and Lieut. W. J. McLean was killed while leading his men across No-man's-land; after Major Gwyn's death Lieut. P. Jerdan assumed command of "B" Company and Sergt. E. W. Sifton of "C" Company single-handedly attacked a machine gun, bayoneting every man of the crew, but was shot by a dying German; approximate casualties for the whole operation were 2 officers killed, Lieuts. - **1917-04-09 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Neuville St. Vaast, France** — Under cover of an intense artillery and machine-gun barrage, the Canadian Corps, assisted by the 5th British Division, attacked and took Vimy Ridge, zero hour 5.30 am; company casualties 1 other rank killed and 6 wounded; one tripod of "B" Section put out of action shortly after zero hour but replaced from the Divisional M.G. Repair Centre; by 9.30 am all objectives of the 1st and 5th Brigades had been taken; at 10.30 am "A" Section received orders to move forward and occupy strongpoints Y and Z; at 12.45 pm "C" Section reported all guns in position covering Bonval Ravine; at 1.10 pm orders received for "F" Battery to withdraw; at 3 pm "A" Section reported strongpoints Y and Z reached at 1.20 pm and occupied by a subsection in each, and under Lieut. Creighton's guidance immediately started work to help the engineers complete the strongpoints; Major Watson visited all of "A" & "C" Sections' guns between 12 noon and 3 pm; Lieut. Grantham reconnoitred the forward area 4–8 pm; Capt. J. E. McCorkell reported back at 7.20 pm; "F.S." Battery under Lieut. A. C. Bowles fired 50,000 rounds during the day and was withdrawn in the evening to dugouts for a night's rest. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Lieut. Creighton; Lieut. Grantham; Capt. J. E. McCorkell; Lieut. - **1917-04-09 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Mount St. Eloy, France** — The attack on Vimy began; battery opened fire at 5.30 a.m., engaging S22b 05.60 with Left Section and S22b 45.25; after first round No. 4 gun went out of action owing to lack of pressure in recuperator, and No. 3 gun also went out temporarily for same reason; at plus 17 battery switched to S23a 25.80 (Left) and S16d 70.25 (Right); No. 3 gun soon in action again; at plus 75 switched to S17c 70.70 (Left) and 18a 1.2 (Right); trails digging in quickly; at 3 hrs 19 min guns ordered to switch to A6c 4.4–A2a 3.9; at 301 & plus 416 [uncertain] guns engaged B1d 4½ to 2.4 until about 12.15 p.m., when ordered to engage [uncertain] Trench; all guns now in action; about 2.30 p.m. switched to Banff Trench at S16d 00.20 until 8.50 p.m.; during this last action 2 guns always in action, sometimes four; washers in the recuperators found too thin, causing a leak in the valve; prisoners in batches of 50 and 100 began coming in past the battery at 9.30 a.m.; battle appears almost a complete success, only on the right the 4th Division held up by Hill 145. | Companies: 4th Division. | Locations: Vimy; Banff Trench; Hill 145. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-04-09 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France (Vimy Ridge attack)** — Cold with rain in the forenoon, clearing in the afternoon, high wind from the south-west. Slow continued bombardment all last night by our guns of enemy trenches and rear defences. At 5:30 a.m. heavy rolling barrage fire commenced by our guns on enemy lines; the bombardment could be seen reaching from Souchez on the north to south of Arras. Our infantry attacked within three minutes of the commencement of the artillery barrage. A contact aeroplane of the 3rd Canadian Division was brought down soon after zero hour, apparently from our own shell. Enemy retaliation to our barrage on the rear area appeared to be slight; a few shells hit near F 10 central along Road La Targette, Mont St. Eloy. Upon orders from the Adjutant, 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers, the O.C. proceeded to the C.R.E. advanced office at 6:15 a.m. Enemy shelling of our rear area in the neighbourhood of our guns increased considerably at 6:45 a.m. Special 4-inch Stokes shells projected by "D" Special Company R.E. gave a great shower of flame and sparks over the enemy line. At 7 a.m. the attack was proceeding satisfactorily and the 3rd Canadian Division had gained its intermediate objectives; casualties very light. At 7:40 a.m. word was received that most of the 3rd [uncertain] Division objectives had been captured, within two minutes of schedule time. At 8 a.m. our artillery observers were observing from Ecole Commune, S 23 c. 05.10, and an observer moving forward to Spandau House, S 29 c. 25.72 (Vimy Map). At 8:10 a.m. a report of the enemy massing for a counter-attack in the neighbourhood of Phillip trench, west of Petit Vimy, S 23 d (Vimy Map); our artillery, which had lessened its fire, opened up and dispersed the enemy formations. The Royal Canadian Regiment reported today to have repelled three local counter-attacks in the neighbourhood of La Folie Wood, S 23 c (Vimy Map). The 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade (42nd Infantry Battalion) reported that the right of the 4th Canadian Division (11th Brigade) appeared to be meeting considerable enemy opposition and had not gained all of Hill 145; consequently the 42nd Battalion's left flank was open and it was compelled to swing back part of a company facing north to protect its left flank, from Blunt trench, S 22 a 95.10, south-westerly to Staubwasser Weg, S 22 a 55.70, which trench was dug only about 4 ft deep; the 42nd Battalion in this trench and the R.C.R. in Swischen Stellung were exposed to enfilade rifle and machine-gun fire and suffered a considerable number of casualties. Later the 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade again reported the 4th Division held up on Hill 145. The enemy shelled fairly heavily Neuville St Vaast, with intermittent shells back on the La Targette–Mont St Eloy road due south of Fort George (Advanced 3rd Canadian Divisional Hqrs). At 8:30 a.m. an enemy fighting aeroplane appeared over our lines north-east of Neuville St. Vaast, and our contact aeroplanes, after engagement by enemy machine-gun fire, were compelled to withdraw farther into our lines. Two of our tanks could be observed mired in front of Thelus. By 9 a.m. our 18 pdr field guns, which had moved forward from the neighbourhood of Neuville St Vaast, had opened fire on the enemy; enemy prisoners commenced coming back under escort, and a larger number of our aeroplanes appeared over our lines about this time. Reserve troops, presumably of the 2nd Canadian Division or 13th British Brigade, could be seen in front of "Elke" trench in close formation in line by platoons, preparatory to proceeding forward. At 10 a.m. approximately 250 German prisoners marched back under escort just south of La Targette Road. Orders now given by the General Staff, 3rd Canadian Division, for the 3rd Canadian Pioneer and 116th Canadian Infantry Battalions' working parties to move forward from 'Dumbell' Camp, Bois du Alleux, and assemble west of the Bethune-Arras Road, S 29 a 2.2, just south of Pont St. to near La Targette; this they did, the 9th Field Company C.E. officers and sappers acting as guides for the 116th Battalion, arriving about noon; the remainder of the 60th Canadian Infantry Battalion moved forward as reserve from this assembly area. Major Dunbar [uncertain], Adjutant 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers, is acting C.R.E. by reason of Col. Anderson having been wounded yesterday. Orders received from the C.R.E. for working parties who were to work in the old 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade area to proceed to work; working parties in the 7th Brigade area not to go out, as the situation on the left is still obscured. Lieut. Robinson with 5 sappers and 50 infantry from the 116th Battalion proceeded forward at 2:50 p.m. and extended the "Y" route to the craters past our support and front lines, the ground being very much torn up from shell fire. Lieut. Walley with his party of sappers and an infantry party, 116th Battalion, proceeded to work at 2:45 p.m. and dug a communication trench from Vernon [uncertain], approximately S 28 a. 4.3., along the old German front line to Artillerie Weg, S 28 b. 01.35 (La Folie [uncertain]) (Report #8). Lieut. Muroie [uncertain] and party left at 2:40 p.m. and proceeded to dig a communication trench from the exit of Orange tunnel, approximately S 28 c 40.65, to Prinz Arnulf tunnel; also a small party of 2 sappers and 25 men from the 116th Battalion proceeded to convert the trench blown by the 172nd R.E. Tunnelling Company and form a communication trench from S 28 c. 6.45 to S 28 c. 6.4 (Report #9). Upon instructions from the C.R.E. the party allotted to Lieut. Alford for work on Staubwasser Weg was turned over to Lieut. Carson of the 7th Field Company C.E. to work on "X" route. Upon receipt of orders from the C.R.E. the O.C. 9th Field Company passed orders on to the 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion and 116th Battalion working parties as to when they would proceed forward to work; certain parties left for work about 2:30 p.m. Lieut. Alford with sappers stood by for further work at night but was not required. Information received through the Division that, from examination of prisoners, the enemy was likely to make a counter-attack for the recovery of lost ground. Bombardment recommenced at 4:20 p.m. on the portion of Hill 145 which had not yet been captured by the 4th Division; the infantry attack to follow at 5:30 p.m., which attack apparently was successful, making the whole operations all along the Canadian Army Corps a decided success. The ground captured by the 3rd Canadian Division was consolidated successfully, the main resistance line being a series of strong points from one to seven along a line from S 28 d [uncertain] and S 29 d 7.8 N.W. to S 22 d 45.95, with about eight advanced posts over the crest in La Folie Wood extending from S 29 b 9.1 N.W. to S 22 b. 7.3 (La Folie Map). Patrols pushed forward to the bottom of the Ridge on the east side. About 10:20 p.m. orders were received from the C.R.E. for Lieut. Jones and his party of sappers and 116th Battalion infantrymen, who had been waiting in the assembly trench along the Bethune-Arras road, to proceed to work as arranged — to make a communication trench from our old front line at approximately S 22 c. 42. 2 1/2 to Staubwasser Weg at S 22 c 6.6 1/2; this was done, and he also constructed a trench joining a fire trench commenced by the 42nd Canadian Infantry Battalion when that battalion swung back its left flank (Report #10). Lieuts. Robertson and West carried on with their sappers in Goodman and Orange tunnels respectively, regulating traffic and operating trucks. #502269 Sergt McKieoy [uncertain], W.S. and #541767 L/Cpl. Sinker, H. of this company each found an enemy machine gun in captured enemy trenches and salvaged same. The remainder of the company at rear billets stood to, ready to move forward at short notice. Casualties: #503096 Corp. McLennan, R.C. and #541912 Spr Collier, S. wounded by shell fire and evacuated; #404787 Spr Anderson, C.A. sick, sent to hospital. | People: Major Dunbar [uncertain]; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Muroie [uncertain]; Lieut. Alford; Lieut. Carson; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Sergt McKieoy [uncertain], W.S. #502269; L/Cpl. - **1917-04-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Neuville St. Vaast, France** — Nothing of importance during the night or morning; rations and water got up to all sections; about 11.30 am "C" Section from the head of Bonval Ravine observed a party of 100 enemy between Petit Vimy and Vimy, opened fire and dispersed them with casualties, as was a second party of about 50 fifteen minutes later; the enemy retaliated by shelling the head of the ravine with about 38 77 mms and sweeping it with machine-gun fire; at 3.40 pm word was received that a counter-attack was expected and "F.S." Battery stood to; at 4 pm "F.S." Battery was ordered to prepare to move forward and Capt. McCorkell took over command from Lieut. Bowles, who was ordered to the horse lines being sick; moving forward at 4.30 pm to relieve guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Co. in "F.1" position, Capt. McCorkell found these guns were not at that location, so he moved the battery to the correct location at 5.35 pm; command of the battery passed from Major Watson to Major Basevi, O.C. 14th Can. M.G. Co.; the order was changed at 6.40 pm, command of "D.1", "E.1" and "F.1" batteries passing to Major Watson, who was ordered to have them take up entirely new positions further forward; casualties total for the two days now 1 other rank killed and 7 wounded. | People: Capt. J. E. McCorkell; Lieut. Bowles; Maj. Basevi; Maj. S. W. Watson. | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. Co. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed, 7 O.R. wounded (two-day total).

- **1917-04-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Cold with a heavy fall of snow. The O.C. attended advanced C.R.E. H.Q. Orders received to carry on the communication trench on the left flank of the 7th Brigade. At 1 a.m. orders were received from the C.R.E. for a communication trench to Artellerie Weg to be constructed, but as work had been put through on the preceding night no party was sent out. Lieut. Alford and a party of sappers, No 4 Section, reported from rear billets to advanced billets. The O.C. proceeded to Pont St Dugouts just in front of the Arras-Bethune Road, S 26 c. 1.8, Sheet France 36 c S.W. Lieut. Robinson with a party of sappers and a working party of 50 men from the 116th Battalion proceeded at 9:30 a.m. to continue work on "Y" route, this route being extended to approximately S 29 a 5-75, being just west of La Folie Wood. Consolidation of captured positions proceeded with (Report #11). The O.C. remained at the C.R.E. most of the day assisting him. Lieut. Robinson and party temporarily quit work on "Y" route and withdrew to the Quarry Line upon word being sent to him by the O.C., and also upon receipt of orders by the O/c infantry working party that the enemy contemplated a counter-attack in the neighbourhood of Petit Vimy; the counter-attack did not develop and work on the "Y" route resumed. On this work — casualties: 1 O. Rank killed and 7 wounded of the 116th Battalion. Work of installing water troughs in the rear of Berthonval Farm, also in the neighbourhood of the Bethune-Arras Road at Arras, was carried on by this company. Lieut. Robertson and West with a party of sappers superintended traffic control in Goodman and Orange Tunnels. #541710 Spr C.T. Care wounded by shell fire — evacuated. | People: Lieut. Alford; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Spr C.T. Care #541710. | Companies: 7th Brigade; No 4 Section; 116th Battalion. | Locations: Pont St Dugouts; Arras-Bethune Road; "Y" route; La Folie Wood; Quarry Line; Petit Vimy; Berthonval Farm; Goodman Tunnel; Orange Tunnel. | Casualties: 1 O. Rank of the 116th Battalion killed and 7 wounded on "Y" route work; #541710 Spr C.T. Care wounded by shell fire, evacuated. | Movement: Lieut. Robinson's party withdrew to the Quarry Line on a counter-attack warning, then resumed work.

- **1917-04-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Cold with snow and rain. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and remained with him most of the morning; later he made an inspection of the forward defences and works being carried on by this company. The 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade relieved the 7th and 8th Canadian Infantry Brigades in the front line, taking over both brigade sections. The O.C. during his tour of inspection discovered an enemy 77 mm field gun with a case of spare parts at S 22 c. 80.65 (Vimy Map) and a medium trench mortar at S 22. c. 6.6. Orders received from the C.R.E. for the remainder of the company at rear billets to be prepared to move forward with transport. Lieut. Robinson with sappers from No 1 Section and an infantry party of 100 from the 60th Battalion worked on improvement of "Y" route, also installing water troughs along the Arras-Bethune road and Berthonval Farm (Report #12). Lieut. Jones with sappers and an infantry party (80) from the 60th Battalion worked on a communication trench ([uncertain] to Staubwasser Weg) (Report #13). Lieuts. Robertson and West with sappers superintended control of traffic in Goodman and Orange tunnels. | People: Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West. | Companies: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade; No 1 Section; 60th Battalion. | Locations: "Y" route; Arras-Bethune road; Berthonval Farm; Staubwasser Weg; Goodman Tunnel; Orange Tunnel. | Movement: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade relieved the 7th and 8th Brigades in the front line.

- **1917-04-12 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Fine and clear; heavy fall of snow during last night. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and also attended a conference with Brig-General Hill, 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade, and battalion commanders, when the scheme of a proposed attack by the 9th Brigade on the west approaches to the village of Vimy and Vimy itself was discussed with battalion commanders: the 60th Battalion to attack on the right, the 43rd on the left and the 58th in the centre; the 52nd Battalion to be in reserve and occupy positions on Vimy Ridge; the 9th Field Company C.E. to assist in consolidation. This operation was to take place in two stages, the first attack to take place in the early morning of 13 April. Lieut. Robinson with sappers and an infantry party from the 116th Battalion established a tool dump in a captured enemy position near Spandau Haus and off Prinz Arnulf Tunnel; an enemy pioneer dump was located near S 29. b. 7.3., containing a considerable quantity of barbed wire and stakes. Orders received from the 3rd Canadian Division for a number of Bangalore tubes to be made up and sent to Birmingham Dump. 9th Brigade patrols pushed forward into Petit Vimy and the outskirts of Vimy; fires observed in [uncertain] Lens. Word received that the attack of the 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade was postponed indefinitely. Lieut. Jones with four sappers demolished a house at S 29 a. 6.8 being used by the Germans as a ranging point (Report #14). Sappers of this company carried on with the installation of water troughs along the Arras-Bethune Road. Lieuts. Robertson and West with a party of sappers superintended traffic in Goodman and Orange tunnels. Several tanks were seen being brought out from Neuville St. Vaast this morning. | People: Brig-General Hill; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West. | Companies: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 60th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 52nd Battalion; 116th Battalion. | Locations: Vimy; Vimy Ridge; Spandau Haus; Prinz Arnulf Tunnel; Birmingham Dump; Petit Vimy; Lens [uncertain]; Neuville St Vaast; Goodman Tunnel; Orange Tunnel; Arras-Bethune Road. | Movement: Proposed 9th Brigade attack on Vimy postponed indefinitely.

- **1917-04-13 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy Ridge, France** — Lieut. McBurny took over command of "F.1" Battery from Capt. McCorkell, who returned to the transport lines; Lieut. Robson reported to Lieut. McBurny and is in charge of "B" Section; the battery is again under control of Major S. W. Watson; the 5th Bde. relieved the 4th Bde. in the afternoon, taking over Bde. H.Q. in the cave at Les Tilleuls, Major Watson moving to this point with the brigade; during the afternoon and evening the line was advanced over the railroad embankment, the town of Vimy having been taken; a reconnaissance was made in the evening by Major Watson and Lieut. Creighton in advance of the railway embankment where the 18th Bn. were found digging in; "A" & "C" sections moved forward and took up positions on the railway embankment, "B" & "D" sections held in reserve at the head of Bonval Ravine; sixteen of the attached Bde. carriers were returned at night; casualties 1 other rank killed and 3 wounded, two of which were caused by a bomb explosion in the bottom of a trench. | People: Lieut. McBurny; Capt. McCorkell; Lieut. Robson; Maj. S. W. Watson; Lieut. Creighton. | Companies: 5th Bde.; 4th Bde.; 18th Bn. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed, 3 O.R. wounded (2 by bomb explosion in a trench). | Movement: "A" & "C" sections forward to the railway embankment.

- **1917-04-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Villers-au-Bois, France** — Clear and fine in the forenoon, cloudy in the afternoon, N.W. wind. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. Orders received for the 9th Field Company C.E. to assist the 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade in consolidating the present position. The O.C. also attended the Brigade Major, 9th C.I.B., and arranged for working parties. A report was received that water in wells in Vimy and the neighbourhood had been poisoned with arsenic by the enemy before his withdrawal. Lieut. Muroie [uncertain] located three additional trench mortars captured from the enemy and located in the captured positions as follows: H.T.M. at S 22. c. 40. 65 and two medium trench mortars at S 22 d. 30. 55. A party of sappers brought out the trench mortar located by the company at S 22. c 65. 60. Lieut. Alford with 12 sappers and 100 men from the 52nd Battalion and 100 from the 116th Battalion completed two open emplacements at La Folie Farm, S 22 d 95. 25, and two bombing blocks, S 23. c. 1. 01; also completed two open emplacements at S 29 c. 15. 20 and one bombing block at S 29. c. 4.4 (Report #15). A party of 5 sappers installed water troughs on the Arras-Bethune Road and made additional fittings and conveniences. #541850 Dvr Holland, P.G. sick, sent to hospital. Lieuts. Robertson and West with a party of sappers superintended traffic in Goodman and Orange Tunnels. | People: Lieut. Muroie [uncertain]; Lieut. Alford; Dvr Holland, P.G. #541850; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West. | Companies: 9th C.I.B.; 52nd Battalion; 116th Battalion. | Locations: Vimy; La Folie Farm; Arras-Bethune Road; Goodman Tunnel; Orange Tunnel. | Casualties: #541850 Dvr Holland, P.G. sick, sent to hospital.

- **1917-04-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S 26 c. 1.8. (36 c S.W), France** — Fine and clear, west wind. Orders received from the C.R.E. that the main Arras-Lens road from the road junction S 29 d 75. 55 to Petit Vimy should be reconnoitred and put in a state of repair. The O.C. attended the 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade and arranged for a working party of 200 men from the 116th Canadian Infantry Battalion. One party proceeded to work in the afternoon and repaired the circular road by way of S 30. a. 6.2 through Petit Vimy and to the water tower just south of la Chaudiere. The 2nd Canadian Division was engaged in repairing the road from the said road junction, S 29 d. 75. 55 (Vimy Map), southerly towards Arras for a short distance (Report #16). Orders received from the C.R.E. for the balance of the company to move forward from Villers-au-Bois and bivouac in the neighbourhood of the Bethune-Arras Road. Capt. Ross moved the transport and balance of the company forward, arriving in the forward area at 4 p.m.; some of the men were accommodated in Pont St dugouts and the remainder under tarpaulins; transport lines at X.25.c.7.6, horses being picketed in the open; transport of a number of artillery units moved to bivouac in the same neighbourhood. Orders received for work to be continued in the morning on the repair of the Arras-Lens road N.E. of La Chaudiere and towards La Coulotte, T.1.a (France 36 S.W.). The O.C. attended the Brigade Major, 9th C.I.B., and arranged for working parties to come from the 52nd Battalion, holding the resistance line in the neighbourhood of La Chaudiere. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and General Staff, 3rd Canadian Division, re this working party, as all of the 16th Battalion were ordered out by the Canadian Corps to assist the 2nd Canadian Division in the repair of the 2nd Division section of the Arras-Lens Bethune road. Orders received from the C.R.E. that Lieut. West and sappers are released from work in the tunnels and are to return to their work. Lieuts. Walley and Murdie discovered a number of German letters and documents in dugouts in the captured portion, which were sent into Intelligence, 3rd Canadian Division. 145116 Spr McEwan, E. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | People: Capt. Ross; Lieut. West; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie; Spr McEwan, E. #145116. | Companies: 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 116th Canadian Infantry Battalion; 2nd Canadian Division; 52nd Battalion; 16th Battalion. | Locations: Arras-Lens road; Petit Vimy; la Chaudiere; La Coulotte; Pont St dugouts; Bethune-Arras Road; Villers-au-Bois. | Casualties: #145116 Spr McEwan, E. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | Movement: Balance of company moved forward from Villers-au-Bois to bivouac near Bethune-Arras Road.

- **1917-04-16 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.5, France** — Fine and clear in the forenoon, cloudy and colder in the afternoon, N.W. wind. Lieut. Walley with a party of sappers from No 2 Section and an infantry party of 125 from the 58th Battalion continued repair of the Lens-Arras road; the road was repaired and cleaned from S.30.a.6.2 to La Coulotte (Report #19). Lieut. Murdie with 2 sappers located two wells, one at S.29.b.90.95. and the other at S.30.a.90.80. Lieut. Alford made a water reconnaissance in and around La Chaudiere (Report #18, the water-samples report dated 15 April). Two sappers with four infantrymen reclaimed German dugouts and repaired same for 9th Brigade H.Q. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. with samples of well water for examination. Orders received from the C.R.E. for two springs located in the neighbourhood of S.29.b.9.9½ and S.30.a.9.8 (Vimy Map) to be conserved and pumps installed. The O.C. inspected work in the forward area where the Lens-Arras road is being repaired and endeavoured to locate two bored wells for water supply. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Alford. | Companies: No 2 Section; 58th Battalion; 9th Brigade. | Locations: Lens-Arras Road; La Coulotte; La Chaudiere.

- **1917-04-17 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.5, France** — Dull and cold, high wind from N.W. Upon receiving an invitation from the C.R.E. to put in recommendations for immediate rewards, the O.C. recommended the following officers, N.C.O.s and men, all for good work in the recent operations which resulted in the capture of Vimy Ridge: Lieut. C.M. Robinson for the Military Cross; Lieut. C.S. Walley for the Military Cross; Lieut. W.C. Murdie for the Military Cross; #502359 Sergt. W.S. McKiroy [uncertain] for the D.C.M.; #541727 L/Cpl. J.C. Dryden for the D.C.M.; #541972 Corporal A.L. Wilson for the Military Medal; #641942 Corporal Wm. Murdock for the Military Medal; #541826 Sapper John Grew for the Military Medal; #502466 2/Corporal A.E. Downes for the Military Medal; #502767 Corporal R.C. Douglas for the Military Medal. The above-mentioned N.C.O.s and men were recommended by the officers of this company with whom they were working on 9 April 1917 and subsequent dates. Lieut. Alford with 1 N.C.O. and 3 sappers made a reconnaissance of the Light Railway along the Lens-Arras road (Report #20). Lieut. West with 4 sappers reported at 58th Battalion Hqrs., but as no men were available for work the party returned to billets. Lieut. Murdie with 8 sappers made a curb and wooden cover for the spring at S.30.a.9.8 (Report #21). Lieut. Walley with 7 sappers from No 2 Section and a party from the 58th Battalion repaired the road from La Chaudiere to Petit Vimy (Report #22). Company transport hauled a large number of shovels to the neighbourhood of La Chaudiere for use of the 8th Brigade. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and also attended the Brigadier, 8th C.I.B., who wishes the O.C. or a representative to proceed to advanced billets near Petit Vimy as liaison officer. The O.C. proceeded to advanced Hqrs. of the 8th Brigade near Petit Vimy. | People: Lieut. C.M. Robinson; Lieut. C.S. Walley; Lieut. W.C. Murdie; Sergt. W.S. McKiroy [uncertain] #502359; L/Cpl. J.C. Murdie. | Companies: No 2 Section; 58th Battalion; 8th C.I.B.; 8th Brigade. | Locations: Vimy Ridge; Lens-Arras road; La Chaudiere; Petit Vimy.

- **1917-04-19 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.8, France** — Fine in the forenoon, cloudy with mist in the afternoon. Capt. Ross with Lieut. West and Jones and 12 sappers proceeded to Advanced 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade Hqrs.; Capt. Ross to remain there as liaison officer, Lieut. West to work with the 1st C.M.R. and Lieut. Jones with the 5th C.M.R., the former holding the outpost line and the latter the La Chaudiere resistance line. Orders received from the C.R.E. that the Lens-Arras road from S.30.a.7.3. to S.29.d.4.2. be screened from enemy view by camouflage screening; this work was commenced by Lieut. Robinson and a party from No 1 Section (Report #27). A report was also called for on the pumping plant found in La Chaudiere for the water pipe line running from and in a S.W. direction towards La Folie Farm. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. Various artillery units moved guns forward today. The 39th Battery C.F.A., which took a temporary position 20 yards in the rear of company billets, moved forward yesterday. Lieut. Alford with 4 sappers and a party of 28 men from the 1st C.M.R. repaired the light tramline (Report #26). Lieut. C.M. Robinson with 2 N.C.O.s and 1 sapper made a reconnaissance of the Arras-Lens Road which is to be camouflaged. Lieut. Murdie with 8 sappers repaired wells and pumps, also fitted up a horse trough (Report #28). Lieut. Walley with 7 sappers from No 2 Section and a party from the 1st C.M.R. repaired roads, also with 4 sappers and a party of 16 men from the 1st C.M.R. repaired dugouts for Brigade Hqrs (Report #29). Lieuts. - **1917-04-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Petit Vimy / La Chaudiere [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report (Report #30, Lieut. Murdie): a water-supply report on the German pipeline from the pumping station at La Chaudiere to a steel tank in La Folie Wood (S.23.c.7.8); the pipe line, about 2 inches in diameter, ran in a trench about 3 feet deep and had many ruptures made by shell fire, and the tank (about 13 ft × 4 ft × 3 ft 6 in) sits in a concrete house; a smaller pipe ran from the tank north-westerly towards La Folie Copse. The Germans appear to have used the light rail line between La Chaudiere and La Folie Wood, with barrel cars at the pumping station. The pipe line is in such bad condition that it would take a great deal of work and many lengths of new pipe. A spring at S.29.b. 9.5:9.0 was cribbed with a barrel and brickwork but presents limited prospects, and a water sample was taken from a well at S.30.a.8.7. | People: Lieut. Murdie. | Locations: La Chaudiere; La Folie Wood; Petit Vimy.
- **1917-04-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.8, France** — Fine and clearing, north wind. 3rd Canadian Division Operation Order No 37 received, whereby the 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade is to immediately consolidate the whole of the captured position by five lines of defence. Capt. Ross, as liaison officer, made arrangements for Lieuts. West and Jones with sappers to direct work of consolidating the outpost line tonight, these officers having reconnoitred the ground today. Lieut. Murdie with 5 sappers worked on water supply arrangements in Petit Vimy and La Chaudiere (Report #30). Lieut. Alford with 5 sappers and parties from the 1st C.M.R. repaired track and road (Report #31). Lieut. Robinson with 13 sappers from No 1 Section built frames for camouflage of the Arras-Lens road (Report #32). Lieut. Walley with 10 sappers and a party from the 1st C.M.R. repaired roads, also dugouts for 8th C.I.B. Hqrs (Report #33). Lieut. West with 4 sappers from No 4 Section and parties from the 1st C.M.R. excavated new trenches (Report #34). Lieut. Jones with 2 sappers and a party from the 1st C.M.R. dug a fire trench; 1 O.R. 1st C.M.R. was killed in this party (Report #35). One horse of the company had to be killed today on account of sickness. | People: Capt. Ross; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Alford; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. West; Lieut. Jones. | Companies: 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade; No 1 Section; No 4 Section; 1st C.M.R.; 8th C.I.B. | Locations: Petit Vimy; La Chaudiere; Arras-Lens road. | Casualties: 1 O.R. 1st C.M.R. killed digging a fire trench; one company horse killed on account of sickness.

- **1917-04-23 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.8, France** — Fine and clear, N.E. wind. Gas alert on. Heavy bombardment commenced by our guns at 4.30 a.m., guns covering from the right of the 3rd Canadian Division front to the south as far as could be seen, also to the north of the 3rd Canadian Division front. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. C.R.E. Operation Order No 38 received, whereby the 7th Field Company C.E. is to relieve the 9th Field Company in the forward area on 24 April; relief to be complete by 6 a.m. 25 April. The 9th Field Company on relief is to join the 8th Field Company and the 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion on work on La Folie road. Capt. McPherson of the 7th Field Company attended at the billets of the 9th Field Company, when the O.C. 9th Company explained in detail the work being carried on by this company, and arranged for the 7th Field Company officers to inspect the works. The following men of this company were granted permission to wear the Good Conduct Badge, for two years' good service with the colours, from the dates set opposite their respective names — #76067 Spr P.L. Hill; #115416 Dvr J. Lees; #484987 Spr B.A. Anderson; #2282 Spr A.E. de la Penotiere; #484778 Spr J. Jacobs; #541841 Spr W. McKenzie — though no dates are in fact written beside the names. Lieut. Jones with 2 sappers located a bore hole at S.24.b.1.9 under the floor of a small house (Report #46). Lieut. Robinson with 3 N.C.O.s and 10 men (No 1 Section) placed camouflage along the Arras-Lens road (Report #47). Lieut. Alford with 14 sappers and parties from the 3rd C.M.R. Battalion worked on the tramline (Casualty C.M.R.) (Report #48). Lieut. Walley with 3 sappers and 11 infantry salvaged barbed wire and stakes (Report #49). Lieut. Murdie with 5 sappers worked on the water supply (Report #50). #472086 Spr Heary, C.R. wounded in the knee by shell fire; evacuated. | People: Capt. McPherson; Spr P.L. Hill #76067; Dvr J. Lees #115416; Spr B.A. Anderson #484987; Spr A.E. de la Penotiere #2282; Spr J. Jacobs #484778; Spr W. McKenzie #541841; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Alford; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Murdie; Spr Heary, C.R. #472086. | Companies: 7th Field Company C.E.; 8th Field Company; 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion; No 1 Section; 3rd C.M.R. Battalion. | Locations: La Folie road; Arras-Lens road. | Casualties: #472086 Spr Heary, C.R. wounded in the knee by shell fire, evacuated; one unnamed C.M.R. casualty on the tramline. | Movement: 7th Field Company to relieve the 9th in the forward area on 24 April, relief complete by 6 a.m. 25 April; 9th to join the 8th Field Company and 3rd Pioneers on La Folie road work.

- **1917-04-24 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | S.26.c.1.8, France** — Fine and clear, N.E. wind. Gas alert on. A party of officers of the 7th Field Company C.E. proceeded with Lieuts. West, Walley, Alford and Robinson to look over the works being carried on by this company in the forward area. Lieut. West was wounded in the foot by shell fire during this tour and evacuated. #502466, 2/Cpl. Downes, Albert Ernest, was killed by shell fire on the Arras-Lens road in the neighbourhood of S.30.a (Vimy Map) while on duty in charge of a party erecting a camouflage screen over the road; the O.C. wished to record the good services rendered by this N.C.O. Lieut. Walley went over the work of construction of the 40 cm tramline eastward from Neuville St Vaast towards La Folie Wood, being constructed by the 7th Field Company C.E., with officers of the 9th Field Company; the O.C. also inspected this work, which is to be worked upon by this company pursuant to C.R.E. Operation Order No 28 [as written]. The O.C. attended the O.C. 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion, when it was arranged that the 9th Field Company C.E. will work upon the forward half of the tramline, i.e. towards La Folie Wood. Lieut. Alford with 7 sappers repaired the light tramline (Report #51, cited in the diary remarks; no report numbered #51 appears in the appendix). Lieut. Jones with 2 sappers located the second bore hole at S.24.b.1.9 (Report #52). Lieut. Robinson with a party of sappers erected camouflage along the Arras-Lens road (Report #53). Lieut. Murdie with 2 sappers was on water reconnaissance in the neighbourhood of Vimy (Report # [uncertain — no number written]). | People: Lieut. West; 2/Cpl. Downes, Albert Ernest #502466; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Alford; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: 7th Field Company C.E.; 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion. | Locations: Arras-Lens road; Neuville St Vaast; La Folie Wood; Vimy. | Casualties: Lieut. West wounded in the foot by shell fire, evacuated; #502466 2/Cpl. Downes, Albert Ernest killed by shell fire on the Arras-Lens road. | Movement: 9th Field Company to work the forward half of the 40 cm tramline towards La Folie Wood.

- **1917-04-28 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embt., France** — During the night of 27/28th the 26th Cdn. Inf. Bn. dug in in T23b, 600 yds in advance of their old line; 2 guns of "B" Section were placed at T23 d 5.9½ to protect the right flank of the 26th Bn. and the brigade front; at 4.25 am the Canadian Corps attacked Arleux-en-Gohelle in conjunction with operations by the 3rd Army further south; Nos. 4, 5, 6 and 7 M.G. Batteries under Major S. W. Watson formed a supporting and protective barrage with the artillery, and the 25th Cdn. Inf. Bn. advanced to connect with the 26th Bn.; the operation was successful and all objectives were reported taken; 162,000 rds S.A.A. expended by the four batteries 4.25–6.55 am; a gun and crew of "B" Section at T23 d 5.9½ was buried by the German counter-barrage at 4.30 am, 2 other ranks killed and 1 wounded, the remainder — Cpl. Ronayne and 1 other rank — dug out unhurt three hours later by Pte. Brown, the gun slightly damaged but not put out of action; at 8.30 pm the enemy put up an S.O.S. on the right flank and all batteries opened fire, 17,000 rds; one gun of the Borden Battery was put out of action by shrapnel but replaced immediately from the Div. Repair Centre; casualties among attached units 1 other rank killed and 2 wounded. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Cpl. Ronayne; Pte. Brown. | Companies: 26th Cdn. Inf. Bn.; 25th Cdn. Inf. Bn.; Borden Battery. | Casualties: 2 O.R. killed, 1 O.R. wounded (company); attached units 1 O.R. killed, 2 O.R. wounded.

- **1917-04-30 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embt., France** — In answer to an S.O.S. at 4.30 am all machine-gun batteries opened fire on their protective barrage for a short time, 25,000 rds; the remainder of the day passed quietly with the usual shelling of the forward area; orders received in the afternoon for Nos. 5 and 6 Batteries (14th Cdn. M.G. Co.) to be withdrawn in the evening to rest, and later word that No. 4 Battery (1st Cdn. M.M.G.) would also be withdrawn, so No. 7 Battery was dissolved and "C" Section was ordered to man positions in the sunken road at T28a 5.5 for indirect fire on the enemy's trenches and wire, and "D" Section to carry out indirect fire on the streets and crossroads in Acheville; the enemy maintained an intensive bombardment on Mt. Forêt Quarries and the forward area from 5.30 pm, evidently suspecting the relief of the 25th Bn. by the 24th Bn. (Signed Maj. S. W. Watson.) | People: Maj. S. W. Watson. | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. - **1917-05-02 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — During the night of 1st/2nd the usual indirect fire was carried out on the usual targets, 24,000 rounds; the enemy retaliated with H.E. and gas shell, doing no damage; the enemy heavily shelled the R.R. Embankment and vicinity of Coy H.Q. between midnight and 2 am with H.E., causing 1 casualty at Coy H.Q.; the 6th Cdn. Inf. Bde. relieved the 24th Bn. in the right half of the divisional sector during the night of 2nd/3rd; Major Watson issued Preliminary Order M.G. 461, and as Coy H.Q. was required for a 6th Bde. battalion H.Q., a new H.Q. was established in the R.R. Embankment at T26.A.6.2; in addition to the company's 8 mobile guns, 2 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. and 6 guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. on the Farbus–Vimy R.R. Embankment and 6 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Co. in the observation line on Vimy Ridge were detached to the 5th Bde.; at 7.30 pm Major Watson received orders to assume command of the barrage guns of the division, Major Eastham having been evacuated sick, and immediately issued the instructions in M.G. 469 and established his H.Q. with the O.C. 6th Bde. in Thelus Mill Cave. | People: Maj. S. W. Watson; Maj. Eastham. | Companies: 6th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 24th Bn.; 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 1 casualty at Coy H.Q.

Williams forward of the Lens–Arras road in the morning, the trenches east of Nine Elms, at present occupied by the 13th Battalion, exceedingly dirty though cleaned up two days ago by a fatigue party obtained by this unit, the battalions occupying them having paid no attention to sanitary orders issued, reported to the A.A. & Q.M.G., and the bodies of two Germans were found and the Camp Commandant of the area notified, the artillery position on the slope of the hill in fairly good shape and the 13th Machine Gun Company lines very dirty, with Thélus and Bois Carré heavily shelled, then in the afternoon rode through the Bunechaut Camp area, where some improvement had been made following the adverse report sent in yesterday, and sent a report to the A.D.M.S. regarding the condition of latrines in the 1st Canadian Divisional area. | People: Sgt. Williams. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-03 | 18th Battalion | Paynesley Tunnel** — Combined 3rd, 4th and 5th May entry: position as yesterday; during this tour much valuable work was done in improving defences, wiring and deepening of trenches, also in the collection of salvage spread over the whole area, each company establishing a dump and rivalling each other in the collection of S.S.A. [uncertain], bombs and equipment; 23 other ranks arrived as reinforcements, 4 other ranks admitted to hospital.

Hennessy at the G.C.M.; an attached man, a corporal, remanded for F.G.C.M. for refusing to obey an order; the Paymaster back to Headquarters Mess; the office now in a Nissen hut; the Train got a narrow squeak of being shelled to pieces on the way to railhead; Grant had a close call from a bomb. | People: Capt. Hennessy; Lt. Grant. | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1917-05-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — Indirect fire midnight to dawn on the streets and crossroads in Acheville and the enemy's support line wire, 10,000 rds; at 3.45 am the 6th Bde., in conjunction with operations of the 1st Cdn. Div. and XIII Corps on the right, attacked the German trench system south of Acheville, the attack not entirely successful, being partly held up by machine guns in a reinforced concrete emplacement on the high ground at U19.C.0.4; the 5th Bde. did not take part, but held the ground already occupied; two of the company's sections, "C" & "D", were employed on barrage work and known as 7 Battery; a counter-attack expected at 8.15 am came to naught on the guns opening up; the transport pack train delivered 30,000 rds to No. 7 Battery; one gun of "C" Section was put out of action at 9.30 pm by a shell bursting close to the emplacement, the No. 1, Pte. D. W. Graham, killed and 2 other ranks wounded, one of whom died at a Casualty Clearing Station. | People: Pte. D. W. Graham. | Companies: 6th Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; XIII Corps. | Casualties: Pte. D. W. Graham killed; 2 O.R. wounded, one died at C.C.S.

- **1917-05-03 | 9th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Alberta) | Bramshott, England** — 12 Other Ranks S.O.S. on proceeding overseas to 10th Battalion — the line is repeated twice as written. Lieut Jones with 46 N.C.O.s and sappers repairing the Vimy Ridge Tramway (Report #4); parties on bunks in dugouts between Pont St and the Quarries, loading engineering material at Bois-des-Alleux, and cleaning and painting wagons and the salvaged heavy trench mortar. | People: Lieut Jones. | Locations: Lens; Pont St; Quarries; Bois-des-Alleux.
- **1917-05-03 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Ecurie, France** — Routine day. Admitted 7 horses. | People: No. 484 Pte. Reidy J. P., rejoined from 1 Canadian Divisional Train | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-03 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright; left at 5.30 a.m. with Col. R. [uncertain] Simpson, C.A.M.C., and Col. Templeton, D.A.D.M.S., for the advanced dressing stations and regimental aid posts, the wounded beginning to come in fairly early and many walking cases met on the way up, returning about 9 a.m. to report to Col. Ford, A.D.M.S., that the wounded were being brought out from the front line satisfactorily, then assisted at the main dressing station, with Col. Ross and Captain Gibson, Canadian Corps, visiting the office, the wounded practically all cleared before 1 p.m., and in the afternoon called on the Camp Commandant of the forward area to arrange for the burial of some dead Germans, with the Sanitary Section lorry loaned to the A.D.M.S. for transport of walking wounded from the hospital at Carency [uncertain] to Barlin. | People: Col. R. [uncertain] Simpson; Col. Templeton; Col. Ford; Col. Ross; Capt. Gibson. | Casualties: none.

Foret Quarries in the evening with gas shells, but fortunately all the rations parties were clear of this area before shelling commenced; 1 other rank slightly wounded. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 O.R. slightly wounded.

Whitley, a company runner, wounded; sections engaged targets at T 3 a, N 32 d, N 33 c and N 34 d with indirect fire. | People: Pte. Whitley. | Casualties: Pte. Whitley wounded. | Movement: —

- **1917-05-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.8, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Bright and warm, east wind. Lieut Jones with 44 N.C.O.s and sappers and 90 O.R. from the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion working on the Vimy Ridge tramway (Report #5); parties erecting and wiring bunks near Pont St, loading trestle wagons with fascines at Bois-des-Alleux, and bringing in an old German heavy trench mortar from the crater line and cleaning it. | People: Lieut Jones. | Companies: 2nd C.M.R. - **1917-05-04 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, very warm and hazy; rode to the Fond de Vase area in the morning and inspected the lines at Bunechaut Farm, the 3rd Brigade Trench Mortar Battery lines in filthy condition, interviewed Captain Tennant, Camp Commandant of this area, and seven shells were sent into Bunechaut Farm this morning, then in the afternoon drove to Camblain l'Abbé, called on the D.D.M.S. Canadian Corps and discussed sanitation during the warm season, suggesting that a separate report be made by the Sanitary Officer on each unit, marking them excellent, good or unsatisfactory, these reports to be published in Divisional Orders, with Major Rankin, Canadian Corps, and Captain McDonald, O.C. 3rd Canadian Sanitary Section, present at the discussion. | People: Capt. Tennant; Major Rankin; Capt. McDonald. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-04 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — 38 NCOs and men from No. 57 General Hospital attached for temporary duty, with Captains W. C. Oram, H. Armstrong and J. Hay, R.A.M.C.(T); the personnel's camp was moved to a more open site on the Sanitary Officer's recommendation, the tents overhauled and only regulation kit allowed, tents folded after the 6.30 morning parade; a Court of Inquiry into the accidental injury to the hand of No. 526604 Pte R. Wolfenden, who had been examining a bullet found outside his tent which exploded, found him free from blame; Surgeon-General Sir William Babtie, V.C., K.C.M.G., C.M.G., D.D.M.S., Boulogne Base, visited the hospital, accompanied by Surgeon-General R. H. S. Sawyer, and Captain G. B. Burney, Assistant-Director, General Voluntary Organization, also visited to enquire as to the regularity and sufficiency of supplies, which he found satisfactory — the O.C. pays tribute to the high class of supplies and timely assistance of the organisation. | People: Capt W. C. Oram, Capt H. Armstrong, Capt J. Hay, Pte R. Wolfenden, Surgeon-General Sir William Babtie, Surgeon-General R. H. S. Sawyer, Capt G. B. Burney. | Movement: 38 NCOs and men attached from No. 57 General Hospital.

Bennett), rifle mechanism and company drill (Lieut. Jones); the route march planned for Wednesday was carried out on Friday on account of weather; the majority of the 2nd class have shown sufficient proficiency to begin a 3rd class on Monday 7 May (the copy letter says 5 May [uncertain]). | People: Lieuts. Bennett and Jones; Maj. P. W. Wetmore. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-05 | No. 1 Canadian Mobile Veterinary Section | Ecurie, France** — Weekly ration statement rendered to Q Branch, Headquarters, 1 Canadian Division. Admitted 8 horses. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-05-05 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, warm; the 1st Canadian Brigade was relieved last night by troops of the 5th Division, the lorry reported at 8 a.m. to move the office supplies of the A.D.M.S. to Bruay, Lt-Col. Scott, 14th Field Ambulance, called and arranged to hold the dugouts used for the A.D.M.S. office and personnel for future medical units, the A.D.M.S. 5th Division later concurring, Staff Sgt. Kitteringham was instructed to move the men into these dugouts, and at Divisional Headquarters Major Wake, D.A.A.G., said the area had been cleaned up and would be left in a sanitary condition by the Division, then in the afternoon drove to Bunechaut Farm, where the lines vacated by the various transports were in a very unsatisfactory condition, the 5th Division not yet having put in a Camp Commandant for the Fond de Vase area, and called to investigate a nuisance complained of in the 2nd Anti-Aircraft Battery, the conditions already remedied, and later called on the D.D.M.S. 13th Corps to arrange for all 13th Corps orders on sanitation to be forwarded, with Pte. Beckerson returned from hospital, very quiet with little artillery fire and few aeroplanes observed. | People: Lt-Col. Scott; Staff Sgt. Kitteringham; Major Wake; Pte. Beckerson. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-05 | No. 1 Company, Canadian Forestry Corps | St. Evroult Forest, France** — A detachment of Scottish Rifles (2 officers and 200 men) was attached for loading and mill work, the French authorities having made civilian labour difficult to employ from the end of March 1917; the company operated the mills and railroad with two locomotives and some twenty-nine cars, loading 15 to 20 trucks a day at St. Evroult Station, and in one month supplied some 30,000 railway sleepers sawn in the mills plus some one thousand tons of defence timber, pit-props and poles (from the retrospective narrative history). | People: none named. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.8, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Bright and warm, S.E. wind. At 8 p.m. a heavy bombardment commenced in the neighbourhood of Lens. An enemy aeroplane flew over the company lines at dusk and dropped bombs in the immediate neighbourhood; no casualties. Lieut Robertson with 46 N.C.O.s and sappers continued work on the Vimy Ridge tramline (Report #7); parties on bunks near Pont St, loading fascines at Bois-des-Alleux, and erecting a Nissen hut at Divisional Hqrs. Enemy counter-battery work on the batteries near the company billets has increased considerably, carried on by heavy guns (apparently naval guns). An enemy aeroplane flew over the camp dropping signals and firing its machine gun, and forced the observers in the kite balloon beside the camp to descend in their parachutes. | People: Lieut Robertson. | Locations: Lens; Pont St; Bois-des-Alleux; Divisional Hqrs. | Casualties: None (bombs dropped near company lines, no casualties).

- **1917-05-07 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | La Targette** — Supply train late again and had to turn back after nearly reaching the railhead, immediately after Traffic wired complaining of delay in unloading; last night a German aeroplane came over these lines 150 yards N.N.W. of La Targette after all our planes had gone home by 8.30 p.m. and tried to set fire to one of our balloons, missing three times with his flares and firing his machine gun on the ground with no damage as far as can be ascertained; the same thing happened on the night of the 3rd, when the plane dropped bombs and did damage, killing two men, wounding several others and killing three horses. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 killed, several wounded, 3 horses killed (German bombing, night of 3 May; the men are not named)

- **1917-05-07 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Farbus–Vimy R.R. Emb., France** — During the past night the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. relieved the 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. in the forward area, the 5th Bde. proceeding to rest camp at Aux Reitz, the company remaining in the line for another 24 hours to cover the relief; the day passed quietly with only the normal amount of shelling up to 10 pm, when the enemy opened a heavy bombardment with gas shells on the whole divisional front from the tops of Vimy Ridge to forward of the Vimy–Farbus R.R. Embankment; No. 7 Battery ("C" & "D" sections) were withdrawn at dusk and proceeded to rest camp at Aux Reitz, fortunately only one casualty during this withdrawal although several men were slightly gassed; arrangements completed and guides provided for the relief of "A" & "B" Sections by one section of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. and one section of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | People: — | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 4th Cdn. M.G. - **1917-05-08 | 18th Battalion | Mt Foret Quarries** — Early in the morning the enemy made a counter-attack against Fresnoy, which had been taken by the 1st Canadian Division on the 3rd instant; the Gloucester Regiment, the left battalion of the division on our right, on whom the brunt of the attack fell, were driven back to a line just east of Arleux, running through T.20.c. and T.20.a.7.4. [uncertain], hence our right battalion, the 19th Canadians, were forced to withdraw from the advanced position in front of Fresnoy at noon to a position running through T.24.c. and T.30.a., connecting with the Gloucesters at T.30.a.7.4. [uncertain]; during this attack our three lines were subjected to heavy artillery fire, and the 4th C.I.B. having lost all touch with the 19th Battalion, Cpl. Randall of the Battalion Scouts succeeded in reaching 19th Headquarters in the Arleux Loop and returned with the necessary information, passing through a very heavily shelled area, for which he was awarded the Military Medal; a second trip was made for the same purpose by Lieut. Eastwood. | People: Cpl. Randall; Lieut. Eastwood. | Companies: 1st Canadian Division; Gloucester Regiment; 19th Canadians; 4th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 19th Battalion. | Locations: Fresnoy; Arleux; Arleux Loop.

Coy., the relief hampered by gas shelling which continued the whole night until 5 am; on completion of the relief at 2 am, "A" & "B" sections proceeded to Aux Reitz, the last section arriving at 8 am; both sections were clear of the forward area before the enemy's dawn counter-attack, in which he recaptured Fresnoy from the 5th British Div. and the portion of the Oppy–Mericourt line held by this division; the remainder of the day was spent resting, the men fatigued, several suffering from the effects of the gas shells; the company bathed at Neuville-St. Vaast; two guns were mounted at dawn for A.A. work at Divisional H.Q., Aux Reitz, and another at the camp. | People: — | Companies: 4th & 14th Cdn. McAmmond, who was in command of our right platoon, under great difficulties established communication with the 19th Battalion, both through advance posts in T.24.c. and along Winnipeg Road (T.23.d.); during a break in communication a pigeon message was sent to Brigade Headquarters, the pigeons flying approximately 6 miles to Ecoivres, where they were trapped and the message wired to Brigade, the whole proceeding occupying 25 minutes. | People: Lieut. J. McAmmond. | Companies: 19th Battalion. | Locations: Winnipeg Road; Ecoivres.

- **1917-05-10 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, warm; with a car to Ecoivres in the morning to interview the O.C. Reserve Ration Dump about the incinerator nuisance, his chief objection being that the smoke from the incinerator and burning manure was unpleasant, telling him this was a technical matter to be decided by the Medical Services, then in the afternoon to Camblain l'Abbé, getting funds from the Field Cashier, calling on the D.D.M.S., Major Rankin, C.A.M.C., in charge of the office, to Hersin for lunch with the 2nd Canadian Field Ambulance, and to Bruay to call on the A.D.M.S. 1st Canadian Division, and on the way to Estrée Cauchie inspecting the detachment and paying, to Camblain l'Abbé paying the detachment there also at Ecoivres, and paying the balance on return, also the water patrol detail attached. | People: Major Rankin. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-05-10 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Surgeon-General T. P. Woodhouse, C.B., D.M.S., Lines of Communication, visited the hospital and expressed his interest in the Canadian Red Cross Hut, exclusively reserved for gunshot wounds of the chest; two cases belonging to the Enteric Group were reported and transferred to No. 14 Stationary Hospital; systematic rodding of the drains is being carried out and all intercepting chambers cleaned; the Admission and Discharge Room has been thoroughly cleaned and limewashed, the woodwork creosoted and the floor well washed; new bins constructed for the refuse in the Destructor Houses so all refuse will be covered until incinerated; Captain C. F. L. Fuller struck off strength on proceeding to 3rd Canadian Division for duty; Captains E. A. McCusker, H. C. Moses and P. Hogan taken on strength, the two former struck off again on being ordered to the 2nd Canadian Division for duty on 23 May, when they had just nicely learned the necessary routine and returns. | People: Surgeon-General T. Hogan. | Movement: Capt Fuller to 3rd Canadian Division; Capts McCusker and Moses to 2nd Canadian Division on 23 May.

- **1917-05-11 | 18th Battalion | T.27.d.3.5.** — During the whole of this tour considerable difficulty was experienced in bringing up rations owing to the enemy use of poison gas and tear shells, the enemy daily at dusk indiscriminately deluging the whole area between Farbus Wood and Vimy Railway with these shells, making it necessary for gas respirators to be worn; despite this Captain G. W. P. Hodgins never failed to deliver rations at Battalion H.Q. in Mt. Forest Quarries, and Lieut. A. A. McLean rendered valuable assistance by personally acting as guide from the railway forward; 6 other ranks admitted to hospital sick. | People: Capt. G. W. P. Hodgins; Lieut. A. A. Wright being detailed to take charge; Lieut. C. E. Lucas completed his task with the loss of 4 other ranks wounded, while Lieut. W. R. Wright and party on returning were heavily shelled in Mt. Foret Road, scattering the party, Lieut. W. R. Wright and Sgt. T. Clark being killed and 6 other ranks wounded. | People: Lieut. C. E. Lucas; Lieut. W. R. Wright; Sgt. T. Clark. | Locations: Mt. Foret Road.

- **1917-05-12 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | La Targette** — About 9 a.m. the Germans threw in some 9 or 10 shells just over the camp, one within 20 yards of a balloon at anchor and one close to an ammunition dump, their range some 200 yards too long for any damage to the Train; Nos. 1 and 3 convoys went out in very good shape; wire came for Capt. Hennessy to report as Staff Captain to the 5th Brigade; Capt. J. Oliphant to take over as Adjutant, Captain Church to be posted as O.C. No. 2 Company and Lieut. Higgins as Supply Officer; Hennessy left this afternoon. | People: Capt. Hennessy; Capt. J. Oliphant; Capt. Church; Lt. Higgins. | Companies: No. 1 Company; No. 3 Company; No. 2 Company; 5th Brigade. | Casualties: none (shelling, no damage)

- **1917-05-12 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, very warm; rode to the Bunechaut Farm area in the morning, the 1st Canadian Division having sent back a fatigue party to clean up the area complained of, then rode over most of the Fond de Vase area and found conditions fairly good, and in the afternoon rode to Mont St Eloi, interviewing the Town Major, Captain Duguid, 15th Battalion, arranging to put extra men on inspection work south of the Mont St Eloi–Arras road, and erected a bath house for the men. | People: Capt. Duguid. | Casualties: none.

Simson. | Companies: 1st C.D.T.; R.G.A. | Casualties: none

- **1917-05-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.8, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Warm and clear, S.E. wind. Lieut Robinson with two parties of 6 sappers and 60 men each from the 116th Battalion working on the Vimy Ridge tramline extension (Reports #20, #21); a party of 25 N.C.O.s and sappers and 70 men from the 116th Battalion ballasting and repairing roadbed along the Vimy Ridge tramline (Report #21a). | People: Lieut Robinson. | Companies: 116th Battalion. | Locations: Gouy; Mont St. Eloy; Arras-Bethune Road; Plank Road; Pylones.

- **1917-05-13 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ariane** — Fine, bright, warm; office work in the morning, then rode to Cambligneul in the afternoon to see Corporal Blondel about the sanitary conditions, who showed several large piles of manure in the yards of billets, with no Canadian troops there now and no fatigue party or transport obtainable to remove the manure, and called on the D.D.M.S. at Camblain l'Abbé, the Ford ambulance car still in the workshop and requiring several days to be repaired. | People: Cpl. D Coy construction proceeded. B Coy completed loop near Le Pendre. C Coy construction and maintenance proceeded; labour attached 4 officers, 260 OR, DCLI. | Companies: A Coy; B Coy; C Coy; D Coy.

Division inspected the Train in the afternoon, spending two hours at it, and presented Meritorious Medals to S.S.M. Proctor and S.S. Wade; the R.C.R. kindly lent their fife band for the march past; the G.O.C. expressed much satisfaction. | People: S.S.M. Proctor; S.S. Wade. | Companies: R.C.R. | Casualties: none

- **1917-05-14 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy Station, France** — The relief completed by 2 am; "C" Section guns in the front line and "D" Section 3 guns at T22 A 9.7 and 1 gun at T29 A 3.0, "A" & "B" sections coming back under orders of the G.O.C. 5th Bde.; 8 guns of the 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. in strong points and 9 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Co. on barrage work at T29 A 3.0 also came under the G.O.C. 5th Bde.; in the morning at about 10 o'clock one gun of "D" Section was put out of action, 2 of the gun crew killed and an attached carrier wounded by shell fire; at 1 pm the enemy commenced shelling the R.R. Embankment from Vimy Station to about 600 yds south, mostly 5.9s, until about 5 pm, one entrance to Advance H.Q. blown in but no casualties; at dusk two sections of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. relieved "A" & "B" sections in positions 300 yds in advance of the R.R. Embankment (O.O. No. 5); further orders — "B" Section only relieved the two sections of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. at T29 A 3.0 forming a protective barrage on the German front line, and "A" Section moved to the old battery position at T16 B 6.0; moves completed and guns in position by 11.15 pm; each section has guns detailed for A.A. work; casualties 2 other ranks killed, 1 died of wounds, 1 wounded, all "D" Section. | People: — | Companies: 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 4th Cdn. M.G. Co.; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 2 O.R. killed, 1 O.R. died of wounds, 1 O.R. wounded ("D" Section).

O'Hagan. | Casualties: none.

Canadian Corps, who expressed great surprise that, considering the heavy fighting and hardships passed through during the last month, it was possible for men to turn out so clean and in such fine condition; 10 other ranks of the 18th Battalion received the decoration of the Military Medal on this parade; at 5.00 p.m. the 18th Battalion relieved the 27th Battalion on the Ridge (observation) Line, with Battalion H.Q. at Thelus Cave. | People: General Sir Julian Byng. | Companies: 4th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 27th Battalion. | Locations: Ridge Line. | Movement: Neuville-St.-Vaast → Ridge Line.

Hamilton [uncertain initials] killed by shell fire near Commandant's House, east of Thelus; one OR killed, one OR wounded (both unnamed). A Coy shelled out of work east of Thelus three times, forced to stop altogether at 3 pm. One OR belonging to 5th Battn CRT reported himself as lost. Instructions from ADMS, Canadian Corps: Major Alger to report to ADMS, 4th Canadian Division; Capt Wilson to remain as MO of this unit. The 9th Field Coy C.E. relieved the 8th Field Coy C.E. in the forward area as from 7:30 p.m. today, and the 8th Field Coy took over the work of the 9th Field Coy C.E. in the rear area as from 7:30 p.m. Lieut. - **1917-05-22 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.9, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Dull and cloudy, S.W. wind. C.R.E. 15/93 dated 22-5-17 received, extracts from 3rd Canadian Division instructions relative to digging assembly (jumping-off) trenches in front of the C.I.B. left area, with a sketch showing the approximate location proposed; later instructions cancelling part were received. The Brigade Major and the O.C. proceeded over the line re general conditions. 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade Operation Order No. 92 dated 22-5-17 received, relative to the relief of the 58th and 116th Canadian Infantry Battalions in the front line by the 43rd and 52nd Canadian Infantry Battalions on the nights of 23–24 and 24–25 May respectively. Lieut. Walley with 15 sappers and parties from the 58th, 43rd and [third battalion number omitted in original] Canadian Infantry Battalions wiring, digging trenches and excavating dug-outs (Report #43); Lieut. Robertson with 17 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 52nd and 116th Battalions consolidating, carrying material and working on dug-outs (Report #44). Lieut. Alford wounded in the leg by shell fire on the way out to the works; he continued work all evening, returned to Advanced Billets, and was then evacuated through the Field Ambulance at Neuville-St-Vaast (Report #45). #715541 Spr Lewis, W. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Alford; Spr Lewis, W. #715541. | Companies: 58th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 52nd Battalion; 116th Battalion; 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade. | Casualties: Lieut. Alford wounded in the leg by shell fire, evacuated; #715541 Spr Lewis, W. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. | Movement: 58th and 116th Battalions to be relieved in the front line by the 43rd and 52nd Battalions on the nights of 23–24 and 24–25 May.

- **1917-05-23 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.9, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Dull and cloudy, S.W. wind. C.R.E. 19/94 received, containing extracts from 3rd Canadian Division Operation Orders relative to preparations for proposed operations. An enemy aeroplane flew over the advanced billets, dropped eight signals, which was followed by heavy shelling of a battery nearby, and opened machine-gun fire, wounding a sapper (name cut off at the foot of the page, [uncertain]). An enemy aeroplane also flew over the rear billets and dropped bombs in the vicinity of Fort George, causing several casualties and forcing the observers of the 24th Kite Balloon Section to descend in their parachutes. Major Robertson with 14 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 52nd Battalion working on a dug-out, repairing Brigade Hqrs and wiring (Report #46); Lieut. Robertson with 17 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 116th and 52nd Battalions digging a communication trench and deepening trenches (Report #47); Lieut. Walley with 13 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 43rd Battalion wiring, improving trench and excavating dug-outs (Report #48). At night Lieut. Walley with sappers and a party from the 43rd Battalion prepared to improve posts pushed forward last night near T.2.c.7.0, but owing to the relief of the 58th Battalion by the 43rd Battalion and enemy shelling, no work was accomplished. #500400 Spr. Smith T wounded by machine gun fire, evacuated; #45228 Dvr Williams, W.J.H. sick, sent to Field Ambulance. Four light draught horses were received by the company today. | People: Major Robertson; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Walley; Spr. Smith T #500400; Dvr Williams, W.J.H. #45228. | Companies: 52nd Battalion; 116th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 24th Kite Balloon Section. | Locations: Fort George; T.2.c.7.0. | Casualties: Sapper [uncertain] wounded by aeroplane machine-gun fire; #500400 Spr. Smith T wounded by machine gun fire, evacuated; #45228 Dvr Williams, W.J.H. sick, sent to Field Ambulance; several casualties (unnamed) from bombing near Fort George.

- **1917-05-24 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France (S26c 1.9, Sht 36c S.W.)** — Cloudy, N.W. wind. A special report was called for by the C.R.E.; the O.C. engaged compiling a detailed description of all the 9th C.I.B. trenches with wire entanglements, showing progress of works, with a plan. Instructions received from the C.R.E. to supervise work on certain dugouts for a Dressing Station for the A.D.M.S. The Brigade Major 9th C.I.B. had a conference with the O.C. re digging the proposed jumping-off trenches; orders received from the 3rd Canadian Division that they are not to be constructed tonight but on the night of 25th–26th. The O.C. with 5 sappers and parties from the 10th Field Ambulance and 52nd Battalion working on the Dressing Station, salvaging and repairing Brigade Hqrs (Report #49); Lieut. H. D. Robertson with 7 N.C.O.s and sappers from No. 3 Section and parties from the 116th Battalion working on dug-outs and trenches (Report #50); Lieut. Walley with No. 2 Section and parties from the 43rd and 58th Battalions digging a jumping-off trench and working on strong points and widening and deepening trenches (Report #51). Five reinforcements arrived from the Base Depot and are taken on the strength of the company as from today. | People: Lieut. H. D. Robertson; Lieut. Walley. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 10th Field Ambulance; 52nd Battalion; 116th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 9th C.I.B. | Locations: Dressing Station. | Movement: Five reinforcements from the Base Depot taken on strength.

- **1917-05-24 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Captain W. J. Enwright ceases to be attached on proceeding to No. 8 Canadian General Hospital; 33 NCOs and men returned to No. 57 General Hospital for duty, their work very much appreciated; the attention of the Sanitary authorities has been directed to the quality of the "French Milk" supplied from local sources — a whole delivery condemned during the week as sour and unfit for use, the milk sour on arrival and curdling when boiled, and a shipment of English milk inspected and found anything but clean, with dust, bran and even straw floating on it and ill-fitting can covers; the cesspit at the rear of the Operating Room is very nearly full again, about one foot from the top of the crown though emptied only a month ago, and the O.C. has recommended connecting it to the main drain; the soakage pit at the new latrine has proven a failure, a simple trench filled with stones now overflowing, and a drain is recommended to carry urine from a properly constructed urinal instead of the bucket system, the whole drain being about 300 feet. | People: Capt W. J. Enwright. | Movement: Capt Enwright to No. 8 Canadian General Hospital; 33 NCOs and men returned to No. 57 General Hospital.
