- **1917-05-28 | 18th Battalion | Mt. Foret Quarries** — At 1.00 a.m. the enemy opened a heavy barrage on Battalion H.Q. Mt. Foret Quarries, our support line at T.23.c.6. and our front line; the barrage on the front line lifted at 1.15 a.m. and two raiding parties, each estimated at 25 or 30 men, one on each side of the Mt. Foret–Acheville Road, were seen approaching our wire, but fire was opened by machine guns and rifles and, unable to get through the wire and checked by our fire, the enemy retired; two of the party on the left frontage got through the wire, one severely wounded and taken, the other giving himself up and immediately sent back to Brigade H.Q., and in the evening a dead German was brought in; on the right frontage a wiring party of an N.C.O. and 6 men were well out in front of our wire when the barrage opened, and Cpl. L. Skilton gave orders for the party to retire, the raiding party being seen and dispersed by our fire; a search party failed to find the three men of the protective patrol who had not returned, only two rifles being found in a shell-hole; at daybreak Huns were seen carrying in casualties and 10 or 12 dead were seen lying in No-Man's-Land at T.18.c.6.5.; our casualties during the raid were 3 men missing, 1 man killed and 1 man wounded. | People: Cpl. L. Skilton. | Locations: Mt. Foret–Acheville Road; Rouvroy Road.

- **1917-05-31 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Nothing of any moment. The month's Agenda records Major J. W. Hutchinson's notes on 146 cases of penetrating gunshot wounds of the chest treated in the past six weeks — 144 with blood in the pleural cavity, 2 with serum; 31 infected (20 streptococcus, 9 bacillus aerogenes capsulatus, 2 pneumococcus), 27 operated on of whom 8 died, 3 of the 4 non-operated cases dying — treated by resection of a rib and cleaning out of blood and clot, and latterly by repeated aspiration and irrigation with Eusol (1 in 2) keeping the chest closed, with seven conclusions; an admissions table for January–March, April and May; a compulsory short course of instruction for ward orderlies instituted at the suggestion of Warrant Officer Sergt-Major Miller (ward ethics, care of ward and sanitation, care of patients, convoys, evacuations, enemata, preparation of cadaver, screen dressings and triangular bandages); the April figures (6,865 admitted — 3,407 walking, 3,458 stretcher; 1,797 to medical wards, 5,068 to surgical); and Captain A. Howard Pirie's article on "Marching Fracture", sent to Headquarters for publication in the R.A.M.C. Journal and "The Lancet", and his paper on "Shrapnel Balls", submitted for publication in "Archives of Radiology and Electrology". | People: Maj J. W. Hutchinson, Sergt-Major Miller, Capt A. Howard Pirie.

- **1917-06-01 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Night comparatively calm; Lt. Soulsby was killed last night (31 May/1 June) at the entrance of his dugout; day quiet round most of the line with usual intermittent shelling of the Culvert and gun pits; aircraft very active — three enemy planes over our positions at 10 a.m. turned back by machine-gun fire, and at 10.45 a.m. four enemy planes attacked one of our scout planes west of the railway embankment and brought it down in flames just behind our front line, both airmen burned to death; enemy shelled front line east of the railway embankment and the Culvert in the afternoon; eight enemy planes over our positions at 8.45 p.m. | People: Lt. Soulsby. | Casualties: Lt. Soulsby killed (night 31 May/1 June); 2 airmen burned to death. | Movement: —

- **1917-06-01 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Cloudy and cool, S.W. wind. Capt. B. Ross returned from leave today. Sappers at rear billets cleaning around billets and preparing and loading material for the forward area. The O.C. with 5 sappers and parties from the 9th Machine Gun Coy worked on Brigade Hqrs and salvaged material (Report #1). Lieut. Robertson with No 3 Section and parties from the 1st and 4th C.M.R. and C.A.M.C. [uncertain] deepened trenches, put in fire steps and worked on dugouts and the Dressing Station (#2). Lieut. Jones with 8 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 4th and 8th C.M.R. and 10th Field Ambulance dug, pumped off trenches and worked on dugouts, strong points and the Dressing Station (#3). Lieut. Murdie with 9 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from infantry battalions widened trenches, worked on dug-outs and carried material (#4). Among the names mentioned in despatches by the Commander in Chief in the Gazette of today is Major Norman Roy Robertson, O.C. 9th Field Coy C.E. Casualties: #532826 L/Cpl Guinet, J.D. and No 504519 Spr Dobson, L. wounded by shell fire and evacuated. | People: Capt. B. Ross; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Murdie; Major Norman Roy Robertson; L/Cpl Guinet, J.D. #532826; Spr Dobson, L. #504519. | Companies: No 3 Section; 9th Machine Gun Coy; 1st C.M.R.; 4th C.M.R.; C.A.M.C. [uncertain]; 8th C.M.R.; 10th Field Ambulance. | Casualties: #532826 L/Cpl Guinet, J.D. and No 504519 Spr Dobson, L. wounded by shell fire, evacuated.

- **1917-06-04 to 1917-06-05 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | J.O. Trench [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report (sheet 46, Lieut. Jones, continued 4–5 June): a party in the new J.O. Trench between Bluenose Sap and the railway embankment came under trench-mortar fire, then rifle grenades and machine gun; several of the party were killed or wounded, and the party was withdrawn on Brigade order, work nil. An earlier party in the same trench was interfered with by our own 18-pdr battery firing short — 3 direct hits on J.O. Trench 20 yds left of the embankment, with shrapnel bursting behind and over the trench (marginal note: "Our own Artillery."). Spr Campbell, C.E., rendered great assistance in "First Aid" under trying conditions. Casualties: "Uncertain, probably 30" killed or wounded (appendix report; not in diary text). | People: Lieut. Jones; Spr Campbell. | Companies: 1st C.M.R. | Locations: J.O. Trench; Bluenose Sap. | Casualties: "Uncertain, probably 30" killed or wounded.
- **1917-06-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Bright and warm, south wind. Enemy aeroplanes flew over rear billets and dropped a number of bombs, one of which slightly wounded #46492 Spr Golding, C.A. and killed an N.C.O. of the 172 Tunnelling Coy, whose billets are close by. Sappers at rear billets carrying on with improving billets, loading material, etc. Lieut. Jones with 6 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 1st & 2nd C.M.R. and 10th Field Ambulance continued work on dugouts and the Dressing Station (#10). Lieut. Murdie with 20 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 1st & 4th C.M.R. and C.A.M.C. wired, deepened and repaired trenches and worked on the Dressing Station (#11). 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No. 31 dated 3-6-17 received, whereby the 7th Field Coy C.E. will relieve the 9th Field Coy C.E. in the forward area on the night of 5–6 June, and the 9th Field Coy C.E. will relieve the 8th Field Coy C.E. on work on the Yellow Line; relief to be complete at 12 noon 6 June. | People: Spr Golding, C.A. #46492; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: 172 Tunnelling Coy; 1st C.M.R.; 2nd C.M.R.; 10th Field Ambulance; 4th C.M.R.; C.A.M.C.; 7th Field Coy C.E.; 8th Field Coy C.E. | Casualties: #46492 Spr Golding, C.A. slightly wounded by an enemy bomb; an unnamed N.C.O. of the 172 Tunnelling Coy killed by the same bombing. | Movement: 7th Field Coy to relieve the 9th in the forward area on the night of 5–6 June; the 9th to relieve the 8th on the Yellow Line, relief complete by 12 noon 6 June.

- **1917-06-05 to 1917-06-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | J.O. Trench / Bluenose Sap [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report (sheet 48, Lieut. Jones, continued 5–6 June): gas attack — both working parties were withdrawn on account of gas (one after 1½ hours, the other after ½ hour at Bluenose Sap); 3 of the 1st C.M.R. were wounded slightly and gassed, and 2 C.E. were gassed. Devotion to duty on the part of A/Cpl. Hopkins in supervising work on C.T. and Spr. Hill is worthy of mention: when the party hurriedly withdrew leaving 3 seriously wounded or gassed men, they remained and brought out the wounded although gas was still present; both were slightly gassed. (The diary text for 5 June records the rescue but not the gas withdrawals or the 5 gassed/wounded.) | People: A/Cpl. Hopkins; Spr. Hill. | Companies: 1st C.M.R. | Locations: J.O. Trench; Bluenose Sap. | Casualties: 3 of the 1st C.M.R. wounded slightly and gassed; 2 C.E. gassed.
- **1917-06-05 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Warm and bright, N.E. wind. The O.C. and Lieut. Robertson proceeded to England on leave. Lieut. Murdie with 14 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 1st C.M.R. and 42nd Battalion deepened trenches and carried and salvaged material (#12). Lieut. Jones with sappers and infantry parties widened and deepened trenches; owing to heavy enemy shelling which caused a number of casualties in killed and wounded, work had to be stopped and the working party withdrawn by order of the 9th C.I.B. (#13). #524429 Spr Campbell, W. rendered great assistance in "First Aid" under trying conditions. Devotion to duty on the part of No 522789 Lce/Cpl Hopkins, W.B., supervising work on C.T., and No 76167 Spr Hill, F.L., is worthy of mention: when the party hurriedly withdrew leaving three severely wounded or gassed men, they remained and brought out the wounded although gas was being put over at the time; both were slightly gassed (#14). | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Jones; Spr Campbell, W. #524429; Lce/Cpl Hopkins, W.B. #522789; Spr Hill, F.L. #76167. | Companies: 1st C.M.R.; 42nd Battalion; 9th C.I.B. | Casualties: A number of casualties in killed and wounded (unnamed) from heavy enemy shelling; three severely wounded or gassed men left during the withdrawal and brought out by Lce/Cpl Hopkins and Spr Hill, both slightly gassed.

- **1917-06-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Fine and warm, N.E. wind. C.R.E. Operation Order No 32 dated 6-6-17 received, whereby on 17 June 1917 the 7th Field Coy C.E. will relieve the 9th Field Coy on the work on the Yellow Line, and on 17 June 1917 the 9th Field Coy C.E. will relieve the 8th Field Coy C.E. on the work on the Brown line and tramline extensions. Lieut. Walley with No 2 Section and parties from the 42nd and 49th Battalions worked on strong points (#25). Lieut. Steeves with 6 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 42nd Battalion wired strong points and excavated a new trench (#26). Lieut. Jones with 2 sappers and party from the 42nd Battalion worked on strong point 1.C. (#27). | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. - **1917-06-18 | No. 1 Canadian Sanitary Section | Ecurie Station** — Fine, very warm; to Ecoivres in the morning, where 40 men and 5 G.S. wagons were removing manure from civilian yards and straightening up the manure dump and refuse pile, seeing the Town Major, then in the afternoon walked to the wagon lines recently vacated by Canadian artillery, most of the latrines not sufficiently covered, reporting the unsatisfactory conditions to the [uncertain] and asking them to send back a fatigue party to clean up. | Casualties: none.

A Coy have completed dugouts for the men stationed at FARBUS Wood, which is constantly shelled. Tracklaying began today on line from Thelus SE, but owing to shelling it has been decided to do this work only at nights. Zivy-Labyrinth line has now been camouflaged. Average number of [uncertain] with scrapers used by A Coy on grade for week ending today = 29. Bn. sent out patrols and found Avion Trench west of the railway strongly manned, and it was reported, though not confirmed, that Avion Trench from the railway to Victoria Road is occupied by the 43rd; about 20 prisoners taken up to this evening; dugouts fairly numerous and in good condition; during the evening patrols from the 43rd, 52nd and 58th entered Avion; one of our sergeants and one O.R. wounded; about 7 a.m. we attacked along the whole front, very successfully. | Casualties: 1 sergeant and 1 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —

- **1917-06-29 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Cloudy and warm, S.W. wind. The O.C. accompanied Col McPhail, C.R.E. 1st Canadian Division, to look over trenches being taken over by the 1st Canadian Division from the 3rd Canadian Division. The enemy could be seen exploding mines in the Lens and Mericourt neighbourhood. Lieut. Steeves with 2 sappers and party from the P.P.C.L.I. improved Blighty trench (#75). Lieut. Robertson with 3 sappers and party from the P.P.C.L.I. deepened and revetted trench and laid bathmats (#76). Lieut. Walley with 5 sappers and party from the R.C.R. continued work improving communication trench (#77). Lieut. Robinson with 3 sappers and party from the R.C.R. erected wire entanglements in front of strong points X, Y & Z, Yellow Line (#78). 10 N.C.O.s and sappers worked at the Machine Gun Fort getting out the gas engine and crating the same. Remainder of sappers continued work cleaning and repairing wagons, equipment etc. | People: Col McPhail; Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Robinson. | Companies: 1st Canadian Division; 3rd Canadian Division; P.P.C.L.I.; R.C.R. | Locations: Lens; Mericourt; Blighty trench; Machine Gun Fort; Yellow Line.

- **1917-06-30 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin / Lestrem / Arras, France** — Weather fine, dull cool with showers in afternoon. This unit is divided up into nineteen camps maintaining the light railways and constructing new lines spurs and sidings; the camps are distributed from Lestrem on the North to Arras on the South. Battalion strength is 36 officers and 1095 other ranks (includes Hospital, on Command, and attached details). Work done during month on narrow gauge lines: miles located 17.64, miles graded 20.52, miles grade repaired 2.70, miles track laid 19.20, miles ballasted 9.04, miles surfaced 11.65; average number of miles maintained 78.49; average number of this unit daily on railway work 847 OR; average daily attached labour 956 OR. Two officers reinforcements from Canadian Railway Troops Depot, Purfleet, reported today. Plan of Lestrem lines attached. Today's attached labour: A Coy 216 OR 92nd Labour Coy, 100 OR 77th Lab Coy; B Coy 1 off 80 OR North Hants Regt, 1 off 172 OR 176th Labour Coy, 23 French Civilians; C Coy Nil; D Coy 50 OR 169th Labour Coy. | Diary signed: J. B. Macdonald, Lt. Col., O.C. 3rd Bn. Can. Rly. Troops. | Companies: A Coy; B Coy; C Coy; D Coy.

- **1917-06-30 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | France** — Cold with heavy rain, N.E. wind. C.R.E. 36/22 dated 29-6-17 repeating the 3rd Canadian Division order that 3rd Canadian Division Operation Order No 109 of 25-6-17 (relief of the 3rd Canadian Division) is cancelled, and a warning order also issued that the 3rd Canadian Division has been ordered to extend its front and take over from the 4th Canadian Division. C.R.E. Office phone warning order that the 9th Field Coy C.E. would proceed into the line with the infantry brigade who will take over this new portion of the front. 3rd Canadian Division Operation Order No 33, copy No 3, of today's date received, whereby the 9th Field Coy C.E. is to relieve the 8th Field Coy C.E. in that portion of the old 3rd Canadian Division front still being retained by the 3rd Canadian Division, namely west of the railway in T.1 and T.2 respectively (Map France 36c S.W.), and to a line on the right joining the 1st Canadian Division, just east of the railway; this relief to be effected on the night of 1–2 July 1917. On 1 July 1917 the 9th Field Coy C.E. is to relieve the 12th Field Coy C.E. in the forward area between the present left boundary of the 3rd Canadian Division and the present left boundary of the 4th Canadian Division. Lieuts. Robertson, Walley, Robinson and Steeves with parties from the P.P.C.L.I., 42nd and R.C.R. Battalions continued work improving Blighty trench and erecting wire entanglements in front of strong points in the Yellow Line. The O.C. with Lieuts. Robinson, Murdie and Steeves and N.C.O.s and sappers from Nos 1 and 4 Sections proceeded to the advanced billets of the 12th Field Coy C.E. and looked over the new trench area being taken over. Lieuts. Murdie and Steeves with parties of sappers proceeded out on the works with parties of the 12th Field Coy C.E. and Pioneers, 4th Canadian Division. #445695 Spr Crowley E.E. sick, sent to hospital. | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Robinson; Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. Murdie; Spr Crowley E.E. #445695. | Companies: 3rd Canadian Division; 4th Canadian Division; 8th Field Coy C.E.; 1st Canadian Division; 12th Field Coy C.E.; P.P.C.L.I.; 42nd Battalion; R.C.R.; Nos 1 and 4 Sections; Pioneers, 4th Canadian Division. | Locations: Blighty trench; Yellow Line; T.1; T.2. | Casualties: #445695 Spr Crowley E.E. sick, sent to hospital. | Movement: Relief of the 3rd Canadian Division (Operation Order No 109) cancelled; the 3rd Division to extend its front and take over from the 4th Division; the 9th Field Coy to relieve the 8th Field Coy west of the railway (T.1/T.2) and the 12th Field Coy in the forward area, both on the night of 1–2 July 1917.
- **1917-06-30 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | Partridge Island → Martello Hotel → New River, N.B. → Partridge Island** — Tactical scheme at New River: with the G.O.C.'s permission the entire battery left Partridge Island on Monday afternoon 25 June, spent the night at the Martello Hotel, and proceeded by Canadian Pacific Railway to New River Station on Tuesday 26 June, pitching 14 tents and building camp kitchens and latrines and laying telephone lines; field tactics and company manoeuvres on Wednesday 27 June, with a route march to New River Beach; camp struck and ground cleaned up on Thursday 28 June, the battery entraining at 5 o'clock for West St. John and the Martello Hotel, and returning to Partridge Island on Friday 29 June. The trip was made without any casualties. See also the letter of 27 July 1917 below. | Locations: Martello Hotel; New River Station; New River Beach. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Partridge Island → New River (25–29 June 1917) → Partridge Island.

- **1917-07-02 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Chateau-de-la-Haie, France** — Fine and warmer, N.E. wind. C.R.E. 6/6 dated 2-7-17: the 123rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion will carry on maintenance and digging of communication trenches from rear to front line. The 3rd Canadian Division provisional defence scheme was received, and notice from the C.R.E. 3rd Canadian Division that orders to move today had been cancelled. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No 36: the 8th and 9th Field Companies will move independently on 3 July to new billets at Chateau-de-la-Haie Area. Lieut Walley with 1 N.C.O. and a party of Sappers proceeded to Chateau de la Haie to take over the billets of the 12th Field Coy C.E. The O.C. attended 9th Bde Hqrs and conferred with the Corps Water Supply Officer. | People: Lieut Walley. | Companies: 123rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion; 8th Field Coy; 12th Field Coy C.E.; 9th C.I.Bde; 3rd Canadian Division. | Locations: Chateau-de-la-Haie; Cyril dump. | Movement: Move to Chateau-de-la-Haie ordered for 3 July.

Calvert to look after this area, and calling on the D.D.M.S. Canadian Corps, then to the Canadian Corps Sports in the afternoon. | People: A/Cpl. Bond; Pte. Calvert. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-07-02 | No. 1 Canadian Veterinary Hospital | France** — 32 animals admitted; 1 died; 27 transferred C.A.D. [uncertain — following words illegible]. | Casualties: 1 died.
- **1917-07-02 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Yesterday being Sunday, Dominion Day was not celebrated until today, when the Canadian National Festival was duly honoured; Sir Arthur T. Sloggett, K.C.B., K.C.M.G., was present at the sports and expressed himself keenly interested in the hospital Orchestra of thirty members, who played various selections for the assembled guests. | People: Sir Arthur T. Sloggett.
- **1917-07-03 | 17th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Witley Camp, Surrey** — 6.30 am No. 3 Section proceeded to entrenching area for field engineering; 12.15 pm [uncertain] Nos. 2 and 4 Sections; 7–8 am range finding, 8–10 scouting, 10–11 semaphore, 11–12 mechanism and immediate action; No. 4 Section 1–2 pm drill (light tripod), 2–3 immediate action with box respirators, 3–4 indication and recognition, 4–5 discussion of Tactical Scheme No. 10.

Received aeroplane photographs showing part of light railway which has been camouflaged; photos show work is well hidden except a continuity of line still showing, now to be obviated by painting the track different colours. Construction of the new line at Lestrem now reported as complete as to grading; 6¾ miles of track has been laid. | Companies: A Coy.

- **1917-07-04 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather fair bright and warm with thunderstorm. This unit is being provided with cotton overalls and they are badly needed. Up to present have experienced difficulty in obtaining connection with Army Telephone lines but today received promise of connection with A.D.L.R. exchange to be put in at once.

- **1917-07-13 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin / Trouville / Bethune / Ecurie / Thelus, France** — Weather fair very warm. Survey party of this unit engaged on light railway work at Trouville rejoined unit. 2 OR proceeded to school of cookery Bethune. 10 a.m.: Ecurie yard, a main transhipping station from broad gauge to light railways, was shelled today for first time; shelling delayed work in yard till noon. No damage to L.R. tracks and little damage to broad gauge. Thelus district was shelled heavily today and SE line broken in two places. Made request to XIII Corps that this unit be supplied with Corps orders.

- **1917-07-18 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather cloudy with showers and thunder. Received enquiry from H.Q. C.R.T. regarding the provision of rifles for the personnel of this unit; replied that the present issue of 25 rifles per company be increased to 50 rifles per company for use of men in most forward part of light railways and against aeroplanes — a full issue would be considered an encumbrance and a hindrance to the work. One officer admitted to F.A. suffering from gastritis. The attached labour required by this unit in future is shown on Appendix I, which does not include Lestrem work. | Appendix I: Distribution of skilled and unskilled labour for maintenance, First Army — A Coy 212 skilled (Major Barber), territory Laurel Loop to Vimy via Portsmouth, Territorial, Thelus–Ecurie; B Coy 212 skilled (Major Stewart), territory Barlin–Savy, Hersin–Aix Noulette, Ablain Branch, Carency Branch; C Coy 160 skilled (Major Mackenzie), territory Camblain Jc. to St. Catherines via Maroeuil & Artillery Corner; D Coy 212 skilled (Major Duff), territory Roclincourt Jc.–Arleux Bailleul, Gavrelle, Roclincourt Branch; Artillery Corner (Lt. Advised B Coy that they were to take over maintenance of line from Barlin to Verdrel on Monday 23rd inst. from A Coy and turn over portion of line from Camblain to Ecoivres to C Coy. | Appendix II: letter E-3-1627 (1 August 1917) from O.C. to O i/c 3rd Div. McCrae and Elder, officers i/c of the Medical and Surgical Divisions, the evacuation was personally supervised and promptly done; orders issued that the Field Medical Card of any patient likely for special evacuation should be filled up and signed in readiness, the Wardmaster to leave a list of selected cases in the ward and clothing to be drawn for all cases for evacuation as soon as so classified. | People: Lt-Col J. - **1917-07-27 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | Partridge Island, St. John, N.B.** — Special remarks letter of 27 July 1917 (Major, C.O., to the C.S.O., N.B. Troops) reporting the week ending 30 June 1917: the full account of the New River tactical scheme — the battery left Partridge Island on Monday afternoon 25 June, lodged at the Martello Hotel, entrained for New River Station on Tuesday 26 June, pitched 14 tents, built camp kitchens and latrines, marked out water facilities and gave instruction in constructing a model camp; the signalling class laid telephone lines and established signalling stations the same day; field tactics and company manoeuvres on Wednesday 27 June, with a route march to New River Beach; camp struck and cleaned up on Thursday 28 June, the battery entraining at 5 o'clock for West St. John and the Martello Hotel, and returning to Partridge Island on Friday 29 June; the trip was made without any casualties, the expenses (except rations) being borne by the battery. | Locations: Martello Hotel; New River Station; New River Beach. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Partridge Island → New River → Partridge Island, 25–29 June 1917.

Received advice regarding a proposed move from this area. | Appendix IV: Summary of work for July 1917 — broad gauge lines NIL; narrow gauge: miles located 12.48, graded 12.37, grade repaired 1.00, track laid 12.38, ballasted 12.69, surfaced 17.04; average miles maintained 88.59; O.R. C.R.T. daily on construction 480, attached labour 537, O.R. C.R.T. daily on maintenance 393; casualties from enemy weapons: officers NIL, O.R. 1; track relaid 7 miles. | Diary signed: J. B. Macdonald, Lt. Col., O.C. 3rd Bn. Can. Rly. Troops.

O'Connell proceeded to 1st Canadian Division, A.D.M.S. 2nd Canadian Division, and O.C. Canadian Cavalry Brigade respectively. Agenda (filed this day): Major L. J. Rhea's pathological findings on Pte McGuigan, 2nd Royal Innis Fus, the third patient to die from the enemy's new gas shell (gassed 21 July, admitted 26 July, died 2 August); Lt-Colonel J. M. Elder's summary of the hospital's surgical work; a report by Lt-Colonels John McCrae and John M. Elder and Major L. J. Rhea on enteric inoculation; and Major Rhea's Laboratory Report. | People: Capt R. D. Moyle, Capt W. E. Guest, Capt J. I. O'Connell, Pte Wm. J. McGuigan, Maj L. J. Rhea, Lt-Col J. M. D. Parsons and 2 other ranks admitted to hospital sick. | People: Lieut J. D. - **1917-08-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Marles-les-Mines, France** — Weather: cloudy and dull, S.W. wind. - **1917-08-09 | 18th Battalion | Bouvigny** — Night of 9/10 August: 4th Brigade was relieved in the Laurent sector by 6th Brigade; A and B Coys were relieved by the 27th Canadian Battalion and C and D Coys in Brigade support by the 31st Canadian Battalion, relief complete at 3.30 am, and the battalion moved to billets at Bouvigny village; on roll-call the 5 men left in No Man's Land were found not to have returned as reported, so a party under Lieut Dougall went up again, found the cellar empty, and on returning located the men at the Right Coy HQ of the 27th Canadian Battalion, having found their own way in. | People: Lieut T. R. Dougall. | Companies: 27th Canadian Battalion; 31st Canadian Battalion; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Movement: Laurent Sector → Bouvigny.
- **1917-08-09 | 18th Battalion | Laurent Sector** — In conjunction with the 20th and 21st Canadian Battalions the 18th raided the enemy's front-line trenches, the whole raiding party under Lt-Col L. E. Jones; zero hour 4.15 am, artillery support very good; the 18th's parties penetrated 100 yards into the German lines, capturing no prisoners but inflicting many casualties and obtaining valuable information on enemy trenches, wire and dug-outs; the battalion's casualties were 4 other ranks killed and 24 slightly wounded, all wounded returned safely; the raiding party was 35 men of C Coy under Lieut H. B. Johnson and 65 men of D Coy under Lieut D. Northcombe and Lieut C. J. Spencer; Lieut Spencer and 7 other ranks, one wounded, were unable to get back in daylight and remained in a demolished cellar all day; Lieut Spencer and one man found their way in during the early night and, assisted by Lieut T. R. Dougall, searched the whole area but could not re-locate the cellar, and the 5 remaining men were reported by 4th Brigade HQ to have come in and reported to another regimental aid post. | People: Lieut-Col L. E. Jones; Lieut H. B. Johnson; Lieut D. Northcombe; Lieut C. J. Spencer; Lieut T. R. Dougall. | Companies: 20th Canadian Battalion; 21st Canadian Battalion; C Company; D Company.

- **1917-08-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Marles-les-Mines, France** — Weather: rain with bright intervals. 3rd Cdn Division Wire G.352 received, confirming the C.R.E.'s instructions for this company to march to Camblain Abbe for manoeuvres. As per orders the O.C. detailed two sections with transport etc. to report to and come under the orders of the O.C. Vanguard (Lt/Col. Sharpe, O.C. 116th Bn). Lieuts. West and Walley with Nos 4 and 2 sections with section transport moved off from camp and passed the starting point of the Vanguard (Fork Road at W.16.c.3.8) at 9.10 a.m. The Vanguard consisted of the 116th Infantry Bn, 43rd Inf. Bn, 2 sections of the 9th F.C.C.E. and one bearer section of the 8th Field Ambulance. The remainder of the company under command of the O.C. marched past the above-mentioned starting point with the Main Guard at 10.20 a.m.; the order of march of the Main Guard being the 58th Inf Bn, 9th C.I.B. H.Qs, so-called Major Sykes's Bde C.F.A. and the 9th F.C.C.E. (less two sections) and two bearer subdivisions of the 8th Field Ambulance. The enemy were represented by the 52nd Bn Infantry. Manoeuvres were held in the Chateau de la Haie area, extending to the east to Carency. Late in the afternoon the manoeuvres were cancelled by reason of the continuous rainfall. The G.O.C. 3rd Cdn Division addressed O.C.s of units, adjutants and company commanders, reference manoeuvres. The company returned for the night to billets (being huts in Maronil Bouche). Verbal orders received from the Bde Major, 9th C.I.B., for the 9th F.C.C.E. to return to Marles-les-Mines on 12 August; this was confirmed by wire B.M. 265 of the 9th C.I.B. | People: Lt/Col. Sharpe; Lieut. West; Lieut. Walley; Major Sykes. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 4 Section; 116th Infantry Bn; 43rd Inf. Bn; 8th Field Ambulance; 58th Inf Bn; 9th C.I.B.; Bde C.F.A.; 52nd Bn Infantry. | Locations: Camblain Abbe; Chateau de la Haie; Carency; Maronil Bouche. | Movement: Two sections with the Vanguard from 9.10 a.m.; remainder with the Main Guard from 10.20 a.m.; company returned to billets at Maronil Bouche for the night.
- **1917-08-11 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | New River, N.B.** — Battery moved from Partridge Island to New River, N.B., and is under canvas there (move between 4 and 11 August; no date for the move itself is given). Great improvement apparent in all branches, particularly march discipline; work along the lines practised at Halifax in artillery training, plus preparing camps and billets, camp sanitation, choosing gun positions and bringing the battery into action; much time to physical training and route marches (Pocologan and return 7 miles, New River Beach 6 miles, Lepreau and return 9 miles); signalling class on all-day visual and telephone schemes; lecture on camp life by Major Wetmore and Capt. Bennett; heavy rain, camp overhauled and drained; health of the men excellent. A duplicate copy of the 11 August letter is filed as the following page. | People: Maj. Wetmore; Capt. Bennett. | Locations: New River; Pocologan; New River Beach; Lepreau. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Partridge Island → New River (under canvas), between 4 and 11 August 1917.

- **1917-08-14 | 18th Battalion | Outposts Line** — Night of 14/15 August: C and D Coys moved into assembly positions along the outpost line and A and B Coys came up into support; at 4.25 am the 18th, in conjunction with other units of the 1st and 2nd Canadian Divisions, attacked the enemy lines to capture and consolidate the enemy support line (Chicory Trench); the attack was entirely successful, the objectives occupied 26 minutes after zero hour with some 65 prisoners captured (165 R.I.R.); Lieuts C. H. Biscoe and L. A. Bis[uncertain]ell were wounded just as they reached the enemy front lines; on the right, by arrangement with the 21st Canadian Battalion, the battalion held Chicory Trench, and on the left pushed posts forward and controlled the railway cutting; consolidation proceeded rapidly, but at 2.30 pm the enemy made a very strong bombing attack on the left of the battalion and the right of the 21st Battalion and succeeded in entering a portion of the newly won trenches. | People: Lieut C. H. Biscoe; Lieut L. A. Bis[uncertain]ell. | Companies: 1st Canadian Division; 2nd Canadian Division; 21st Canadian Battalion; C Company; D Company; A Company; B Company. | Locations: Chicory Trench.

- **1917-08-15 | 18th Battalion | Outposts Line** — During the enemy counter-attack Lieut A. A. McLean was killed by a sniper while leading men up the Lens–Bethune road; Lieut T. R. Dougall and men of the scout section made a reconnaissance patrol forward about 300 yards from the newly won position and returned with valuable information and a complete Minenwerfer crew of 20 men as prisoners; three platoons of the support companies were sent up to reinforce D Coy, and Lieut J. M. Fisher prepared a counter-attack with the 21st Battalion, launched at 5 pm with artillery assistance, which easily regained the lost trenches and captured 10 prisoners; Sgt M. Dunsford very gallantly led his men to the attack and, although severely wounded shortly after entering the enemy front line, continued to direct his men by his example until the objective was reached, refusing to be carried out until the more serious cases had been evacuated; Lieut G. C. Brachin [uncertain] arrived as reinforcement. | People: Lieut A. A. McLean; Lieut T. R. Dougall; Lieut J. M. Fisher; Sgt M. Dunsford; Lieut G. C. Brachin [uncertain]. | Companies: 21st Canadian Battalion; D Company. | Locations: Lens–Bethune road.

- **1917-08-15 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Lens Sector** — Operations as per Operation Order No. 18 a complete success; zero hour 4.25 am and all guns went over as directed and arrived at their objective, with the exception of No. 3 Gun of "D" Section, knocked out by a direct hit by a shell; a new gun was procured from Ordnance and a new team made up and the gun put in position before nightfall; reports in the O.C.'s hands at 10 am from Lieut. Much, O.C. "C" Section, and Lieut. Creighton, O.C. "D" Section; 3 O.R. killed and 7 O.R. wounded; enemy tried desperately to retake the ground with heavy counter-attacks every few minutes but to no avail; "A" & "B" Sections under Lieut. [uncertain] and Lieut. MacLaren carried on with the barrage as laid down in barrage instructions, expending 75,000 rds S.A.A., under Major Bassevi, O.C. 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy., Group Commander. | People: Lieut. Much; Lieut. Creighton; Lieut. [uncertain]; Lieut. MacLaren; Major Bassevi. | Companies: "C"/"D" Sections; "A"/"B" Sections; 14th Cdn. M.G. Coy. | Casualties: 3 O.R. killed; 7 O.R. wounded; No. 3 Gun, "D" Section knocked out by a direct shell hit.

- **1917-08-15 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — Barrage fire on enemy positions maintained 5–10 a.m., about 460 rounds fired; at 8 a.m. enemy heavily shelled our rear position, No. 1 gun put out of action, and we had 4 casualties: Gnr. Fairfowl killed, Bdr. Horwill [written "Norwill" on the casualty page], Gnr. Altham and Gnr. Mitchell W.H. severely wounded; C.O. desires to place on record the coolness and devotion to duty shown by the officer, NCOs and men of this section at a time when it was essential that fire should be maintained; names of Lieut. Hoare, Cpl. Troop and Bdr. Horwill submitted to H.Q. for consideration of award in connection with the above action. | People: Gnr Fairfowl; Bdr. Horwill [written "Norwill" on the casualty page]; Gnr Altham; Gnr Mitchell W.H.; Lieut. Hoare; Cpl. Troop. | Casualties: Gnr Fairfowl killed; Bdr. Horwill, Gnr Altham, Gnr Mitchell W.H. severely wounded.
- **1917-08-15 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Marles-les-Mines, France** — Weather: bright with a shower of rain. Company engaged in rifle exercises. No's 3 and 4 sections under Lieuts. Robertson and West proceeded to the area north of Bruay and carried out scheme No 1, laid down by the C.R.E., being siting and laying out strong points and a defended locality. Nos 1 and 2 sections proceeded with instruction in musketry and extended order drill under Lt Jones. Lt Murdie still engaged in supervising the construction of divisional horse standings under the direction of the C.R.E. and Q Branch, 3rd Cdn Division H.Q. Information received from the office of A.A.G. 3rd Echelon that 20 days' extension of leave had been granted to Lieut. Robinson of this company, to cover the period which he spent in hospital in England while on leave. The 8th C.I.B. marched through Marles-les-Mines this morning en route for the Chateau-de la Haie area to carry on manoeuvres. The 123rd Pioneer Bn moved out from billets today in Marles-les-Mines for the same purpose. | People: Lieut. Robertson; Lieut. West; Lt Jones; Lt Murdie; Lieut. - **1917-08-16 | 18th Battalion | Outposts Line** — About noon Lieut Dougall, 1/Sgt C. K. Routley and 19 other ranks crossed the railway cutting and went forward along Cotton Trench to N.13.b.5.0, where they were fired upon from Aloof Trench and could see it heavily held; turning about, they met enemy parties on the way back and were practically surrounded, but Lieut Dougall sent up his artillery signals and under cover of the fire succeeded in returning to the lines with only one casualty; there was no unusual activity during the remainder of the day. | People: Lieut T. R. Dougall; Sgt C. K. Routley. | Locations: Cotton Trench; Aloof Trench.
- **1917-08-16 | 18th Battalion | Outposts Line** — Evening of 16 August: the battalion was ordered to attack the enemy trenches between the Lens–Grenay and Lens–St Pierre railways in conjunction with the 4th Canadian Division, the objective being Aloof Trench and thence to connect to Chicory Trench on the left; two platoons of A Coy were detailed for the attack and one platoon of B Coy in support; a reconnoitring patrol of Lieuts Dougall, MacDonald and Sloan and 4 N.C.O.s covered the ground, but on their way back a bomb was thrown into the party which killed Lieut MacDonald and wounded Lieut Sloan; on Lieut Dougall's report the plan was changed from a frontal attack to pushing across the railway cutting from the trenches at N.13.b.2.2 as soon as the artillery barrage lifted, the later plan being sanctioned by the Brigade, with zero hour set for 4.35 am. | People: Lieut MacDonald; Lieut Sloan; Lieut T. R. Dougall. | Companies: 4th Canadian Division; A Company; B Company. | Locations: Aloof Trench; Chicory Trench.

- **1917-08-17 | 18th Battalion | Outposts Line** — In the early hours the assaulting platoons were taken forward, and while giving assistance in placing the men Lieut Dougall was mortally wounded by an enemy 5.9 shell; the attack went forward at the proper time and occupied Cotton Trench from N.13.c.6.9 to N.13.b.2.2 in the face of heavy enemy shell fire, and after disorganization on the withdrawal of troops on the right, the parties were re-organized and posts established, Amulet Trench being found untenable; Capt J. B. Bell, Adjutant, sent up further supplies of bombs and left Capt D. A. G. Parsons in charge, and the position was completely secure by 7.30 am; Lieut W. H. Fenton and a small party searched the houses in the railway cutting and reported the enemy building Aloof Trench to the left to connect with Cinnabar Trench, which the artillery acted on; from 2 to 4 pm forward posts reported the enemy assembling in houses on either side of the Lens–Bethune road and in Chicory Trench, and the artillery took very effective action; at 4 pm a small enemy party of about 15 men attempted to raid the posts at N.13.b.65.40 but were driven off without casualties to the battalion; Lieut H. B. F. Ralph was admitted to hospital sick. | People: Lieut T. R. Dougall; Capt J. B. Bell; Capt D. A. G. Parsons; Lieut W. H. Fenton; Lieut H. B. F. Ralph. | Locations: Cotton Trench; Amulet Trench; Aloof Trench; Cinnabar Trench; Chicory Trench; Lens–Bethune road.

- **1917-08-18 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | New River, N.B.** — Signalling class under C/Sergt. Dean, O.S.S., making good progress: a discarded telephone line from New River Station to New River Beach, four miles, was overhauled and repaired, field wires run to the camp grounds, and the line connected to the N.B. Telephone Company's line, establishing communication between the camp and all points; the telephone company complimented the class and furnished an instrument; examinations of the present class begin 21 August. Route marches gradually increased to about 20 miles per day, with very little fatigue shown apart from a few blistered heels. On Thursday 16 August the battery marched 16 miles to the town of St. George, welcomed by the Mayor (Mayor Lawrence), the St. George Band and the citizens, dinner in the vestry of St. Mark's Church, addresses by the Mayor, Dr. H. I. Taylor, M.L.A., and Rev. Mr Spencer, a half holiday, a visit to the Imperial Theatre (Mr Frawley), photographs, and entrainment back to camp; the first body of troops seen in the town for 30 years — the town once maintained a company of artillery of the 3rd Regt. C.G.A., the mother unit of this battery. | People: C/Sergt. Dean, O.S.S.; Mayor Lawrence; Dr. H. I. Taylor, M.L.A.; Rev. Mr Spencer; Mr Frawley. | Locations: New River Station; New River Beach; St. George; St. Mark's Church. | Casualties: none (a few blistered heels only). | Movement: route march New River → St. George (16 miles), 16 August 1917.

- **1917-08-28 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Weather: cloudy and cold, S.W. wind. 9th C.I. Bde Operation Order No 112, copy no 9, dated 28-8-17 received, whereby the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion of the 8th C.I. Bde will relieve the 52nd Battalion in Brigade Reserve on the night of 28–29 August 1917. Lieut. Walley with No 2 Section and parties from the 116th Battalion digging trench, making dugout reconnaissance and patrolling the railway (Report #11). Lieut. Jones with No 3 Section and a party from the 116th Battalion digging a new trench and making a reconnaissance of dugouts (Report #12). Lieut. Sharp with the Brigade wiring party erecting barbed wire entanglements, double apron fence 3-strand (Report #13). Lieut. West with a party of sappers laying out practice trenches with tape for the use of the 52nd Battalion, 9th C.I. Bde. Sappers at rear billets making signs for the forward area, building stables and cleaning and painting wagons. #502767 Corp Douglas, R.C., killed by shell fire, was buried today in the Military Cemetery at Fosse 10, R.a.d. v.4 [uncertain] (Sheet France 36 B), Row C, Grave 43. The O.C., his section officer, and orderly officer, with the majority of men of No 2 Section, attended the funeral. Capt. Vipond, Chaplain, 58th Canadian Infantry Battalion, performed the funeral services. #502543 Dvr McRae, J.A. sick, sent to hospital. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Sharp; Lieut. West; Corp Douglas, R.C. #502767; Capt. Vipond; Dvr McRae, J.A. #502543. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 9th C.I. Bde.; 2nd C.M.R. Battalion; 8th C.I. Bde.; 116th Battalion; 52nd Battalion; 58th Canadian Infantry Battalion. | Locations: Fosse 10. | Casualties: #502767 Corp Douglas, R.C. buried at Fosse 10 Military Cemetery, Row C, Grave 43; #502543 Dvr McRae, J.A. sick, sent to hospital. | Movement: 2nd C.M.R. - **1917-08-28 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — A tremendous gale, almost amounting to a cyclone, did considerable damage — no buildings suffered, but the outer roofs of 20 hospital marquees are beyond repair and the remaining tents are strained; a tree had to be removed by the Canadian Red Cross Hut, and the Engineers' hut within the grounds had its side blown in; neighbouring camps were in a worse plight, and no less than 521 patients were admitted from No. 32 Stationary and 54 and 55 General Hospitals, a constant stream from 1.30 p.m. (two entries, diary-text pp. 2 and 3, combined here). | Movement: 521 patients admitted from No. 32 Stationary, 54 and 55 General Hospitals.

- **1917-08-30 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Weather: dull and cloudy with showers, west wind. The O.C. with Lieuts. Case tried and the prisoner returned to the company under close arrest pending the decision of the court. Lieut. Walley returned to the advanced billets. Lieut. Walley with No 2 Section and parties from the 116th Battalion cleaning out and deepening trench, digging a support line, making dugout reconnaissance and repairing track (Report #17). Lieut. Jones with No 3 Section and a party from the 116th Battalion cleaning and deepening trench; also sappers repairing the railway (Report #18). Lieut. Sharpe with the Brigade wiring party carrying in material and salvaging wire (Report #19). Sappers at rear billets making and painting signs for the forward area, building horse stables and making cooking utensils for the 9th Trench Mortar Battery. #504581 Spr Ayliffe, H.T. wounded by shell fire on the works, evacuated. | People: Lieut. Walley; Lieut. Steeves; Spr Taylor, C.M. #541841; Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Sharpe; Spr Ayliffe, H.T. #504581. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 116th Battalion; 9th Trench Mortar Battery. | Locations: Barlin. | Casualties: #504581 Spr Ayliffe, H.T. wounded by shell fire on the works, evacuated; #541841 Spr Taylor, C.M. tried by Field General Court Martial, returned under close arrest pending the court's decision.

- **1917-08-31 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Avion** — Medium trench mortar fired 9 rounds on wire at N33 a 5-7, unable to continue firing owing to heavy retaliation; heavy trench mortar fired 6 rounds at Red Chateau (N33a 40-70) obtaining one direct hit and 7 rounds at N33 b 1-8 to N33 b 3.6, rear of the railway embankment, with good bursts; Forward Headquarters 3rd C.D.T.M.B.'s at Bois de la Chaudiere; month-end summary: the medium and heavy batteries' work for August was very satisfactory despite heavy rain-fall nearly all month and emplacements in the outpost line; tasks were wire-cutting for raids, destroying machine-gun emplacements and enemy trench mortars; seven officers from the 4th C.D.T.M.B.'s were attached to the batteries for instruction | People: 4th C.D.T.M.B.'s (seven officers, unnamed) | Companies: none | Casualties: one sergeant wounded, who will probably lose the use of his right hand (reported in the month-end summary; no name, date or battery given) | Movement: Forward Headquarters 3rd C.D.T.M.B.'s at Bois de la Chaudiere

- **1917-09-01 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Cool and cloudy with showers, west wind. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No 43 Copy No 3 dated 1-9-17 received: the 1st Canadian Division will relieve the 3rd Canadian Division from the Lens-Bethune Road (exclusive) to Nestor trench (inclusive), complete by 6 a.m. 6-9-17; the 9th Field Coy C.E. and the Brigade Wiring party to be relieved by the 3rd Field Coy C.E., and to relieve the 210th Field Coy R.E. in the Right Brigade area of the 21st English Division, Neuville-St-Vaast area, marching there on 6 September and clear of present billets by 9 a.m. Lieut Steeves with one Sapper explained to officers and men of the 52nd Battalion the method [uncertain] of operating mobile charges for a pending raid. Lieuts Walley and Jones did a successful night's work putting across a new jumping-off trench opposite Cinnibar trench under bright moonlight. Lieut Sharpe's wiring party erecting barbed wire entanglements. Sappers at Rear Billets cleaning and painting wagons. Reports #1, #2, #3. | People: Lieut Steeves; Lieut Walley; Lieut Jones; Lieut Sharpe. | Companies: 3rd Field Coy C.E.; 210th Field Coy R.E.; 52nd Battalion; 1st Canadian Division; 3rd Canadian Division; 21st English Division; Brigade Wiring party. | Locations: Lens-Bethune Road; Nestor trench; Cinnibar trench; Neuville-St-Vaast. | Movement: Company to march to Neuville-St-Vaast area 6 September.

- **1917-09-04 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Bouvigny → Vimy (Aux Ritz)** — Company paraded at 7 a.m. and moved to new Transport Lines near Aux Ritz Corner (A 8 c), arriving at 12 noon; rest of day spent preparing for the trenches; on night 4th/5th the 9th Can. M.G. Coy relieved the 92nd Machine Gun Company (Imperial unit): A Section and B Section guns at Aintree, Ascot, Auk and Buffalo; B Section in reserve at Condor; C Section at Badger and Bulldog; D Section in reserve at Coyote and Cobra; one B Section gun at Antelope under command of 15th Can. M.G. Coy; relief completed by 12 midnight; between 12 and 1 a.m. enemy fired a considerable number of gas shells, causing quite a few casualties among the infantry during a relief, and 2 O.R. of ours wounded gassed; gas shells had a mustard odour; strength going into the line 10 officers, 178 O.R. and 44 attached O.R. - **1917-09-06 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Day very quiet except four heavy shells on the Lens-Arras Road at 2.15 p.m.; at 5.30 p.m. enemy struck a dump away to our left which burned for about an hour; at 7.30 p.m. our artillery on the left started a bombardment which quietened down in five minutes; at 9.55 p.m. enemy artillery opened up on targets near Avion, heavy at first but soon slackening; scattered shelling near our batteries during the night. (O.O. No. 75, dated 6 Sep 1917, attached: 8 guns to relieve 8 guns of 10th Can. M.G. Coy on night 7th/8th.) | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-09-06 | 9th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Alberta) | Bramshott, England** — Net decrease 10 Other Ranks. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-09-06 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — At about 1 a.m. enemy carried out an unprecedented bombardment of this village — gas shell, H.E. and shrapnel fired into all parts of the village, undoubtedly the heaviest bombardment yet experienced by this battery; lasted till 3.45 a.m.; considered at least 5,000 gas shells fired, some of very large calibre; owing to effective precautions taken, casualties small — only 3 men gassed: Grs. Brunton and Thorne, and 1st A.M. Lee of the R.F.C.; at about 7 a.m. an enemy shell burst on roadway near battery position, and Gr. E. F. Martin was killed; two S.O.S. calls responded to and fire put on to Lens area at 7.35 and 8.20 p.m. | People: Gnr Brunton; Gnr Thorne; 1st A.M. Lee (R.F.C.); Gnr E. F. Martin. | Companies: R.F.C. | Locations: Lens. | Casualties: Gnr E. F. Martin killed; Gnr Brunton, Gnr Thorne and 1st A.M. Lee (R.F.C.) gassed.
- **1917-09-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | A.14.a.5.6. (Sheet 51 B), France** — Bright and warm in the forenoon, rain in the afternoon and evening, S.W. wind. Company fell in at 7 a.m. and marched off at 7:30 a.m. to new billets at A.14.a.5.6., near Aux Reitz Corner, arriving 11:50 a.m.; billeted in huts. Sappers and wiring party marched over Lorette Ridge; cyclists and Drivers proceeded by road via Gouy Servins and Villers-au-Bois Station. The 9th Field Coy C.E. took over officially the work in the forward area at 6 a.m. On arrival the Company took over the Rear Billets of the 210th Field Company R.E. at A.14.a.5.6., of inferior quality, consisting of "Bivies" [uncertain] and several Armstrong huts, horse standings unfinished. Major Robertson proceeded to Advanced Hqrs of the 9th Infantry Brigade and conferred with the Brigade Major 9th C.I. Bde re works; no work arranged as the 9th C.I. Bde had not yet completed relief. Lieut West and sappers proceeded to the forward area to locate dugouts for Advanced Billets; the Brigade southern boundary was altered at the last minute to permit the 210th Field Coy R.E. to retain their Advanced Billets. | People: Major Robertson; Lieut West. | Companies: 210th Field Company R.E.; 9th Infantry Brigade; 9th C.I. Bde. | Locations: Aux Reitz Corner; Lorette Ridge; Gouy Servins; Villers-au-Bois Station. | Movement: Bully-Grenay → A.14.a.5.6. near Aux Reitz Corner; company took over work in the forward area at 6 a.m.

- **1917-09-07 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Vimy** — Day very quiet; at 5.30 p.m. enemy shelled our anti-aircraft battery (13 pr.) in S 18 c, then shortened range into T 17 d and T 13 a; at 9 and 9.30 p.m. about 15 H.E. shells between S 24 a and S 32 a; during the night 9.30–11 p.m. reliefs carried out: four guns of B Section relieved four guns of No. 4 Section 10th Can. M.G. Coy in Keene group, four guns of D Section relieved four guns of No. 3 Section 10th Can. M.G. Coy in Bluenose group, one C Section gun at Badger replaced a B Section gun in Buffalo; posts on both sides shelled during the night; at 12.01 a.m. enemy shelled our front line 500 yards to the left; 1–2 a.m. two or three heavy explosions in or near Avion; aircraft active on both sides. (After Order to O.O. 75, dated 7 Sep 1917, attached.) | Companies: B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

C.R.E. 152/37 received giving policy of work: several new communication trenches, improving fire trenches, erection of screens, construction of mule tracks and establishment of certain R.E. dumps. Instructions later that Brigade wirers are to wire the front-line trench of the 9th C.I. Bde. No dugouts found in the forward area; sappers making excavations in the "Brown" line trench for the Company to live in in the Advanced area. | People: Major Robertson. | Companies: 9th C.I. Copy of 3rd Canadian Division Division G.903 [uncertain] received advising of intended projection of gas by E. Special Company R.E. on the front of the 31st Division on the night of 9–10 Sept 1917. O.C. attended the Brigade Major 9th C.I. Bde and arranged working parties; the 800 men required are not available from the 9th C.I. Bde, the Reserve Battalion being some distance in the rear. O.C. proceeded to Advanced Billets in the old German Gun (B.1.c.95.60) to live. Lieut West with No 4 Section and infantry party (wirers) making living trench and living quarters. - **1917-09-13 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — Sir Henry Burdett, K.C.B., K.C.V.O., author and statistician, visited the hospital and was very much interested in the work and the remarkable statistics furnished him, and the small mortality considering the numerous cases that have passed through the hospital; all ranks warned that disciplinary measures will be taken against any member of the unit reported for gambling (entry split across diary-text pages 1–2). | People: Sir Henry Burdett.

- **1917-09-14 | 18th Battalion | Avion** — At 1.00 pm the battalion moved off from Villers Camp on route to the trenches in front of Avion, halting at La Targette corner for supper and resting before passing over the top of Vimy Ridge in the order A, B, C, D and HQ, guides being picked up at La Folie Farm about 8.30 pm from the 1st C.M.R., whom they were relieving; the enemy artillery was extremely quiet and the relief was completed without casualty at 11.45 pm, with A Coy in the front line, B and C Coys in close support and D Coy in reserve, Battalion HQ in gun pits and dugouts in the Bois de Chaulière, a former German big-gun position. | Companies: 1st Canadian Mounted Rifles; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: La Targette; La Folie Farm; Bois de Chaulière; Vimy Ridge. | Movement: Villers Camp → Avion.

- **1917-09-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | A.14.a.5.6. (Sheet 51 B), France** — Clear and cool, S.W. wind. O.C. attended the C.R.E.; policy and progress of work discussed. On instructions received, no new front-line trench (or jumping-off trench) will be constructed as originally intended — this work is abandoned; also wiring in front of the proposed trench is abandoned. 9th C.I. Bde Operation Order No 118 Copy No 11, dated 13-9-17, received: on the night of 15th + 16th Sept 1917 the 116th Battalion will relieve the 58th Battalion in the front line. The 31st Division on the right of the 9th C.I. Bde discharged gas from gas projectors at about 12.40 a.m. today into the enemy lines just north of Fresnoy. Information received that Lieut H.D. Robertson, injured and evacuated to England, has been struck off the strength of this Coy from 20-8-17. Lieut West with No 4 Section and party from the 58th Battalion digging trench and working on Ammunition dugouts. Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section and parties from the 43rd and 116th Battalions digging a new trench and deepening and widening trench. Lieut Murdie with sappers from 2 and 3 Sections and infantry parties deepening and widening trench and erecting screen. Lieut Sharpe with wiring party taking material forward. Reports #29, #30, #31, #32. | People: Lieut H.D. - **1917-09-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line and Close Supports** — At 4.00 a.m. a small enemy patrol approached our wire and was driven off by our Lewis guns; at 2.00 p.m. an enemy plane flying very low patrolled the lines for about an hour and was engaged by our Lewis guns and machine guns without result; at 11.30 p.m. Brigade notified that the Division had picked up the enemy message "EVERYTHING READY", indicating a raid, and all ranks stood to; a heavy barrage fell on the immediate left at 2.00 a.m. and an intense bombardment north of Lens at 4.30 a.m.; at about 9.30 p.m. another small enemy patrol was observed outside the wire but our patrol found no trace of them; another enemy dump in rear of Mericourt was exploded by our artillery at about 6.00 a.m. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1917-09-18 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | A.14.a.5.6. (Sheet 51 B), France** — Cloudy and cold with showers, S.W. wind. O.C. attended the Bde Major 7th C.I. Bde and the O.C. P.P.C.L.I. Battalion and made arrangements for working parties to carry on policy of work for the completion of trenches and establishment of forward dumps. The relief of the 9th C.I. Bde by the 7th C.I. Bde commenced last evening; relief to be complete tonight; working parties cut down in consequence. A party of enemy officers was observed yesterday afternoon peering at our front line through glasses. After a fifty-minute barrage [inserted: in the evening] bombardment of our front line (Totnes trench), centre and right flank of the 9th C.I. Bde, the enemy raided our trenches, capturing one wounded man and leaving behind one of his men as prisoner. C.R.E. with Adjutant called at Advanced Billets in Gun Pits. Lieut West with No 4 Section and parties from the 116th Battn cleaning, deepening and widening trenches; also completed work on Ammunition dugouts. Lieut Murdie with sappers from Nos. 2 and 3 Sections and party from the 116th Battn laying bath mats and widening trench. Lieut Sharpe with Bde. wiring party carrying material and working on dugouts. - **1917-09-21 | No. 3 Canadian General Hospital (McGill) | Boulogne, France** — The Boulogne Base Medical Society met in the hospital in the Canadian Red Cross Recreation Hut; after tea provided by the O.C. and served by the Nursing Sisters, papers were discussed by the hospital's officers — (1) yaws, cases exhibited by Major J. G. Browne; (2) treatment of infected haemothorax by operation and closure by Major J. W. Hutchinson; (3) method of examining direct smears from haemothorax cases by Major R. J. Rhea, O.C. Sappers at rear billets working on horse standings and preparing and loading material for the forward area. 3rd Canadian Division G.339, Copy No. 8, dated today, received, whereby according to instructions received from the Canadian Corps the operations now in preparation have been postponed; the 1st Canadian Division will be prepared to relieve the 4th Canadian Division, and the 2nd Canadian Division will be prepared to relieve the 3rd Canadian Division; infantry reliefs to be completed by 12 noon, 6 Oct 1917. | People: Lieut. Sproule; Lieut. - **1917-10-08 to 1917-10-18 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Cité de Caumont, France** — Major S. A. Heward proceeded on leave to England and Captain H. R. N. Cobbett took over temporary command; owing to removal of greater part of artillery from this sector, and apparent scarcity of ammunition, operations practically ceased; during this period battery did not fire more than an average of 50 rounds per diem, chiefly harassing fire; at about 11.30 p.m. on 17th, word received to move to Belgium, and at hour [uncertain] stores and kit were loaded on lorries in a heavy rain storm; battery paraded at 12.30 p.m., leaving behind a rear party of 1 officer (Lieut. E. S. Hoare) and 10 other ranks; proceeded to rendezvous at Hersin, where met by ammunition column; whole column proceeded by road through Noeux-le-Mines and Bethune to Hazebrouck, arriving about 4.15 p.m. | People: Maj. Hoare. | Locations: Hersin; Noeux-le-Mines; Bethune; Hazebrouck. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Cité de Caumont–Hersin–Hazebrouck; rear party left behind.

- **1917-10-19 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Wieltje, Belgium** — Bright and cool in the forenoon, rain in the afternoon and evening. Company fell in at 8:15 a.m. under Lieut. West, marched to Caestre, from where they proceeded by bus to Ypres and then marched to a camping ground near Wieltje (C.27.b.2.3 Sheet 28 N.W. Belgium), where canvas shelters were erected for the night. Transport moved up independently under Capt. Ross and parked near the transport lines of the 4th Field Company, N.Z. Engineers (H.1.d.9.6 Sht 28 Belgium). Major Robertson accompanied the O.C. 4th Field Company, N.Z. Engineers, over the works of this company in the forward area: the construction of a double infantry track of trench mats from the neighbourhood of St. Jean easterly, passing south of Hill 35 and Hill 37 to the top of Abraham Heights on the Gravenstafel Ridge, approximately 5 miles; work includes maintenance of the portion already constructed, parts of which are frequently destroyed by enemy shell fire. It was noted by Major Robertson that the present front line, as being taken over from the N.Z. Division by the 9th C.I. Bde, is in the same locality and approximately 100 to 200 yards ahead of the old front-line trenches occupied by the 10th Infantry Battalion in April 1915 just prior to the German attack on 22 April 1915; these trenches were being worked upon by Major Robertson, then a lieutenant in the 2nd Field Company C.E. | People: Lieut. West; Capt. Ross; Major Robertson. | Companies: 4th Field Company, N.Z. Engineers; 9th C.I. Bde; N.Z. Division; 10th Infantry Battalion; 2nd Field Company C.E. | Locations: Caestre; Ypres; Wieltje; St. Jean; Hill 35; Hill 37; Abraham Heights; Gravenstafel Ridge. | Movement: Caestre → Ypres (bus) → camping ground near Wieltje (march); transport independently to 4th Field Company N.Z. Engineers' transport lines.

- **1917-10-20 | No. 1 Company, Canadian Forestry Corps | Crecy Forest** — Retrospective narrative history of the unit (April 1915–September 1917) signed by Capt. H. Hellmuth, O.C. No. 1 Can. Forest Coy. (stamp: CRECY FOREST, L. OF C. GROUP, date 20-10-17); the narrative records the company working in Crecy Forest (chiefly beech and hornbeam), with a mill turning out road slabs and planking and charcoal burning for trench supplies, some ten kilometres of railroad to be constructed, and work likely to last eight to twelve months; it notes 15 drafts sent to the Infantry and 5 to the Royal Flying Corps since the unit received its establishment, and that the company has no connection with the Canadian Forestry Corps, formed some six to eight months after the company began operating in France; one corporal, Corpl Le Duc, has never been with his unit, being in charge of contractors at Crecy Forest (from the retrospective narrative history). | People: Capt. - **1917-10-22 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ypres, Belgium** — Dull and cloudy, N.W. wind. Policy of work: Canadian Corps G 859/2520-11 and C.R.E. 29-25 received, which includes in the work of this company the construction and maintenance of double duckboard track No. 5. The 4th Field Company, New Zealand Engineers, moved out and vacated billets in Ypres, which this company then moved into, the same being in old cellars on the north side of Ypres; they also vacated transport lines at H.1.d.9.6 (Sheet 28 Belgium) and the 9th Company C.E. horses were then moved in as per orders. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and received the policy of work and orders as to how this company is to be employed during pending operations. C.R.E. 19/9 received, under which two sections of this company are to be held in reserve and two sections employed with 100 attached infantry in pushing forward No. 5 track, as in para. 12 (c) of the instructions for the offensive; also this company to construct such crossings of the Ravebeek as desired by the G.O.C. 9th C.I. Bde. The conduct of #541907 L/Cpl. Bester, F., of this company is commended: on the afternoon of the 22nd some enemy shells struck the Wieltje road near Spree Farm and wounded a number of men; a team of horses farther up the road bolted and would have run over the wounded men but were prevented from doing so by this man, who ran forward and stopped the team regardless of his own safety. Lieut. West with 68 sappers and 200 infantry from the 58th Battalion repairing the bathmat walk (Report #16). Lieut. J.W. Baldock and 8 other ranks arrived from the Canadian Base Depot and are taken on the strength of this company as from today. #502692 Spr (A/L/Cpl) Tanner, T.M., wounded by shell fire; evacuated. | People: L/Cpl. Bester, F. #541907; Lieut. West; Lieut. J.W. Baldock; Spr (A/L/Cpl) Tanner, T.M. #502692. | Companies: 4th Field Company, New Zealand Engineers; 58th Battalion; Canadian Base Depot; 9th C.I. Bde. | Locations: Ypres; Wieltje road; Spree Farm; Ravebeek. | Casualties: #502692 Spr (A/L/Cpl) Tanner, T.M. wounded by shell fire, evacuated. | Movement: 4th Field Company, New Zealand Engineers, vacated billets and transport lines in Ypres; 9th Field Company moved into the old cellars on the north side of Ypres.

- **1917-10-23 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ypres, Belgium** — Dull and cold, west wind. The O.C. attended Brigadier Gen. Hill and the Bde Major, 9th C.I. Bde, and conferred re bridges over the Ravebeek, when four bridges to the north of the Gravenstafel road and two to the south were asked for; some of these are supposed to be now in position according to the report of the New Zealand Division. Lieut. West with two N.C.O.s reconnoitred the Ravebeek creek with an officer of the 58th Battalion and representatives of the 43rd Battalion, and the sites chosen for crossings were settled and agreed upon by these battalions. It was found from the report of the Col. of New Zealand Engineers that no possible bridges existed over this stream at supposed places. Lieut. Murdie with sappers made a special reconnaissance in the forward area and secured samples of German concrete in strong points, as directed by the C.R.E.; report and samples turned into the C.R.E. office. Lieut. Jones with 44 sappers and parties from the 5th C.M.R. Battalion laying and repairing bath mats, track No. 5 (Report #17). | People: Brigadier Gen. Hill; Lieut. West; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Jones. | Companies: 9th C.I. Bde; New Zealand Division; New Zealand Engineers; 58th Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 5th C.M.R. Battalion. | Locations: Ravebeek; Gravenstafel road.

- **1917-10-26 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Attack launched at 5.40 a.m. by 8th and 9th Can. Inf. Brigades on the Passchendaele outer defences, including Bellevue Spur; guns jumped off with the infantry as pre-arranged. On the 4th C.M.R. frontage Lieut. Searles and two guns took up positions at D 4 b, consolidating after the infantry retired and left them isolated; Searles went back, reorganised the infantry and led them forward to consolidate the crest; eight machine guns were taken from pill-boxes at D 4 b but could not be brought out. Sniping battery D 4 a: four guns under Lieut. Duthie reached D 4 a and came into action; when the infantry retired the guns were withdrawn after losing 1 officer and 2 gun crews, then two guns advanced again under Sgt. Love to defensive positions at D 4 a, later moving back to D 4 a. On the 43rd Bn. frontage Lieut. Ellis M.C. was wounded in the shoulder but carried on, getting two guns into action at D 4 d at 6 a.m.; two guns were knocked out before reaching position; Ellis was evacuated at 9 a.m., leaving guns to Pte. Scott C.H. and Pte. Gallant E. At 10 a.m. a party of enemy estimated at two companies was engaged on the Mosselmarkt–Gravenstaple Road with heavy casualties inflicted; at 4 p.m. guns engaged enemy coming up to counter-attack positions, and at the attack on the Camouflage pill-boxes guns neutralised enemy machine-gun fire and engaged escaping enemy, several surrendering. On the 58th Bn. frontage two guns under Lieut. Madgett jumped off at zero, waited about 100 yards, then on the retirement of the infantry made a stand under heavy fire until the 58th Bn. advanced over them, when they withdrew as the gun was out of action. Sniping guns D 16 b opened fire on Meetcheele and Grafh Wood until +120, firing again on 27th. Casualties: officers wounded Capt. E. I. H. Ings, Lt. M. L. Ellis, Lt. J. H. Duthie; 8 O.R. killed, 30 O.R. wounded; reinforcements 10 O.R. | People: Lieut. Searles; Lieut. Duthie; Sgt. Love; Lieut. Ellis M.C.; Pte. Scott C.H. 252201; Pte. Gallant E. 437170; Lieut. Madgett; Capt. E. I. H. Ings; Lt. M. L. Ellis; Lt. J. H. Duthie. | Companies: A Section; B Section; C Section; D Section. | Casualties: Capt. E. I. H. Ings, Lt. M. L. Ellis and Lt. J. H. Duthie wounded; 8 O.R. killed; 30 O.R. wounded. | Movement: —
- **1917-10-26 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Heaviest day since arriving in area; in conjunction with attack by 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions, fired attack barrage 6–9 a.m.; throughout day several concentration shoots and 3 calls on S.O.S. lines carried out; in all 1,031 rounds fired, gun detachments carried out tasks in excellent manner; battery position lightly shelled during period, without damage or casualties. | Companies: 3rd Canadian Division; 4th Canadian Division. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-10-26 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ypres, Belgium** — Cold with rain, east wind. The 9th C.I. Bde., with the 43rd and 58th Battalions, attacked the Bellevue Spur at 5:40 a.m. and got part of their objectives. The 8th C.I. Bde. also attacked on the left and the 4th Canadian Division on the right, each taking some objectives. Lieut. Jones with sappers from Nos. 1, 2 and 3 Sections assembled last night with 100 infantry from the 116th Battalion, prepared to push forward with the building of bathmat walk No. 5; the party waited all night and this morning the G.O.C. 9th C.I. Bde decided that, in view of the heavy fighting and casualties sustained by his brigade in the attack and the objectives gained, it was not advisable for this party to go forward. This supports the view that large parties cannot work in view of the enemy in daylight immediately after an attack unless the attack has progressed so deep as to disturb the enemy guns. Lieut. Baldock with 7 sappers and a party from the 42nd Battalion carrying bathmats and signs (Report #23). Lieut. Murdie with 8 sappers and a party from the R.C.R. carrying and laying bathmats (Report #24). Lieut. Walley returned from on leave (Report #25). | People: Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Walley. | Companies: 9th C.I. Bde.; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 8th C.I. Bde.; 4th Canadian Division; No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 116th Battalion; 42nd Battalion; R.C.R. | Locations: Bellevue Spur. | Movement: Lieut. Walley returned from leave.

- **1917-10-28 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 9 a.m. hostile shelling commenced and continued throughout day, becoming very intense between 5 and 6 p.m.; many rounds burst in battery position, but no damage done; detachments took what little cover was available, no casualties; aeroplane shoot abandoned owing to poor visibility, but 143 rounds fired on various targets and on S.O.S. lines, also concentrations (No. 5 + 9); Evasive Farm, E 8 c. 88.90, also shelled by us; many improvements made to battery position by working parties, but much remains yet to be done. | Locations: Evasive Farm. | Casualties: none.

- **1917-10-30 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | FRONT-LINE** — Passchendaele attack, zero hour 5.50 a.m.: A and C Coys in the first wave and B and D in the second attacked the BLUE line; the intermediate objective was reached but the 30-minute barrage halt let the enemy re-organise on the high ground, and C Coy under Major Prarkes took and held Vapour Farm and Source Farm with both flanks in the air while A Coy, its right flank left in the air by the 49th Battalion, was held up with severe casualties. Capt Maron (O.C. D Coy), Capt Ireland (M.O.) and Lieut Rogers were killed, Capt McGuish (replacement M.O.) was wounded and later died, and Lieuts Jones, Harold, Millar and Dunning (seriously) were wounded; casualties were estimated at about 350 by midday and 75 per cent by 1.35 p.m., and 51 unwounded German prisoners were captured at Source Farm. | People: Major G. R. Prarkes [uncertain spelling]; Capt Maron; Capt Ireland; Lieut Rogers; Capt McGuish; Lieut J. G. Jones; Lieut Harold; Major Duggan; Lieut Millar; Lieut Dunning; Lieut Hall; Capt W. J. - **1917-10-30 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 5.55 a.m. opened up on line barrage in support of further attack by 3rd and 4th Canadian Divisions; at 8.30 a.m. protective barrage fired and continued till 11.30 a.m.; No. 1 + 3 guns go out of action; S.O.S. lines re-adjusted to roads leading from Passchendaele Church, N and E, but at 1.15 p.m. firing on original protective barrage lines; attack reported very successful; Crest Farm, one of our targets, reported demolished; recommendation for M.C. forwarded to H.Q. for an officer of battery for conspicuous gallantry and devotion to duty, and recommendations for M.M. forwarded for one N.C.O. and one man, in connection with duty at Hamburg O.P. on 27th; advance party of new section (No. 3) arrived — Lieut. Starr and 25 other ranks. | People: Lieut. Starr. | Companies: 3rd Canadian Division; 4th Canadian Division. | Locations: Passchendaele Church; Crest Farm; Hamburg O.P. | Casualties: none. | Movement: advance party of No. 3 section arrived (Lieut. Starr and 25 O.R.).
- **1917-10-30 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Ypres, Belgium** — Cold with rain, south wind. Lieut. Baldock with 4 sappers and a party from the 42nd Battalion carrying bathmats (Report #32). Lieut. Steeves with a party of 6 sappers and a party from the 42nd Battalion carrying and laying bathmats; also with a party of 9 sappers, repairing bridges (Report #33). Lieut. Walley with a party of sappers from No. 2 Section attended at Hqrs R.C.R., Otto Farm, and waited from zero on, prepared to move forward with a party of 100 infantry from the R.C.R. upon receiving word from the 7th C.I. Bde to do so; this party waited until 5 p.m. today and was then cancelled by the Brigadier General, 7th C.I. Bde, there being no infantry parties available for work. The 7th C.I. Bde. attacked this morning at 5:40 and obtained part of their objectives on the Bellevue Spur; the 8th C.I. Bde. also attacked and obtained part of their objectives, the division on their left having been held up, interfering somewhat with their operations. The 4th Canadian Division also attacked along the ridge towards Passchendaele and obtained their objectives. Lieut-Col. T.C. Irving, C.R.E. 4th Canadian Division, was killed last evening by an enemy bomb in Ypres. Major Robertson and Capt. Ross attended the funeral at Brandhoek; the funeral was largely attended by O.s C. Field Companies, including three O.s C. of Field Companies (Major N.R. Robertson being one) who had served under him as lieutenants. Enemy aeroplanes bombed the vicinity of the billets; no casualties. | People: Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. Walley; Lieut-Col. T.C. Irving; Major Robertson; Capt. Ross. | Companies: 42nd Battalion; No 2 Section; R.C.R.; 7th C.I. Bde.; 8th C.I. Bde.; 4th Canadian Division. | Locations: Otto Farm; Bellevue Spur; Passchendaele; Ypres; Brandhoek. | Casualties: Lieut-Col. T.C. Irving, C.R.E. 4th Canadian Division, killed by enemy bomb in Ypres on the evening of 29 October; no casualties from the aeroplane bombing of the billets.

Creighton moving off at 6.30 a.m. and arriving at 4 p.m., while the company, less transport, entrained at Caestre at 12.45 p.m. and proceeded via Godewaersvelde and Poperinghe to the Asylum at Ypres, detraining and marching through Ypres to lines at 1.3.d.1.4 at 3.15 p.m., taking over the lines of the 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; at 5 p.m. "D" Section (1 sergeant, 1 corporal and 24 men) under Lt. H. A. McBurney moved off for the line and relieved four barrage guns of the 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy. under Lieut. Stinson at Seine Corner (D.16.d.0.80), relief complete by 9.45 p.m., reporting to Capt. Grantham, barrage group commander at Tyne Cot (D.17.a.45.20); casualties "NIL". | People: Lt. Creighton; Lt. MacLaren; Lt. H. A. McBurney; Lieut. Stinson; Capt. Grantham. | Companies: 16th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; "D" Section. | Casualties: none | Movement: Labrearde–Caestre–Ypres–Potijze area.
