- **1917-11-02 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — 28 rounds 3–3.24 am on a hostile battery at E2d 17.92; barrage at 5.55 am, 24 rounds, ceased 6.19 am; battery heavily shelled with H.E. 8-in and 4.1-in and shrapnel 7.30–11 pm, yet a night task of 50 rounds and a barrage of 22 rounds were pulled off without the loss of a single man; enemy then put over a heavy gas barrage, all ranks working in S.B.R.s. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-02 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | St. Jean → Abeele/Watou** — Day fine, light clouds, cool; transport under Lieut. Clark left lines at 8.15 a.m. for new camping ground at Trappiste Corner; company paraded at 8.30 a.m. and marched off at 8.45 a.m., arriving at the entraining point ([uncertain] asylum, Ypres) at 9.30 a.m.; entrained at 10.45 a.m., the 7th, 8th and 15th M.G. Coys also on the same train as well as the Princess Pats, 49th and 52nd Bns.; train left about 11 a.m. and arrived at Abeele at 11.45 a.m.; company marched to a farm at K 24 b, about halfway between Abeele and Watou, where billets had been arranged by Lieut. Rayner; company housed in tents except B and C Sections in a barn; transport arrived about 2 p.m. at Trappiste Corner and all was settled in the new camp late in the afternoon. | People: Lieut. Clark; Lieut. Rayner. | Companies: B Section; C Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: St. Jean → Abeele → Watou area (K 24 b).
- **1917-11-02 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 3 p.m. concentration on enemy wire at D.66.65.40, and at 4 p.m. opened up barrage fire (Varb.) [uncertain]; on these shoots 84 rounds expended; bursts of fire kept up on a line 500° east of S.O.S. line; further concentration placed on W.25.c.28 [uncertain], total 60 rounds fired; battery position heavily shelled, percentage of gas shell observed; one man, No. 2163349 Gunner J. W. Brown, reported slightly gassed and admitted to hospital, otherwise no harm done. | People: Gnr J. W. Brown (No. 2163349). | Casualties: Gnr J. W. Brown slightly gassed.

- **1917-11-03 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Day bright; at 5.05 a.m. an S.O.S. went up and "D" Section's 4 barrage guns opened fire at once, and at 5.45 and 6.15 a.m. the S.O.S. was again sent up by the battalions of the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. holding the front line, the guns firing on S.O.S. lines, several guns having fired 350 rds S.A.A. before the S.O.S. rocket reached the ground, with 13,000 rds S.A.A. expended; enemy shelling was very severe in the early morning, slackening at 8 a.m., about 75 8-inch shells falling near Seine Corner, and enemy aircraft flew low over the lines all afternoon; between 5 and 7 p.m. the enemy put down a heavy barrage with no direct hits on the trench occupied by the barrage guns, but during the bombardment attached carriers Pte. Douville G. and Pte. Davies T.E. were hit and both died of their wounds while being carried to the dressing station; during the night 4,000 rds S.A.A. were fired on Passchendaele crossroads; casualties 2 men killed. | People: Pte. Douville G.; Pte. Davies T.E. | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; "D" Section. | Casualties: 2 killed — Pte. Douville G. and Pte. Davies T.E. (attached carriers; died of wounds en route to dressing station).

- **1917-11-03 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Enemy shelled the position with 8-in from 5.30 am; S.O.S. call answered despite the shelling, 40 rounds; shoot 10 am–1.15 pm on Vocation Farm with visual observation, 50 rounds, very good results, several hits; 20 rounds 4.30–4.50 pm bursts of fire on the enemy's lines of approach; enemy came back at 5.30 pm with 5.9-in and shrapnel until 9 pm, the pole of the wireless station cut in two, no casualties; 50 rounds 9 pm–3 am on a target in V24d and [uncertain]. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1917-11-03 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Battery position again heavily shelled, large numbers of H.E. and shrapnel falling near the guns; put two bursts of fire on to a line from 100 to 300 yards east of S.O.S. lines, 36 rounds expended; also participated in 3 large concentration shoots on areas N25.c.40.90-70.90+40.50 and W25a 60-20.75-35-60.20, in which 220 rounds expended. | Casualties: none.

(2) Lieut. Jones, night of 3–4 Nov — party of 1 officer and 135 other ranks of the 3rd Battalion and 4 other ranks of the 9th F.C.C.E., 4.30–7.30 p.m., carried 140 bathmats from Bilge Dump to the dump at Abraham Heights (4 sappers remained as guard until relieved 4 Nov); and a party of 1 officer and 105 other ranks of the 123rd Battalion Pioneers and 10 other ranks of the 9th F.C.C.E., 4.30–9.00/11.00 p.m., carried 180 bathmats from the dump at Abraham Heights to the end of Track 5, replaced the centre strip on each mat ready for laying, but it was too dark for laying to advantage; route reconnoitred in advance and parts of the track repaired where broken. | People: Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Jones. | Companies: 4th Battalion; 3rd Battalion; 123rd Battalion Pioneers. | Locations: Spree Farm; Abraham Heights; Otto Farm; Bilge Dump; Track #5. | Casualties: Nil.
- **1917-11-03 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W., Belgium** — Dull, south wind. Message received from the G.O.C. 1st Canadian Corps congratulating the Canadian Corps on the success of the operations carried out by them. Great difficulty experienced pushing forward the bathmat walk, Track No 5, in the forward area: darkness and depth of mud make grading and laying bathmats very difficult, long sections already laid are frequently removed, presumably by infantrymen desiring to build bivies or on which to sleep; last night 260 yards of track in front of Abraham Heights was torn up and the mats removed, and the mats have in some cases to be carried by hand nearly four miles. Lieut. Baldock with 11 sappers and a party from the 4th Battalion carrying bathmats (Report #5). A guard of 1 N.C.O. and 3 sappers placed on the bathmats. A party of 4 sappers and 35 men from the 4th Battalion repairing the bathmat walk, Track No 5. Lieut. Jones with 15 N.C.O.s and sappers and parties from the 3rd Battalion and 123rd Pioneer Battalion carrying bathmats (Report #6). | People: Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Jones. | Companies: 4th Battalion; 3rd Battalion; 123rd Pioneer Battalion. | Locations: Abraham Heights; Track No 5.

- **1917-11-04 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Rain in the early morning; at 5 a.m. Lt. Creighton left the transport lines with a pack train of 35 animals loaded with 50,000 rds S.A.A., dumped at Seine Corner, the train returning at 8.15 a.m. with no casualties although the enemy shelled the road near Zonnebek continuously; one crew of "C" Section under Acc. Cpl. Berrick was sent up to report to Lieut. McBurney and placed at D.16.d.55.85 for anti-aircraft work, firing 1,000 rounds at enemy aircraft during the day, and one gun of "D" Section fired 500 rds S.A.A. at an enemy plane which appeared to land behind Passchendaele; during the day, on orders from Capt. Grantham, Lt. McBurney took a party of 8 men to D.11.c.90.30 and began work on a new 8-gun battery position, the party working only 15 minutes before being forced to stop by enemy shelling; between 9 p.m. and midnight 4,000 rds S.A.A. were fired on Passchendaele crossroads; in accordance with 2nd Cdn. Divl. M.G. Battn. O.O. No. 55 para. 6, "B" Section less 1 gun under Lt. Hobson relieved 3 guns of the 4th Cdn. M.G. Coy. (1 gun at D.12.a.45.00, 2 guns at D.12.c.30.70), and 1 gun of "A" Section took up position at D.12.a.30.90 under Sgt. Tingley of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy., relief complete at 10 p.m., all these guns being mobile and under Major Pearce, mobile group commander; during the afternoon the enemy fired 8 5.2-inch high-velocity shells in and about the transport lines; casualties "Nil". | People: Lt. - **1917-11-05 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Seine Corner** — Day fine; between 11.30 p.m. 4th inst. and 4.30 this morning the enemy fired about 70 high-velocity 5.2-inch rounds in and about the transport lines, wounding Pte. Larson A.P. (who died later at the dressing station), Pte. Campbell E., Pte. Dills C.E. and Pte. Landry J., while Pte. Wallace A.G. was wounded but remained on duty, and two saddle and two light draught horses were killed and one saddle and eleven light draught horses wounded; enemy aircraft were very active from daybreak all day, a pack train of 25 animals under Sgt. Christie carried 50,000 rds S.A.A. to Seine Corner, the enemy shelled the whole area heavily from 5 to 8 a.m. and shelled the area about "B" Section with heavies during the day, and in "D" Section Pte. Coaton A.C. and Pte. Barrett H. were wounded; Lce. Cpl. Sillers and 8 men of "D" Section worked all day on the new battery position while the remainder carried 33,000 rds S.A.A. to new positions; at 4 p.m. Lt. Gibson left the transport lines with two crews of "A" Section and one crew of the 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy., taking up positions with the 26th Battn., "D" Section under Lt. McBurney moved to a new position at D.11.c.30.30, and Capt. McCorkell went to advanced 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. headquarters to act as M.G. liaison officer during the operations. | People: Pte. Larson A.P.; Pte. Campbell E.; Pte. Dills C.E.; Pte. Landry J.; Pte. Wallace A.G.; Sgt. Christie; Lce. Cpl. Sillers; Pte. Coaton A.C.; Pte. Barrett H.; Lt. Gibson; Lt. McBurney; Capt. McCorkell. | Companies: "D" Section; "A" Section; 6th Cdn. M.G. Coy.; 26th Battn.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. | Casualties: 1 killed — Pte. Larson A.P. (wounded, died later at dressing station); wounded — Pte. Campbell E., Pte. Dills C.E., Pte. Landry J., Pte. Coaton A.C., Pte. Barrett H.; Pte. Wallace A.G. wounded, remained on duty; 2 saddle and 2 light draught horses killed, 1 saddle and 11 light draught horses wounded.
- **1917-11-05 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Mills Camp, Wattou Area** — Companies carried on checking up equipment; 65 reinforcements received from C.C.R.C., chiefly old men who had left the battalion at Les Brebis. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-05 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Barrage fire from 4 am on M lane east of the main Westroosebeke Road, 50 rounds to 4.50 am, then barrage in lanes M and A, 106 fuze used entirely; shoot at 2.30 pm on Venture Farm, a very strong point with a reinforced concrete pill-box, observed by Lieut H. M. Stairs, 1 O.K. in the first 30 rounds, then finished by registration, 63 rounds in all; 24 rounds 4.45–5.15 pm on barrage in battery lanes L and M; shoot of 75 rounds from 9.10 pm against Virile Farm and Vocation Farm without observation; hostile shelling below normal, a dump at Spree Farm blew up about 6.30 pm but no casualties; shelled intermittently overnight by a 4.1-in gun, no damage. | People: Lieut H. M. Stairs. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area** — Fine, scattered clouds, cool; physical drill at 6.30 a.m.; company parade in fighting kit at 9 a.m.; squad drill 10–11 a.m., spare parts gone over 11–12, new guns replacing those damaged in the fighting of 26th and 30th October tested by firing into a bank; at 1.30 p.m. divisional armourer inspected guns, two sent away for slight repairs. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 10.35 a.m. concentration placed on E9c 15.30, and similar shoot on same target at 2.55 p.m., total 42 rounds fired; barrage Y(a)(b) put up at 4.45 p.m.; in evening further concentrations placed on E7a 91.51, firing 42 rounds; harassing fire on roads leading to Wrath Farm maintained throughout the night, 120 rounds fired; intermittent enemy shelling on battery position 1.00–3.00 p.m. | Locations: Wrath Farm. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Abraham Heights, Belgium [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work reports (sheets 8, 10–11): (1) Lieut. Baldock — carrying party, Spree Farm to the cache at Abraham Heights, 7.30–10.30 a.m.; 8 sappers and 100 men of the 15th Battalion; 200 bathmats carried and deposited in the cache beside Track #5, about 500 bathmats in the cache at 10 a.m.; the officer in charge of the infantry party reported at 7.30 a.m. instead of 6 a.m. and said he was unable to find Pommerin Castle [uncertain]. (2) Unnamed officer [uncertain] — bridge work on Track 5, 2.30–9 p.m., 1 officer and 12 other ranks: bridge D.10.a.8.2., 30 bathmats of approach repaired; bridge D.10.a.25.55, 28 bathmats of approach repaired both sides with tape guides placed; bridge D.10.a.20.75, 8-foot span rebuilt with 12 bathmats of approach and tape guides both sides; bridge D.10.a.1.8., 20 bathmats of approach repaired with tape guides; 20 new bathmats [uncertain]. (3) Lieut. Murdie — 2 sappers, 4–7 p.m., laid 120 yards of bathmat on No. 5 Track at Abraham Heights where mats had been lifted and carried off (D.15.b.5.6. to D.10.b.25.10 [uncertain]); and 1 officer, 3 other ranks and 100 men of the 123rd Battalion, 2–9 p.m., laid 250 yards of tape from D.4.C.88.40 to D.4.d.45.85, and carried 350 bathmats from the cache on Abraham Heights to D.9.b.98.65. and laid them towards D.10.a.5.9. for about 700 yards — a new, shorter alternative route across the Ravebeek, passing between Bridges 1 and 2 north of Gravenstafel Road and joining a path crossing D.10.a.2.6., because Crossing #4, where Track 5 crossed, was being shelled regularly; beyond the end of the bathmat walk the ground was fairly firm and would provide fairly good walking. | People: Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: 15th Battalion; 123rd Battalion. | Locations: Spree Farm; Abraham Heights; Pommerin Castle [uncertain]; Ravebeek; Gravenstafel Road. | Casualties: Nil.
- **1917-11-05 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W., Belgium** — Dull, S.W. wind. Instructions received from the C.R.E. that one section of the 7th Field Company C.E. would work on bathmat track No 5 under the supervision of the 9th Field Coy C.E., commencing tomorrow; the O.C. conferred with the O.C. 7th Coy re their employment; they are to carry on with repair work of the said track. A party of 6 sappers repairing portions of the bathmat walk damaged by shelling; also a party of 3 sappers preparing bathmats for the carrying party. Lieut. Baldock with 8 sappers and an infantry party from the 15th Battalion carrying forward bathmats (Report #8). Lieut. Steeves with 12 sappers repairing bridges (Report #9). Lieut. Murdie with 8 sappers and a party from the 123rd Pioneer Battalion laying tape and carrying bathmats (Report #10). | People: Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: 7th Field Company C.E.; 15th Battalion; 123rd Pioneer Battalion. | Locations: Track No 5.

- **1917-11-06 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Rain at intervals; a pack train of 25 animals under Lt. Creighton carried 50,000 rds S.A.A. to Seine Dump; at 6 a.m. the 1st and 2nd Cdn. Div'ns. attacked and captured Passchendaele, the 26th Cdn. Inf. Battn. of the 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde. attacking on the right, and the 3 crews under Lt. Gibson advanced with the first wave of the 26th Battn., taking up positions of 2 guns at D.6.d.50.65 and 1 gun at D.6.d.55.05 with no casualties in reaching their objectives, but shortly afterwards Lt. Gibson was wounded by shrapnel in the jaw and over the eye and Sgt. Chamberland took charge; enemy fire was intense all day, in "D" Section Pte. Green H. was killed and Pte. Cook P.R. wounded, barrage guns responded to 3 S.O.S. calls, firing 60,000 rds S.A.A. during barrage and S.O.S. calls and 6,000 rds in harassing fire at night, enemy artillery fire was very heavy from 8 p.m. to midnight, "B" Section on the right was heavily shelled but escaped casualties till 3 p.m., when the right position was practically destroyed, both guns being blown out of the trench, Pte. Osborn A.J. being killed and two of the crew buried but soon dug out by Pte. Wilton R.J. and Pte. Bruce R.B., and the left crew suffered heavily, Pte. Butler T. being killed and Pte. McGrouther R. and Pte. Drysdale wounded. | People: Lt. Creighton; Lt. Gibson; Sgt. Chamberland; Pte. Green H.; Pte. Cook P.R.; Pte. Osborn A.J.; Pte. Wilton R.J.; Pte. Bruce R.B.; Pte. Butler T.; Pte. McGrouther R.; Pte. Drysdale. | Companies: 26th Cdn. Inf. Battn.; 5th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; 2nd Cdn. Div.; "D" Section; "B" Section. | Casualties: 3 killed — Pte. Green H., Pte. Osborn A.J., Pte. Butler T.; wounded — Lt. Gibson (shrapnel, jaw and eye), Pte. Cook P.R., Pte. McGrouther R., Pte. Drysdale.

- **1917-11-06 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Guns in action continuously; three heavy barrages 6 am–2.45 pm, 244 rounds, against Vine Farm, Vocation Farm and V30b; strong point in W19c, cross roads at W25a, Waist Farm and main roads north-east of Waist Farm also engaged; two S.O.S. calls answered; No 2 Gun out of action twice but got into good order; 11 casualties in the early part of the day, 4 by H.E. and 7 by shrapnel, 3 later returned to duty, 8 named men sent down the line; 523 rounds expended, the heaviest day of the month. | People: Gnr Stevenson (303567); Gnr J. Owens (1260577); Sgt E. C. Cornell (346891); A/Bdr D. D. Campbell (346821); A/Bdr D. Ryan (346808); Gnr C. J. LeBlanc (303371); Gnr J. Hoag (314745); Gnr E. F. Boulding (1250701). | Companies: — | Casualties: 11 wounded (4 by H.E., 7 by shrapnel); 3 returned to duty, 8 sent down the line
- **1917-11-06 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area** — Physical drill at 6.30 a.m.; company parade not called at 9 a.m. owing to rain; sections carried on in tents studying mechanism of the gun, various stoppages and immediate action; rest of day spent quietly; four O.R.s promoted acting corporals and 1 O.R. acting sergeant to replace casualties in recent operations. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-06 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — In conjunction with attack by Canadian Divisions this morning at 6 a.m., opened up with attack barrage, immediately followed by protective barrage, maintained up to 3 p.m.; S.O.S. call promptly responded to at 5.40 p.m. and continued until situation again quiet; enemy shelled battery position and vicinity heavily for greater part of day, but did no damage. | Companies: Canadian Divisions. | Casualties: none.

[uncertain]; a guard of 4 sappers for the bathmat dump at Abraham Heights to 12 noon. Party was caught in an enemy barrage and only 30 of the party got up to the job. | People: Lieut. Walley. | Companies: 123rd Battalion. | Locations: Duck Lodge; Abraham Heights. | Casualties: Three Pioneers (unnamed).
- **1917-11-06 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W. (Ypres)** — Dull and colder with rain, S.E. wind. This company's billets [uncertain] were shelled early this morning by an enemy high-velocity gun; no casualties. The First Canadian Division attacked at 6 a.m. today eastward along the Bellevue Spur, capturing the "Green" line and all objectives. The Second Canadian Division also attacked at the same time, capturing the Green line and all objectives, including the village of Passchendaele. German prisoners were marching back by the company billets in Ypres at 8:30 a.m. Lieut. Walley with a party of sappers and a party from the 123rd Pioneer Battalion laying bathmats and taping for a new bathmat walk (Report #11). | People: Lieut. Walley. | Companies: First Canadian Division; Second Canadian Division; 123rd Pioneer Battalion. | Locations: Bellevue Spur; Passchendaele; Ypres. | Casualties: No casualties (billets shelled).

- **1917-11-07 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W.** — Cold with rain, S.E. wind. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. with a representative of the 8th Field Coy C.E., when orders were received for this company to carry on with the construction of a bathmat walk from the forward slope of Abraham Heights, branching off from track No 5 at I.9.d.8.6, Sheet 28 Belgium, easterly across Marsh Bottom and along the southern slope of Bellevue Spur towards Passchendaele. The First British Division to take over track No 6 by reason of a change in boundary between the First British Division and the First Canadian Division. The 8th Field Coy C.E. were given the work of continuing the left branch of Track No 5 past Wolf Copse and double-bathmatting the same from Abraham Heights forward. One section of the 7th Field Coy C.E. is put on the maintenance of track No 5 to the west of Abraham Heights. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. and arranged working parties for tomorrow. Copy of a wire received from the 3rd Canadian Division dated 7-11-17, addressed to the C.R.E., received today, advising that the Military Medal has been awarded to #541721 L/Cpl. Curtis, G.E. and #502880 Spr (A/L/Cpl) Shepherd, W., for the good work and assistance rendered by these N.C.O.s to Lieut. West in the construction of the bridges over the Ravebeek on the night of 24–25 Oct 1917. Lieut. Sproule, 6 sappers and a party from the 14th Battalion carrying bathmats; 1 N.C.O. and 3 sappers guarding bathmats (Report #12). A party of 7 sappers preparing bathmats for carrying and repairing the bathmat walk. | People: Lieut. Sproule; L/Cpl. Curtis, G.E. #541721; Spr (A/L/Cpl) Shepherd, W. #502880; Lieut. West. | Companies: 8th Field Coy C.E.; 7th Field Coy C.E.; First British Division; First Canadian Division; 14th Battalion. | Locations: Abraham Heights; Marsh Bottom; Bellevue Spur; Passchendaele; Wolf Copse; Ravebeek; Track No 5; Track No 6.

- **1917-11-08 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — At 9 a.m. relieved 35-2 Siege Battery and took up counter-battery work; position now in D.25.b 88.23 on Zonnebeke Road; position extremely poor, very many disadvantages; tasks of minor nature, several bursts of fire, and harassing fire on roads and enemy positions in Moorslede; subjected to very heavy enemy shelling, approximately 1,200 rounds of H.E. and shrapnel, but little damage resulted; only one gun in action, others out for temporary repairs. | Companies: 35-2 Siege Battery. | Locations: Zonnebeke Road; Moorslede. | Casualties: none. | Movement: relieved 35-2 Siege Battery; position D.25.b 88.23.

May as F.O.O. observing from the open under heavy shelling until he had observed 28 bursts and obtained good registration, 50 rounds in all; barrage 4.30 pm, ceased after 12 rounds; 56 rounds 6.5–7 pm on barrage; harassing fire kept up until 4.30 am mostly on strong points and lines of approach; enemy shelled back areas heavily with 6-in and 9.2-in naval guns, the square in front of the Cloth Hall receiving much attention; no casualties. | People: Lieut F. Div., at 10.30 a.m.; the General congratulated both companies on their excellent work during the 3rd Divisional attack on Bellevue Spur on 26th and 30th October and the 9th Coy on holding the new line for some time without infantry support; during the afternoon a warning order came in of a move tomorrow; limbers packed as far as possible; during the evening the movement order arrived — move to 'D' Camp just beyond St. Jean; O.C. - **1917-11-10 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Passchendaele sector** — Combined 9–12 November tour entry: during the whole of this tour the officers and men held this part of the line under the most severe conditions possible; great difficulty was experienced in evacuating casualties from the front line to R.A.P.s and dressing stations; the front-line trenches were subjected to frequent barrages and the rear country was also heavily shelled and bombed; the supports were reached by a series of tracks, being trench-mat walks, and rations had to be carried by mules up these tracks, each track being subjected to continual shellfire, the transport and ration parties escaping with the loss of 3 men killed and 1 mule which fell off the duckboard track and, owing to the depth of the mud, had to be shot; splendid work was done by the battalion stretcher bearers in tending and evacuating the wounded.

- **1917-11-10 | 5th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Field** — Rain during the day; at 6.05 a.m. the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. of the 2nd Cdn. Div., in conjunction with the 1st Cdn. Div. gaining all their objectives while the 1st Imperial Division on the left was held up, the 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde. meeting no resistance but the 1st Cdn. Div. meeting considerable; the barrage guns fired 14,000 rds S.A.A. during the attack and 4,500 rds on the S.O.S. call at 3 p.m., and during the afternoon rain fell heavily and the positions were nearly washed away. | People: — | Companies: 4th Cdn. Inf. Bde.; 1st Cdn. Div.; 1st Imperial Division. | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Mills Camp, Wattou Area** — Gas helmet and squad drill in the morning; practice attacks on pill boxes by platoons in the afternoon. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Watou area → E Camp, St. Jean** — Everyone up by 4.30 a.m.; it had rained heavily through the night and rain came down again heavily as the company marched off about 6.30 a.m.; met convoy of busses on the Watou-Abeele road and embussed at K 18 b; the 7th, 8th and 15th M.G. Coys also moved by this convoy, and the 43rd, 1st C.M.R. Bns., [uncertain] T.M.B. and Bde. HQ; by 7.45 a.m. all settled in the busses to the Asylum in Ypres, where they left the conveyances and marched to camp — D Camp was too small for the four companies and E Camp was allotted to us (C 27 d); housed partly in huts and partly in tents; transport left lines at 9.15 a.m. via Poperinghe, Vlamertinghe and Salvation Corner, arriving about 2 p.m.; ground deep with mud and water, but everyone settled by dark with a good hot dinner; many heavy guns in the vicinity active through the night, some enemy shelling a few hundred yards in our rear. | Casualties: none. | Movement: Watou area → E Camp, St. Jean (by bus via Ypres).
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — One gun opened up in response to S.O.S. call at 2.50 p.m., 10 rounds fired; several bursts of fire placed in W.26.d, about 45 rounds expended; eventually stopped by enemy neutralising fire, unusually heavy; no damage done, gun went into action again later; during night maintained fire on enemy roads, gun positions, etc. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W.** — Dull with rain, south wind. The First Canadian Division attacked this morning at 6:50 a.m. and gained its objective, contour 62, north of Passchendaele Village. The First British Division also attacked at the same time north of the First Canadian Division, and gained some of their objectives. The O.C. attended a conference at the C.R.E. office and received instructions to have Meetcheele and Bellevue reconnoitred with a view to building two defended localities for the protection of Bellevue Spur. The O.C. also attended the G.O.C. and Brigade Major, 9th C.I. Bde., at Wieltje and conferred with them re the type of defended localities desired by the 9th Brigade, who are to occupy them. Lieut. Steeves with 8 sappers and a party from the 123rd Pioneer Battalion carrying and laying bathmats (Report #17). Lieut. Murdie with 4 sappers reconnoitring bridges and strong points. 9 sappers preparing stakes for the bathmat walk and repairing the bathmat walk. [Interlineated line, partly illegible: the 9th C.I. Bde. moves forward today from an uncertain area to the Wieltje area.] | People: Lieut. Steeves; Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: First Canadian Division; First British Division; 9th C.I. Bde.; 123rd Pioneer Battalion. | Locations: Passchendaele; Meetcheele; Bellevue; Bellevue Spur; Wieltje.
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Meetcheele, Belgium [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work report (sheet 22, Lieut. Murdie; filed out of order, second page on p. 50 before the first page on p. 51): 1 officer and 5 other ranks, 7.00 a.m.–3.30 p.m.; 200 yards of 2-strand fence erected from D.5.c.8.5 to D.5.b.20.05, locality D, per the map (scale 1:2500) of the Meetcheele S.P. [uncertain] scheme issued by the 3rd Canadian Division. The Meetcheele [uncertain] area was heavily shelled from 9.30 a.m. to 1.30 p.m., so it was impossible to work in the neighbourhood of D.5.b.8.2.; several enemy planes watched the area for a considerable time, and no party was available from the garrison in the area, the 42nd and R.C.R. Battalions, as those men were on duty forward of the area. | People: Lieut. Murdie. | Companies: 42nd Battalion; R.C.R. | Locations: Meetcheele [uncertain]. | Casualties: Not stated.
- **1917-11-10 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | West St. John → Partridge Island, St. John, N.B.** — Good work done by the working party on Partridge Island during the week; the remainder of the battery was moved back to the Island on Wednesday and Friday, where it is hoped training in gunnery may now be carried out if permission is granted to dismount one of the 4.7 Q.F. guns (travelling carriage) for practical work (letter of 10 November 1917). Diary: route march, physical training, sections 1 and 2 moved to Partridge Island, sections 3 and 4 moved back. | Casualties: none. | Movement: West St. John → Partridge Island (7 and 9 November 1917).

- **1917-11-11 | 185th Battalion | Witley Camp, Surrey** — Church parade in the Battalion Mess Room. Inspection by [uncertain] O.C.
- **1917-11-11 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Passchendaele sector** — Combined 9–12 November tour entry: during the whole of this tour the officers and men held this part of the line under the most severe conditions possible; great difficulty was experienced in evacuating casualties from the front line to R.A.P.s and dressing stations; the front-line trenches were subjected to frequent barrages and the rear country was also heavily shelled and bombed; the supports were reached by a series of tracks, being trench-mat walks, and rations had to be carried by mules up these tracks, each track being subjected to continual shellfire, the transport and ration parties escaping with the loss of 3 men killed and 1 mule which fell off the duckboard track and, owing to the depth of the mud, had to be shot; splendid work was done by the battalion stretcher bearers in tending and evacuating the wounded.
- **1917-11-11 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin / Lebuquiere, France** — 1st Army cool and fine; 3rd Army raining. HQ CRT requested names of N.C.O.s and O.R.s for promotion in two additional Railway Construction Battalions being formed. Timber forwarded from Arras depot for tent floors for C & D Coys. Orders to prepare to hand over 20 miles and 5 sappers to the new 11th & 12th Battalions. Lieut. R. P. Williams [uncertain] of B Coy awarded the Military Cross. | People: Lieut. R. P. Williams [uncertain] (Military Cross). | Companies: B Coy.

- **1917-11-11 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — No early barrage, day fairly quiet; 10-round shoot on a farm in V19b 90.20 and a 75-round shoot 1.30–4 pm on a farm in V24d 30.95, both very good; heavy rain all day; gas bombardment around the battery position 10.30 pm–midnight, guns kept in action with all ranks wearing gas masks, no casualties. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-11 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | E Camp, St. Jean** — Fine today with one or two light showers; accommodation made more comfortable, men cleaned up revolvers and rifles in the morning; enemy shelled the area intermittently during the day with H.V. shells and shrapnel; the 15th Cdn. M.G. relieved 8 guns each by the 13th and 3rd [uncertain] in Battery No. 5 (D 11 a) and Battery No. 6 (D 5 c); four guns of the 8th [uncertain] relieved four guns of the 3rd [uncertain] in Battery No. 7 (D 5 c), and four guns of the 7th [uncertain] relieved four guns of the 13th [uncertain] in the same battery; Capt. - **1917-11-11 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Moorslede subjected to 16 rounds rapid fire at 6.45 a.m.; no other targets during the day; from 9 p.m. onwards through the night harassing fire kept up on enemy positions at E3a 20.5 and E26.5-6; battery position again subjected to heavy enemy fire, secured direct hits on "pillboxes" in which detachments had taken cover; as a result 2 casualties (shell shock) — A/Sgt R. J. Taylor and Gnr H. Spinney; billets also subjected to hostile shelling and one shell smashed in a cellar used as telephone cabinet; as a result one casualty, Gunner M. R. Jones, and communication to group and battery temporarily broken; Lt. A. C. Kray [uncertain] proceeded on leave to England this date. | People: A/Sgt R. J. Taylor; Gnr H. Spinney; Gnr M. R. - **1917-11-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W., Belgium** — Cloudy with showers, N.E. wind. Lieut. Walley with a party of sappers reconnoitred the Bellevue and Meetcheele areas with a view to constructing defended localities. C.R.E. 19-81, with a copy of the 3rd Canadian Division outline of the scheme of defence being taken over by the 3rd Canadian Division, received today, whereby the 8th Field Coy C.E. will relieve the 9th Field Coy on the construction of bathmat track No 5; the 9th Field Coy C.E. is to take on the construction of two defended localities at Meetcheele and Bellevue with two sections, one section to be available for works at 3rd Canadian Divisional Hqrs and the other section in reserve. Upon orders from the C.R.E., four drivers and four pack mules were supplied today to the 3rd Canadian Division Pack Train for work with them. 3 sappers laying tape for the extension of the Right Southern branch of track No 5. The neighbourhood of this company's billets was shelled again this morning by an enemy H.E. gun. | People: Lieut. Walley. | Companies: 8th Field Coy C.E.; 3rd Canadian Division. | Locations: Bellevue; Meetcheele; Track No 5.

J. Gander, Capt V. M. Eastwood M.C., Lieut J. N. Mowbray, Lieut E. C. [uncertain], Lieut J. F. Perkins, Lieut W. E. Mitchell and Lieut W. S. Caldwell (gassed). | People: Capt W. J. Gander; Capt V. M. - **1917-11-13 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Night harassing fire continued to 5 am; morning barrage at 5.15 am; Howitzer No 249 received from the workshop and set up, No 3 Gun dismounted as the foundation was too poor, the gun having sunk into the soft ground; 81 rounds from 10.35 am on the farm at V24d 30.95, stopped at 4 pm by an S.O.S. call; enemy laid a violent barrage on our line around Passchendaele Ridge intending a large counter-attack, the artillery opened fire and the bombardment continued until 5.57 pm, the counter-attack failed, the artillery credited with responding so quickly and effectively to the S.O.S.; 100 rounds overnight on the farm and roads in V24d 30.95. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | St. Jean, X Camp** — Weather fine and mild; company bathed in the morning 9–11 and 2–3 in the afternoon, baths small but all put through and received a change of underclothes; day uneventful, a little shelling by the enemy of our camp area and in Ypres. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

- **1917-11-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W., Belgium** — Cloudy, S.W. wind. Warning order received from the C.R.E. of the probable relief of the 3rd Canadian Div. Engineers by the Divisional Engineers of the 8th British Division. The enemy heavily shelling the forward area all day, and barrage fire in the evening. Order from the C.R.E. to hold working parties going out in the evening on account of enemy shelling; infantry carrying parties having received instructions from the 3rd Canadian Div. not to proceed forward. Lieut. Sproule and party proceeded forward to meet carrying parties who turned up and carried on with the work as arranged (Report #18). Lieut. Baldock with 18 sappers building a fence and repairing a foot bridge at the Yser Canal (Report #19). | People: Lieut. Sproule; Lieut. Baldock. | Companies: 3rd Canadian Div. Engineers; 8th British Division. | Locations: Yser Canal.

- **1917-11-14 to 1917-11-19 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — No guns arrived from workshop yet; opportunity taken to improve battery position and commence a new one; work frequently interrupted by hostile shell fire, and during this period two small cartridge dumps blown up; no other damage done and no casualties caused; letters of appreciation received from G.O.C.R.A. Canadian Corps (Army Commander's appreciation of artillery's splendid work in the Passchendaele operations) and from General Commanding 2nd Army, Gen. H. Plumer — "I should be glad if you would express to all Brigades, Groups and Batteries of Artillery who have served in the 2nd Army throughout the offensive operations this summer + autumn, my appreciation of the splendid work they have done — I fully realise how arduous this work has been. I know that they have suffered heavy losses, and have had to remain in action under the most trying circumstances for very long periods — They have never flinched or abated their efforts for a moment but have steadily continued to overcome all difficulties, and as a result they have contributed very materially to the success achieved." | People: Gen. H. Plumer. | Companies: Canadian Corps; 2nd Army. | Casualties: none.
- **1917-11-14 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W., Belgium** — Clear in the forenoon, cloudy in the afternoon, S.W. wind. 9th C.I. Bde. Operation Order No 129, copy 12, dated 14-11-17, received today, whereby the 9th C.I. Bde. is being relieved by the 7th C.I.B. in the front line on the night of 14/15 Nov 1917. C.R.E. 19-28, giving extracts from 3rd Cdn Division Operation Order No 139 dated 13th inst., received, whereby the 8th British Division, less artillery, will relieve the 3rd Canadian Division in their present sector on the night of 17/18 Nov 1917; the Divisional Engineers and 123rd Pioneer Battalion being relieved under arrangements made between the C.R.Es concerned, transport to move by road. Extracts from table "B", 3rd Cdn Division Operation Order No 139, received, whereby the 9th Field Coy, 7th Field Coy and 123 Battalion are in the 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade group for the purpose of marching out. The O.C. conferred with the Brigade Major, 7th Brigade, re work by garrisons of defended localities "C. & D.", and arranged for parties for tomorrow. Trestle wagons of this company, with teams and drivers, have been working steadily each day hauling material under the direction of the C.R.E. representative at Vlamertinghe R.E. Park. Lieut. Baldock with 17 sappers erecting a wire fence along the Yser Canal bank, the Paymaster having fallen in last night and [uncertain — interlineated words illegible] (Report #20). A party of 12 sappers preparing stakes and wire for carrying forward. | People: Lieut. Baldock. | Companies: 9th C.I. Bde.; 7th C.I.B.; 8th British Division; 3rd Canadian Division; 123rd Pioneer Battalion; 7th Field Coy; 7th Canadian Infantry Brigade. | Locations: Vlamertinghe R.E. Park; Yser Canal. | Movement: 8th British Division to relieve the 3rd Canadian Division on the night of 17/18 November 1917.

- **1917-11-16 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Morning barrage at 6.30 am, 46 rounds to 7.35 am; nearly the whole day taken up by a shoot on Venison Farm in V24d 30.90, 150 rounds, finished 6 pm; S.O.S. calls at 6.58 pm and 7.5 pm, 23 rounds each on V24b 90.15; 100 rounds overnight into Venison Farm; hostile shelling very quiet. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1917-11-16 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Passchendaele** — Fine, mild; rations brought up by carrying party; just after getting a gun into position last [uncertain] at D 6 b the shelter containing Pte. Burnett and Pte. McGregor was hit with a shell and both were killed; Pte. Shields of B Section was slightly wounded by a shell falling near the position; during the day the gun crew in position V 30 c was put out of action by shell — Ptes. McLean, Boyle and McNounn were wounded and gun and equipment lost; crew at Waterloo brought up to replace them and placed in position a short distance from the old position; shelling of the forward area pretty heavy all day, and the Meetcheele–Bellevue Road so constantly shelled there is very little of it left; during the evening the right flank of the Corps on our left advanced without artillery preparation and captured Vocation Farm by a surprise attack. | People: Pte. Burnett; Pte. McGregor; Pte. Shields; Pte. McLean; Pte. Boyle; Pte. McNounn. | Companies: B Section. | Casualties: Pte. Burnett and Pte. McGregor killed; Pte. Shields slightly wounded; Ptes. McLean, Boyle and McNounn wounded. | Movement: —
- **1917-11-16 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | I.8.a.4.4., Sheet 28 N.W.** — Dull with showers, south wind. Copy of 3rd Cdn Division Operation Order No 140, dated 15th inst., received, whereby the 3rd Canadian Division will continue its move concentrating in the St. Hilaire area, First Army, according to the table; the division upon arrival to be held in First Army Reserve. The move from the present Corps area to St. Venant to be in accordance with orders from Q. Branch, 3rd Cdn Division, and from St Venant to the St Hilaire area by G.O.C. Brigades; the 9th Field Company C.E. is in the 7th Infantry Brigade group for the purpose of this move. 3rd Cdn Division Q/S/A/3/11/12 of the 16th inst. received, whereby, inter alia, the transport of the 9th Field Coy C.E., being in No 2 Group of 7th Brigade Group, is to move under the orders of Capt. Ross to Caestre on 18 Nov 1917. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No 45 of the 15th inst. received, whereby on the 17th inst. the 9th Field Coy C.E. is to hand over their billets to the 15th Field Coy R.E. and to march to Vlamertinghe, and to hand over their work on the night of 17–18 Nov 1917 to the 2nd Field Coy R.E. An advance party with an officer of the 2nd Field Coy R.E. reported at the advanced billets of this company and were furnished guides from this company to the billets of the 8th Field Coy C.E., which they are taking over. The O.C. 2nd Field Coy R.E. also called on the O.C. 9th Field Coy C.E., and the works being carried on by this company were explained and arrangements for taking over by the R.E. of the works discussed. Information received that a farm at Vlamertinghe (V.4. c.2.6, Sheet 28 N.W. Belgium) will be available for the transport of field companies while in the Caestre area. Lieut. Baldock with 14 N.C.O.s and sappers repairing [uncertain] at the Yser Canal (Report #24). | People: Capt. Ross; Lieut. Baldock. | Companies: 3rd Canadian Division; 7th Infantry Brigade; 15th Field Coy R.E.; 2nd Field Coy R.E.; 8th Field Coy C.E. | Locations: St. Hilaire; St. Venant; Caestre; Vlamertinghe; Yser Canal. | Movement: Company transport to Caestre on 18 November under Capt. Ross; company to march to Vlamertinghe on 17 November.

Baldock. | Locations: Yser Canal. | Casualties: Not stated.

- **1917-11-17 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Vlamertinghe, Belgium** — Dull and colder, S.W. wind. The O.C. attended the C.R.E. re final handing over. A party of the 15th Field Coy R.E. called at the advanced billets and inspected the same. Sappers of the 9th Field Coy C.E. marched from billets at Ypres to the Hop Factory, R.E. Park, Vlamertinghe, independently under their section officers, leaving Ypres at 9:30 a.m.; transport reported from the transport lines and moved off with the sections with equipment. Billets were arranged for the company in the Hop Factory temporarily. The 15th Field Coy R.E. took possession of the company's advanced billets. Lieut. Walley accompanied two officers of the 2nd Field Company R.E. over the works in the forward area, explaining the location of the proposed defended localities; maps and plans of these localities having been handed over by the O.C. to the O.C. 2nd Field Coy R.E. The O.C. with two N.C.O.s remained at Ypres during the day, rejoining the company at Vlamertinghe in the evening. | People: Lieut. Walley. | Companies: 15th Field Coy R.E.; 2nd Field Company R.E. | Locations: Ypres; Hop Factory, R.E. Park, Vlamertinghe. | Movement: Ypres → Vlamertinghe (Hop Factory, R.E. Park).

- **1917-11-19 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | St. Jean → St. Floris** — Fine, light clouds, mild; company moved off from X Camp about 9.30 a.m. and embussed near Asylum Corner, Ypres, about 11 a.m., the 7th [uncertain] moving at the same time; taken by busses to St. Vevant via Bailleul and Hazebrouck, arriving about 4 p.m.; a guide took us to St. Floris where we billeted for the night; transport joined us there. | Casualties: none. | Movement: St. Jean → St. Floris (by bus via Bailleul, Hazebrouck).
- **1917-11-19 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Havreskerque, France** — Cloudy and dull. The company fell in under Major Robertson and moved off at 8:15 a.m. and marched by way of the Vlamertinghe–Ypres Road to Kruisstraat, where they embussed on lorries with other units of the 7th Infantry Brigade group; nine lorries being allotted to this company. Leaving about 12 noon, the company proceeded by way of Dickebusch, Kemmel, Locre, Bailleul and Merville to Havreskerque, where it debussed and marched to billets in farm houses on the Merville Road just west of le Sart. The transport under Capt. Ross marched today from Hondeghem, where they had remained overnight, to billets near le Sart. Major Robertson rode to 7th C.I. Bde. Hqrs. at Robecq in the evening for orders. 7th C.I. Bde. appendix "B" to 7th C.I. Bde. Operation Order No 122, 19th inst., received, whereby the 9th Field Coy is to pass the starting point P.26.c.20.00, St Venant outskirts, at 8:15 a.m., following the 7th Field Coy C.E., and to proceed by any route except the Busnes–Lillers Road to la Tiemard, St Hilaire area. | People: Major Robertson; Capt. Ross. | Companies: 7th Infantry Brigade; 7th Field Coy C.E.; 7th C.I. Bde. | Locations: Kruisstraat; Dickebusch; Kemmel; Locre; Bailleul; Merville; Havreskerque; le Sart; Hondeghem; Robecq; St Venant; Busnes–Lillers Road; la Tiemard; St Hilaire. | Movement: Vlamertinghe → Kruisstraat by march, then by lorry via Dickebusch, Kemmel, Locre, Bailleul and Merville to Havreskerque; transport Hondeghem → billets near le Sart.

- **1917-11-21 to 1917-11-27 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Billets [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix training program (sheet 25), week ending 27 November 1917: 21 Nov — inspection of kit and improvement of billets (1st day in billets); 22 Nov — morning squad drill, section drill, saluting, physical drill and gas drill, afternoon sports; 23 Nov — morning squad drill, saluting, section drill, physical exercise, manual exercise and gas drill; 24 Nov — morning manual exercise, gas drill, saluting and bayonet instruction, afternoon leave (Saturday); 25 Nov — church parade (Sunday); 26 Nov — morning physical drill, saluting, gas drill and a lecture on guard duties and guard mounting, afternoon sports competition between No. 1 and [other] sections, football; 27 Nov — morning gas drill, physical drill, bayonet instruction and a lecture on grenades, afternoon sports (section competition). | Locations: Billets. | Movement: 1st day in billets, 21 November 1917.
- **1917-11-21 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | la Tiemard, France** — Dull with showers, S.E. wind. The company paraded and an inspection of kit and overhauling of equipment was carried on. The company commenced a syllabus of training as per the Schedule of Training (Report #25). The O.C. attended the C.R.E. Office in Norrent Fontes and endeavoured to obtain material for horse lines and for training purposes; none obtainable which would be of any use. Warning order received from the C.R.E. to hold one officer and a section of sappers prepared to proceed to the 3rd Canadian Division Wing, C.C.R.C. Training School, Ferfay, for the purpose of constructing huts, etc. Orders received from the C.R.E. to send an officer and one section (complete) of sappers to Clarques, where they would be attached to the First Army Trench Mortar School and billeted there; their work to be done under orders of the C.R.E. First Army. | Companies: C.C.R.C. Training School; First Army Trench Mortar School. | Locations: Norrent Fontes; Ferfay; Clarques.

- **1917-11-30 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Ypres, Belgium** — Enemy opened heavy fire on the battery at 7 am, forcing crews to take cover, Bdr Magee seriously wounded; S.O.S. call immediately answered despite very heavy shelling; Gunner C. G. Roome, on his own initiative, took command of No 2 Gun after its only N.C.O. was wounded and kept it going throughout the S.O.S.; a shell struck the cartridge dump behind No 2 Gun setting the cartridges on fire, Lieut F. R. Fraser at great personal risk fought the flames and saved a quantity of cartridges; enemy aeroplanes very active, three planes came down close to the battery position, two British (one pilot killed in the fall after jumping) and one German; 10 rounds in the morning on Hill 50 and two barrage shoots in the afternoon, 48 rounds; fire kept up overnight on farms, roads and tracks. | People: Bdr Magee; Gunner C. Sir Douglas Haig on the operations. Gen. Lipsett then inspected the Mounted Section and horses at Estree Blanche and appeared pleased with his inspection. | People: Major General Lipsett; Gen. Coys also sent representatives; a reconnaissance of the line including present M.G. positions was made on the Avion–Mericourt front, at present held by 1st and 2nd Can. - **1917-12-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Verquin, France** — Clear, S.W. wind. Company fell in and moved off under the O.C. at 8.15 a.m., passing the starting point of the 9th C.I. Bde in l'Eclere [uncertain] at 9 a.m., and marched via Busnettes, Chocques, Fouquereuil and Fouquieres to Verquin, arriving at about 11.45 a.m. The company billeted in houses in the town; horses in standings under cover. Major Robertson rode to 9th C.I. Bde Hqrs. in Fouquieres and interviewed the Acting Bde. Major re policy of work to be followed on the line, the same to be one of defensive wiring. 9th C.I. Bde Operation Order No 134 Copy No 19 dated 20-12-17 received today. Under orders from the C.R.E. the company to move to Mazingarbe tomorrow. 3rd Canadian Divisional Engineers Operation Order No 47, copy No 3, received, whereby inter alia the 9th Field Company C.E. will take over work in the 33rd Brigade, 11th British Division, from the 68th Field Company R.E., and a portion of the 34th Brigade Sector from the 86th Field Company R.E.; relief to be complete by 6 a.m. 23 December 1917. Boundaries of the area being looked after by this company: from the front line at N 2.d.4.9 (Lens Sh 36C S.W) along Nestor trench inclusive to N.12.5.5, along the railway inclusive; Double Crassier, to Fosse 5 de Bethune; southern boundary being [second] railway line to the south. Refilling point today was at Hesdigneul. | Companies: 9th C.I. The O.C. and Lieut Jones attended the rear billets of the 68th Field Company R.E. at les Bechis and made final arrangements re taking over; it having been ascertained that the 68th Field Company R.E. were moving from advance billets today, although relief was not to be completed until the morning of the 22nd, a party of 2 N.C.O.s and 8 men from 3 and 4 Sections proceeded to advanced billets and reported to Lieut West to hold billets etc. and to be there in case of emergency. S.W.); Pioneers and 8th Field Company C.E. to carry on with wiring on the left and 7th Field Company C.E. on the right. Arrangements made for supply of material; the same arrives at Osler Dump from the R.E. Park by petrol-driven tram cars and is pushed forward from Osler Dump on push trucks to the forward area. The 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade took over the forward area from the 11th British Division at 6 a.m. today, the 43rd Canadian Infantry Battalion being in the front line on the right and the 116th Canadian Infantry Battalion in on the left. The trenches as a whole are not in a very good state of repair and require considerable repair work as well as construction of new trenches and dugouts. - **1917-12-29 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Liévin, France** — Aeroplane shoot from 9.25 am on Hostile Battery MX59, a difficult target partly concealed by clumps of trees, visibility very poor and the shoot unsuccessful, 38 rounds, plane gave C.I. at 11.30 am; ordered by Group to concentrate on trench mortars in the railway embankment in M34c, plane given H.Q. [as written] and 10 rounds rapid fired at the trench mortars, then resumed the shoot with the plane; 10 rounds rapid at 2 pm in the cemetery at M33b and 10 rounds at 3 pm on M33d 90.90, both without observation; Howitzer No 251 removed to railhead during the night; gas alarm at midnight proved false, no gas came over the position. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1917-12-29 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | les Bechis, France** — Dull and cold, N.W. wind. Major Robertson attended a conference with the C.R.E., the three Field Company Commanders and the O.C. 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion, when general policy of work in the Divisional area was agreed upon. Attached party of 2 officers and 100 other ranks reported tonight. Enemy shells the neighbourhood of advanced billets each night with gas shells. The O.C. conferred with the G.O.C. 9th C.I. Bde. Ordered to get up special wiring material for wiring Masons House Post; attached infantry from the 43rd Battalion under sappers did the work. Lieut West and No 4 Section moved to rear billets after night work, and Lieut Walley with No 2 Section moved up to advanced billets. Lieuts West and Jones carried on work of erecting wire entanglements and cleaning trenches (Reports #13 and #14). Two officers and 100 other ranks (25 from each battalion, 9th C.I.B.) reported tonight to work with the 9th F.C.E. as a permanent working party. | People: Lieut West; Lieut Jones; Lieut Walley. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 4 Section; 3rd Canadian Pioneer Battalion; 43rd Battalion; 9th C.I.B. | Locations: Masons House Post.

- **1918-01-12 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — At 3.10 a.m. the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion carried out a successful raid with the assistance of artillery, trench mortars and machine guns; they entered the enemy's trenches at H 32 d and H 25 d, securing 2 prisoners belonging to 2nd Coy, 1st Battn., 213th R.I.R., and suffered very light casualties, only four men slightly wounded; a number of dugouts were bombed and casualties inflicted; our part consisted of covering all approaches to the points of entry — 9 of our machine guns with the assistance of 6 guns of the 1st Motor M.G. Brigade fired 3,650 rounds from 2.10 a.m. until 3 a.m.; a strange thing happened when Sergt. Bullock was firing a gun at N 1 a: he had only fired 250 rounds when an enemy bullet struck the [uncertain] on the crank handle, breaking it off and slightly wounding the sergeant in the hand, and another bullet pierced the [uncertain] of the muzzle cup, putting the gun out of action; the sergeant remained on duty; situation normal during the balance of the day, usual artillery exchanges, trench mortar work and machine-gun fire; two enemy planes over our lines in the morning and three of ours over on his side. | People: Sergt. Bullock. | Casualties: Sergt. Bullock slightly wounded in the hand; 2 prisoners taken (enemy, 213th R.I.R.). | Movement: —
- **1918-01-12 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Thelus, France** — Gun positions: 2 guns at Angres, 4 at Petit Vimy; work now wholly counter-battery. Aeroplane shoot attempted but given up after 10 rounds through engine trouble of the plane. Four N.F. calls answered on targets OY36, OY28, OY29 and NX63, 100 rounds fired; Angres section fired 25 rounds on target H8 NX63. Enemy artillery fairly quiet. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-01-13 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — Cold and clear; observation planes on both sides busy; scouting planes indulged in three [uncertain]; a new feature today — one of our Stokes trench mortars fired 20 rounds at a Hun plane that found the high altitudes too cold and sought a warmer level; 2 enemy balloons up from 9 a.m. to 12 noon; one of the entrances of a dugout at N 1 b occupied by a gun crew of C Section was blown in by a 4.1" at 5 p.m.; at 11.40 a.m. enemy heavily bombarded the east side of Loos for eight minutes; usual artillery, trench mortar and machine-gun activity. | Companies: C Section. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

Colonel McIntyre, several movements in company drill were carried out, and the inspecting officer congratulated the commanding officer on the efficiency of his company and awarded him first place in the battalion; the company returned to Nedon at 4 p.m., where a company inspection was held by the O.C., "A" Section being chosen as the cleanest and most soldier-like section, and the transport section under Lieut. Gill and nineteen other ranks entered the enemy lines at H.32.d.75.45 at 11.20 p.m. and returned at 11.35 p.m. with one wounded and one unwounded prisoner and a captured light machine gun, eight Germans known killed, our casualties one other rank wounded. | People: Capt. E. Gill. | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 OR wounded; enemy 8 killed, 2 prisoners taken, 1 light machine gun captured.
- **1918-01-14 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — A snowfall of two or three inches during the early hours affords a welcome relief to the eyes; situation normal; A Battery under Lieut. Adams, 1st C.M. M.G. Brigade, relieved by B Battery of the same unit at 6 p.m. under Lieut. Trench; all preparations made and calculations checked for the coming raid; the 5th C.M.R. Battalion carried out what was to be a 'stealth' raid at 11 p.m. — raiding party of 2 officers and 26 O.R.s penetrated the German line at H 32 d, captured 2 prisoners of the 209th R.I.R. and one machine gun, suffering only 1 O.R. wounded; the idea was to cut the wire by hand and carry on without assistance, failing this a T.M. rocket (red-green-red) was to be fired calling for a 'box' barrage; promptly at 11.30 p.m. the signal rocket went up and all arms immediately responded — we fired 15,000 rounds in 30 minutes in answer to this call; in view of an anticipated German relief during the night 7,750 more rounds were fired on the main avenues of approach. | People: Lieut. Adams; Lieut. Trench. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded (5th C.M.R.); 2 prisoners and 1 machine gun captured (enemy, 209th R.I.R.). | Movement: —

- **1918-01-16 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — Situation remains unchanged; enemy continues to pound our front and support lines and communication trenches with various calibre shells and trench mortars, and keeps up counter-battery work, our batteries in and around Loos getting the most attention; machine guns becoming more active, sweeping Hill 70, our support and communication trenches; our machine guns fired 21,000 rounds on selected targets on the other side of the line; rain let up at noon. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —
- **1918-01-16 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Thelus, France** — Hostile battery NZ 86 at N22 b.70 65 engaged with neutralizing fire, 50 rounds; enemy artillery maintained harassing fire 10 a.m.–5 p.m. on S.30.a.b., position of 1st Can. Hvy. Bty. | Companies: 1st Can. Hvy. Bty. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-01-16 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | les Brebis, France** — Cloudy with rain, night very dark, S.W. wind. Lieut West with No 4 Section and a party from the 52nd Battalion wiring, repairing the dressing station and placing gas curtains (Report #45). C.S.M. with 5 sappers and an infantry party, carrying material, revetting fire bays and improving trench (Report #46). Capt. Miller inspected trenches and found that, owing to frost coming out of the ground and rain, the trenches where not floored or revetted were in very bad shape. Special report on deep dugouts and trenches compiled and forwarded to the C.R.E. | People: Lieut Murdie; Lieut West; C.S.M.; Capt. Miller. | Companies: No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 58th Battalion; 52nd Battalion.

- **1918-01-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Still rainy, Nuns Alley and Noggin Trench absolutely impossible, with overland bathmat routes laid between company headquarters and the front-line posts; the enemy was quiet but very alert, his machine-gun fire sweeping the parapet continuously, our sniper claims one observed hit at H.32.d.90.05 and an enemy sniper wounded one of our men slightly. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 1 OR slightly wounded (enemy sniper).
- **1918-01-17 | 9th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Hill 70 sector** — Rain started again in the early hours and continued all day; all dugouts leaking badly, making living conditions miserable and making it very hard at Coy HQ to carry on the orderly room work; we fired 13,000 rounds from dusk till dawn on targets given through Division; 100,000 rounds of S.A.A. were brought up from the [uncertain] on the light railway; Captain Perry and 3 other officers of the 2nd Can. M.G. Coy visited our positions today with a view to relieving us shortly. | People: Captain Perry. | Casualties: none. | Movement: —

J. Miller. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section. | Locations: Fouquereuil; Bethune; Berguette; Lambres; Lietres; Signal School. | Movement: Company moves out of Le Brebis 22 January — Nos 2 & 3 Sections to Fouquereuil; Nos 1 & 4 Sections and Hqrs to Lambres via Bethune and Berguette.
- **1918-01-20 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | les Brebis, France** — Cloudy and warmer, S.E. wind. C.R.E. 48-2, in continuation of O.O. 48, received, whereby two sections of the 9th Field Company C.E. with transport complete will march from les Brebis on the 22nd inst. to Fouquereuil, First Army R.E. Workshops. Two sections and Hqrs., dismounted, to march from les Brebis to Bethune, reporting to the R.T.O. Bethune by 9 a.m. 22nd inst.; they will entrain under orders of the R.T.O. and detrain at Berquette [uncertain] and march to Lambres. Transport of two sections and Hqrs. will proceed by road on 22nd inst. from les Brebis to Lambres. The 9th Field Company C.E. will take over work at the Signal School, Liettres [uncertain], from the 1st Field Company C.E. under the C.R.E. First Army Troops. 9th Field Company C.E. Operation Order dated 20-1-18 (Report #55). Lieut Murdie with No 2 Section and a party from the 116th Battalion repairing the bridge at N 7 a 30.05. (36C), patrolling and repairing pipe line and placing gas curtains (Report #56). Lieut Baldock with No 3 Section, carrying material, placing gas curtains, repairing Hqrs T.M. Battery and repairing pipe line (Report #57). | People: Lieut Murdie; Lieut Baldock. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 1st Field Company C.E.; First Army R.E. Curren from C Company patrolled the right frontage till 10 p.m., and at 12.15 a.m. two officers and seventeen other ranks left No. 1 Post, Mericourt Road, found an old German post, heard the enemy talking, and threw several bombs amongst a party of 16 Germans working through the wire, evidently causing several casualties, moans being heard, before withdrawing safely at 2.45 a.m.; one enemy plane was brought down at approximately 1.11 [uncertain]. | People: Lieut. Bde: erecting wire entanglements in front of all fire trenches, repairing and maintaining all communication trenches, certain new support trenches to be dug and a new system of strong points built and wired in Avion village for front line defence. - **1918-02-27 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | La Targette, France** — Clear in the forenoon, cloudy in the afternoon, rain in the evening. The O.C. attended a conference at the C.R.E. office when all company commanders and the C.O. Pioneer Battalion were present. Policy of work discussed. Also the official announcement of the reorganization of Field Companies, Tunnelling Companies and Pioneer Battalions into Engineer Battalions, and various returns called for in connection with the reorganization. The O.C. returned to advanced billets. Lieut Jones with No 3 Section proceeded to advance billets and Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section returned to rear billets. No working parties from the 9th C.I. Bde tonight except trench wardens, owing to relief of front line battalions by support battalions. At the request of the G.O.C. 9th C.I. Bde, Major Robertson with Lieut Sproule reconnoitred the site of 6 strong points suggested for front line defence of Avion Village, particularly with reference to dugout accommodation, and a report was rendered. Party of No 2 Section building bunks and a new dugout added to advanced billets. The company at rear billets proceeding with ploughing and cultivation of one acre of land in the neighbourhood of the company rear billets. | People: Major Robertson; Lieut Sproule; Lieut Jones; Lieut Steeves. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; Pioneer Battalion; 9th C.I. Lieut Murdie with No 2 Section and parties from the 52nd and 58th Battalions, salvaging material, cleaning trenches, wiring and carrying material. Lieut Jones with No 3 Section, repairing gas curtains in dugouts, salvaging material and improving billets. Lieut Murdie with No 2 Section and parties from the 52nd and 58th Battalions, carrying material, making fire steps, cleaning trench and constructing wire entanglements. - **1918-03-04 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Sains-en-Gohelle, France** — Cold and foggy; enemy raided our front shortly before 6.00 am; all lines held up until 6.15 am, when both lines to 14th Brigade C.F.A. disconnected; magneto line to 13th Brigade C.F.A. disconnected at 6.31 am; Fullerphone line to 13th Brigade C.F.A. disconnected at 6.40 am; 14th Brigade C.F.A. magneto line in at 7.18 am; 13th Brigade C.F.A. got through their lateral to 14th Brigade C.F.A.; 13th Brigade magneto line in at 7.55 am; 14th Brigade Fuller line in at 9.00 am; line trouble in each brigade was all on about 200 yards of overland from brigade H.Q. to the buried cable test box; communication from brigades to batteries, O.P.s and infantry liaison maintained by lateral lines throughout. | People: — | Companies: 13th/14th Bdes C.F.A. | Casualties: none

Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section and a party from the 43rd Battalion repairing dugouts, improving advanced billets and salvaging ammunition. - **1918-03-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Mericourt sector, France** — The battalion's raid on the enemy trenches: at 12.45 a.m. the Officer Commanding and the Adjutant proceeded to advanced Battalion Headquarters, at 3.45 a.m. the raiders, 5 officers and 151 other ranks under Major T. D. Sneath M.C., left our line and, after a splendid artillery and machine-gun barrage, entered the enemy wire through the gaps, reached all objectives, destroyed machine-gun emplacements and dugouts, took 19 other ranks prisoners and killed many who resisted, returning under cover of a smoke screen; our casualties were Major T. D. Sneath M.C., O.C. Raid, and 4 other ranks killed and 22 other ranks wounded, exclusive of 4 other ranks slightly wounded and at duty. | People: Major T. D. Sneath M.C.; Lieut. Atto; Lieut. Morrisey; Lieut. Tixon [uncertain]; Lieut. Spence. | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 officers and 4 ORs killed (Maj. T. D. Sneath M.C. and, per the 17 March burial entry, Lieut. K. I. Somerville, and 4 ORs); 22 ORs wounded (+ 4 slightly wounded, at duty); enemy 19 prisoners taken, many killed.

- **1918-03-15 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | La Targette, France** — Clear and cold, north wind. Major Robertson attended a demonstration held by the First Army Officer in charge of mines as to the ability of our tanks to cross a series of craters. Craters were blown by 50 lbs of ammonal inserted through a bore hole to a depth of 6 feet; a second charge was then laid in the bottom of the first crater to increase its size. The result was to make the crater approximately 26 ft across the top and 8½ ft deep with steep sides. The tank went in and out of the series of craters without difficulty. It was suggested that had the mud been deep at the bottom of the crater, the thread of the tanks would probably have sunk in so deeply as to mire the tank. Lieut Sproule with No 4 Section and parties from the 42nd Battalion deepening and repairing trenches and working on dugouts for command posts. Lieut Baldock with No 1 Section and parties from the R.C.R. carrying material, cleaning out trenches and erecting wire entanglements. Lieut Murdie with No 2 Section and parties from the 42nd Battalion salvaging and carrying material, revetting trenches and placing signs. Lieut Serson [uncertain] with sappers from No 4 Section and a party from the 42nd Battalion repairing dugouts and erecting gas curtains. (Reports #46–49.) | People: Major Robertson; Lieut Sproule; Lieut Baldock; Lieut Murdie; Lieut Serson [uncertain]. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 4 Section; 42nd Battalion; R.C.R.

Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section salvaging material, relaying bathmats and wiring. Lieut Jones with No 3 Section and parties from the 42nd Battalion and R.C.R. repairing bathmats, deepening trenches and repairing dugouts. Lieut Baldock with No 2 Section and parties from the 42nd Battalion and R.C.R. cutting fire bays, repairing dugouts, preparing trenches for revetting and carrying material. - **1918-03-27 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Lens Canal–Arleux** — 27–31 March: the main resistance line of the Division was changed from the front line to a line about 500 yards in rear, the original front line being held with outposts to withdraw in the event of an attack. Mortars on the front were withdrawn and work commenced on emplacements to cover the new line; by the end of the month 6 mediums and one heavy were in action covering the new resistance line. While work was on an emplacement covering Arleux, Sgt. Maj. M.M. [uncertain] Coburn and Sgt. Head were killed by one shell. Monthly totals: 1,793 rounds 6" and 342 rounds 9.45" fired in counter-mortar work, harassing fire and destructive shoots. | People: Sgt. Maj. M.M. [uncertain] Coburn; Sgt. H. W. - **1918-03-28 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — S.O.S. (Oppy) quickly responded to at 6 a.m., 41 rounds fired; N.F. calls very frequent throughout the day, about 150 rounds fired; at 1.05 p.m. a further S.O.S. (Oppy) answered, 53 rounds fired; during the night, 50 rounds expended harassing fire on enemy roads; rear section became active and opened up on the same S.O.S., firing 51 rounds, and responded to N.F. calls during the night; Thelus (billet) very heavily shelled throughout the day, as was Vimy and Petit Vimy, and roads [entry ends mid-sentence]. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-03-28 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Fort George, France** — Clear and colder in the forenoon, cloudy in the afternoon, N.W. wind. The vicinity of the company rear billets was shelled from 5 a.m. The company with transport moved out of camp at 10 a.m. — sappers to trenches in rear near Fort George and transport to a sunken road west of Berthonval Wood (X.28.c.8.8, Sheet 36B). #502759 2/Cpl Hopkins W.B. wounded by shell fire, evacuated. Neighbouring units suffered a number of casualties. Sappers at rear billets stood to, ready to move forward to the Green line switch at ½ hour's notice, and at 9 p.m. stood down, ready to move forward at two hours' notice. Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section and parties from the 49th and 42nd Battalions clearing dugout entrances and wiring. Lieut Jones with No 3 Section and parties from the 42nd Battalion repairing dugouts and carrying material. (Reports #93–94.) | People: 2/Cpl Hopkins W.B. #502759; Lieut Steeves; Lieut Jones. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 3 Section; 49th Battalion; 42nd Battalion. | Locations: Fort George; Berthonval Wood; Green line switch. | Casualties: #502759 2/Cpl Hopkins W.B. wounded by shell fire, evacuated; neighbouring units suffered a number of casualties (no names given). | Movement: Company moved out of rear billets at 10 a.m. — sappers to trenches near Fort George, transport to a sunken road west of Berthonval Wood.

Lieut Steeves with No 1 Section and parties from the 42nd and 49th Battalions salvaging and carrying material, cleaning out trenches and repairing dugouts.
