- **1918-04-02 | 17th Canadian Machine Gun Company | Ecurie, France** — "A" Battery: O.C. Company and O.C. "A" Battery reconnoitred machine gun positions on Vimy Ridge line between railway embankment and Goulet wood; No. 7 Gun occupied new position; ammunition supply carried up to approximately 11,000 rounds per gun; day particularly quiet. "B" Battery: all men improving quarters and digging trenches. Rear H.Qrs.: two hours drill, remainder fatigue work and company transport lines. | Locations: Vimy Ridge; Goulet wood.
- **1918-04-02 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants., England** — Training as usual; Brigadier-General F. S. Meighen, D.S.O., C.M.G., Commanding Canadian Troops, Bramshott, visited the area inspecting camp [uncertain — remainder of sentence illegible]; 1 officer taken on from N.S.R.D., 1 officer struck off on transfer to 25th Canadian Reserve Battalion, Seaford, on proceeding overseas to [uncertain]. | People: Brig.-Gen. F. S. Meighen, D.S.O., C.M.G. | Companies: 25th Canadian Reserve Battalion, Seaford.
- **1918-04-02 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Neuville Vitasse** — Position as shown; there was no shelter in any of the trenches, so funk holes were dug and improved as opportunity occurred; in answer to S.O.S. on the left flank the battalion opened a heavy barrage on the enemy front and support lines, which drew retaliation, suffering several casualties — Lieut. G. N. Tucker wounded, 3 other ranks killed in action and 30 wounded; owing to erratic enemy shelling it was impossible to keep telephonic communication with the companies, runners working at night instead, communication with Brigade H.Q. being kept up except for short intervals. | People: Lieut. G. N. Tucker.
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather fine and cool. Heavy shelling at Vimy Village, 5 blowouts; one shell crater took 19 men 6 hours to fill, full detachment 16 hours to repair the 5 blowouts. Preliminary arrangements completed to grade a new lateral line from Savy north. Artillery Corner shelled for the first time, with H.E. and gas shells; one blowout. | Locations: Vimy Village; Savy; Artillery Corner.
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Div'l H.Q's Chateau D'Acq, Adv Corps Line (Fort George), France** — A silent period was in force at all wireless stations with test messages sent once daily, visual stations were all working satisfactorily, and 2,941 messages, 1,037 despatches and 21 Specials were handled. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Div'l H.Q's Chateau D'Acq, Adv Corps Line (Fort George), France** — Usual routine work was maintained, reports from all sections stated the enemy remained quiet and communications good, an effective system established by Arty Bde sections working with Liaison Officers speeded up calls for retaliation from detached guns, and 2,892 messages, 985 despatches and 14 Specials were handled. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Supply Column | Haillicourt** — Issued 25,160 men's and 6,149 horses' rations; weather clear & mild. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | La Targette** — Weekly mileage: the Train covered 7,442 miles for the week ending 31 March (8.13 miles per wagon per day); 394 miles on farm work, and potato planting began on the Divisional Farm. | People: — | Companies: Nos. 1–4 Companies. | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | S 30.a** — Left Group mortars heavily engaged by enemy 5.9" and 4.1" batteries; no injury to personnel or damage to material. | People: none | Companies: Left Group | Casualties: none | Movement: none
- **1918-04-02 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Aux-Rietz, France** — Fair and cool; Capt. M.L. Maitland became lines officer for the 4th and 5th C.D.A.s and the 6 brigades under them. | People: Capt. M.L. Maitland. | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Bray, France** — Weather fine and windy; an enemy battery busy firing up the lines, and the detachment very conveniently billeted. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 5th Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Maroeuil, France** — Brigade attached to 4th Canadian Division and took over the Oppy Section of that front. | People: — | Companies: 4th Canadian Division | Casualties: none | Movement: Attached to 4th Canadian Division; took over Oppy Section
- **1918-04-02 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Cellars Camp, Neuville St Vaast, France** — Fine; the battalion carried on with platoon in counter-attack, musketry, fire orders and platoon organisation, and at 6.30 p.m. three companies (A, B and C) proceeded on a working party to dig a new trench to be known as "Beehive Trench" in the area of T.27.b.4, Battalion Headquarters being established at approximately T.16.d.3.2 in the Brickpiles, the companies returning to Cellars Camp about 11 a.m. on the 3rd; the Officer Commanding instructed each company to have eight scouts in addition to those on Battalion Headquarters, Lieut. Atto, the intelligence officer, training them. | People: Lieut. Atto. | Companies: "A" Coy.; "B" Coy.; "C" Coy. | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-02 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — No. 2 Gun shifted to a new position further forward using the light line railway; wire from 42nd C.C.S. that Major T. W. F. MacDonald had died of wounds received 29 March; S.O.S. call answered with 6 rounds, successful aeroplane shoot on H.B. NX 63 (1 O.K., 2 M.O.K.s), night firing on hostile billets and H.B. NZ38. | People: Major T. W. F. MacDonald. | Companies: 42nd C.C.S. | Casualties: Major T. W. F. MacDonald died of wounds | Movement: No. 2 Gun moved forward.
- **1918-04-02 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Many short bursts of fire placed on hostile batteries and on S.O.S. lines Acheville; concentrations on H.B.s at U.14 b+a at 5.40 a.m., 60 rounds fired; many rounds of harassing fire on enemy positions in Rouvroy; aeroplane shoot at 3.10 p.m. on H.B. at U.1 d 8.0, 200 rounds fired, reported as successful; concentrations on H.B.s continued 10.30 p.m.–12.30 a.m.; rear position engaged several H.B.s with short bursts; night firing from both positions; enemy shelled battery position, T.25a and S.24d, with H.E., shrapnel and gas; no casualties and no damage. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-02 to 1918-04-03 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Red Line / Avion, France [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — No. 1 Section night work, 2–3 April: built 68x double apron fence on the Red Line crossings (63x at La Coulotte Road, 5x at the tramway crossing); revetted and bathmatted Saskatoon Trench; repaired the D.O. at N.26.C.3.0; worked the D.O. at N.32.d.2.4; cleaned 65x of Beaver Trench from Avion Support forward. Two parties' reports are marked "Report later". Casualties Nil. | Companies: P.P.C.L.I.; 49th Battalion; 42nd Battalion. | Locations: Red Line; La Coulotte Road; Saskatoon Trench; Adept Dump; Beaver Trench; Avion Support. | Casualties: Nil.

Sproule), 2–3 April: a dugout party at T9 C 2040 was called off on account of shelling; 400x double apron fence was put up from T3 C6 080 to T9 88590, completing 3 belts west of Souris Road; 82 coils of barbed wire carried from La Coulotte to Victoria Road junction and Red trench; steps dug on Beaver C.T. from Adept 7 to Avion Support; a trench widened and deepened from 3'-6" x 3'-6" to 5' x 3' (Red trench). | People: Lieut. Sproule. | Companies: No. 4 Section; P.P.C.L.I.; R.C.R.; 49th Battalion. | Locations: Souris Road; La Coulotte; Victoria Road; Red trench; Beaver C.T.; Adept 7; Avion Support; Doris Dump.

Sproule with No 4 Section and parties from the P.P.C.L.I., R.C.R. and 49th Battalions carrying material, widening and deepening trench and improving dugouts. Lieut. Serson with sappers from No 1 Section and parties from the 49th Battalion deepening trenches and wiring. Lieut. Steeves with No 1 Section and parties from the 49th Battalion and P.P.C.L.I. cleaning out and revetting trenches, excavating for dugouts and carrying material. - **1918-04-03 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Neuville Vitasse** — Considerable movement was observed in Neuville St Vaast, just in front of the line, and the artillery were very active, putting several barrages on the village and at one time making two direct hits on enemy parties; a patrol of 6 other ranks under Lieut. Spencer, returning from a reconnaissance patrol, ran into an enemy machine gun which opened fire, wounding 2 of the scouts; the patrol covered the whole battalion frontage during the night; 1 other rank killed in action, 3 other ranks wounded, and 6 other ranks arrived as reinforcements. | People: Lieut. Spencer. | Locations: Neuville St Vaast.

"C" Coy detachment at Sailly evacuated by enemy shell fire, moved to La Bourse and continued maintaining. | Companies: A Coy; B Coy; C Coy. | Locations: Cardinal Spur; Savy; Sailly; La Bourse.

- **1918-04-03 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Cellars Camp, Neuville St Vaast, France** — Rainy; Headquarters Company (signallers, snipers, scouts and Lewis gunners) carried on training under their specialist officers, "A", "B" and "C" Companies rested after the previous night's working party, "D" Company worked all day on "Grange" and "Goodman" tunnels and "Spanderu" House, and at 10 p.m. orders were received that the battalion would relieve the 58th Canadian Infantry Battalion in the right front line of the Acheville sector on the night of 5th–6th; the battalion attended a concert by the Dumbell Concert Party at the Y.M.C.A. cinema, Neuville St. Vaast. | People: — | Companies: 58th Cdn. - **1918-04-03 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 5 a.m. opened up on S.O.S. lines Acheville, firing 20 rounds; harassing and neutralizing fire on various H.B.s maintained throughout the day, about 80 rounds fired; rear position shelled Henin Letard Road; programme of night firing from both positions; during the morning the enemy carried out what appeared to be an observed shoot on position S.24d; No. 4 gun pit damaged and gun temporarily put out of action; no casualties. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-03 to 1918-04-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Goodman Tunnel / Spandau Haus / Avion, France [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — No. 2 Section day work, 3 April: commenced clearing out 3 entrances of Goodman Tunnel (1 completed) and opening 2 entrances to Spandau Haus, work proceeding slowly as the tunnelling was in bad condition, 200 sandbags filled. No. 4 Section night work, 3–4 April: carrying bathmats and mining sets to Adept and Red trenches, wiring the Red Trench and Actress Trench, cleaning the Adept Extension, and dugout work at T.9.C.2040 and T.2.d.3030. No. 1 Section night work, 3–4 April: cleaned and widened 120 yds of Halifax Trench, placed a belt of double apron wire in front of Yarmouth Trench, cleaned Beaver Trench, pushed material from La Coulotte to Avion Dump, drifted the D.O. at N.32.d.2.4, and bathmatted Saskatoon Trench. Casualties Nil. | People: W.C. Murdie; J.E. Sprunk [uncertain]; J.V. Brown T. G. slipped and ruptured himself, sent to hospital; Grand Trunk trench again heavily shelled. "B" Battery: everything quiet on our front. - **1918-04-05 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants., England** — Training as usual; kit inspections of Draft 199 held by General Staff in the morning; 28 other ranks taken on on arrival from Canada, 1 from N.S.R.D.; 1 officer struck off on transfer to Canadian Engineers Training Depot, Seaford; 1 other rank struck off as deserter, 5 to N.S.R.D., 20 to Royal Canadian Regiment in Field, 10 to N.S.R.D. | Companies: Canadian Engineers Training Depot, Seaford; Royal Canadian Regiment.
- **1918-04-05 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Neuville Vitasse** — A patrol of 13 men under Lieut. S. G. Stokes and Sgt. Burns went out at about 5 p.m. to clear out the French [uncertain] through N.19.a.60.85 in order to establish a protection on the flank of both the front and support lines; they successfully bombed down about 150 yards, then withdrew a short distance and established a post at N.9.a.70.90, inflicting many casualties on the enemy, all of whom belonged to the 15 R.I.R., the party carrying out the work without casualty; at 9.30 a.m. the enemy attempted to raid the trenches of the right flank battalion, the 19th Canadian Battalion, coming over in 3 waves (about 300) but only succeeding in reaching the wire and suffering very heavy casualties; during the afternoon a German was found in a sap leading from a post on the right flank and sent to H.Q.; considerable artillery activity on both sides; 3 other ranks killed in action and 16 other ranks wounded. | People: Lieut. S. G. Stokes; Sgt. Burns. | Companies: 19th Canadian Battalion.
- **1918-04-05 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather cloudy and cool, showery at intervals. 18 blowouts on the Vimy section, enemy fire kept up continuously. "B" Coy authorised to construct a new line from Barlin to Cairo Junction. "D" Coy selected a new camp site at Hayplock [uncertain] for a detachment of 50 O.R. to maintain lines from Villers-au-Bois to Laurel Junction at Mont St Eloy. 19 O.R. reinforcements received. Divion selected as rendezvous in the event of retirement. | Companies: B Coy; D Coy. | Locations: Vimy; Barlin; Cairo Junction; Hayplock [uncertain]; Villers-au-Bois; Laurel Junction; Mont St Eloy; Divion.

- **1918-04-05 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Hostile batteries at U.14 a+b again subjected to short bursts of fire, 36 rounds fired; harassing fire placed on L'Homme Mort at U.2.a. and roads at U.13, 14 and 19, about 36 rounds expended; at 11.30 p.m. commenced a heavy gas bombardment with H.E. and gas shell, maintained throughout the night, firing 600 gas shell and 128 H.E. shell; rear position maintained harassing fire on enemy roads and light railways, and fired 158 gas shell into Chez Bon-Temps. | Casualties: none.

No. 4 Section night work, 5–6 April: carried knife rests to Actress Trench, pushed material from Cycle dump to the Red trench and Betty dump, cleaned and bermed Cyril Trench, fitted dugout T.9.C.2040, widened the Red Trench, and completed 2 belts of double apron fence from Victoria Rd to the Tram line; salvaged and hauled 120 knife rests from Givenchy to Cycle dump. Dewhurst, 709728 Private W. B. Stenson and Private J. [uncertain] Worthy (attached 8th Cdn. Inf. Bde.), and the enemy artillery was more active than usual around the forward area with 3 direct hits in Hudson Trench; a warning order was received that the battalion would be relieved by the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion on the night of 10/11th April. | People: Sgt. W. Mann; Pte. J. Cusack; Sgt. C. H. Simpson; Pte. L. Shaw; Sgt. T. Louis; Cpl. M. Fleiser; L/Cpl. W. Anderson; Pte. F. R. Dewhurst; Pte. W. B. Stenson; Pte. J. [uncertain] Worthy. | Companies: 2nd C.M.R. Bn. | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-08 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Harassing fire on Rose Cottage and Noyelles Road in the early morning; heavy gas bombardment 4.30–4.58 a.m., H.B.s NX71 and NZ37 neutralized in S.B.R.s; Noyelles harassed in the afternoon and tramways at night. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-08 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Neutralization fire placed on H.B.s U.1.a and U.9.d., and harassing fire on many enemy roads and positions throughout day and night, 46 rounds fired; rear position fired 45 rounds on to roads and enemy trenches; enemy artillery fired into Vimy and vicinity intermittently during the day; no damage and no casualties. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-08 to 1918-04-09 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Goodman Tunnel / Red Line, France [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — No. 2 Section night work, 8 April: material carried from Brewery to Avion Dump, dug-outs in Avion Support. No. 3 Section day work, 8 April: Goodman Tunnel — Dorsett Drive entrance excavated from the top, Bay St entrance (1 frame in entrance, 1 in gallery, 25 yds lining) and P.S. Line entrance strengthened; Spandau Haus — 4 entrances cleaned out, 3 now usable, 4 new frames placed; Red Mill locality — 2 Bee Hive shelters placed for stores. No. 4 Section, 8 April: pushed bathmats and sandbags to Betty dump, dugouts T.9.C.2040 and T.2.d.3080, Adept Trench bathmatting, Red Trench cleaning and wiring, and a special party collecting trucks at Doris dump. No. 2 Section, 9 April, Bois de Chaudiere locality: carried stakes and wire from Victoria Dump to Hayter Trench; cleaned 65x of Bluenose Trench and 100x of Pictou Trench; wired 240x in front of Yarmouth Trench, work completed; carried stakes and wire from Victoria Dump to Halifax Trench. | People: J.W. Babcock; J. S. Jones [uncertain]; J.E. Sprunk [uncertain]. | Companies: 58th Battalion; 42nd Battalion; 49th Battalion; R.C.R.; P.P.C.L.I. | Locations: Goodman Tunnel; Dorsett Drive; Bay Street; P.S. - **1918-04-09 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants., England** — Training as usual; 4 other ranks taken on from N.S.R.D.; 1 officer taken on from N.S.R.D., 1 officer struck off on proceeding overseas to 26th Battalion, 4 officers to Royal Canadian Regiment. | Companies: 26th Battalion; Royal Canadian Regiment.
- **1918-04-09 | 18th Battalion | Relief** — Battalion moved off in fighting order to relieve the 31st Canadian Battalion in the Purple Line system (Brigade reserve), the relief being completed about 8.45 p.m.; Battalion H.Q. at R.30.a.21.5; rations were sent up to the men in the line ready cooked and the men were supplied with "Tommy Cooker" in rear to enable them to heat their meals; the 19th Canadian Battalion was in the front line, with a [uncertain] Guards unit on the right flank in reserve. | Companies: 31st Canadian Battalion; 19th Canadian Battalion. | Locations: Purple Line; Vimy Ridge. | Movement: Berles au Bois → Purple Line.

Capt Wilkinson and detachment shelled out of ZELOBES and proceeded to HINGES. Artillery Corner shelled, no damage. | People: Capt Wilkinson. | Companies: A Coy; C Coy. | Locations: Zelobes; Hinges; Artillery Corner. | Casualties: several O.R. slightly gassed, 3 admitted to hospital.

- **1918-04-09 | 5th Canadian Divisional Train (Detachment) | Bray, France** — Drew from Frevin Capelle railhead by horse transport the first time, loaded at 7.45 a.m., with the wagon clearing the railhead first and then delivering to the units; heavy shelling over and about the lines from 2 p.m. to 6.30 p.m. and intermittently through the night, and 126778 Dvr. Clark wounded in the left leg in the afternoon at the lines, his promotion to the rank of [uncertain] having appeared in 4th Cdn. Div. Routine Orders of today; weather dull and cold. | People: Dvr. Clark (126778). | Companies: 4th Cdn. Div. | Casualties: Dvr. Clark (126778) wounded, left leg, by shelling

- **1918-04-09 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Acheville sector, France** — Dark with a very heavy fog all morning, lifting about noon; the enemy artillery was quiet until 4 p.m., then opened up with various calibres along Vancouver Road and the communication trenches, with a considerable number of gas shells, and at 6.30 p.m. concentrated on the Beehive defences, Vancouver Dump and the trenches leading back from Canada, our communications being cut with "A", "B" and "D" Companies, as many as 28 breaks being found in the line; our casualties during the bombardment were very light, one killed, two wounded, one gassed and one concussion, the last being buried very badly; at 10 p.m. an enemy patrol worked down Antelope Alley toward our block and was engaged by our post and driven off, and at 1.10 p.m. an enemy patrol attempted to raid our post on Saskatchewan Road but was repulsed, while a daylight patrol of one officer and 11 other ranks reconnoitred up Manitoba Road and Hudson Sap, finding enemy blocks unoccupied and a large dugout formerly used as an R.A.P. in good condition. | People: — | Companies: "A" Coy.; "B" Coy.; "D" Coy. | Casualties: 1 OR killed, 2 ORs wounded, 1 OR gassed, 1 OR concussion.
- **1918-04-09 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — H.B. NZ38 neutralized at 3.20 p.m., harassing fire on Noyelles and approaches in the evening, 5 rounds neutralizing H.B. NZ40; hostile shelling below normal. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-09 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Concentration at 8.25 a.m. on H.B.s in U.14 a+b, 45 rounds fired; further concentration at 11.30 a.m. on Hudson Post T.24c, 50 rounds expended; harassing fire on H.B.s maintained during afternoon and night; rear position carried out harassing fire shoots on to enemy trenches, Fresnoy Park and Acheville; enemy fired about 60 rounds 4.2-in. and 5.9-in. H.E. into S.24c. and S.24d. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-09 to 1918-04-10 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Hayter Trench / Avion Support, France [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — No. 4 Section, 9 April: pushed bathmats to Betty dump and salvaged mining sets and stakes; dug out T.9.C.2040; Adept Extension cleaning and bathmatting (work interrupted by shelling); dugout T.2.d.3030; Red Trench berming, widening and cleaning; completed 165x double apron fence on the Red Trench, completing 3 belts from the Tram line west to the Lens-Arras Rd; carried knife rests and concertinas from Betty dump to Actress, Soucie and wire parties; cleaned 45x of Irish Trench. No. 2 Section, 9 April: material from Brewery to Avion Dump; dug-outs in Avion Support; carried concertinas and knife rests from La Coulotte to Cyril, Balsam, Beaver, Columbia and Adept. No. 3 Section day work, 9 April: Goodman Tunnel — Dorsett Drive entrance (3 frames, 5 yds lagging), Bay St entrance completed, P.S. Line entrance; Spandau Haus — 3rd entrance 50% completed, No. 2 entrance still with no passage through. No. 2 Section, 10 April: completed 300x double apron fence on Hayter Trench and repaired the second belt; no material pushed to Avion Depot as no push trucks were available; dug-outs in Avion Support; put in trench blocks at Cyril #27 and #30, Souris #29 and Avion #28; dug-out in Saskatoon Rd. Casualties Nil. | People: J.E. Sprunk [uncertain]; J.W. Babcock; J. S. Battalion would relieve us instead of the 102nd, the relief being a good one, with the exception of "B" Company, which had one platoon relieved which went off without reporting, and enemy artillery of all calibres mixed with gas shells was very active throughout the relief, which was not complete until 1.15 a.m. on the 12th. | People: — | Companies: 102nd Cdn. - **1918-04-11 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | F.5.d.4.3. Sheet 51c, France** — Clear, S.W. wind. Warning order received from the C.R.E. for the company to be prepared to move on the 12th; a rear party to be left at advanced billets to hand over work. Lieut. Jones with a party of cyclists proceeded to the advanced billets of the 466th Field Company R.E. 9th Canadian Brigade Operation Order No 154 dated 11-4-18 received, whereby the 3rd Canadian Division will take over the whole front of the 4th Division — Lens Section, St. Emile Section and Hill 70 Section; the 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade will take over the St. Emile Section from the 139th Infantry Brigade on the night of 11th/12th April 1918. Lieut. Sproule with No 4 Section and parties from the R.C.R., 42nd and P.P.C.L.I. Battalions wiring, carrying material, repairing dugouts and cleaning and widening trenches. Lieut. Baldock with No 2 Section and parties from the R.C.R., 42nd and 49th Battalions repairing dugouts, erecting trench blocks, and cleaning out and repairing trenches. An advanced party from the 7th Field Company C.E. arrived at advanced billets and work in the Avion Section was handed over to them. Major Robertson and Nos 2 and 4 Sections returned to rear billets in trenches at Fort George. | People: Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Sproule; Lieut. Baldock; Major Robertson. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 4 Section; 466th Field Company R.E.; 3rd Canadian Division; 4th Division; 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 139th Infantry Brigade; R.C.R.; 42nd Battalion; P.P.C.L.I.; 49th Battalion; 7th Field Company C.E. | Locations: Lens Section; St. Emile Section; Hill 70 Section; Avion Section; Fort George. | Movement: Lieut. Jones with cyclists to the 466th Field Company R.E. advanced billets; 7th Field Company C.E. advanced party arrived; Major Robertson and Nos 2 and 4 Sections to rear billets at Fort George; company warned to move on 12 April.

- **1918-04-12 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Successful shoot at 9.07 a.m. on H.B. at U.1.d.79.01 with aeroplane observation; calibration completed satisfactorily on Railway Cottage at 12.30 p.m.; opportunity targets of enemy movement engaged during the afternoon, parties dispersed; rear section fired 60 rounds on H.B.s U.14.1, U.14.2 and U.14.7 in 10-minute bursts of fire; enemy shelling nil. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-12 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Clear and cool, north wind. Capt. Miller, Lieut. Baldock and Lieut. Serson proceeded to the rear billets of the 466th Field Company R.E.; No 3 Section and 6 other ranks of No 2 Section proceeded on bicycles to the rear billets of the 466th Field Company R.E. The balance of the company with transport, under Major Robertson, moved off at 7 p.m. via Souchez and Ablain-St Nazaire to a field just outside Bully-Grenay (R.11.c.2.7. Sheet 36a), where the company bivouacked for the night as the billets of the 466th Field Company R.E. will not be vacated until tomorrow; the night move was made because the Souchez–St. Nazaire road cannot be used in daylight, being in view of the enemy lines. Relief of the 466th Company R.E. by this company complete by 6 p.m. today. No 3 Section and No 2 Section except 6 other ranks proceeded to advanced billets in Cité St Pierre (M.11.d.25.50. Sheet 36c SW). 3rd Canadian Division Engineer's Operation Order No 53 received, issued in conjunction with 3rd Canadian Division G 676 and O.O. 155, whereby the 3rd Canadian Division will relieve the 46th Division by 6 a.m. 13th April 1918; by the order the 9th Field Company C.E. is to hand over work in the Avion Sector, new boundary, to the 7th Field Company C.E., and the work between the new boundary and the present southern boundary to the 10th Field Company C.E. | People: Capt. Miller; Lieut. Baldock; Lieut. Serson; Major Robertson. | Companies: No 2 Section; No 3 Section; 466th Field Company R.E.; 3rd Canadian Division; 46th Division; 7th Field Company C.E.; 10th Field Company C.E. | Locations: Souchez; Ablain-St Nazaire; Bully-Grenay; Cité St Pierre; Avion Sector. | Movement: Company moved at 7 p.m. via Souchez and Ablain-St Nazaire to bivouac outside Bully-Grenay; No 3 Section and No 2 Section (less 6 other ranks) to advanced billets in Cité St Pierre; relief of the 466th Field Company R.E. complete by 6 p.m.

- **1918-04-13 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Clear and cold, north wind. C.R.E. 19-81 received, whereby the sections of the Field Companies in brigade areas are to come under the orders of the G.O.C. Brigade concerned and are to be allotted battle positions. The sections of the 9th Field Company C.E. at rear billets will remain as divisional reserve and, on an attack appearing imminent, stand to ready to move at 1/2 hours' notice and send two runners to the C.R.E. Office for orders. Lieut. Baldock with No 2 Section and parties from the 116th Battalion carrying material forward ready for starting work. Lieut. - **1918-04-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Cité Ste Pierre** — Lieut Loy M.C. in charge of signal communications; active firing policy inaugurated and all available men used to construct new emplacements; strength 10 officers, 171 O.Rs. | People: Lieut J. A. Loy M.C. | Companies: none | Casualties: none | Movement: none
- **1918-04-15 | 5th Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Aux-Rietz, France** — Dull and cold; Lt. H.K. Cox attached to D.T.M.O. 5th C.D.A. to install communication to T.M. batteries which are going into action from Souchez river to Avion. | People: Lt. H.K. Cox. | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1918-04-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Support Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Dull and cloudy; the day passed fairly quietly with very little shelling on the front, and the battalion supplied working parties for new shelters in Aeroplane Trench, wiring the Blue Line between Netley and Hythe Alley, fire-stepping and cleaning New Cut, and maintaining Railway Alley and Netley Alley. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-15 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Nil. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-15 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — 30 rounds harassing fire on various H.B. positions 6–7 a.m.; two shoots of neutralizing fire on H.B. at U.8.b.11.9, 55 rounds fired; during the night 60 rounds harassing fire on H.B.s at O.25.c and O.35.c. At about 10 a.m. the enemy commenced shelling position S.24.d., firing about 20 rounds H.E., apparently for ranging; at 2.30 p.m. a heavy bombardment on the same location, about 200 rounds; one shell burst in No. 1 gun pit, in which Lieut. E. A. MacKenzie and the gun crew were working. Lieut. E. A. MacKenzie (severely wounded), Bombr. J. T. Wentzell (killed), Gnr. E. C. Parslow (died of wounds), Gnr. C. G. Leroux (died of wounds), Gnr. L. L. Lawrence (severely wounded), Gnr. J. Barclay (died of wounds), Gnr. Croft (wounded), Gnr. Bateman (severely wounded) and Gnr. A. N. Matheson (wounded); no material was damaged. | People: Lieut. E. A. MacKenzie; Bombr. J. T. Wentzell; Gnr. E. C. Parslow; Gnr. C. G. Leroux; Gnr. L. L. Lawrence; Gnr. J. Barclay; Gnr. Croft; Gnr. Bateman; Gnr. A. N. Matheson. | Casualties: 4 killed/died of wounds (Bombr. Wentzell; Gnrs. Parslow, Leroux, Barclay); 5 wounded (Lieut. MacKenzie; Gnrs. Lawrence, Croft, Bateman, Matheson).

- **1918-04-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Support Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Fine but dark, visibility poor; the enemy was very active throughout the day shelling both forward and rear areas and especially around Loos, the battalion supplied the usual working parties, "D" Company proceeded for a bath to the Divisional Baths at Les Brebis in the morning and "B" Company in the afternoon, "A" Company evacuated Loos and Tosh Alley and established Company Headquarters in Chirngowen O.P., and decorations were announced for the raid on the enemy trenches: the Military Cross to Captain J. Smith found unconscious in bed and died despite two hours' resuscitation, Medical Officer giving heart failure as the cause; buried the same afternoon at Ablain St Nazaire; two S.O.S. calls in the evening answered with 5 rounds each on S.O.S. lines St Emile, 10 rounds on H.B. - **1918-04-17 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Several hostile batteries subjected to bursts of rapid fire during the day, over 100 rounds fired; two shoots of neutralizing fire on H.B.s U.8.b. 10.29 and U.8.b. 20.68; harassing fire on enemy roads and light railways during the night; rear position fired 68 rounds on H.B.s in connection with a pre-arranged counter-battery scheme; enemy artillery shelled S.24, S.30, T.25 and T.19 with shrapnel and gas; Thelus subjected to harassing fire, in which A/Corpl. H. W. Horwill (M.M.) was wounded; no damage and no other casualties. | People: A/Corpl. H. W. Horwill. | Casualties: 1 wounded (A/Corpl. Horwill).

Lieut Noble's detachment of "C" Coy repaired 11 blowouts in his lines today. A plot of ground at Ecoures [uncertain] was allotted to this battalion at Ecoures [uncertain] and farming commenced — 65 acres in all. | People: Lieut Noble. | Companies: B Coy; C Coy. | Locations: Ecoures [uncertain].

- **1918-04-19 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Fine with a little snow in the afternoon, visibility very good; a great deal of movement was observed in the enemy lines and trains running north from Sallaumines, our artillery were very active on enemy defences, a patrol of 5 Huns attempted to enter our trenches at N.28.a.27.9 at 4 a.m. but was driven off by our sentries, one thought to be hit, our snipers report 3 observed hits, and No. 243073 Private Dessureault J. of "B" Company was shot dead by a private of the 52nd Cdn. Inf. Battalion who took Dessureault for a Hun as he could speak but very little English, a court of enquiry being held that afternoon with all evidence forwarded to Brigade Headquarters. | People: Pte. Dessureault J. | Companies: "B" Coy.; 52nd Cdn. Inf. Bn. | Casualties: 1 OR killed — Pte. Dessureault J. (shot by a private of the 52nd Cdn. Inf. Bn. in error).
- **1918-04-19 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Exceptionally quiet; 8 rounds in reply to an S.O.S. call at 10.09 p.m. and a programme of harassing and neutralizing fire during the night. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-19 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Neutralization of H.B.s carried out both morning and afternoon, as many as five separate shoots of 10 rounds each; calibration completed successfully in 14 rounds on Railway Cottage U.1.C.1; harassing fire maintained on enemy roads during the night, and a large night programme on H.B.s at U.8.b.11.8. and U.9.b.51.33 in accordance with Counter-Battery Order No. 64, 300 rounds fired; rear section carried out calibration, firing 40 rounds, target at T.11.a.55.95; enemy apparently carried out registration on cross roads in S.30.a, firing several rounds at [uncertain] 10.45. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-04-20 | 18th Battalion | Relief** — During the night of 20/21st the battalion relieved the 28th Canadian Battalion in the front line; the battalion moved off from Berles au Bois in fighting order at 3.30 p.m., stopping at Wailly for a hot meal before proceeding into the line, the relief of the 28th Battalion being completed by 11.45 p.m.; disposition being A and B Companies in the front line with C and D Companies in close support, the front line running from N.13.b to M.23.b and Battalion H.Q. at M.23.a 50.90; 2 other ranks returned from hospital. | Companies: 28th Canadian Battalion; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: Wailly. | Movement: Berles au Bois → Front line (via Wailly).
- **1918-04-20 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather fine. 9 other ranks of 1st Battn C.R.T. who had been received in exchange for men of this unit who volunteered for Palestine were today returned to 1st Battn. "C" Coy reports the Beuvry line broken in 13 sections, and heavy shelling at Mansion House. | Companies: C Coy. | Locations: Beuvry; Mansion House.
- **1918-04-20 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Adv HQ's Sains-en-Gohelle / Rear HQ's Chateau de la Haie, France** — Work commenced on the bury at rear Headquarters with 125 yards put down, work started on burying cable from Fosse 5 to Fosse 11 in the mine galleries, both shifts laid about 800 yards, the cable work done by 1st Corps was found to be of poor quality with cable laid on spikes and joints only taped, and 3,354 messages, 1,433 despatches and 6 Specials were handled. | People: Capt McCready; Lt McPherson; A.D. Signals. | Companies: 1st Corps; 7th Bde. | Casualties: none

- **1918-04-20 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Cité Ste Pierre** — 6" T.M.s active engaging hostile T.M.s, registering targets for night firing — S.O.S., in retaliation and on targets of opportunity. | People: none | Companies: none | Casualties: none | Movement: none

- **1918-04-20 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Fine, visibility good; the enemy's artillery was more active than usual, a barrage was laid down on the front line immediately north of us at 4 p.m., taking in part of our left flank, which gradually moved northwards, considerable movement in the enemy's rear areas was reported, two reconnaissance patrols had nothing unusual to report, we fired about 150 .45 gas shells [uncertain] in H.29.2.c and N.3.c., which apparently had good effect on the enemy, and orders were received that the 1st and 4th Canadian Mounted Rifles Battalions would raid the enemy's trenches at 1.30 a.m. on the morning of the 22nd, and that we were to give the 1st C.M.R. Battalion every assistance possible. | People: — | Companies: 1st C.M.R. Bn.; 4th C.M.R. Bn. | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-20 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Enemy troops observed on Canada Road at 2.25 p.m., 6 rounds fired into them; aeroplane shoot on NX65 abandoned after 15 rounds in mist. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-04-20 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Hostile batteries at U.8.b.11.8 and U.9.b.51.33 engaged 6–7.20 a.m. under C.B.O. No. 64, 135 rounds fired; aeroplane shoot commenced at 5.10 p.m. on H.B. at U.8.b.52.29 but discontinued as unsuccessful owing to very poor visibility; during the night, sharp bursts of fire on H.B.s and harassing fire maintained, 70 rounds fired; enemy artillery very active, over 300 rounds reported on S.24d and S.30; no damage nor casualties. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-04-21 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Hill 70 sector, France** — Fine, visibility good; the enemy's artillery was very active on the front line, Hythe Alley and Hurdle Trench between 2 a.m. and 5 a.m., causing considerable damage to the trenches and killing two of our men and wounding six more, our snipers claim one observed hit and one doubtful, and our artillery carried out a destructive shoot on the enemy's wire to facilitate the raiding parties, the 1st C.M.R. Battalion to raid about H.32.d.9.6 with 2 officers and 60 other ranks, the 4th C.M.R. Battalion about H.26.d.3.0 with 3 officers and 60 other ranks, and the 9th Cdn. Inf. Bde. sending two parties over at about N.14.a.7.2 and N.8.b.7.6. | People: — | Companies: 1st C.M.R. Bn.; 4th C.M.R. Bn.; 9th Cdn. Inf. Bde. | Casualties: 2 ORs killed, 6 ORs wounded.

- **1918-04-21 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 10.30 a.m. a shoot with aeroplane observation carried out on H.B. at U.8.b.52.20, completed successfully, 300 rounds fired; H.B.s at U.8.b.11.8 and U.9.a.73.35 engaged in accordance with C.B.O. No. 65; during the night harassing fire on enemy roads and tramways; rear position also carried out C.B.O. No. 65 programme on H.B.s U.7.b.0.31.c. and U.1.a. during the night. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-04-22 | 18th Battalion | Front line** — During the night of 21/22nd working parties from the battalion cleaned and repaired trenches; Lieut. G. T. Spencer (Assistant Officer), Sgt. Manby and 4 scouts reconnoitred the entire system of surrounding trenches to obtain the line and posts; observers discovered what appeared to be part of the enemy's new front line trench at N.19.b.35.75, and several scouts lying in shell holes in No Man's Land were able to observe it, Scout Rymol [uncertain] claiming 1 [uncertain]; at 12.30 p.m. a German sentry was observed in a post at N.19.b.80.20 and Sgt. Manby with 4 scouts set out to secure him but were held up by wire in front of the post, so Sgt. Manby shot the sentry; Germans were observed in the church of Neuville Vitasse, which is being used as an observation post. | People: Lieut. G. T. Spencer; Sgt. Manby; Scout Rymol [uncertain]. | Locations: Neuville Vitasse; No Man's Land.
- **1918-04-22 | 3rd Battalion, Canadian Railway Troops | Barlin, France** — Weather cloudy and cool. Grading commenced on a new line connecting the Ecurie system with the Roclincourt line — a "balloon line" to serve batteries in the Roclincourt district should St Catherine's line be destroyed. | Locations: Barlin; Ecurie; Roclincourt; St Catherine's.

- **1918-04-28 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 10.55 a.m., a successful calibration carried out with Y Section, Sound Ranging, O.K. being reported; H.B.s U.8.b, N.39c and N.30.b. neutralized, 45 rounds expended; at 11.10 p.m. a concentration placed on H.B.s at U.9.a.28.66 and U.9.a.30.55, 75 rounds fired; enemy roads and tramways harassed during the night, 120 rounds fired; S.24d again received attention from the enemy, about 30 rounds gas and H.E. reported; no damage and no casualties. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-04-28 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Bully-Grenay, France** — Dull and cloudy with showers, N.W. wind. No 1 Section attended bath parade. Lieut. Jones with No 3 Section completed wiring of Bully Switch. Lieut. Murdie with No 2 Section and parties from the 43rd and 58th Battalions cleaning out trenches, placing gas curtains, excavating for a Dressing Station, building a fire bay, and salvaging material. Lieut. Sproule with No 4 Section and parties from the 43rd Battalion and 7th Machine Gun Company wiring, salvaging material, repairing pipe line and working on a machine gun emplacement. One sapper, name inserted above the line and read as "Bomb" [uncertain], slightly wounded; at duty. 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade Operation Order No 159 received, whereby two battalions in the front line were to be relieved by two battalions in reserve — later cancelled. C.R.E. 37/81 received, being policy of dugout work, providing, inter alia, for improvement of three battalion headquarters; Major Robertson conferred with the Brigade Major, work to be commenced on the 2nd left front battalion headquarters first. C.R.E. 19/96 referring to G 210 received, giving warning of the intended relief of the Canadian Corps by the 17th and 18th Corps; relief to commence night of 30th April–1st May 1918, later postponed 24 hours. 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade B.M. 10 received referring to the same matter. Advanced billets slightly shelled by the enemy. | People: Lieut. Jones; Lieut. Murdie; Lieut. Sproule; Major Robertson; Sapper "Bomb" [uncertain]. | Companies: No 1 Section; No 2 Section; No 3 Section; No 4 Section; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion; 7th Machine Gun Company; 9th Canadian Infantry Brigade; 17th Corps; 18th Corps. | Locations: Bully Switch. | Casualties: One sapper, "Bomb" [uncertain], slightly wounded; at duty.

- **1918-04-29 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Lens–Bethune Road sector, France [APPENDIX ENTRY]** — Appendix work reports, 29 April: No. 4 Section wired and repaired 100 yds of double apron fence between Cut Off Trench and Counter Alley, repaired 720 yds of double apron fence from Canteen to Carfax, repaired the Douglas push line and returned a salvaged push truck to Eddy Dump, picked up all material along the Douglas push line, patrolled and repaired the pipe line to Cow Alley, and worked on a dugout at Champlain Emplacement (N.1.C.80.40, entrance cleaned out, 10 in. drifted in, one set placed); No. 2 Section cleaned out trenches in Counter (60 yds), Cosy (10 yds) and Nestor (15 yds), repaired 75 yds of wire (N.8.a.8.7 to N.8.a.8.5), salvaged screw stakes, wooden stakes, coils of wire and two pumps complete with hose, drove a 3½ ft face on a dugout on Cosy (frames placed and lagged, steps built), improved the St Pierre Switch trench, excavated to find a cellar at N.7.b.1.5, and repaired four curtains on tunnel entrances. Casualties nil (No. 2 Section). | People: Lieut. W.C. Murdie [uncertain]; J. E. [uncertain], Lieut. | Companies: No. 2 Section; No. 4 Section; 43rd Battalion; 58th Battalion. | Locations: Cut Off Trench; Counter Alley; Canteen; Carfax; Douglas Dump; Eddy Dump; Cow Alley; Champlain Emplacement; Counter Trench; Cosy Trench; Nestor Trench; St Pierre Switch trench. | Casualties: Nil (No. 2 Section).

Green of "Company in the Attack in open warfare", "A" and "B" Companies and battalion specialists attending in the morning and "C" and "D" Companies in the afternoon, "D" Company repeating the exercise in the afternoon, and orders were received from the 8th Canadian Infantry Brigade that the battalion would move from its present location on the morning of the 5th and march to Witterness. | People: Lieut. - **1918-05-04 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Hostile batteries at U.14.a.72.66 and U.14.a.55.45 each subjected to 10 rounds rapid fire at 12.55 p.m.; calibration successfully carried out at 6.10 p.m.; aeroplane shoot on H.B. at U.12.b.64.46 successfully completed, 250 rounds fired; H.B. at U.8.b.11.19 neutralized at 10.25 p.m.; rear section carried out a programme of harassing fire during the night on enemy roads, firing 80 rounds; enemy artillery shelled S.24.d and T.25.d with H.E. and gas shell; Lieut. P. C. Harding posted to unit for duty. | People: Lieut. P. C. Harding. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-05-04 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Marquay, France** — Dull, north wind. Company engaged in gas drill, squad drill and rifle exercise. 9th C.I. Brigade O.O. No 161 received, with a march table attached, whereby the 9th Field Company C.E. is to move first on the brigade march from Marquay to Burbure; head of column to pass from Marquay at 10 a.m. and not to cross the Pernes–Divion Road before 2 p.m. The O.C. attended the Brigade Major at La Thieuloye re certain points re the move. C.R.E. 19-20 referring to 3rd Canadian Division O.O. 158 received, whereby the 9th Field Company C.E. is to move from Marquay to Burbure under orders of the 9th C.I. Brigade, and advising that the C.R.E. office is to open in Norrent Fontes. #502881 Spr. T.B. McLeod sent to hospital sick. Five reinforcements arrived from the Base Depot and are taken on the strength of the company as from this date. | People: Spr. T.B. McLeod #502881. | Companies: 9th C.I. Brigade; 3rd Canadian Division. | Locations: Burbure; Pernes–Divion Road; La Thieuloye; Norrent Fontes. | Casualties: #502881 Spr. T.B. McLeod sick, sent to hospital. | Movement: Company to march Marquay → Burbure on 5 May.

Baldock with pontoons etc. joined the company on the line of march at Rainbeet. Company billeted in Burbure in houses and barns; horses under corrugated iron shelters. | People: Lieut. - **1918-05-14 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — 18 rounds on Ivy Cottage for registration of No. 2 gun using ground and balloon observation; destructive aeroplane shoot on headquarters in N30b 40.70, 120 rounds, 1 Y, 8 Z's, 7 A's and 3 M.O.K.s, houses badly knocked about with 2 large and 1 small explosion; second aeroplane shoot in the evening on H.B. - **1918-05-14 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 3.10 p.m. an aeroplane shoot commenced on H.B. at U.14.a.49.52, completed at 6.40 p.m., 300 rounds fired; N.F. call answered at 9 p.m.; harassing fire during night on Betrincourt Farm, 60 rounds fired; rear section fired 25 rounds harassing fire on to Maud Villas N.36.c, and 40 rounds on to enemy roads at N.30.c. and N.36.b.; hostile artillery activity nil. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-05-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Quarbeque, France** — Fine; the battalion paraded on the alarm post for the O.C.'s inspection, after which the battalion was to have carried out a tactical exercise, this however was cancelled, and companies carried on independently with the training syllabus laid down — musketry, rapid loading and aiming, judging distances, fire orders, fire control and post action drill — specialists carrying on under specialist officers, and recreation in the afternoon. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-05-15 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Hostile shelling at times above normal with two destructive shoots by the enemy, during which 3 Other Ranks were wounded; 15 rounds on NX 28 by balloon observation; evening aeroplane shoot on H.B. NX 66, 120 rounds, satisfactory results. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 3 Other Ranks wounded (unnamed)
- **1918-05-15 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Unsuccessful aeroplane shoot given up after 32 rounds; shoot again attempted on same target, H.B. at U.2.b.26.90, this time successfully, shoot completed to 300 rounds; several N.F. calls answered and much harassing fire carried out, 125 rounds fired; rear section fired 130 rounds into Mericourt at T.6.a. and cross roads at N.30.a.; enemy fired about 270 rounds of H.E. and shrapnel into S.24.d. and vicinity; no damage and no casualties caused. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-05-15 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Burbure, France** — Clear and warm, west wind. Under authority Canadian Corps A.105-2 of 17-4-18 and War Office letter 121/0. 3783 (S.D.2) dated 5-5-18, batmen for the three surplus subalterns in Field and Army Troops Companies and Canadian Engineers are authorized to be found from within the existing establishment. Company engaged in manoeuvres: advancing in skirmishing order etc. under the O.C. in the neighbourhood of the woods to the N.E. of the company billets; target practice in the afternoon. Company supplied almost daily a wagon with team, or a tradesman, to work with the Area Commandant near Burbure.

- **1918-05-17 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Burbure, France** — Very warm, S.E. wind. Official information received that the reorganization of the Canadian Engineers into Engineer Battalions would shortly become effective. One N.C.O. and three men, considered unfit for front line work, were transferred to the Canadian Engineers Reinforcement Depot today. Company training today as follows: gas drill instruction and musketry, extended order drill, pontoon and trestle bridging. A confidential letter was received from the C.R.E. inviting recommendations for certain appointments for officers; also instructing this company to arrange, on paper only, for three of their sections, including transport, to remain as at present to form a nucleus of three companies of a battalion; the fourth section to detail one N.C.O. and 7 other ranks to the Bridging Train, the remainder to be split up among the other three sections. The 123rd Pioneer Battalion was also instructed to divide their four companies into 4 parts or groups for distribution. Nominal rolls of the above, showing trades, were sent to the C.R.E. | Companies: 123rd Pioneer Battalion. | Casualties: One N.C.O. and three men transferred to the Canadian Engineers Reinforcement Depot as unfit for front line work.

- **1918-05-24 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Burbure, France** — Dull with rain, S.E. wind. Company training as follows: gas drill, lecture, rifle ranges. Major Robertson attended a conference at the C.R.E.'s Office in Norrent Fontes, where the C.R.E., his adjutant, the Colonel of the 123rd Battalion and the O's C. 7th and 8th Field Companies C.E. were present. It was officially announced by the C.R.E. that the reorganization of the Canadian Engineers would be effected at once — including the Field Companies C.E., Canadian Pioneer Battalions, 5th Canadian Divisional Engineers, and men at the Canadian Engineers Reinforcement Depot in France, and affecting certain men at the Canadian Engineers Training Depot, England. Authority for this reorganisation was approved in War Office letter telegram No 76962, dated 3-4-18, and Canadian Corps A105-1 of 6-4-18. 3rd Canadian Engineers Brigade C.R.E. 11/245 of 27-5-18 subsequently received, setting out further particulars of this reorganisation. The principle governing appointments was announced as follows: officers nominated by the C.E. Canadian Corps from the seniority lists of officers, Pioneer officers, 5th Canadian Divisional Engineers, and Canadian Army Troops Companies; no Engineer subalterns to be promoted unless they had served 9 months in France; Pioneer subalterns not to be promoted unless they had previous engineer experience in civil life; promotions in future to be by seniority. The O.C. 123rd Pioneer Battalion informed the conference that his Companies A, B and C had been kept practically intact in certain groups and Company D had been divided into thirds, each third being joined to one other company for allotment to Engineer Battalions; the 9th Canadian Engineer Battalion received "C" Company and 1/3 of "D" Company of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion. The transport, horses, bicycles etc. of the 123rd Battalion are also to be divided among the 7th, 8th and 9th Canadian Engineer Battalions. It was directed by the C.R.E. that company funds of the old units should remain as company funds of the new units respectively, including canteen funds and funds comprising the old company's proportion of Y.M.C.A. profits; the funds of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion being distributed among the new Engineer Battalions (7th, 8th and 9th). The bandsmen of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion are being distributed among the 7th, 8th and 9th Engineers Battalions. The 3rd Canadian Division Bridging Unit is being formed with the equipment formerly with the 7th, 8th and 9th Field Companies C.E.; personnel and horses being allotted from the new Engineer Battalions of the 3rd Canadian Division Engineer Brigade, the officers being allotted similarly to the officers in other units. The 9th Canadian Engineer Battalion, 3rd Canadian Engineer Brigade, is to be commanded by Major N. R. Robertson, formerly O.C. 9th Field Company C.E. The officer appointments for the new battalion are listed in the diary (p. 17): 2nd in command Major Boone, C.A.; Adjutant Lieut. C. McN. Steeves; O/C S&T A.S. Houston; Q.M. Capt. Magg [uncertain]; M.O. Brogdon; "A" Company O.C. Capt. J.J. Miller with Lieuts. A.M. West, E.P. Taylor, S.C. Dixon, J.G. Ferguson, J.E. Sproule, F.S. McBrine; "B" Company O.C. Capt. A.H. Macdonald with Lieuts. R.B. Gibson, F.S. Jones, R.B. Perrault, H.L. Chittenden, H.V. Serson; "C" Company O.C. Major E.P. Brown with Lieuts. J.M. Fitzgerald [uncertain], C.S. Walley, J.W. Mangus [uncertain], W.C. Cole, W.C. Murdie, J.W. Baldock, B.H. Cronyn. Warning order received that the 9th Field Company C.E. would move to Auchy-au-Bois on the 25th for the purpose of reorganization. 3rd Canadian Division Engineers Operation Order No 56 of today's date received, reciting in accordance with Canadian Corps G.783/1-31 of 23-5-18 and 3rd Canadian Division G 718 of 24-5-18 that the reorganization of Canadian Engineers units would commence at once: 3rd Canadian Engineers Brigade will be formed at Norrent Fontes; the 7th Canadian Engineer Battalion will be formed at Ligny-les-Aire by the 7th Field Company C.E. and groups 1, 2 and 3 of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion; the 8th Canadian Engineer Battalion will be formed at Westrehem by the 8th Field Company C.E. and groups 4, 5 and 6 of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion; the 9th Canadian Engineer Battalion will be formed at Auchy by the 9th Field Company C.E. and groups 7, 8 and 9 of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion; the above groups to join their units on 25 May 1918. The 3rd Canadian Division Pontoon Bridging Unit is to be formed at Auchy, 29 May 1918, subsequently changed to Nedonchelle and 28 May 1918. C.A.M.C. personnel under orders from 6 A.M.C. to join units on 27 May. | People: Major Robertson; Major N. R. Robertson; Major Boone, C.A.; Lieut. C. McN. Steeves; A.S. Houston; Capt. - **1918-05-25 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Aeroplane shoot commenced at 2.31 p.m. on H.B. at U.8.b.84.68 and brought to a successful conclusion at 5.55 p.m., 200 rounds fired; rear section carried out very successful shoot on enemy trench at N.34.d.58.90 to N.34.b.70.10, several O.Ks reported, and neutralized two hostile batteries Nos U.W.57 and U.W.79, firing 50 rounds; usual night firing programme by both sections. | Casualties: none.
- **1918-05-25 | 9th Field Company, Canadian Engineers | Auchy-au-Bois, France** — Dull and cloudy, S.E. wind. C.R.E. 11-154 of 25-5-18 received, giving an amended list of officers selected for temporary appointments to battalions and the Bridging Unit as approved by the C.E. Canadian Corps, whereby inter alia the 2nd Section of "B" Company, 9th Canadian Engineers Battalion, is to be commanded by Lieut. H.L. Chittenden C.E. (from C.E.R.D.) vice Lieut. J.E. Sproule, who has not completed his 9 months in France; also advising Lieut. Walley and Lieut. Chittenden to report to the 9th C.E. Battalion. Reinforcements from C.E.R.D., including 5th Canadian Division Engineers, to be expected at the rate of 100 other ranks per battalion in a few days. The 9th Field Company C.E. fell in on parade with transport at 7:30 a.m., moved off at 8 a.m. under command of Major Robertson, and proceeded via Hurionville and Amettes to Auchy-au-Bois, where the company billeted in very congested billets in the west end of the village. Groups 7, 8 and 9 of the 123rd Pioneer Battalion also marched in and billeted further west in the hamlet of Tatineloux [uncertain]. The 8th Field Company with their groups of pioneers also moved in and billeted in Auchy-au-Bois temporarily. **This is the last 9th Field Company diary entry; the diary of the 9th Field Company ends here.** | People: Major Robertson; Lieut. H.L. Chittenden; Lieut. J.E. Sproule; Lieut. Walley. | Companies: 9th C.E. Battalion; 8th Field Company; 123rd Pioneer Battalion; 5th Canadian Division Engineers. | Locations: Hurionville; Amettes; Tatineloux [uncertain]. | Movement: Burbure → Auchy-au-Bois.
- **1918-05-25 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | Red Head Camp, St. John, N.B.** — Syllabus followed, except that on Friday (24 May) a general holiday was observed; starting Tuesday, the morning parade was blown at 8.00 a.m. instead of 8.45, the work being moved ahead and the extra time used in the afternoon for section and company drill, with much improvement noted; attention also directed to saluting (letter of 25 May 1918, Camp Red Head, Major, O.C.). Diary: lectures on conduct in camp and in town, personal hygiene, venereal disease, camp sanitation and military law. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-05-26 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Neuville Vitasse** — Desultory shelling by the enemy over the whole area and rear country; a courageous act was done this morning by 219203 Cpl. J. A. Kelley, who at 2.15 a.m. with a covering party left our trench at N.19.a.70.89 and proceeded up an old communication trench towards enemy lines to locate the positions and defences of an enemy post, got close up to the post, shot 2 of the occupants and dragged the third across the barrier as a prisoner, and returned safely to our line; shortly after, a party of the enemy estimated at 15 to 18 came down the trench toward the raided post, and Cpl. Dougall and sentries in A Company immediately opened fire, one of the enemy being seen to fall and the remainder disappearing. | People: Cpl. J. A. Kelley; Cpl. Dougall. | Companies: A Company.

- **1918-05-27 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven, France** — Heavy gas bombardment of yellow and blue cross gas from 1.57 to 2.57 a.m., over 1,000 shells in an hour, gas shells freely mixed with 5.9" H.E.; gas curtains lowered and S.B.R.s adjusted, only two casualties, both signallers working on the signal lines; gas shell holes treated with chloride of lime; 120-round aeroplane shoot on NX37 in the morning, successful. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 signallers gassed (unnamed)
- **1918-05-27 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — Enemy gas bombardment continued until 5.45 a.m.; no material damage caused, but Gnr. F. Holland, Gnr. J. J. Lynch and Gnr. J. Moreland all gassed, none dangerous; aeroplane shoot commenced at 10.57 a.m. on H.B. at U.15.d.65.11 but unsuccessful, again attempted at 5.07 p.m., this time successfully, 200 rounds fired; harassing fire on enemy roads and junctions during the night; rear section fired 55 rounds on enemy trench at N.36.d.90 and N.36.c.95.10; enemy artillery activity nil during the day. | People: Gnr. F. Holland; Gnr. J. J. Lynch; Gnr. J. Moreland. | Casualties: 3 O.R. gassed (Gnrs. Holland, Lynch, Moreland), none dangerous.

- **1918-05-28 | 18th Battalion | Front line, Neuville Vitasse** — During the night of 27/28th the battalion raided 2 enemy posts at approx. N.19.a.70.50 and N.19.a.90.85: No. 1 party of four bombers under Lieut. Sheridan left our trench and bombed the post at N.19.a.73.80, throwing twenty bombs into the post, while No. 2 party of 8 Battalion Scouts under Lieut. J. W. MacRae, with Bomb Sgt. J. Manly, rushed the barricade at the second post and bombed up the trench; both parties were prevented from following up by our own barrage opening up around them, and both returned to our lines without casualty. | People: Lieut. Sheridan; Lieut. J. W. MacRae; Bomb Sgt. J. Manly. | Companies: Battalion Scouts.

- **1918-06-03 | 5th Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Waverly Camp, France** — Fair but cooler, visibility good; aeroplane shoot carried out by X2 on hostile trench mortar, 50 rounds fired; 20 rounds fired from Y2 with ground observation, good results; Y2 put in action and registered; mobile sections turned out for practice, time taken 38 minutes. | People: — | Companies: X Battery, Y Battery | Casualties: none
- **1918-06-03 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bomy, France** — Fine; the battalion participated in 3rd Cdn. Division Tactical Scheme No. 4 in conjunction with other battalions of the 8th Cdn. Inf. Brigade, 7th Cdn. Inf. Brigade, one brigade C.F.A., two machine gun companies, C.L.H. and two detachments of Field Ambulance, assembling in the field east of Reclinghem at 9.30 a.m. and receiving orders to follow the 4th C.M.R. Battalion as far as Delette and then attack and make good Hill 140, Enquinegatte, Bassée-Boulogne, Marthes and Ham, the attack on Hill 140 commencing at 1.35 p.m. and progressing satisfactorily until information was received that the enemy was attacking in force at Petigny, the battalion being ordered to hold ground on Hill 140, detach 2 companies and attack the enemy advancing on Petigny from the north, before which attack could be developed it was stopped by the 1st and 2nd C.M.R. Battalions, the battalion then proceeding to carry out the original orders and developing a strong attack on Equinegatte when the "Dismiss" was sounded at 5.20 p.m. | People: — | Companies: 4th C.M.R. Bn.; 1st C.M.R. Bn.; 2nd C.M.R. Bn. | Casualties: none

- **1918-06-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bomy, France** — Showery; the battalion participated in 3rd Canadian Divisional Scheme No. 5 and formed part of a Southern Force comprising Headquarters 3rd Canadian Division, 7th and 8th Cdn. Inf. Brigades, one squadron Cdn. Light Horse, 3rd Cdn. Div. C.F.A. (skeleton), 3rd Cdn. M.G. Battalion less one company (skeleton) and one aeroplane, assembling at 9 a.m. south of Big Wood west of Cuhem, and at 10 a.m. orders were received that the 5th C.M.R. Battalion would be "Detached Force" to the Southern Forces and would clear Bomy and Petigny and make a demonstration on the right flank of the enemy to divert attention from the attack by the main Southern Force, Bomy being cleared by 10.30 a.m. and the troops north of Bomy by 11.30 a.m., strong opposition being met on the high ground W.N.W. Petigny at 12.10 p.m., with little progress from that point, and strong attacks being made on the enemy positions until the advance again continued toward Equinegatte, when the "Dismiss" sounded and the battalion returned to billets. | People: — | Companies: 7th C.I.B.; 8th C.I.B. | Casualties: none

- **1918-06-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bomy to Flechin, France** — Fine; the battalion participated in 3rd Cdn. Division Tactical Scheme No. 7 and formed part of the Western Force, rendezvousing on the Reclinghem–Petigny Road half a mile east of Reclinghem, and received orders to seize Bomy, the western edge of Big Wood east of Bomy, Hill 105 and the crossing of the Laquette River, moving forward at 9 a.m. and reporting Bomy clear of the enemy at 9.40 a.m. and Petigny captured at 10 a.m., and by 10.30 a.m. the enemy had been cleared and the advanced guard were on Hill 105, at 12.25 p.m. the enemy attacked in strength and at 1.55 p.m. the battalion was withdrawn to the high ground west of Bomy and Petigny, where with the 1st C.M.R. Battalion they withheld the enemy attacks, and at 5 p.m. the enemy made a strong attack on Hill 140 held by the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion, instructions being issued for A Company to reinforce the 2nd C.M.R. before the "Dismiss" was sounded; instructions had been received that the battalion would vacate Bomy and be billeted in Flechin, and at the conclusion of the manoeuvres the battalion paraded in the square at Bomy and proceeded by route march to Flechin, arriving in billets at 8 p.m. | People: — | Companies: 1st C.M.R. Bn.; 2nd C.M.R. Bn.; "A" Coy. | Casualties: none | Movement: Bomy–Flechin (route march).

- **1918-07-01 | 5th Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Waverly Camp, France** — The only event of importance in the war was the Canadian Corps sports held at Tinques; the unit was forced to enter the long hopping contest and feels entitled to the rated Class A; allotted transport did not report, but all men got there safely and returned without walking; Canadian women were at the gathering; staff cars served refreshing drinks but the E.F.C. was woefully inadequate; those without pull or friends in high places came home after; the D.T.M.O., who did not enter the contest, rode home and his groom now considers him a hero. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-07-01 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front Line, Mercatel sector, France** — Fine; the 5th C.M.R. Battalion relieved the 22nd French Canadian Battalion in the front line, right sub-section, Mercatel sector, relief complete by 2.10 a.m., the enemy very quiet with very little artillery, trench mortar or machine-gun activity during the day, and three patrols left our line at 11 p.m. to cover the battalion frontage, under Lieut. Weldon (19 other ranks), Lieut. Savage (17 other ranks) and Lieut. Smith, while companies carried on constructing funk holes and trench maintenance; Dominion Day sports were held at Tinques under the auspices of the Canadian Corps, with three entries from this battalion, but they were defeated in the finals. | People: Lieut. Weldon; Lieut. Savage; Lieut. Smith. | Companies: 22nd Cdn. Bn. (relieved). | Casualties: none | Movement: Bellacourt–front line, Mercatel sector (relief of 22nd Cdn. Bn.).
- **1918-07-01 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven / Neuville St Vaast, France** — Corps sports at Tinques, all available men sent by lorry; H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught visited First Army including Canadian Corps H.Q. and the sports; North Section at Lieven heavily gassed during the night with no casualties; hostile batteries neutralized at 11.45 a.m. and 9.30 p.m., harassing fire at night. | People: H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught. | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1918-07-02 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Lieven / Neuville St Vaast, France** — During the previous night's gas bombardment 2–5.9" yellow cross gas shells fell in No. 1 gun pit and several around No. 2 pit; despite large gas concentrations the section carried out a destructive aeroplane shoot on a hostile battery at O14c 23.62 wearing S.B.R.s and anti-gas gloves, very successful (6 Y's, 8 Z's, 6 A's, 4 M.O.K.s, large explosion at Z3); destructive aeroplane shoot on UW 63, 9 Z's, 11 A's, 1 M.O.K., No. 2 pit received a direct hit; both positions heavily shelled 2–3 p.m. and again about midnight. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none
- **1918-07-02 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 11 a.m. H.B. at O.25c 23.60 [uncertain] subjected to 20 rounds neutralizing fire, battery reported silenced; during the night harassing fire maintained on enemy positions at O.25c 30.25 and U16 70.95, 60 rounds fired; rear section carried out calibration on Acheville Church and fired 50 rounds at enemy dump at N29b 13.53; enemy 5.9 battery attempted to range on No. 4 gun (S. 2nd) [uncertain] with air burst, apparently given up as unsuccessful. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-07-05 | 9th Canadian Siege Battery | Petit-Vimy, France** — At 5.45 p.m. a shoot with aeroplane observation commenced, 3 O.K.s reported during ranging; while the shoot was in progress the personnel of the battery was relieved by the personnel of the 7th Can. OY 92 by Lieut. D. A. Guildford, observed by Lieut. W. M. Ballantyne seriously wounded, a shell splinter penetrating the neck just behind the jugular vein, his life saved by No. 346944 Cpl. W. Forsythe, who staunched the bleeding with his hands under heavy shell fire until first aid could be applied. | People: No. 314726 Gnr. W. M. Ballantyne; No. 346944 Cpl. W. - **1918-07-20 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | Battery Point Camp, St. John, N.B.** — Weather much better and the syllabus carried out with good results; a layers class of 20 other ranks were examined at Partridge Island and, with two exceptions, passed the tests with good marks; a draft of 75 men was selected on Friday (19 July) for overseas, including the majority of the signalling class which had just completed training; new classes in signalling and gunnery have been selected to begin next week's syllabus; arrangements are being made with the S.O.O. for two old Armstrong 40-pounder guns on travelling carriages, which will greatly facilitate section gun drill (letter of 20 July 1918, Major, O.C.). - **1918-08-02 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Namps au Monts and Rumaisnil to Plachy Buyon, France** — Heavy rain; orders were received at 2 a.m. that the battalion would witness a tank demonstration, two companies participating, at Bois de Bacouel, and also that the battalion would vacate the present billets at 9.30 p.m. and march to Bois de Hebecourt and bivouac there, at noon the battalion with Lewis gun limbers proceeded to the demonstration, at 4.50 p.m. orders were received that the battalion would be billeted in Plachy Buyon, all details proceeding direct to Plachy Buyon at 5 p.m., tea being served to the men at 6 p.m. with no more rations or tea, the battalion parading at 8.45 p.m. and moving off at 9 p.m. and marching to Plachy Buyon, where, in spite of the rain and no rations, the spirits of the men were splendid, and on arrival rations were in and the men were given a good supper. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Namps au Monts / Rumaisnil–Plachy Buyon.

- **1918-08-07 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | St Nicholas area, France** — Fine weather; operation orders for the advance were received, apparently on a big scale, the principal feature being the absence of a preliminary bombardment, the O.C. attended a conference held at Brigade Headquarters, Gentiles Wood, at 12 noon, in the afternoon extra rations were issued, making a total for each man of 48 hours in addition to iron rations, also an extra water bottle, with [uncertain] bombs, stretchers and etc. to be issued, the O.C. returned at 5 p.m., a conference of company commanders was held at 5.40 p.m., operation orders were issued at 8 p.m., and at 8.30 p.m. field kitchens etc. were sent to transport, as all 1st line transport had to be clear west of the Avre River by 9 p.m., the battalion moving forward to assembly positions in the order Headquarters, A, B, C, D. | People: — | Companies: "A" Coy.; "B" Coy.; "C" Coy.; "D" Coy.; H.Q. - **1918-08-08 | 18th Battalion | Front line — Marcelcave** — Zero hour was 4.20 a.m.; heavy fog obscured the German line, and German heavy artillery laid a light barrage on the battalion's position shortly before the attack, ceasing just before the Canadian guns opened with no preliminary bombardment. The battalion jumped off at 4.20 under a creeping barrage, closely co-operating with tanks: "C" Coy. on the right flank in contact with the 1st Cdn. Division, "B" Coy. in the centre, "A" Coy. on the left connecting with the 19th Cdn. Battalion, and "D" Coy. in support. The objective, some 200 yards east of Marcelcave and the adjoining quarry, was reached by 7.45 a.m.; five 5.9 howitzers and three 7.7 mm guns were captured at Marcelcave, with signal equipment and surgical and medical stores, and the battalion pushed on to establish a line of defence about 300 yards beyond. Lieut. Ferguson was wounded in the jumping off, Capt. Michell [uncertain] and Capt. Wigle were wounded in the first half mile, and Lieuts. Faulkner and Sheridan were wounded a short time later; Capt. T.H.O. Rayward's work against machine-gun nests was exemplary. Approximately 30 killed and 120 wounded were sustained in the advance; 56 other ranks arrived as reinforcements and 2 other ranks proceeded on leave. | People: Lieut. Ferguson; Capt. Michell [uncertain]; Capt. Wigle; Lieut. Faulkner; Lieut. Sheridan; Capt. T.H.O. Rayward. | Companies: 1st Cdn. Division; 19th Cdn. Battalion; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: Marcelcave; Villers-Bretonneux. | Movement: Jumping-off line → Marcelcave and quarry.
- **1918-08-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Domart, France** — The battle commenced at 4.20 a.m. with a heavy short bombardment, many tanks and aeroplanes, telephonic communication was lost with the brigades from the start, visual signalling became effective after the dust and smoke cleared, cable wagons followed the brigades where possible, and towards evening Divisional and Brigade HQs grouped in Valley Wood with good telephone communication before moving to Hamel Wood, with 2 O.Rs. casualties for the day and Capt. K.M. Campbell taking over command. | People: Capt. K.M. Campbell. | Companies: — | Casualties: **2 O.Rs. — casualties for the day** | Movement: Domart–Valley Wood–Hamel Wood.
- **1918-08-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Plachy Buyon** — If the attack gains its objectives the Train may move forward to Boves and M.T. will come into use again, as the long haul over very bad roads is telling on the horses; at 2 p.m. orders came to move at once to Bois de Gentelles, then changed to Domart owing to the success of the advance. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: ordered to Domart.
- **1918-08-08 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Boves / C.4.d Central (Sheet 66E)** — Amiens offensive: D.T.M.O. and officers commanding X3c and Y3c proceeded forward to the assembly position in front of Gentelle Woods in the evening with gun crews and mobile mortars; at 4.20 a.m. the mobile mortars left the assembly position and proceeded to C.4.d Central, arriving 5.30 a.m.; 2 mules killed and 3 O.Rs wounded; officers went forward to reconnoitre and found the infantry moving forward without resistance, and assisted in carrying out the wounded; at 8 a.m. mortars moved forward to C.12.a 20.70 and at 11 a.m. to D.7.a 70.50 where the night was spent; constant communication with 7th Cdn Infy. Bde; officers reconnoitred roads to the Red Line towards Beacourt. | People: none | Companies: X3c M.T.M. Battery; Y3c M.T.M. Battery; 7th Cdn Infy. - **1918-08-08 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | St Nicholas area, France** — At 12.30 a.m. the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion arrived in busses at 12.20 a.m. and were guided to their assembly positions by officers of our B and D Companies, at 3 a.m. Lieut. Logie's patrol returned and stated that only one C.M.H. [uncertain] man could be found and that he had died from his wounds, at 4.20 a.m. the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion proceeded to advance on Les Quesnoy, at 6 a.m. the Brigadier-General of the 96th Inf. Bde., 32nd Imperial Division, arrived at our headquarters and stated that his brigade was going through the 2nd C.M.R. and pushing on, information being received later in the morning that the 2nd C.M.R. Battalion had captured Les Quesnoy after hard fighting and that the 1st C.M.R. had pushed through them to the north and had reached the old British front line of 1916, and at 3 p.m. operation orders were received that we were in Corps reserve and would immediately consolidate a main line of defence east of Bowohor [uncertain], Battalion Headquarters moving to K.22.65060. | People: Lieut. Logie. | Companies: 2nd C.M.R. Bn.; 1st C.M.R. Bn.; 96th Inf. Bde., 32nd Imperial Div. | Casualties: none

- **1918-08-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Amiens area, Corps reserve, France** — At 2 p.m. information was received that the 32nd Division had met with strenuous opposition, and transport rejoined the unit at 5 p.m., field kitchens immediately being sent to companies and the men given a good meal, the diary noting it seemed strange that 24 hours ago they had captured this ground and tonight they were undressing and going to bed well behind the lines in Corps reserve; casualties for the operations were 2 officers wounded (Lieut. Atto M.C. and Lieut. Poley, wounded at duty), 2 other ranks killed, 2 died of wounds, 50 wounded, 1 wounded at duty and 2 missing, totals 2 officers and 57 other ranks, with over 100 prisoners taken, and trophies of 1 4.1 howitzer carriage and ammunition limber, 1 medium minenwerfer, 1 heavy machine gun, 4 recaptured Lewis guns, 1 light machine gun, 1 automatic rifle, 2 horses, 1 recaptured British [uncertain] wagon and 9 pineapples, a number of wagons captured in Arvillers being left in the hands of the French. | People: Lieut. Atto M.C.; Lieut. Poley. | Companies: 32nd Imperial Div. | Casualties: 2 officers wounded; 2 ORs killed, 2 ORs died of wounds, 50 ORs wounded, 1 OR wounded at duty, 2 ORs missing; enemy over 100 prisoners.

Buscroft on IA 65, 10 A's, 11 Z's, 4 Y's and 1 O.K., Z6 an O.K. on No. 3 pit; second shoot of 50 rounds observed by Lieut. E. S. Bushell, very successful, large explosion and good M.P.I.; 195 rounds counter-battery work, 40 rounds harassing fire and 39 rounds destructive work on a dump at Neuville Farm in S16d, dump destroyed. | People: Lieut. - **1918-08-11 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Amiens area, Corps reserve, France** — A conference at Brigade Headquarters at 2 p.m. for battalion commanders and adjutants informed them that the 7th Brigade would go through the 32nd Imperial Division at dawn on the 12th, push forward for 24 hours, when the 9th Brigade would go through them, and at the end of another 24 hours the 8th Brigade would go through the 9th Brigade, and at 5 p.m. information was received that both the 7th and 9th C.I. Brigades would pass through the 32nd Imperial Division; there were numerous enemy bombing planes over at night but no damage was done in our area, Lieut. Short proceeded on leave and Lieut. Ganong reported back from leave, bringing 53 reinforcements, and casualties were Lieut. Porter wounded, D Company 1 killed, 1 died of wounds and 4 wounded, B Company 4 wounded, and A Company 4 missing, the enemy apparently bringing up his artillery and offering a stout resistance. | People: Lieut. Brigade, the remainder of the brigade moving tomorrow night, 20/21, by bus, transport moving independently; at 6.30 p.m. orders were received to pass the starting point (W.10.4 south-west of Demuin) at 10.40 p.m., the battalion falling in at 7.45 p.m. and moving off at 8 p.m., forming the starting point at 10.35 p.m., orders then being received re entraining and that the route to the station was changed, the new orders being to proceed via Dennes [uncertain] and entrain at 3 a.m.; 78 reinforcements were received, 40 of them being French Canadians and rather a poor class. | People: — | Companies: 7th C.I.B. | Casualties: 4 horses killed, 1 horse wounded (no personnel hit). | Movement: Le Quesnel Wood–Boyes (march; to entrain).
