- **1918-08-26 | 18th Battalion | Telegraph Hill — Guémappe** — At 3.00 a.m., following an intense 5-minute barrage, the battalion jumped off from Tilloy Trench in front of Telegraph Hill in support of the 21st Cdn. Bn.; the tanks detailed to go over with the battalion failed to turn up per schedule, having got lost in the darkness. Minorca Trench, the first objective, and Southern Avenue Trench, the second objective, were both won by 8.00 a.m., with "D" Coy. holding the latter in conjunction with the 21st Cdn. Bn., "A" Coy. remaining in Gordon Trench and "B" Coy. at Minorca Trench. Lieut. McVardy [uncertain] had gone only a short distance from the assault trench when he sustained mortal shrapnel wounds. At 1 o'clock the battalion was ordered to capture the village of Guisappe [uncertain] (Guémappe); after personal reconnaissances in broad daylight and under severe fire by Major C.M.R. Graham and Capt. D.A.G. Parsons, M.C., O.Cs. respectively of "D" and "C" Coys., "C" and "D" Coys. advanced at 4.00 p.m. and captured the ruined town, in the face of terrific machine-gun and artillery barrages. Lieut. Brackin [uncertain], who had done brilliant work up to this moment, was instantly killed by a shell, and Capt. Parsons and Lieut. Edwards sustained wounds that resulted in their immediate evacuation. "C" and "D" Coys. occupied and consolidated Stag Trench, and "A" and "B" Coys. moved forward to Rake and Gordon Trenches respectively. At 11 p.m. "A" Coy. under Lieut. Spence went forward and captured Cavalry Trench, but the unit on their immediate left was held up, and the company, after 4 hours of desperate fighting, was compelled at 3.00 a.m. on the 27th to withdraw temporarily to Rake Trench. Approximately 10 killed and 15 wounded all ranks; 1 other rank returned from leave and 1 other rank was on leave, and 2 other ranks returned from 1st Army Rest Camp. | People: Lieut. McVardy [uncertain]; Major C.M.R. Graham; Capt. D.A.G. Parsons; Lieut. Brackin [uncertain]; Capt. Parsons; Lieut. Edwards; Lieut. Spence. | Companies: 21st Cdn. Bn.; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: Tilloy Trench; Telegraph Hill; Minorca Trench; Southern Avenue Trench; Gordon Trench; Guémappe; Stag Trench; Rake Trench; Cavalry Trench. | Movement: Tilloy Trench → Minorca Trench → Guémappe / Stag Trench.

- **1918-08-26 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Monchy-le-Preux area, Arras–Cambrai Road, France** — Diary text: "See appendix"; from Appendix 9, Summary of Operations 26–28 August: zero hour 3 a.m., the 8th C.I. Brigade attacking to capture the enemy positions from the Arras–Cambrai Road to the Scarpe River in conjunction with the 2nd Canadian Division, the 5th C.M.R. Battalion being allotted the Green Line, the Red Line and Monchy village and the protection of the right flank, with "A" and "C" Companies forming the attacking waves, "A" on the right, "B" in support and "D" in reserve; the barrage opened and appeared somewhat ragged, a number of shots falling short and inflicting casualties on our own men, Capt. W. J. Atherton, O.C. "A" Company, being killed by one of our own shells shortly after his company moved forward, strong opposition was encountered at Halifax Trench, which was overcome by Lewis gunners and rifle grenadiers, six enemy heavy machine guns, three anti-tank rifles, two light trench mortars and about sixty prisoners being taken there, and at 3.30 a.m. the first objective (Green Line) was reached simultaneously by the two attacking companies. | People: Capt. W. J. Atherton. | Companies: "A" Coy.; "B" Coy.; "C" Coy.; "D" Coy.; 4th C.M.R. Bn.; 2nd C.M.R. Bn.; 1st C.M.R. Bn. | Casualties: Capt. W. J. Atherton killed (by one of our own shells); other casualties in the 26–28 August operations are given under 28 August.

- **1918-08-27 | 18th Battalion | Rake Trench — Sensée River** — With the Arras-Cambrai Road as the left boundary, the battalion, supported by the 20th Cdn. Bn., attacked Villers Cachicourt [uncertain] at 10 a.m.; by noon Vis-en-Artois and the Sensée River and Sensée River Valley had been reached. A barrage scheduled to continue after half an hour's curtailment failed to materialise, so an outpost line running from Vis-en-Artois along the west bank of the river had to be formed. Major McIntosh, Acting O.C. of the battalion, was wounded while reconnoitring forward positions, and command of the unit fell to Major Bell. Lieut. Spence, D.C.M., "A" Coy., was shot and killed by a German sniper, and Lieut. Gerrard suffered severe wounds from shell fire. 3 other ranks went to England for an Officers Course and 2 other ranks to England for an R.A.F. Course. Approximately 15 killed and 150 wounded all ranks. Major J.J. Richardson returned from an Officers Course in England; 4 other ranks went to and 2 returned from hospital, and 1 other rank was on leave. | People: Major McIntosh; Major Bell; Lieut. Spence; Lieut. Gerrard; Major J.J. Richardson. | Companies: 20th Cdn. Bn.; A Company. | Locations: Vis-en-Artois; Sensée River; Arras-Cambrai Road. | Movement: Rake Trench → Vis-en-Artois / Sensée River.

- **1918-08-28 | 18th Battalion | Sensée River — sunken roads** — Zero hour for this day's operation was set for 12.30 noon; the battalion was in support of the 20th Bn. Heavy casualties were suffered in the advance to the slope of the Sensée River, machine-gun nests and wire in the German line being equally heavy. Capt. Mackadie was shot through the head and instantly killed while rushing a German gun post; Lieut. Cole, shot through the eye, was afterwards found dead; Major Graham and Lts. Lawrence, Donaldson and Krug were wounded. Under terrific fire the battalion was compelled to temporarily withdraw and take up a line in the sunken roads fronting the German wire east of the Sensée River. 52 other ranks arrived as reinforcements and 3 other ranks were on leave; approximately 10 killed and 70 wounded all ranks. | People: Capt. Mackadie; Lieut. Cole; Major Graham; Lieut. Lawrence; Lieut. Donaldson; Lieut. Krug. | Companies: 20th Cdn. Bn. | Locations: Sensée River. | Movement: Sensée River line → sunken roads east of Sensée River.

Gibson continued his poled cable line to these HQs, completing it at 10 a.m., poled cable proved much better than hastily laid overland lines, wire trouble in the afternoon was cleared by 5 p.m., and the Division was relieved by 4th British Division, relief complete at 6.30 p.m., with all personnel except one office relief and Lieut. Pryde returning to rear HQ at Duisans. | People: Lieut. Gibson; Lieut. Pryde. | Companies: 8th C.I. Bde.; 9th C.I. Bde.; 4th British Div. | Casualties: none | Movement: London Cave–Duisans.

- **1918-08-28 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Remy Wood / Cojeul River area, France** — Diary text: "See appendix"; from Appendix 9, Summary of Operations: at 3 a.m. an operation order was received that the 23rd Canadian Battalion and the 5th C.M.R. Battalion, with artillery support, would attack the front and support trenches in O.11.d.–O.17.b. and Remy Wood at 12.30 p.m., the battalion moving forward to its assembly positions at 10.30 a.m. while still en route being subjected to intense shelling and heavy gas shelling, necessitating the wearing of small box respirators from noon until zero, and at zero the barrage opened, the attacking companies jumping off at zero plus 20, considerable machine-gun opposition being encountered at the junction of Black Trench and Remy Lane, the front line being rushed under cover of Lewis guns, the support line being successfully rushed, and at 1.15 p.m. the objectives had been gained, three wounded prisoners being sent back; the position was heavily shelled during the afternoon and evening, at 9 p.m. twelve enemy planes patrolled the position and dropped bombs, and at 9.30 p.m. the O.C. 1st Royal Warwicks reported at Battle Headquarters, his battalion being on its way in with orders for the relief of the 5th C.M.R. Battalion, the relief being completed at 1 a.m. on 29 August, when the battalion moved back and rested in O.30, the old trench system just east of Arras; casualties for the 26–28 August operations were Capt. W. J. Atherton and 13 other ranks killed, 1 other rank died of wounds, Capt. F. Gill, Lieuts. E. R. [uncertain], R. D. Farley, J. J. Gendreau and C. W. McArthur and 15½ other ranks wounded [as transcribed], 6 other ranks missing and 2 other ranks wounded at duty (26 August), and for 28 August, 4 other ranks killed, Capt. J. A. Balance, Capt. P. H. Wade, Lieut. P. F. Parizeau and Lieut. H. A. Smith [uncertain] and 126 other ranks wounded, 4 other ranks missing, 1 missing believed killed in action, and Capt. P. W. Freeman and Lieut. J. V. Young wounded at duty, with approximately 300 prisoners taken on the 26th and about 20 on the 28th. | People: Capt. W. J. Atherton; Capt. F. Gill; Lieut. E. R. [uncertain]; Lieut. R. D. Farley; Lieut. J. J. Gendreau; Lieut. C. W. McArthur; Capt. J. A. Balance; Capt. P. H. Wade; Lieut. P. F. Parizeau; Lieut. H. A. Smith [uncertain]; Capt. P. W. Freeman; Lieut. J. V. Young. | Companies: 23rd Cdn. Bn.; 43rd Cdn. Bn.; 4th C.M.R. Bn.; 1st Royal Warwicks; "A" Coy. | Casualties: 26 August: Capt. W. J. Atherton and 13 ORs killed, 1 OR died of wounds, 5 officers and 15½ ORs wounded [as transcribed], 6 ORs missing, 2 ORs wounded at duty; 28 August: 4 ORs killed, 4 officers and 126 ORs wounded, 4 ORs missing, 1 OR missing believed killed, 2 officers wounded at duty; approx. 320 prisoners taken.

- **1918-08-31 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Blangy / Pampoux, France** — At 5.30 p.m. orders received to remove the two guns from Blangy to a more advanced position near Pampoux to reach the whole of Brebieres, guns to be in action by 11 p.m. 1 September; guns went out of action at 8.30 p.m. and were pulled out during the night; 11 rounds on Vitry Church, 50 on Vitry Station and 35 counter-battery work; work during the latter half of the month exceptionally heavy — with the exception of three weeks' intensive training in February, the battery had now been constantly in action, mostly in very advanced positions, for 16 months without a break, the last rest of 10 days being in May 1917. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Blangy–Pampoux (in progress).

- **1918-09-02 | 5th Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Arras, France** — Mortars attached to the Canadian Motor Machine Gun Brigade in action on the Cambrai Road near Dury, doing effective work against enemy transport, machine gunners and reinforcements; one of the unit's lorries hit and blown up; Capt Wood's detachment of 2 mortars attached to the 10th C.I.B. left Arras at 5 a.m. for Vis-en-Artois. | People: Capt Wood | Companies: Canadian Motor Machine Gun Brigade; 10th C.I.B. | Casualties: 1 other rank killed, 3 officers and other ranks wounded (diary); appendix lists Gnr. Brigade | Casualties: 2 other ranks killed (incl. 1 M.T. driver), 8 other ranks wounded (incl. 1 M.T. driver), 3 officers wounded | Movement: To Wancourt and the Cambrai Road.
- **1918-09-02 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Gouves to Arras, France** — The battalion paraded at 8.30 a.m., from 9 to 12.30 companies carried on independently with physical training and bayonet fighting, drill and organisation, at 5 a.m. orders were received to be ready to move at four hours' notice and at 10 a.m. to be ready at one hour's notice, at 3.30 p.m. the order was received that the battalion would proceed to Arras by march route, and at 5 p.m. the battalion moved off, arriving in Arras at 7.30 p.m., on the road passing thousands of Hun prisoners and hearing the wildest rumours regarding a great advance by the 1st and 4th Divisions, later information being received that the Drocourt Line had been broken through, 4,500 prisoners obtained, and patrols pushing on. | People: — | Companies: 1st Cdn. Div.; 4th Cdn. Div. | Casualties: none | Movement: Gouves–Arras.
- **1918-09-02 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Spider Corner / Pampoux, France** — Guns at Spider Corner went out of action at 8 p.m. and were pulled out to move forward to new positions at Pampoux (H17c), to be in action by daylight; crews, already after a 24-hour shift, worked through the night, 2 guns in action by 5 a.m. and the third by 10 a.m.; 653 rounds fired, 14 N.F. calls answered plus 1 from the balloon section and several zone calls, 80 rounds harassing fire at night on Brebieres and 159 rounds in support of the infantry attack in the early morning. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Spider Corner–Pampoux.

Ingersoll reported for duty, Lieut. J. A. Adamson was appointed Battalion Staff Officer, vice Lieut. L. Atto (wounded), and Pte. Lancaster was wounded in the leg by an H.E. shell. | People: Lieut. - **1918-09-07 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Eterpigny / Pampoux, France** — Two guns in action at Eterpigny came under 42nd Brigade R.G.A. for tactical purposes; in the afternoon the enemy opened a destructive shoot on the new position with 5.9" and 8", 2.15–3.30 p.m., over 300 shells fired into or around the position, which was quite open with very little cover, but fortunately no casualties and no damage to material; three guns at Pampoux fired 260 rounds on selected targets. | People: — | Companies: 42nd Brigade R.G.A. | Casualties: none

- **1918-09-07 | 9th Overseas Battery Siege Artillery | Battery Point Camp, St. John, N.B.** — Only a proposed syllabus survives for this week (the typed year reads "1916" [uncertain]; the day-dates — Monday 2 to Saturday 7 September — fit September 1918). The covering letter of 9 September 1918 reports the schedule of work for last week was carried out with excellent results; one of the guns here has been elevated for instructional work, and a dug-out has been constructed, so a thorough practical knowledge is being acquired by the men of the classes. | Casualties: none.

- **1918-09-10 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Vis-en-Artois area, France** — The O.C., Lieut.-Colonel M. Rhodes D.S.O. M.C., proceeded on leave to England, and Major J. S. E. Todd M.C. took over command of the battalion, a working party of 2 officers and 100 other ranks was detailed to report at Division, a salvage party of 1 officer and 20 other ranks per company cleaned up Square O.20, a warning order was received that the battalion would relieve the R.C.R. in right support, and at 2 p.m. Major Todd, with a party from each company, went forward to reconnoitre; Major General Lipsett, the Divisional Commander, visited the battalion at 4 p.m. to say farewell prior to his leaving to take over command of the 4th Imperial Division, all officers and N.C.O.s being paraded to meet him, and he expressed his regret at leaving the division and congratulated and thanked the battalion for the loyal support given him and the splendid work done whilst he had been Divisional Commander, Brigadier General Draper suitably responding on behalf of the battalion, the O.C. being on leave and Major Todd away reconnoitring. | People: Lieut.-Colonel M. Rhodes D.S.O. M.C.; Major J. S. E. Todd M.C.; Major General Lipsett; Brigadier General Draper. | Companies: R.C.R. | Casualties: none
- **1918-09-10 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Cagnicourt, France** — Quartermaster's stores and remaining heavy stores brought up, completing the move; 690 rounds expended, including a destructive shoot on a hostile battery at XA 14a 50.45 conducted by Lieut. - **1918-09-15 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | P.36.b.70.90, Canal du Nord, France** — Orders were received that at dawn the battalion was to send a reconnoitring party to the forward areas to arrange about relieving the 1st C.M.R. Battalion in the line, at 1 p.m. the enemy commenced to shell the battalion headquarters, which was in a gun pit with a roof about two feet thick, Major Todd, Lieut. Ince and Lieut. Cooks vacating it and moving out into the road, the enemy continuing to shell the locality until he obtained a direct hit, the M.O., Padre and Lieut. Cooks, who had taken refuge in an old bluff, being badly shaken up and gassed, the Padre, Capt. Nicholson, being evacuated; orders were received for the relief of the 1st C.M.R. Battalion, which commenced at 9 p.m., and at midnight the Adjutant of the 1st C.M.R. Battalion received a telephone message stating there was trouble in the Crater (from the O.C. C Company, 1st C.M.R. Battalion), Lieut. Ganong, O.C. A Company, 5th C.M.R. Battalion, asking permission to go forward with his platoon and investigate, which was granted, and at 4.10 a.m. he reported that the situation was normal. | People: Major Todd; Lieut. Ince; Lieut. Cooks; Capt. Nicholson. | Companies: 1st C.M.R. Bn.; "A" Coy.; "C" Coy. (1st C.M.R. Bn.). | Casualties: M.O., Padre (Capt. Nicholson, evacuated) and Lieut. Cooks shaken up and gassed.

- **1918-09-16 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front line, Canal du Nord, France** — The relief was reported completed at 4.10 a.m., the enemy artillery was very active and succeeded in bringing down two of our balloons, at 5.30 the O.C. A Company telephoned that there was trouble in the Crater and that he was going forward to investigate, the C.O. proceeding forward at 7.30 p.m., Capt. Craig, 8th C.I.B., reporting for liaison, and at 10.30 a.m. Major Todd returned having made preparation to retake the crater, from which the battalion had been driven out, but on consultation with brigade it was decided to hold an outpost line immediately west of the crater, from which command of the canal could be obtained; Lieut. Ingersoll, Assistant Staff Officer, reported that at 9 p.m. the night previous he had made a reconnaissance of the crater and had found it unoccupied, and could not find any trace of the missing men (18 men reported missing, believed either wounded or killed), harassing fire being employed on the canal area all day, and at 5 p.m. D Company commenced to relieve A Company, the line being drawn in in accordance with further instructions from brigade; one of our 6-inch howitzer guns fired short, killing 2 and wounding 8 of our men. | People: Capt. Craig; Major Todd; Lieut. Ingersoll. | Companies: 8th C.I.B.; "A" Coy.; "D" Coy. | Casualties: 2 ORs killed, 8 ORs wounded (own 6-inch howitzer firing short); 18 men missing, believed wounded or killed; 2 balloons brought down.

- **1918-09-18 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Front line, Canal du Nord, France** — The relief was complete at 1 a.m. and the battalion had also taken up the new outpost line in accordance with instructions from brigade, the night passing quietly, the enemy appearing to have withdrawn his guns further north, and a warning order was received that the battalion would be relieved the night of 19/20 by two Imperial battalions, the London Scottish and the 1st London Regiment, many aerial combats taking place during the day; at dusk B Company, in right support, relieved the left company of the 2nd Battalion in the line, A Company, 1st Canadian Battalion, moving into right support and coming under the command of the C.O. 5th C.M.R. Battalion, company commanders from the London Scottish and the 1st London Regiment reporting and being sent to the companies they were to relieve, and two offensive battle patrols patrolling the frontage from 12 to 2 a.m. but not seeing any of the enemy west of the canal. | People: — | Companies: London Scottish; 1st London Regt.; 2nd Bn.; "A" Coy. 1st Cdn. - **1918-09-24 | 18th Battalion | Buissy Switch, from V.11.d.65.20. to V.30.b.25.00.** — Battalion rested during the day; two gas projections were successfully carried out during the night of 23rd/24th, "C" Company projecting 1,900 drums of pure phosgene gas from V.8.d.7.4. on targets astride the Arras-Cambrai Road and on the line of the Canal du Nord at zero hour 2.30 a.m., and "B" Special Coy. R.E. projecting 1,500 drums from W.19.d.7.6. on targets in W.20.d., W.21.a. and c. and the Canal du Nord bank at zero hour 12.20 a.m., with no hostile action following; our heavies fixed on and dispersed a hostile battery in W.20.b. at 11.20 a.m. and silenced another in W.1.a. at 4.30 p.m.; 1 other rank was wounded. | Companies: C Company; B Special Coy. R.E. | Locations: Arras-Cambrai Road; Canal du Nord.

- **1918-09-26 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Simencourt to Croisilles to Reincourt area, France** — The battalion paraded on the battalion alarm post at 11.30 a.m. and marched to Wancourt (the transport moving by road to the new area), entraining there for Croisilles, and on reaching Boyelles it was found that 200 yards of track had been torn up, the battalion detraining, marching two kilometres and then entraining again, arriving in Croisilles at 10.30 p.m. and immediately detraining, then marching to the new area in U.23.d., and after about a kilometre's march the enemy opened fire on the road with his long-range guns and obtained a direct hit on the transport, which was in front of the battalion, two men being killed and eight wounded and two horses killed, the rain starting and the road becoming very slippery and making marching difficult, especially near Bullecourt, where the ground was covered with shell holes, the battalion reaching the new area (near Reincourt) at 5.45, U.23.d.70.00., 2 a.m. | People: — | Companies: — | Casualties: 2 ORs killed, 8 ORs wounded; 2 horses killed. | Movement: Simencourt–Wancourt (march)–Croisilles (train)–Reincourt area (march).

- **1918-09-27 | 5th Canadian Divisional Trench Mortar Group | Hendecourt, France** — Orders for mobile mortars; Lt Williams and Lt Montgomery with 4 mortars and crews left for the vicinity of Quarry Wood at 5.45 p.m.; wagon lines established at E 9 d 2.0 at 10.30 p.m.; Lt Williams delayed reporting to 9th C.I.B. until 12.30 a.m. after his runner, an officer and 2 men of the 44th Battalion were gassed en route. | People: Lt Williams, Lt Montgomery | Companies: 9th C.I.B.; 44th Battalion | Casualties: 4 men gassed (Lt Williams's runner, an officer and 2 men of the 44th Bn) | Movement: Hendecourt to Quarry Wood area.
- **1918-09-27 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Reincourt area to Inchy Cross, France** — At 5.45 a.m. the 1st and 3rd Canadian Divisions attacked in conjunction with troops on the right and left, at 11.30 a.m. a telephone message from the B.M. stated that the battalion would move forward in conjunction with the remainder of the 3rd C.I. Brigade to Inchy Cross, H.Q. D.4.d.4.5., confirmed by Lieut. B. Long at 10.40 a.m., at 11.20 a.m. the battalion moved off and arrived in the new area at 2 p.m., H.Q. D.4.d.4.5., orders being received to be ready to move at a moment's notice, information being received that the 1st Canadian Division had captured Bourlon Wood and occupied the Blue Line, and at 6 p.m. orders were received that the battalion would move at once, but these were cancelled when the battalion was informed it would not move until morning; the men enjoyed some hot tea, and Lieut. Dibble reported for duty. | People: Lieut. B. Long; Lieut. Dibble. | Companies: 1st Cdn. Div.; 3rd Cdn. Div.; 3rd C.I.B. | Casualties: none | Movement: Reincourt area–Inchy Cross.

- **1918-09-29 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Assembly area, Cambrai front, France** — The battalion moved off at 3.10 a.m. and reached the assembly area at 6.30, R.4.F.9.c.70.30., the 8th C.I. Brigade, in conjunction with the 9th C.I. Brigade on the right and the 7th C.I. Brigade on the left, attacking, the 1st and 2nd C.M.R. attacking, the 4th C.M.R. in support and the 5th C.M.R. in reserve, zero at 8 a.m., the battalion reaching the assembly area without sustaining any casualties, the enemy apparently fighting very hard in front of Cambrai, and later in the afternoon the situation improving, the 11th Battalion and the 1st C.M.R. capturing the "Olle" [uncertain], English regiments also pushing up on the south of Cambrai; apparently the battalion would not move tonight, and rations and field kitchens were brought up and the men dug into funk holes and made themselves as comfortable as possible. | People: — | Companies: 1st C.M.R. - **1918-10-01 | 18th Battalion | Buissy Switch & Hindecourt Support Line, V.30.b & d.** — At 06:00 the battalion moved across the Canal du Nord, resting for the day in open fields south of the Arras-Cambrai Road in W.23. & 24.; at dusk it moved to divisional support positions in Haynecourt village, Battalion Headquarters in an old German machine-gun dugout at X.9.c.10.20. - **1918-10-01 | No. 1 Company, Canadian Forestry Corps | In the Field** — Monthly summary, 1st–31st October: on the evening of 2nd October a phone message from District Headquarters called for a draft of 100 men from the District as infantry reinforcements, the Company's proportion 15; men from other companies reported here on the 3rd and the complete draft proceeded to C.E.R.C., Aubin St. Vaast, on 4th October, conducted by Capt. Hutchison and Lieut. Scott, arriving 12 noon; the Company's quota was raised to 18 after men from other companies failed the local medical examination. Loss of the drafted men and sickness amongst the P.O.W. attached labour considerably handicapped operations; during the week of the 19th, 4 trainloads of road slabs (27,286 pieces) were despatched by rail; the sidings and dump at Madicourt [uncertain] are now in daily use, shipments being made over them to the capacity of available rolling stock. Maj. A. J. Bell struck off strength on transfer to District Headquarters and appointed 2nd in Command, No. 9 District C.F.C. (21st October); Capt. W. Hutchison taken on strength on transfer from Headquarters. Influenza broke out early in October in the camp of the 10th P.O.W. Company and by the end of the month 80% of the Company were either evacuated to hospital or sick in lines; the epidemic was confined to that company. During the month a new Bath House and Y.M.C.A. Hut were completed for the use of the men. | People: Capt. W. Hutchison; Lieut. Scott; Maj. A. J. Bell. | Casualties: none among the Company's own men; influenza in the 10th P.O.W. Company — 80% evacuated to hospital or sick in lines by the end of the month. | Movement: draft of 18 men to C.E.R.C., Aubin St. Vaast, 4th October; Capt. Hutchison arrived from District Headquarters, 3rd October; Maj. A. J. Bell transferred to District Headquarters, 21st October; Capt. W. Hutchison taken on strength from Headquarters.

- **1918-10-10 | 18th Battalion | Bn. HQ, Chateau Escaudoeuvres; T.10.d.40.50** — At 06:00 the battalion assembled in T.20.a. & d. and advanced to the jumping-off position in T.6.c. & d., jumping off under an artillery barrage at 07:00 with Battalion Headquarters in a funk hole in the railway cutting at T.10.d.40.50, the 19th Battalion on the right and the 6th Brigade on the left; the barrage was not good, and progress was retarded half an hour by our own shells breaking just ahead of the jumping-off position. "A" and "B" Companies (left and right respectively) led off, "D" Company in support and "C" Company in reserve: "A" Company reached old trenches in T.10.b. and T.11.a. but was stopped by enemy machine-gun fire from the left flank, the brigade on the left not having got forward, while "B" Company reached the river in T.11.b. & d. and formed and held a line there. About 13:00 the 19th Battalion with cavalry patrols was swung over from the right to outflank the high ground in U.2.c. but was unsuccessful owing to intense machine-gun fire and our artillery being out of range, and at 14:00 Lieut. L. J. Boulton with nine men established a post in the railway embankment at T.11.b.60.60., east of a river [uncertain] found to be dry; no further attempt was made to advance, and the night passed very quietly. | People: Lieut. L. J. Boulton; Lieut. W.A. Cash; Lieut. J. Spyer; Lieut. H.N. Wilson; Lieut. A. E. Babcock; Lieut. J.C. Little; Bateman. | Companies: A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company; 19th Battalion; 6th Brigade. | Movement: Chateau Escaudoeuvres → T.20.a. & d. → T.6.c. & d. → T.10.b./T.11.a. & b. | Casualties: Lieut. W.A. Cash and 6 O.R.s killed; Lieuts. J. Spyer, H.N. Wilson and A. E. Babcock and 70 O.R.s wounded; Lieut. J.C. Little and Bateman reported missing.

- **1918-10-11 | 18th Battalion | Bn. HQ, Escaudoeuvres** — At 09:00 the battalion, in support to the 20th and 21st Battalions, advanced from trenches in T.10.b. & T.11.a. & b., "C" and "D" Companies on right and left front respectively, "B" Company in support and "A" Company in reserve, Battalion Headquarters in the cellar of a farm house at T.12.a.90.10 about 09:30. The two front-line battalions swung over too far to the left, and "C" Company, when the line was threatened by enemy tanks, took up a position in C.31.c. and turned back three enemy tanks by concentrated rifle [uncertain], Lewis gun and machine-gun fire, turning five enemy machine guns around for the purpose; the front-line battalions being driven back by the enemy tanks on the left and the Imperial Brigade on the right also withdrawing, "C" Company dropped back to the support position in U.1.c., then immediately advanced with "B" Company to a sunken road in T.6.b. and U.1.a., forming a line there with the 20th and 21st Battalions and a few men of the W. Yorks Regiment. At 16:30 "C" and "D" Companies, attached to the 21st Battalion, advanced under an artillery barrage to N.30.d. & C.25.c. & b., but the Imperials on the right not getting forward, the troops were drawn back to form a line through N.36.d. & C.31.c. & d., in which position they were relieved by the 51st Division; relief was complete at 23:00, "C" and "D" Companies being relieved by the Gordons and "A" and "B" Companies by the Seaforth Highlanders, and on relief the companies moved independently to billets in Escaudoeuvres. Lieut. J. A. McMillan returned from leave, Capt. T.H.O. Rayward (and batman) proceeded to the 12th Instructors Course at Senior Officers School, Aldershot, 1 other rank proceeded to and 1 returned from a Corps Gas Course, and 5 other ranks proceeded to and 2 returned from hospital. | People: Capt. W. J. Baxter; Lieut. T. V. Milford; Lieut. J. A. McMillan; Capt. T.H.O. Rayward. | Companies: A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company; 20th Battalion; 21st Battalion; 51st Division; Gordons; Seaforth Highlanders; W. Yorks Regt.; Imperial Brigade. | Locations: Escaudoeuvres. | Movement: Trenches, T.10.b./T.11.a. & b. → Escaudoeuvres. | Casualties: Capt. W. J. Baxter, Lieut. T. V. Milford and 54 O.R.s wounded; 11 O.R.s killed; 18 O.R.s wounded—gassed.

- **1918-10-14 | 18th Battalion | Right Front Line, N.5.d.20.55. to N.22.b.00.90.; Bn. HQ, Hordain, N.16.b.70.50** — Upon receipt of a warning order all preparations were made for going into the line, rear details moving back to Eswars, and the battalion went forward at dusk, relieving the 24th Canadian Battalion in the right front line from N.5.d.20.55. to N.22.b.00.90., Battalion Headquarters in a chateau at Hordain at N.16.b.70.50 formerly used by the enemy as a hospital; relief was complete at 20:25. During the night the battalion area was heavily shelled with high-explosive and gas shells; 1 other rank was wounded, 2 other ranks proceeded on and 1 returned from leave, 4 proceeded to and 20 returned from hospital, and 3 arrived as reinforcements. Appendix No. 3 (18th Bn. Order No. D.250) and Appendix No. 4 (disposition sketch) are attached. | Companies: 24th Canadian Battalion. | Locations: Eswars; Hordain. | Movement: Thun-Leveque → Right Front Line (Hordain). | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded.

- **1918-10-16 | 18th Battalion | Right Front Line, N.5.d.20.55. to N.22.b.00.90.** — During the night of 15th/16th patrols covered the battalion frontage: Lieut. A. S. Jones with 8 other ranks patrolled N.16.a. and c. up to our position in N.10. and found the ground dry and level and not swampy until the area immediately north of the platoon in N.10. central, while enemy machine guns swept the area from approximately N.15. central; on attempting to cross the canal in a punt, Lieut. Jones and 2 other ranks were fired on by a machine gun in a house at N.16.c.50.20., and our post at N.16.c.65.15. reported constant movement and noises in this house, from which six of the enemy left at dawn and proceeded north-west, disappearing behind a hedge at N.16.c.10.20. Another patrol of Lieut. Jones and 6 other ranks crossed the bridge at N.23.a.70.70. in the early morning and patrolled down the road south of the canal for 300 yards, then south to N.22.a. central and along the road running north-east to the bridge in N.22.a.70.70., with no enemy seen or heard; our artillery was active during the day. Lieut. J. Hammond and W. A. Rooney and 4 other ranks arrived as reinforcements, Lieut. H. A. Secord proceeded on leave and one other rank returned from leave, 3 other ranks proceeded to and 5 returned from hospital, and 3 other ranks went to First Army Rest Camp. | People: Lieut. A. S. Jones; Lieut. J. Hammond; W. A. Rooney; Lieut. H. A. Secord. | Companies: First Army Rest Camp. | Locations: Canal de L'Escaut.

- **1918-10-18 | 18th Battalion | Right Front Line, N.5.d.20.55. to N.22.b.00.90.** — A daylight patrol of Lieut. Stokes and 3 battalion scouts reconnoitred our post in N.5.c.00.40. and as far as N.5.d.65.90., with no enemy seen, hostile machine guns active from N.4.b.35.40., the party returning at 12:00; there was very little artillery activity on either side during the day and the weather was fair but very misty. During the evening the battalion was heavily shelled with high-explosive and gas, and 1 other rank was wounded. In accordance with 4th C.I.B. Order No. 26 and 18th Battalion Operation Order No. D.251 the battalion was relieved by the 20th Canadian Battalion, relief complete at 21:10, and on relief the companies moved independently to Thun-Leveque, taking over the billets formerly occupied there; 2 other ranks proceeded on and 2 returned from leave, and 3 returned from hospital. Appendix No. 5 (Operation Order No. D.251) is attached. | People: Lieut. Stokes. | Companies: 4th C.I.B.; 20th Canadian Battalion. | Locations: Thun-Leveque; Canal de L'Escaut. | Movement: Right Front Line → Thun-Leveque. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded.

- **1918-10-20 | 18th Battalion | Paillencourt, N.26.a.50.85.** — This entry covers 20–21 October as written. The mornings were occupied with company and unit inspections, with parades for kit shortages also held, and for the remainder of the day the battalion rested in billets, many of the men going fishing in the nearby canals. On the 20th Lieut. Col. Jones proceeded to Paris on leave, Lieut. MacRae [uncertain] to England on leave, and Lieut. L. J. Boulton to the Officers Rest House, Paris–Place, and Lieut. T. V. Milford died of wounds at No. 33 C.C.S.; 2 other ranks returned from hospital. On the 21st Lieut. Benden and one other rank returned from leave, and 3 other ranks returned from hospital. | People: Lieut. Col. Jones; Lieut. MacRae [uncertain]; Lieut. L. J. Boulton; Lieut. T. V. Milford; Lieut. - **1918-10-23 | 18th Battalion | Aniche, C.6.d.20.70.** — The billets of the entire battalion here are without doubt the best and most comfortable ever occupied in this country; the town itself is practically free from damage by shell fire during the recent advance, there are no civilians in the town, they having been forced by the enemy to accompany him in his retirement, and the numerous gardens about the town were well stocked and furnished a plentiful supply of vegetables for the men. - **1918-11-09 | 18th Battalion | Frameries** — Battalion moved off in fighting order at dawn and jumped over the 25th Canadian Battalion between Elouges and Wasmes, meeting no opposition as it moved to Frameries, where Battalion Headquarters was established; rear details moved off at 10.00 hours and marched via Dour, Petit Wasmes and Paturages to Frameries, the people along the route cheering the troops and loading them with flowers and food; during the night the battalion pushed forward and established a line of posts through Morchain. Appendix 9's narrative adds that the 18th (left) and 21st Battalions attacked with the 19th and 20th in support, "A" Company on the right and "B" on the left, advancing some 14,000 yards to a line east and north of Noirchain before being held up by an enemy machine-gun nest on the high ground at Ciply; at dusk patrols pushed forward and by midnight the whole of Ciply was in the battalion's hands, "A" Company holding the line along the railway at Q.25, and "B" Company under Lieut. Goodman completed the capture of Ciply (North) and was in communication with "A" Company by midnight; a platoon under Lieut. Smith surprised German sappers about to blow a road mine at V.11.a.60.35, shooting dead the sapper about to fire it, while a platoon under Lieut. Morgan cleared German machine-gun nests. | People: Lieut. Smith; Lieut. Morgan; Lieut. Goodman. | Companies: 25th Canadian Battalion; 21st Battalion; 19th Battalion; 20th Battalion; A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company; 3rd Canadian Division; 63rd Naval Division. | Locations: Wasmes; Dour; Petit Wasmes; Paturages; Morchain; Noirchain; Ciply. | Movement: Elouges → Frameries.

- **1918-11-10 | 18th Battalion | Ciply, L.2-33.97** — At 04.00 hours the battalion pushed forward and established posts in Ciply and Hyon, meeting very little opposition; rear details moved up from Frameries and reached Ciply about 10.00 hours; there was considerable scattered shelling of the village and vicinity until 15.00 hours, when the enemy guns were silenced by our batteries; 4 other ranks proceeded on leave, 5 returned from leave, 1 returned from hospital, 10 other ranks were wounded and 1 other rank killed in action. Appendix 9 adds that the 19th and 20th Battalions were due to jump through at about 08.00 hours but, the 18th having advanced so rapidly, did not overtake them until after 09.30; forward patrols had several encounters with the retiring enemy and the most forward post was established on high ground on the outskirts of Hyon (Q.20.c.40.60); the narrative gives the operation's total casualties as twelve (two killed and ten wounded), against the diary text's one killed and ten wounded on this day. | Companies: 19th Battalion; 20th Battalion. | Locations: Hyon. | Movement: Frameries → Ciply. | Casualties: 1 O.R. killed in action; 10 O.R. wounded.

- **1918-11-11 | 17th Canadian Reserve Battalion (Nova Scotia) | Bramshott, Hants.** — Armistice signed at 0500 and fighting ceased at 1100, 1559th day of the War; training in morning; afternoon declared a holiday by General Officer Commanding, all training dispensed with; canteens and messes opened for troops all afternoon; smoker and concert in Sergeants' and Officers' Messes in evening. | Companies: N.S.R.D.
- **1918-11-11 | 18th Battalion | Ciply** — At 07.25 hours a wire was received from Brigade stating that hostilities would cease at 11.00 hours that day and the battalion was to stand fast at the line reached at that hour; the battalion's forward post at the cessation of hostilities was at Q.19.d.30.40 (Sheet 45); a battalion parade was held at 11.30 hours, Major Bell congratulating the battalion on its fine work during the recent operations; as an appreciation, the Maire, on behalf of the villagers of Ciply, presented the battalion with a Belgian flag. Lieut. A. T. Fergusson and 2 other ranks returned from leave, 1 other rank returned from course, 13 other ranks returned from hospital, and 1 other rank was wounded-gassed. | People: Maj. Bell; Lieut. A. T. Fergusson; Maire of Ciply. | Casualties: 1 O.R. wounded (gassed).
- **1918-11-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Mons, Belgium** — Headquarters moved to Mons, the office being established at 1800 hours, a rear office was left in Jemappes to handle No. 3 Section, which had not moved forward, No. 3 Section relieved No. 2 Section in the line after the cessation of hostilities, and 2 pair of D.8 twisted wire were laid between Jemappes and Mons using a further 20,000 yards of cable. | People: — | Companies: No. 2/3 Sections | Casualties: none | Movement: Jemappes–Mons
- **1918-11-11 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Train | Jemappes–Mons** — At 8 a.m. news that the Germans would sign the Armistice at 11 a.m.; Mons captured before daylight; Gen. Sir Arthur Currie made his triumphal entry at 3.30 p.m., addressed the crowd and presented his lance with the Canadian Pennant to the Mayor; Train H.Q. spent the first night after the Armistice in Mons; Lieut. Lawrence reported died in England of the 'Flu. | People: General Sir Arthur Currie, General Stewart, Lieut. Lawrence. | Companies: — | Casualties: Lieut. - **1918-12-01–1918-12-31 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Jemappes, Belgium** — Monthly summary: the month passed very quietly at Jemappes, morning parades at 9 a.m. and a syllabus of training (foot drill, gun drill, physical training), afternoons devoted to outdoor games and evenings to concerts and entertainments; sightseeing trips to Brussels curtailed by transport difficulties; Christmas spent with an excellent dinner of plum pudding, turkey, fruit, nuts and beer, followed by an entertainment assisted by a blind professor of music and dances in the evening; usual parades resumed on the 28th; nothing unusual in the latter part of the month. | People: a blind professor of music (unnamed). | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1918-12-13 | 18th Battalion | Duisdorf, Germany 2-I 7 D 35.49** — The battalion moved off in full marching order at 08.00 hours and marched via Bonn, crossing the River Rhine there, to its final destination in the town of Hennef. Passing through Bonn the battalion marched with rifles at the slope and bayonets fixed and passed in review at the east end of the Bonn Bridge before the Corps and Divisional Commanders, Lieut.-General A. W. Currie, Corps Commander, taking the salute, with Maj.-Gen. W. F. Burstall, Commander of the Division, and the Divisional Staff immediately in rear of Lieut.-Gen. Currie on the reviewing stand. On arrival in Hennef at 13.30 hours Battalion Headquarters was located in the office of a manufacturing establishment on Frankfurter-strasse and Headquarters officers were billeted in a large chateau nearby; the men of "A", "B" and "D" Companies were assigned billets in the private homes of the civilian population, and "D" Company proceeded without delay to Happerschoss to be on duty as Outpost Company. 3 other ranks returned from leave. | People: Lieut.-General A. W. Currie; Maj.-Gen. W. F. Burstall. | Companies: A Company; B Company; D Company. | Locations: Bonn; River Rhine; Frankfurter-strasse; Happerschoss. | Movement: Duisdorf → Hennef (via Bonn, across the Rhine).

D. A. New of the Canadian Signal Pool, C.C.R.C., attached to the wireless section, was awarded the Military Medal while Lieut. H. Pryde and 1 O.R. rejoined from leave. | People: Lieut. H. Pryde; Spr. D. A. New | Companies: 7th C.I.B.; 3rd M.G. Bn | Casualties: none | Movement: Division Headquarters Mons–Nivelles

Conforming with Army Orders, the Burgermeister instructed the population to report to Battalion Headquarters for identification passes, giving a description of the holder with a photograph attached, and several men with knowledge of the German language were selected for battalion duty as interpreters. 1 other rank proceeded on a Hand Compositors Course, 6 other ranks returned from leave, 2 other ranks of the Canadian Corps Cyclists returned to their unit, and 2 other ranks went to hospital. | Companies: Canadian Corps Cyclists.
- **1918-12-14 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Nivelles, Belgium** — Office traffic was recorded, a mass meeting of soldiers of 7th C.I. - **1918-12-15 | 18th Battalion | Hennef** — The battalion formed up on parade and marched through the town to a theatre, in which nothing in the way of amusement had been presented for quite some time, and there held Church Service; the padre, being in fine form, gave an excellent sermon which was thoroughly appreciated by all members present. 1 other rank proceeded to Brigade Duty as Paymaster's Clerk.
- **1918-12-15 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Nivelles, Belgium** — Office traffic was recorded, No. 2 Section and transport left Nivelles at 0730 hours by a circuitous route to avoid the main square, the precaution proving unnecessary as the temper of the men had changed during the night, all battalions paraded at full strength except a few irreconcilables who remained behind and were now A.O.W., the section went into billets in Genval, communication with 3rd C.D.A. - **1918-12-18 | 18th Battalion | Allner, 6 C 99.99, Germany 2-L** — The men have now fully recovered from the hardships of the march and are training as per the syllabi attached, the spirit of the men superb and entering into the daily routine with an eagerness and willingness proverbial with the Canadians as a whole. - **1918-12-23 | 18th Battalion | Allner** — The battalion continued training as per the syllabi attached and maintained control of the area, with the duties of District Commandant and Town Major combined in the towns of Hennef (north of the railway), Allner, Happerschoss, Heisterschoß, Probach [uncertain] and Welderoven, in the person of the O.C. Battalion; the Headquarters Officer has an office at Hennef permanently for stamping identification cards, district administration is carried on through the Quartermaster, and no civilians are employed. One railway post stands on the broad gauge railway station at Hennef, with telephone connection to the Inter-Allied Railway Commission at Cologne, and on the outpost line there are two main control posts, four subsidiary posts and two patrols (reference map Germany 2-L), guarding bridges and permitting traffic with neutral territory only through the main control posts. No. 377222 Pte. Pihl W. (193 Labour Coy.) and No. 316786 Pte. Wieber J. (11th Coy. Cdn. Forestry Corps) are attached from 4th C.I.B. as interpreters at the Railway Central Post, and no I. (B.) Police are attached. 3 other ranks proceeded on leave and 3 returned from leave, 5 other ranks were attached to 2nd Divisional Train, and 1 other rank went to hospital. | People: Pte. Pihl W. (No. 377222); Pte. Wieber J. (No. 316786). | Companies: 193 Labour Coy.; 11th Coy. Cdn. Forestry Corps; 4th C.I.B.; 2nd Divisional Train. | Locations: Hennef; Allner; Happerschoss; Heisterschoß; Probach [uncertain]; Welderoven; Muschmuhl; Muehlhal [uncertain]; Euel; Triesch; Winterscheid; Brohl-Scheid; Cologne.

- **1918-12-25 | 18th Battalion | Allner** — "A MERRY CHRISTMAS TO ALL." Christmas Day dawned bright and clear, with just a touch of snow upon the ground, and the members of the battalion were in excellent spirit, thoroughly prepared for anything the day might bring forth. The officers had made every preparation for a fine Christmas dinner: the tables in the different company mess-rooms were teeming with good things — "A" Company in a large hall in the northern section of the town, "C" Company in a picturesque theatre in the centre of the town, "D" Company in one of the town's schools, and "B" Company, on duty as Outpost Company, in one of the schools in Euel — the mess-rooms decorated in a pleasant Christmas-like style and the tables loaded with roast turkeys, oranges, nuts, ginger ale cakes, turkey, meats, vegetables, Christmas plum pudding and other items. Lt.-Col. L. E. Jones and staff officers and the officers of the different companies attended each of the dinners, and during the dinner Lt.-Col. Jones made a very felicitous speech of appreciation, wishing the battalion a very Merry Christmas and every prosperity for the coming year — the anniversary year of the Ending of the War — and complimenting the men upon their share of the conflict; the men rose and gave him three of the most hearty cheers and a "Tiger". 2 other ranks proceeded on leave and 3 returned. | People: Lt.-Col. L. E. Jones. | Companies: A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: Euel.

- **1918-12-25 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Maransart** — In the morning a voluntary service was held in the Hall at Maransart, Capt. Caldwell of the 2nd C.M.R. officiating, and final preparations for the men's dinner that night were completed; in the afternoon the C.O. visited all companies whilst at their dinner, all officers and men being of the opinion that this has been the best Christmas the battalion has spent in this country, A Company having the distinction of dining in a café just alongside the "Lion of Waterloo", and later information was received from Brigade that the 8th C.I.B. Group would move into the 5th Army area on the 27th inst., so the battalion officers' dinner will be held the next night, the 26th, about 300 individual Christmas parcels and 2,000 cigarettes having been received and distributed. | People: Capt. - **1919-01-01–1919-01-31 | 5th Canadian Siege Battery | Jemappes, Belgium** — Monthly summary: battery remained billeted in Jemappes with 1st Brigade C.G.A.; on 4 January the Brigade was inspected by the G.O.C.R.A. in the square at Jemappes, guns, cookhouse, guard and billets visited afterwards; on 16 January XXII Corps H.A. was inspected at Mons by the Corps Commander, three lorries conveying battery personnel, medals and decorations presented to 107 officers and men, and a letter of congratulation for the smart appearance and steadiness of the men received from the G.O.C.R.A. the next day; great strides in the educational scheme, classes in gas engines, mathematics and French started with great enthusiasm, and a Brigade cinema inaugurated by members of the Brigade; nothing of especial interest during the month. | People: Major N. - **1919-01-16 | 18th Battalion | Allner** — The battalion continued training as per the syllabus attached (Appendix 16) and educational work was carried on as usual; the diary records the Defence Scheme in case of renewal of hostilities or enemy attack (copy attached, Appendix 17): on warning of renewed hostilities the brigade reserve battalion would push forward to the Rheinbreitbach–Eudenbach–Muhleip–Eitorf line, while if the enemy attacked without warning "B" Company would withdraw from the Brohl area to the heights Weisterschloss and Happerschoss, "D" Company would occupy the Schloss Allner and the high ground to the north-east, destroying the bridges over the river Sieg, "C" Company would occupy Hennef covering the railway lines, and "A" Company, in battalion reserve, would move to Weingarts-Gass; companies would act on the word "Positions", "A" Company reinforcing on "Battle-positions" and counter-attacking on "Drive Back". Lieut. J. Morgan proceeded on leave to the United Kingdom with 5 other ranks, and Capt. C. H. Boulden and 1 other rank returned from leave. | People: Lieut. J. Morgan; Capt. C. H. Boulden; Lieut. C. Cook. | Companies: A Company; B Company; C Company; D Company. | Locations: Rheinbreitbach; Eudenbach; Muhleip; Eitorf; Brohl; Weisterschloss; Happerschoss; Schloss Allner; Hennef; Weingarts-Gass; River Sieg.

- **1919-02-07 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Hem** — The battalion fell in column of route on the main Roubaix Road at 0930 hrs. and proceeded by march route to Willems, but at 1200 hrs., when within five kilometres of Willems, information was received that there was no train for the 1st C.M.R. Bn., whose billets they were to occupy; the battalion was halted and the men given hot tea, at 1500 hrs. orders were received that 12 officers and 310 other ranks would proceed on 8 days' leave to England via Calais and on completion of leave report at Bramshott, at 1530 hrs. the party proceeded under command of Maj. J. S. E. Todd, M.C., and later instructions were received that the battalion, less officers and men proceeding on leave, would proceed to Hem, arriving at 1700 hrs. and not completely housed until 1930 hrs. owing to great difficulty securing billets. | People: Maj. - **1919-02-28 | 18th Battalion | Fosses, I.35.75.** — Battalion training and educational work as per the syllabus (Appendix 28). The battalion soccer team played a team from the Canadian Engineers at Godinne to-day, four motor lorries carrying the team and supporters to and from the game, the score 4–1 in our favour. During this month three days' leave has been granted to men desiring to visit Brussels and other towns in this vicinity where the battalion was billeted on the march to Germany. During the latter part of December, in connection with the "Khaki University", educational classes were inaugurated while the battalion was stationed at Hennef [uncertain] in Germany, to prepare the men for entry into civilian life on return to Canada, with courses in agriculture, business, motor mechanics and elementary work; one hour of each day is given over to educational work, and the scheme has received the enthusiastic support of all ranks. Lt-Col. L. E. Jones proceeded on leave, 4 other ranks went on leave, and 2 other ranks went to hospital. | People: Lt-Col. L. E. Jones. | Companies: Canadian Engineers. | Locations: Godinne; Brussels; Hennef [uncertain], Germany. | Casualties: 2 other ranks to hospital.

- **1919-03-06 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bramshott** — Presentation of Colours: the battalion paraded at 1130 hours, at twelve noon Sir George Perley arrived accompanied by Mrs. Perley and was met by the Divisional Commander, Maj.-Gen. Loomis, C.M.G., D.S.O., and the Brigade Commander, Brig.-Gen. Draper, C.M.G., D.S.O., the King's and Regimental Colours were consecrated by the Chaplain General of the Forces, Maj.-Gen. Taylor Smith, assisted by Lieut.-Col. Almond, Capt. Kelly and Davis, and Sir George Perley, High Commissioner of Canada, then presented the Regimental Colours to the battalion on behalf of the Eastern Townships, the battalion marching past on completion of a most impressive ceremony, after which the Divisional Commander entertained at luncheon; information was received that the battalion would sail from Liverpool on the 8th inst. and that the men from the Maritime Provinces would proceed to "A" Wing the next day, the 7th inst. | People: Sir George Perley; Mrs. Perley; Maj.-Gen. Loomis; Brig.-Gen. Draper; Maj.-Gen. Taylor Smith; Lieut.-Col. Almond; Capt. Kelly; Davis. | Companies: — | Casualties: none

- **1919-03-08 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Bramshott** — The last Part II Orders were issued, all officers and other ranks were struck off strength and the battalion ceased to exist as a unit in England; the battalion paraded in rear of the Bn. Orderly Room at 0630 hours, the Officer Commanding addressing the battalion before moving off, entrained at Liphook Station at 0900 hours, Liverpool was reached at 1910 hours, arrangements for embarking were good and by 2000 hours the men had been given tea and sandwiches and were aboard the Carmania, the Divisional Commander, Maj.-Gen. - **1919-03-17 | 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company | Bramshott Camp, England** — The remaining officers were struck off strength, O.M.F. of C. to C.E.F., thereby completing the disbandment of the 3rd Canadian Divisional Signal Company as a unit, the other ranks' drafts being Montreal 29, Toronto 65, Winnipeg 38, Hamilton 7 and Halifax 1, total 139 as typed in the diary, all drafts reporting to their respective draft officers at "F" Wing, Bramshott, to be absorbed into drafts proceeding as a body to their respective dispersal centres in Canada on the S.S. Cedric, Part II Orders No. 30 dated 18 March 1919 having been issued disposing of all personnel, the Company having been formed in the field in December 1915 under Major T. E. - **1919-03-17 | 5th Canadian Mounted Rifles | Halifax** — Reveille at 0500 hours, everyone hurried on deck and Canada was in sight once more; breakfast at 0630 hours, at 0730 hours the battalion fell in, the bands of the P.P.C.L.I., 49th Bn. and 4th C.M.R. massed on the boat deck playing national airs as the ship approached the dock, moored alongside No. 2 wharf at 0800 hours, met by Mr. Soles of the Eastern Townships Associated Boards, who advised that the battalion would travel on the C.P.R. through the Eastern Townships and stay off at Sherbrooke for two hours; at 1000 hours the battalion disembarked and once more set foot on Canadian soil after an absence of three years and eight months, the battalion proceeding in two trains, the first under the command of the O.C. and the second under Major Todd, M.C., and on arrival in Montreal marching through the town to the Peel St. Barracks, saluting the Colours for the last time and turning in their arms, the men whose relatives reside in Montreal being allowed to proceed to their homes and the remainder being instructed to report at 1430 hours the next day, when demobilization was completed. | People: Mr. Soles; Maj. Todd. | Companies: — | Casualties: none | Movement: Halifax–Montreal by train (via Sherbrooke); final entry of the diary.

- **1919-03-31 | 18th Battalion | Fosses, I.35.75** — "C" and "D" Companies and Battalion Headquarters formed up in the square in front of the Hotel de Ville at 08:45 hours in Full Marching Order and moved off at 09:00 hours for Auvelais, where they entrained for Le Havre at 11:00 hours together with three companies of the 19th Canadian Battalion; the train was made up of box cars, each equipped with a stove and sufficient straw, and the men were furnished with blankets; the Y.M.C.A. provided free tea at the station and had a car allotted for their use as a canteen, and also provided games, sporting goods and reading matter for use during the stops; the Corps and Divisional Commanders were at the station for a short period before the train left; the train pulled away at 12:30 hours, the first stop being made at Mons at 18:00 hours for supper and recreation; the day was ideal as to weather and the first day of the return journey to Canada found everyone in the best of spirits; the syllabus for the day was attached as Appendix No. 29. The diary ends here, signed by Lieut.-Colonel L. E. Jones, Commanding Officer. | People: Lieut.-Col. L. E.
